Although lacking in certain umami flavours of non-vegan sushi, all items on the plate were still well crafted and had soft sushi rice with a light chew, crisp vegetables, creamy elements like avocado or tofu. Thus every mouthful felt satisfying and flavourful, with ingredients that complement rather than complete.

Their Crunchy Tempura consisting of Fresh Shitake, Cauliflower, Broccoli and Enoki Mushroom, with their homemade batter, were all well fried, leaving each piece, golden brown and crispy on the outside. Complemented well with the natural sweetness of vegetables and texture. The Tempura Dipping sauce was too mild though.

Next that was served to our table was their Yasai Hand Roll that was filled with Vegetable Salad, Cucumber, Carrot, Purple Cabbage, G-Ken Floss, Vegan Mayonnaise, Toasted Sesame and Wrapped with Seaweed. Its fresh tasting, crisp and balanced.

Similar fillings to their Tempura Hand Roll, except for Mushrom Tempura, minus G-Ken Floss and Purple Cabbage. This Hand Roll has more crunch and umami from the mushrooms. Both Hand Rolls were done right and every bite was satisfying.

Then came their signature Kusa Ramen with Level 4 Spiciness. We are consistently looking forward to taste the different broth offered by vegan/vegetarian restaurant/cafe for their ramen, thus when their Kusa Ramen was served, we tasted the broth immediately. This time round a spicy base.

The broth was indeed spicy as warned by the service staff when we ordered, but still manageable and not overwhelming for us.
Its not just broth of chilli, but an aromatic broth simmered with chilli oil, garlic and umami-rich stock.

Overall, the toppings of Wakame, Silken Tofu, Broccoli, White Cabbage, Keto Noodles (Chewy) and the Spicy Broth mixed well enough together in a deep bowl. Every mouthful was hearty and fiery, good for spicy food lovers.

We ordered their Immune Boaster Congee with fungus and cabbage, to take the heat off the spicy ramen. Its flavourful but we didnt really like the coarse/firm texture of the rice grains.

Overall dining experience was good not only because of their food, but also the setting of the Japandi Styled interior. Its spacious, cosy and rather comfortable. Service Staffs were friendly and efficient, but could have been better if they were more attentive as we need to press button for service, even though there was some only another table of patrons during our dinner.

We will return when we visit KL again to try their other dishes like Miso Ramen, other type of sushi and maybe their fried rice.

name: Eslite Spectrum Kuala Lumpur
street: L1 01-34, LEVEL 1(L145, Starhill Gallery, 181, Jln Bukit Bintang
reviews: A very nicely designed and spacious, yet cosy bookstore and you will really enjoy the ambience here. Very tempting to just grab a book. We also had coffee inside the messengers cafe tucked in a corner of the bookstore. A very nice and relaxing experience

Absolutely love Eslite Spectrum KL. The space is beautifully designed which very spacious, artistic, and super cozy for both reading and relaxing. They’ve curated such a great mix of books, culture, and community. The staff are friendly and helpful, which makes the experience even better.

It’s not just a bookstore, but more like a cultural hangout spot, and I always walk away feeling inspired and calm. Definitely one of my go-to places in KL. Highly recommend it to anyone who loves books or just wants a quiet, creative place to chill.

Massive bookstore that is warm and conducive for reading. They have tables and seating area just for that purpose. Unlike others, the books are not wrapped and allow people to browse. That is certainly a huge plus point.

name: The Oriental Park KLCC
street: Lot G48 - 139, Ground Floor, Park Side , KLCC
reviews:
Decent $$$ fusion food and drinks, with nice dinner ambience, next to KLCC fountain

A good spot to chill and relax with decent food and service by the KLCC park and front row view of the dancing fountain. Good wise is decent but pricey. A large % is for the location and vibe.

A tad loud for decent conversation. But this spot is designed for drinks with friends. The big range of drinks, alcoholic and otherwise.

Food wise, I liked the Bask cheese cake the best. Won't comment on the others as they are ok, and not outstanding for the price point. The lamb was delish, not gamey yet with a well grilled bark and succulent inside. The steak was disappointing though. Quite a few order were poorly executed. The medium rare turned out to be well done. The marrow was somewhat plastic-ky.

Ambience is nice though, to just chillax with a cocktail or 🥃 or two.

Great service from Shafiq. Attentive and with service with a smile.

Finally had the chance to have dinner here and it was up to my expectations! Already tried their tiramisu the day before and that was really good so i came back for dinner tonight! for dessert i had the cheesecake it was one of the best truly! The food was amazing, the pulled lamb bao was so delicious and sweet. My favourite part of this restaurant is probably the varieties in the menu, i love how the grilled salmon has like ulam kerabu salads, interesting. Also not to forget the amazing ambiance and atmosphere, that was what had me intrigued n attracted to try this place out! So calming and relaxing, love coming here alone. Lastly, shoutout to Nazim for assisting me with my orders and was able to clearly explained to me about the menus n recommended me some good stuff! <3

Was surprised at how wonderful this place is. We were looking for a place to eat , drink, and watch the fountain show: we landed here.
Greeted by a friendly hostess (Yat) who went out of their way to help us find a perfect table for the show. Then, we had fantastic service from Fairudz and Erica. Could not tell that Erica was new at their job either. Truly outstanding service where it was a cherry on top that we had delicious food . Specifically loved the soba goreng which tasted like something you’d get in Penang Mamak mee stalls! The seri muka was great but def could use more Malibu and pandan syrup.

name: ren
street: Lot 252, Second Floor, Petronas Twin Tower
reviews:
The restaurant is quite comfortable, though you might have to wait a bit to be seated during dinner time since it gets pretty busy. The menu is varied, and honestly, the flavors feel authentic, rich, and really satisfying. Prices are affordable and definitely match the quality of both the food and the service.

The only downside was the greeter at the entrance, who came across as a bit unfriendly and slightly condescending. Aside from that, the overall dining experience was enjoyable and worth it.

Special shoutout to our waitress, Suzanna from Sabah, who was incredibly attentive, quick, and genuinely warm throughout the whole experience. She really made us feel welcome and taken care of, such a gem!

REN has quickly become our favorite Chinese restaurant in KLCC, we honestly wish we had discovered it sooner! Their Peking Duck (especially with the current promo) is absolutely worth it, perfectly crispy on the outside, juicy on the inside, and paired beautifully with their flavorful sauces.

We also loved the Sweet & Sour Chicken and the Fried Noodles with Truffle & Duck. Every dish was thoughtfully prepared and full of flavor. The service was excellent too, the staff were genuinely friendly, attentive, and accommodating.

The ambiance is elegant yet welcoming, making it ideal for both family gatherings and casual meals with little ones.

If you’re craving authentic Chinese food and Peking Duck done right, REN is definitely a must-try!

Good food, especially the dry la mian beef brisket and dumplings.  Although uses only chicken meat but it was delicious.

Great job from Service team.

name: AOOO Melbourne Cafe
reviews:
Only Review you will need to read. I’m from Germany and travelling KL, I looked for a cozy cafe with good food and found this gem.

First of all the staff is super friendly and kind. The cafe is located in a good area with plenty of other things around to do. It’s also great for working as it is not too loud but still has chill music in the background.

The menus is good a lot of choices and people who say it’s “overpriced” are imo a bit strange, it’s normal prices and plenty of choices. Would definitely come back again.

An unassuming cafe on a side lane, they serve decent coffee and cakes. The Flat White I ordered came with latte art, which was superfluous for a true Melbourne style coffee place. The Long Black was hot and aromatic.

The Salated Caramel Cheese Cake was good. I was told it’s made by a French pastry chef. A bit expensive but good quality and taste. This is Recommended.

I like the cool vibe of the place. Reminiscent of some Melbourne cafes too.

PAPA SAYS: 👍🏻 homely, cosy cafe serving great music and healthy food

Chanced upon this little cafe that used to be a records shop - the owners refurbished it into a nice homely cafe. You can tell this is a family-run business with the friendly service and food options, ranging from yummy western breakfasts, to asian bowls if you'd like a hearty meal.

We ordered the chicken bagel, aooo egg breakie, and roasted veggies which were good. Sit around with a cuppa and a book, and you'll feel right at ease here.

name: Restoran Daawat
reviews:
This restaurant was an unexpected but incredible find while walking through the busy food street. The signboard caught my attention, and stepping inside felt like discovering a hidden Kerala corner right in the middle of Kuala Lumpur. The food is genuinely authentic — no shortcuts, no fusion attempts, just proper Kerala flavours. I tried the kizhi porotta and porichu varattiya kozhi, and both dishes were outstanding. The porotta was soft with the right amount of stretch, and the chicken had that deep, roasted spice profile you’d expect back home.

What makes the place even better is the atmosphere. Despite being in a busy area, the restaurant feels calm, warm, and welcoming. The staff were attentive, friendly, and clearly proud of what they serve. It’s rare to find a spot abroad that nails Kerala taste this well. If you’re craving real Kerala food, Dawaat is absolutely worth stopping for.

Attaching the latest menu for reference

A big compliment to Restaurant Daawat and the entire team — especially Nurul, Ashiq, Richu, Mugeen, and Ajmal. The staff are incredibly friendly and always welcome everyone with a genuine smile, which makes the experience truly special.
The food is absolutely authentic — you can really feel the spices in every bite. I especially love the Lemon Soda with Pudina, Bru Coffee, and the Black Pepper Fried Rice — it’s on a whole different level and my absolute favourite!
I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for great food and warm hospitality. Nurul, thank you for always welcoming my guests so kindly, and to all the staff — thank you for the wonderful hospitality and care you show at your restaurant. 🌟🍽️

I recently visited Restoran Daawat in Bukit Bintang for lunch, and it was a wonderful experience. The restaurant truly lives up to its name, offering some of the best Kerala-Malabari, South Indian, and North Indian dishes all under one roof.

The food was flavorful, authentic, and freshly prepared. I especially enjoyed the rich spices and the homely taste that reminded me of traditional cooking. The menu has plenty of options, so there’s something for everyone.

Service was warm and attentive, and the atmosphere was clean and welcoming—perfect for both quick meals and family dining. Definitely a must-try if you’re in Bukit Bintang and craving authentic Indian food!

name: Emily Darling Cafe
reviews: Emily Darling is famous of thier croissant, they make the best so far that I had tasted. The environment is always quite confortable and nice to enjoy coffee and cake. The owner love plant, you could see lots of plant in front of the shop as well as inside the shop. With his green fingers tge plant look refreshing and you could enjoy the green and relax in this environment. We love it. The light snack are great as well, must try when you happen in Penang Road.

Nice café serving drinks and cakes/pastries. Looks a bit of a jungle from the outside with all the plants.  Inside is pretty much painted all black, with quirky brightly coloured decor.  Food and drinks were nice, but a little bit overpriced compared to similar cafés we visited.  Although it was quiet and relaxed atmosphere, only 4 people were there including us - nice!

We visited this café over the Christmas period and absolutely loved it. The selection of homemade pastries is incredible — croissants, pain au chocolat, and a standout chocolate-orange pain au chocolat with a beautiful orange filling that was genuinely memorable.

The coffee was delicious and perfectly made, and the atmosphere inside was so warm and Christmassy. The decoration felt thoughtful and welcoming, and really brought to mind a traditional French pâtisserie.

Everything we tried was excellent, and it was a lovely place to stop and enjoy the festive season. Highly recommended if you love great coffee and exceptional pastries.

name: Masjid Jamek Lookout Point @ River of Life
street: River of Life, Leboh Pasar Besar
reviews:
Stopped by here during my morning run, and it’s such a peaceful spot to start the day. The river views are beautiful, especially in the early morning when it’s quiet and the city is just waking up.

It’s clean, scenic, and perfect for a quick pause, photos, or just to catch your breath before continuing your run.

A peaceful and scenic spot in the heart of the city, with great views of the River of Life and the beautiful Masjid Jamek mosque. The area is full of character – from colourful street art on the nearby buildings to the gentle mist flowing over the riverbanks. It’s a lovely contrast of heritage and modern KL life.

Masjid Jamek itself is one of the oldest mosques in Kuala Lumpur, officially opened in 1909. Built at the confluence of the Klang and Gombak rivers (where the city was founded), it was designed in a Mughal style by British architect A.B. Hubback. This spot truly feels like the birthplace of the city.

Definitely worth a stop, especially for a quiet stroll, photos, or to appreciate how KL’s history blends with today’s urban energy.

🌟 Masjid Jamek Lookout — A quick photo stop 🌟

📍 Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
⭐ 6/10

I visited Masjid Jamek Lookout in the morning, but honestly, the view wasn’t as beautiful as I expected. The sunlight was quite harsh, and the river didn’t look very clear.

✨ What I liked:
•	Open view, easy spot for quick photos with the mosque and bridge in the background.
•	Breezy and a nice place for a short walk.
•	Close to other tourist attractions, so it’s convenient to stop by.

⚠️ What could be better:
•	Morning light is too strong for good photos.
•	Not much to do except take pictures — gets boring quickly.

📌 Tip: Visit during late afternoon or sunset for better lighting and a nicer atmosphere when the lights come on.

#MasjidJamek #KualaLumpur #MalaysiaTrip #LookoutPoint #TravelReview #PhotoSpotKL #VisitMalaysia

name: P. Ramlee Memorial House
reviews:
P. Ramlee memorial house located at Jalan Dedap in Kuala Lumpur brings back nostagia. Displaying few original property of the famous director- actor-  singer and composer, this small house kept valueable memories. Entry is free.
Tan Sri P. Ramlee won oscars and timeline of his career tell stories. Together with wife, Puan Sri Saloma, both contributed much of malay theatre success and fame. P. Ramlee personal Datsun BAD 3608 is parked and displayed near the entrance. His Director chair and some filming equipments are there as well. Few of Puan Sri Saloma's outfit are there for viewing. Overall this memorial brings joy to their fans and filming industry.
Excellent! Worth visiting! What a great artist that we couldn't replace him till now!!! I love P Ramlee.

Well organised memorial house. Highly recommended. There are some merchandise available. Also, an Indian stall to have light meal before and after your visit. Do support them. All staffs are friendly.

name: Golden Triangle KL
reviews: Best place to take a good picture of Twin Towers. Watch out for the traffic and crowds 😉🫡

You’ll find all luxury brands in the mall. It gives a vibe of Dubai mall but doesn’t beat it. Could be more organized. I found limitation in the food court. Everything closes at 10 PM and no one accommodates you after that so make sure that you are well planned to call off your day by 10 PM.

The most beautiful part of KL. Must visit all these places including Pintonas Saloma LED bridge. Go to the view point of Petronas and have some beautiful clicks. Also visit Suria, KLCC park, KLCC Aqueria and Menara (KL Tower). Lovely places to visit in KL. Dont forget to visit Jlan Alor, Bukit Bintang road side shops and Changkat. Enjoy the ride!

name: Kesum Art Restaurant
reviews:
Now… I am not sure why this restaurant doesn’t get a higher rating than 4.6 bcos I must say it is one of the best eats for me in Penang.

I was sceptical when I saw the bunting that claim their satay is probably the best in town. Well, there is some truth to it. The satay is huge and well charred. The peanut sauce could be better but still good.

Now, I an Asam Pedas raving-die-hard fan and I was drawn to their Asam Pedas Ekor. Unfortunately, it was available. So I tried the fish. While it is not the best I have had, it is above average especially if you like the Asam more than the Pedas.

This restaurant doesn’t dish out excellent portions. Due to that, their V4M (Value for Money) rating is quite high especially their set meals. Go for the set meals guys.

Service is great and feels personal. Ambience also is relaxing and pleasant.

Parking might be a little hard then again this is Georgetown, right? I would use Grab since the restaurant is not located at an alley but at a busy main road with no road shoulder in front. If you are driving, park and walk to the restaurant.

We went there with my parents, and my mother got food poisoning shortly after eating a shrimp dish.

It’s unfortunate because the food was tasty, the prices were reasonable, and the service was friendly. However, the freshness and overall hygiene of the food are a serious concern.
Everything is great! Food is super delicious. Even the kids meal was great! Instead of typical fast food they serve proper kids meal.

name: Four Hands
reviews: The price of the good here may be high, but that’s just an indicator of the quality of the food you get. All of the dishes were amazing such as the fried turnip cake and the bbq pork bun. My favourite however was the chee cheong fun with the fried shrimp as it was both smooth and crispy. The service here was also really good as the staff were friendly and hospitable. Overall, a great experience.

Fantastic dim sum. One of the best outside Hong Kong. Went there at about 4pm and the restaurant was empty.

The chye tow kway comes in big cubes - stir-fried with bean generous portion of bean sprouts, garlic, chye poh and egg. The dish features delightful of textures - soft, moist and springy interior and crispy, slightly charred edges on the outside. It comes with rich, sweet-savoury flavour. A must try!

Yam ball or 'woo kok' served hot. The crispy exterior texture, deep fried till beautiful golden brown, shatters upon biting. The smooth, tender-smashed yam provides an earthy and subtle flavour that compliments well with the char siew filling. The only minus point is the char siew is too little.

Egg tart is good. Creamy, silky custard with buttery, flaky crust.

Shrimp is plump and crunchy in siew mai. The subtle natural sweetness that comes from the fresh shrimp is rich and satisfying. A basket comes in 4. Goes well with sambal chilli.

The MUST-ORDER dish is the chee cheong fun with shrimp. The silky delicate skin flows smoothly in the throat. The shrimp were deep fried with flour before rolling into the skin. The two compliment so well with the sweet-savoury soy sauce. It is truly heaven! You will regret it if you didn't order this dish.

Service is good. Food served hot. Place is clean.

The dim sum here is really delicious and beautifully presented — both the taste and the look are on point 💯
Their salted egg lava tart is a must-try! Crispy on the outside, with creamy custard that oozes out in every bite.
The glasshouse setting adds such a cozy and aesthetic vibe — definitely worth a visit!

name: Yew Yew Coffee @Chinatown KL
street: 1st Floor, FB1, Bangunan Ka Yin, 63-D, Jalan Sultan
reviews:
Ordered latte, matcha Latte, and the Biscoff and original croffles.

The coffee was good, dark chocolatey so suits most people's taste. We ordered the matcha less sweet but still was quite sweet, also was one of the grassier matchas I've tasted (not my preference).

croffles were quite yummy though!! though a bit expensive and not anything novel.

the seating area is small and cozy, and staff were really sweet!

I came here with a friend for coffee after our lunch. It’s a hidden gem.

We ordered ice long black with single origin bean. It’s light roast, hence has a fruity profile. This is how i like my ice long black.

The place is small, but cozy. No big table. Just a long table facing outside window. The window is tinted, so we didn’t feel the glare from afternoon sun. We enjoy our chit chat while looking at passing moments outside.

Will i come back?
Yes
Probably yes
Maybe ✅ (if i’m at petaling street)
Probably no
No

Hesitant to try caramel latte as someone who ain’t a fan of something gourmand sweet, but this is something to risk for. Skip long lines at other cafes and drop by here. As a tourist and a coffee lover, this so far is on my top 3.

Ps, the downside is, the place is a kiosk so there’s limited sitting only. But if you’re on the go, then no prob at all ☺️

name: Junk Cafe @ Chinatown KL
reviews:
Cool bar/ eatery in Chinatown.
We went for lunch and had nasi lamak and a dry curry dish.
The curry was a stand out. Super flavourful and perfectly spicy.
My partner loved the nasi lamak.
I had a chilli/ mango cocktail and it left a spicy kick,also wasn't too sweet.
The decor is really cool. That is what bright us in.
Prices are reasonable for a touristy spot.

A hidden gem in Chinatown!
Super convenient location near Pasar Seni MRT.
Love the vintage-meets-Asian decor — feels quirky, nostalgic, and full of character.
Live band after 8:30pm is the real highlight; great vibe with a mix of locals and tourists.
Food ranges from brunch to late-night bites, and the menu is surprisingly varied.
Perfect spot to unwind, chat, and enjoy the atmosphere.
Highly recommended!

Had a really great time at Junk Cafe! The food was delicious – the prawns were super fresh and the salmon had an amazing texture, really satisfying to eat. Around 8:30pm there was a live band, and the vocalist was so thoughtful, going around to chat with each table. At 10pm they even had a fun coin challenge that added to the vibe. The place is filled with antiques, and I love how even the cocktails are served in vintage glasses. Such a unique and memorable spot!

name: Fritz
street: Level 23A Tower B, The Troika, 19, Persiaran KLCC
reviews:
We dined as a group of four and spent just over 200MYR per person, and it was totally worth it. The food was fantastic - the Brie salad and patatas bravas were delicious starters. The steak frites, best ordered medium well, was juicy and flavorful, while the steak tartare was tasty and came in a satisfying portion with fries on the side. The Fritz burger was juicy and full of flavor.

Cocktails were a highlight - the Negroni was smooth and unique with coffee beans soaked in the vermouth, and the Hemingway daiquiri was crisp and refreshing. For dessert, the cognac-flambéed crème brûlée and rich chocolate ganache were perfect endings.

The ambiance was lovely with a comfy temperature and French and English jazz playing softly in the background, creating a relaxed vibe. Jack, our waiter, was extremely attentive and friendly - you’re in great hands if he’s serving you. Highly recommend this spot for a chilled, delicious dining experience!

Celebrated my girlfriend’s birthday here. Wonderful KL view with Merdeka 118 an KL Tower although is cloudy. We ordered Fritz Steak and Smoked Salmon and crème brûlée for dessert . The taste was surprisingly good and the portions were not small also. Mr Pipi served us throughout the dinner and he can take fantastic photos. Will definitely recommend to others who like to have decent French cuisine in KL!

I chose this restaurant to celebrate my boyfriend Birthday, and it exceeded my expectations.
The staff name  was serving us was welcoming and even sang a happy birthday's song to my boyfriend, which was a lovely touch. Every dish was flavorful and well-prepared, and the ambiance created a warm and relaxing atmosphere. It was a memorable evening, and I highly recommend this place for special celebrations. PS special thanks to PiPi for the wonderful and warm service!

name: Wholey Wonder Damai
reviews:
The ramen was unfortunately too spicy for my taste. I was expecting a more balanced, umami-rich broth, but the overpowering spices and oil masked the other flavors. I would say it tastes like laksa rather than ramen🥲 I hope the restaurant can warn people about the spice level when ordering...

Meanwhile the food was a let down, we really enjoyed the atmosphere and service was really accommodating 🙏

Beautiful environment for outdoor seating. It's not hot if seated at the long table as there's sufficient fans. Garden area might be hot if the weather is super sunny.

Food is not advertised as vegetarian and they dont look like one until you read the description carefully. Nevertheless, they are pretty good and very healthy, ramen is very flavourful but noodles on the soft side. Kimbap flavour is very clean, slightly sour and coconuty. Nothing too burden to eat. Price is reasonable for a cafe pricing

We had a great time dining with our pets

everyone working there was SO kind and the space is beautiful. i love the garden and the fact that you can sit outside is great. also everything is plant based and that’s so nice since i’m vegan.

we ordered the mala ramen and the signature caesar salad. the ramen was good but had a lot of vegan meat in it, however if you like that, definitely give it a try!

i got the salad though. i usually really like salads and always try and get a vegan caesar if it’s available since it’s my favorite kind. also i asked for no cherry tomatoes so if they’re what makes this salad great, i apologize for a skewed review.

the greens, which were spinach, lettuce and kale, were really fresh and pretty. the kale was not seasoned or massaged though which made trying to eat it really difficult and unpleasant. the toppings were avocado and pecans since i didn’t get cherry tomatoes. the avocado was great but the pecans were also completely unseasoned. the dressing was slimy, a little foamy, and very bland. i could only taste something that reminded me of vinegar. overall it was a really bland and sour salad but all the vegetables were really fresh and the presentation was so pretty! i think there are some great options on the menu, i just wouldn’t recommend the salad and if you’re someone who isn’t a fan of fake meats, choose carefully.

name: 鉄板上ちゃん
reviews: Great restaurant to dine at if you're hungry after a visit to Nabana  no Sato. Waitresses were friendly but did not speak much English; there was no English menu either but google translate always does the trick. Went with their top seller the Bolognese Okonomiyaki and also the pepper fried rice and the seared tuna which was recommended. Bolognese Okonomiyaki was a delight  and a departure from the classic Okonomiyaki flavours. The pepper fried rice was very tasty too! The star for me was the seared tuna, which you can taste that smokiness/charredness while the tuna itself melts in your mouth. Overall great skill by the chef but note that it's a relatively small restaurant with perhaps a longer waiting time as there is only one chef.
Lovely little restaurant , good food great service.  If you are visiting World outlet and the light forest, worth to drop by.
Yummy.. fusion dish.. very special

name: Malaya Cafe on Rodger Street
street: LOT G, Pacific Express Hotel Central Market, Central Market, 23, Jalan Hang Kasturi
reviews:
Nice and ventilated place. I took the nasi lemak with fired chicken. You could taste the coconut from the rice, plus the chicken was week fried. The chilly sauce on the side was also flavorful.
I paid 7.4 euros for the nasi lemak + the spring rolls, so it is not cheap compared to other places but the taste is good and is close to the central market.

I recently dined at Little Malaya Cafe and had a wonderful experience! It was my first time trying the butter fish, and it was absolutely delicious. My brother ordered the dry chili chicken rice, which was equally impressive. Both dishes were packed with flavor and prepared to perfection.

What made the experience even more special was the outstanding service. The staff were attentive and friendly, and the chef even came out to check if the food met our expectations—a thoughtful touch that shows their dedication to customer satisfaction.

If you’re in the area, I highly recommend stopping by Little Malaya Cafe. The food, service, and atmosphere make it a must-visit spot!

Got the Lunch Set, Butter Milk Heritage +1 drink (from 11am-3pm) for RM19. Super good buttermilk chicken, maybe even one of the best for me. Chicken was still crunchy even when it’s “ber-kuah”. 10/10 would come here again if I’m nearby Central Market.

name: Kobe Steak Restaurant Mouriya Lin
street: Kitanagasadori, 1 Chome−9−8 クイーンズコーストビル 2F
reviews:
Loved the kobe beef here, with wonderful service and ease of booking. We booked before arriving in Japan through their website, and was replied to promptly in English through our email. No downpayment required. We had the Kobe beef ribeye and rump steaks for 2 of us, and wow did the rump steak made an impression on us. For the pricing, we got a perfectly fatty and chewy piece of beef that was perfect in both flavor and softness. The ribeye in comparison was twice as expensive, but was only fattier in comparison, not worth the extra price. All the sets come with appetisers and grilled vegetables, though we recommend upgrading the rice to garlic rice. The garlic rice was intensely fragrant, cooked with the beef fats and panfried garlic. The salad and dessert was alright, but nothing mindblowing compared to the rump we had. The soup came with beef bits that was great, but honestly, the rest came up on top. Servers spoke great english and prob chinese and were very accomodating and kind so do pay this a visit if you are up for some quality beef.

You have to enter the restaurant through a lift on the ground floor once you find the building. The restaurant name is on the building but come in slightly earlier tonfind the restaurant as it might be slightly difficult.

Absolutely amazing experience at Mouriya Lin, and one I hope to repeat at some stage.
We had a little trouble finding the restaurant at the beginning as it's on the second floor and you have to look for the little signs on the wall as you come down the street. Once inside, the decor was really elegant, as were the uniforms of the staff. We were shown to our seats in front of the teppan and the chef came out soon and introduced himself and the meat we had selected (we pre-booked online)
The service started with a delicious consommé soup with small pieces of beef in it. Then there was a salad with a sensational sesame dressing, followed by the main event and the beef, along with its various grilled vegetable accompaniments. I can genuinely say the beef was like nothing I've ever had, the marbled fat giving it a unique flavour and texture. We went with the chefs recommendation of medium rare and enjoyed it immensely. Not an every day experience, but definitely one to come back to.

I had an excellent dining experience in this branch. I went for the 200g A5 Kobe Rib eye and prawns. The way the food is prepared resulted to delightful flavors for every part. I would not hesitate another booking in the future. I would specifically mention my chef who thoughtfully guided me on this dining pleasure.

name: Art House Gallery Museum of Ethnic Arts
street: Lot 3.04 & 3.05, Level 2, Annexe Building, Central Market, 10,, Jalan Hang Kasturi
reviews:
An absolute hidden gem! The Art House Gallery Museum of Ethnic Arts is a remarkable treasure trove of cultural heritage, showcasing a superb and thoughtfully curated array of ethnic art and artifacts from around the world. Each piece is displayed with care, offering visitors a truly immersive and enriching experience.

The owners are exceptionally warm, welcoming, and knowledgeable—genuinely passionate about the stories behind the objects and eager to share insights with visitors. Their hospitality added a personal and memorable touch to our visit.

There are also some wonderful and unique items available for purchase, ideal for collectors or anyone looking for a meaningful keepsake. Though slightly tucked away, this spot is absolutely worth seeking out—an unmissable experience for anyone in the area with an interest in art, culture, or history. Highly recommended!

It's an amazing place for those who loves culture and archeology !

The owner knows a lot about every pieces in  its gallery ! He is very nice and if you have any questions , do not hesitate ! He will help you .

I am lool forward to come again and buy some new stuff !

Absolutely amazing collection of artifacts and original historical objects from all over South-East Asia and around, with specific emphasis on Borneo. Very helpful and welcoming hist and a paradise shopping fir any antiquities lover!

name: Ten
reviews: Standard charcoal grilled unagi-fish hitsumabushi-don with deep flavor. The 3rd step adding dashi-seasoning is strongly recommended. Good for visitors for Atsuda Shingu shrine. No need to lineup at noon 1pm. (note: no foreign language guide of hitsumabushi steps, so learn it in advance)
First time have a eel, it was amazingly good
Their Unadon is very delicious including rice. The dessert is also very good as not too sweet. I will definitely come back again when I visit Atsuta Jingu :)

name: Din Sun Kopitiam 鼎盛茶室@茨厂街
reviews:
Overall, this was a very good Kopitiam experience. We ordered the classic Kaya toast, soft boiled eggs and kopi. The Kaya toast was good, great amount of Kaya jam and chunks of butter. The eggs were nice and runny, perfect for dipping the toast in. The coffee was good as well.

The service was quick, staff are kind and the place is nice and fun design. We were the only tourists eating here.
Went here with my family first day arriving in KL. The vibes are great. I would recommend the bubur ayam, it is amazing😁 The nasi lemak is very well balanced and the sambal is not too spicy. 👍

We ordered the dragon fruit dim sum, sui mai, radish stirufry and cold milk tea. The food was packed with flavour, and made fresh! Our waitress Kaizama was soo lovely and took the time to explain to us the dishes. The restaurant has plenty of seating and the inside has that traditional touch! Highly recommend this place!!

name: Journey Ellephants
reviews: We ended up at this restaurant because we couldn't get a reservation at Horaiken. However, we quickly realized that this restaurant is phenomenal, and our choice was unexpectedly correct. Needless to say, their grilled eel (Hitsumabushi) was fantastic. Additionally, they had a wonderful selection of sake. I definitely have to come back for dinner.

Lovely staff, super tasty unagi, grilled to perfection. I have eaten a lot of unagi, including several upscale places, but this was the first time that the provided pepper mix was served in a grinder- making it suuuper fresh and tasty. The complementary pickles were also extraordinarily flavorful, I've probably never had such a good takuan radish. The owner apparently likes traveling and shows his passion in the restaurant's design. Overall a great experience and if I have the chance I'll come back.

If you come before the opening, you need to fill in your details to reserve a slot.

Seating areas are exclusively limited.

While waiting there’s a park opposite the store.

I had the Grilled ell rice bowl Jyou ¥3520.

If you’re seated at the counter you would be able to see the chef grilling.

The food taste fantastic. Great job.

Will come visit next time.

name: Esplanade Walkway
reviews: Esplanade Walkway in George Town is a peaceful and scenic place to relax and enjoy the sea view. The walkway is clean, well-maintained, and perfect for walking, jogging, or simply sitting and enjoying the breeze. It’s a great spot for sunset views, photos, and spending quality time with family. The nearby heritage buildings and open space make the experience even better. Highly recommended for visitors and locals alike.

A perfect spot to clear your mind.

Absolutely stunning views of the sea today. It’s such a peaceful place to relax, watch the cargo ships, and enjoy the sea breeze. The water was calm and the sky was an incredible shade of blue. Even the local wildlife crow seems to enjoy the view. Highly recommend coming here for a walk or just to disconnect for a bit

A nice place to have a relaxing stroll in the evening. Lots of local picnicking or just simply enjoying a free time and the sea breeze. A few buskers usually use the occasion to perform.

There's a couple of food courts in the area, including the newly renovated one next to the Cornwallis Fort's moat that sells very popular mee sotong.

name: Laman Perdana
reviews: Laman Perdana in Kuala Lumpur is a true oasis of peace in the heart of the city. It delights with beautifully maintained greenery, picturesque paths, and modern architecture that blends seamlessly with nature. It's the perfect place for a walk, relaxation, or a picnic with the family. In the evenings, the park takes on a unique charm thanks to its subtle lighting and pleasant atmosphere. Cleanliness, safety, and excellent location make you want to return. Definitely one of the most beautiful places in Kuala Lumpur! 🌿✨

Laman Perdana in Kuala Lumpur is a charming spot within the Perdana Botanical Garden. Entry was free, and the available restrooms were clean and well-maintained. Everything felt very peaceful, the perfect place for a relaxing walk or to unwind surrounded by nature right in the heart of the city.

Nice place to spend some time enjoying the many attractions for free. Must see while you are here is the Sunken Garden, an instagrammers delight. There is plenty of seating around it in the shade, while you wait for the many people photographing to disperse. It has a lot of delightful colour.

name: Tanah Aina George Town Cafe
reviews:
Tanah Aina is an oasis in downtown George Town offering nice Malay cuisine, done with a modern touch, yet still faithful to traditions. The cafe's tastefully appointed setting lends a relaxed ambience, adding to the pleasure of eating here. The service is nice and friendly too.

For lunch, we had the delicious Gado-Gado, Cucur Udang, Lontong, Nasi Briyani Lamb, Nasi Briyani Chicken and Mee Rebus Kambing.

To finish off the satisfying meal, we had lovely Cucur Pisang (also known as Cekodok or Kueh Kodok) and the not-to-be-missed Roti Banyak Kaya (toasted homemade bread with sumptuous kaya). We did, however, miss the not-to-be-missed Pengat Durian with durian from Tanah Aina's own estate.

It's not surprising it's hard to resist making return visits.

Honestly, I never knew this café existed in Georgetown. The funny thing is, it’s tucked right in between very familiar buildings and landmarks, yet somehow remains impressively hidden. A true stealth café. I stumbled upon it purely by chance while scrolling through Google Maps in search of something to eat.

As expected, Tanah Aina lives up to its brand reputation. The moment we stepped inside, expectations were met without trying too hard. This particular outlet is on the narrow side, but clever interior styling makes you forget about the space constraint almost instantly. The café is immaculately clean, calm, and comfortable, best of all, not a trace of kitchen aroma invading the serene ambience (which is always a big win).

We were warmly greeted by the lady manager, who dressed very elegantly and carried herself with genuine politeness, first impressions done right!!

Food-wise, I went for the classic fish and chips, perfectly crisp and satisfying. My son ordered the Tanah Aina fried rice, which was flavourful and well-balanced, while my husband chose the lontong, a comforting, authentic dish done justice. For drinks, since I was already rather full from café-hopping earlier, I kept it simple with iced water. My son enjoyed a refreshing watermelon juice, and my husband opted for an ice-cold Coke to “cleanse his tummy” (his words, not mine 😄).

Everything tasted decent and authentic, with thoughtful seasoning and respectable portions. The plating and presentation were top-notch, clean, elegant, and very Instagram-friendly.

This is the kind of café I truly appreciate. A place where you can dine in peace, unhurried, calm, and comfortably forgotten by the outside world. I sincerely hope Tanah Aina continues to maintain this standard and sustains the quality their customers have come to expect.

A hidden gem worth discovering and revisiting.

⭐ Rating: 9/10
We ordered the Briyani Lamb and Fish & Chips. The rice was very flavorful, and the lamb was so tender. For the Fish & Chips, I really liked the coating as it was a bit spicy, just the way I like it! The atmosphere was cozy, classy, and chill, and the waiter was really kind. I loved their service. The price is a little bit pricey, but I guess you’re also paying for the nice ambience. Overall, 8.5/10 — definitely recommend to others!

name: The Forest - Mansion
reviews: We stumbled upon this place on a Sunday night and we were lucky to get the last seats available. Fully-booked. Ordered the beauty and the beast Christmas set and add-on RM20 for two glasses of red wine. The food was fusion and they were great. We enjoyed everything that was served and ambience is good. Highly recommended.

1st time here with colleagues.
Their lunch set really worth it.
Taste not bad and big portion.
And their service super good.
But one things which is susah find parking better car pool or grab come here.
Their environment here so chill. Its great place gather with frens.
Also they have beer! And can party here.

First of all, the service is impeccable. From the moment we arrived until the end, they served us with a smile. They patiently explained the menu and what they offer. We ordered the set lunch, which included a drink, main course, and soup. You can add an additional RM6 to upgrade your drink to coffee and an extra RM2 for ice cream (which you can get for free with a Google review). The portion of the set lunch is substantial and delicious. The location is good, but parking can be quite challenging

name: SoraCafe 有馬温泉
reviews: this is an associated cafe with the onsen hotel that i stayed at. so we got a complimentary breakfast set here. it's a lovely bright cafe that offers many lovely pastries, both sweet and savoury. there are cookies and cake box set to buy too. for the breakfast set, egg, bacon and yoghurt are fixed, then we pick our own pastry from the counter. all looked so good. it's also served with juice. we picked a seat that's right next to the window, it's such a lovely moment to enjoy the breakfast under the sunlight through the window. a good start of the day!

very lovely cafe, food is very delicious. Chicken Curry is very creamy and probably the best I have ever had. The staffs are all very lovely. The coffee and cake is great. The atmosphere is very good and the design concept of interior, utensils, table etc is super cool, reflecting the concept of Sora (sky)
the place is so clean and pretty! The manager is so much kind to treat me and the important thing is the coffee and tart is sooooo good!!! If i have another chance, I want to try to eat Monblanc! 😋😋

name: Petaling Street Street Art
reviews:
I wanted the ultimate "Instagram vs. Reality" shot, in this hidden alleyway in Chinatown/Petaling Street.

Standing here feels like being in two time periods at once. At eye level, i have the charming, rustic yellow shophouses and vibrant red lanterns that scream traditional KL culture. But look up, and you’re hit with the breathtaking scale of Merdeka 118, the world’s second-tallest building.

Where Heritage Meets the Skyline 🎨✨
Wandering through the heart of Kuala Lumpur, I stumbled upon this explosion of color that tells the story of a city caught between two beautiful worlds.

Every stroke on these walls whispers tales of tradition—ceremonial umbrelas, vibrant batik patterns, and faces that carry generations of Malaysian heritage. Then, rising boldly through it all, a gleaming blue tower pierces the sky, reminding you that this is a city that refuses to choose between its past and its future.

This is what I love about KL. It doesn't hide its contradictions; it celebrates them. Ancient temples stand next to glass skyscrapers. Street hawkers serve century-old recipes in the shadow of luxury malls. And here, on an ordinary downtown street, art declares: "We are both, and we are proud."

Travel tip: Don't just rush to the iconic landmarks. Sometimes the real soul of a city is painted on its walls, waiting for curious wanderers to stop and listen to what it has to say.

Where: Downtown Kuala Lumpur
Vibe: Cultural collision in the best way possible
Must-do: Slow down, look up, and let the streets tell you their stories
What's the most unexpected art you've discovered while traveling? 💭
We visited this street to have a look at the wall murals. The street is not very long but has many wall paintings. Worth a quick look when in the area.

name: Presgrave Street Corner Heng Kee Char Koay Teow 三条路炒粿条
reviews:
So good I had to order a second round immediately. I ended up finishing two large plates back-to-back—no regrets!

​If you’re looking for a plate that hits every single mark of a legendary Penang Char Koay Teow, this is the spot. They don’t hold back on anything:

​Wok Hei: 10/10. That perfect smoky char in every strand of noodle. ✅

​The Goods: Plenty of Chinese sausage, fresh cockles, and those essential crunchy lard bits. ✅

​Double Egg: You can get both Duck egg (for richness) and Chicken egg. ✅

​Freshness: Perfectly timed chives and sprouts. ✅

Service with a smile ✅

​Everything is there. Don't waste your time with a small, just go straight for the special, large size (or two!). Easily one of the best 👍👌
Delicious char kway teow. We shared one big portion. The wokhei was really good. Comes with lap cheong, prawn and hor fun. You have to buy a drink to sit there.

We came to Penang for char koey tiew. We have tried many different shops including Michelin start restaurants. But nothing as good as this young chef. She should be Michelin ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️  clams are fresh and the taste is amazing without MSG.

name: TUAH 1895 • Bukit Bintang City Centre
reviews:
A Moment of Urban Stillness
There's something deeply meditative about watching a city breathe from above. Perched at Tuah 1895 viewing deck, Kuala Lumpur unfolds before you in layers—the sleek Coway monorail gliding silently across its elevated tracks, the striking geometry of modern towers piercing soft evening clouds, reflections dancing across glass facades that hold entire cityscapes within them.

The white-domed architecture frames it all perfectly, a contrast of heritage and progress, grounding you in a space between past and present. Below, the rhythm of the MRT becomes a kind of urban poetry—each passing train a reminder that cities are alive, constantly moving, yet somehow timeless when you pause to truly see them.

This is the kind of healing KL offers those who know where to look: not in the rush, but in the stillness above it. An open view, a gentle breeze, and the quiet satisfaction of watching a city that never stops... while you, just for a moment, do.

Sometimes the best souvenirs aren't things—they're these pockets of peace we tuck away in memory.

This was my first time visiting and capturing this view with my Redmi note 13 pro 5g and it was truly a beautiful experience, especially at night.
For those coming for the first time, here’s a simple guide:
Park at the underground car park (RM5 per entry)
Take the lift up to Level 1
Open the door to step out to the viewing deck
The view of PNB Merdeka 118 from here is amazing and peaceful.
The deck wasn’t crowded, so you’ll get ample space and better angles if you come on a Sunday night from 7:55 PM to 11:55 PM.
Highly recommended for anyone who wants to enjoy the city view or capture night photography.
Ada bar Dan restaurant at ground floor . Ok for a picture .

name: Kuromon Onabeya
reviews: Kuromon Onabeya was a fantastic lunch stop. The sushi bowl was fresh and perfectly balanced, and the udon tempura soup was pure comfort with a rich broth and light, crispy tempura. A fun twist we loved: there’s a small ledge over the bar where you can prop your phone and record your meal—perfect for capturing the moment. Great food, friendly vibes, and a little extra charm made it a standout in Osaka. 🍣🍜📱
Our favorite oden shop! The oden soup's very comforting and good, perfect for the cold weather. We usually order their oden whenever we visit Kuromon 😋
nice food, fast service. my daughter enjoy ramen so much. I do enjoy my salmon bowl, and Tonkatsu curry udon. yum!

name: スカスカ
reviews: This restaurant brings us on a nostalgic journey with Chef Warti’s authentic delicious Indonesian food. Entering the restaurant, you feel like you have stepped into Indonesia with the thoughtful decorations and gentle local music. The service is amazing and friendly. The food, especially the beehoon goreng, spicy kangkong, ayam goreng and avocado shake (with chocolate sauce) reminds us of home in Singapore too. Chef’s sambal is the best we have had in Japan.
Delicious Indonesian food 🇮🇩, waiters are very attentive, and super nice atmosphere. Plus it’s all at an affordable price.

Great restaurant! The staff was very patient with my Japanese, then it turned out they speak English excellently. Here’s a picture of the ¥1000 set with chicken soup.  Everything was wonderful, but that soup was sublime. It was my first time eating Indonesian food but it won’t be my last. We will be back!

name: KOBE BEEF DININGモーリヤ
reviews:
I had the A5 Kobe Beef Sirloin and it truly melts in your mouth. If you’re planning to enjoy a full meal, I’d recommend going for the 140g cut for a satisfying experience, though the 100g portion is perfect if you just want to sample Kobe beef.

The onion soup and salad were also excellent.
What made the experience even more memorable was the incredible service; the chef and waitress were warm, welcoming, and made the whole meal feel special.

Suffice to say, I highly recommend to visit Mouriya if you’re in Kobe. It’s a must-try, especially with their 140 years of heritage.

This place is a-ma-zing! Once you see the sign, you'll need to go into the corridor below it and take the lift up to level 2.
We went at about 6pm on a Saturday and it had great ambiance and the booths were spacious and clean. Our server was attentive and lovely, he offered to take photos of us with the food. He spoke good English and was very prompt in clearing our table and fetching more drinks. We got the 6800 yen pp set and it was a really decent amount of food, particularly considering the price. Photos are in order of set:

Small restaurant on the 2nd floor.  Visited here for lunch.  Menu was in English.  Very friendly staff who also spoke English.

Started with the Kobe beef and onion soup, then a salad, then came the entre... Three different cuts of grilled Grade A5 Kobe beef.  The soup was delicious.  The salad had a tad too much vinegar for my taste.  But the meats were perfectly cooked... so flavourful, tender and juicy!

Fair prices, and definitely worth every yen.  Highly recommended!

name: Maguro Entoki
reviews:
The tuna was so fresh, tasty and it literally melted in my mouth, this was the first thing I ate in Japan, I do not regret it!!
The ladies working there were very kind, enthusiastic and funny. This is a place to visit when in Osaka!
Excellent food served by very hospitalable hosts. Really fresh stuff and yet affordable. Staff speaks decent english as well. Several places in Kuromon market are hyped but this place stands apart.
Mind blown by the tuna. Top quality, yet affordable. It was so good we had to come back again. Staff are super friendly and the shop is a nice haven from the busy Kuromon Market

name: Sunken Garden
reviews: The Sunken Garden in the Perdana Botanical Gardens is a peaceful green space that feels like a quiet oasis in the middle of the city. The garden lies below ground level in a circular design with neatly trimmed shrubs, colorful flower beds, and a central star-shaped pond that creates a balanced, relaxing scene perfect for photos and slow walks. You’ll find shaded benches around the top of the garden where you can sit, rest, and take in the fresh air away from the street noise. The paths and planting style give it a calm, orderly feel that makes it ideal for a morning stroll, quiet reflection, or reading under trees. Many visitors say it’s well maintained, clean, and very pleasant on a warm day, though it doesn’t have coffee shops or direct public transport access inside the garden itself. Because it’s inside the larger botanical gardens, you can easily pair it with visits to other sections like the Hibiscus and Orchid Gardens or the Deer Park, making your day out in nature even richer.

This was our favourite attraction at the gardens. It’s so pretty and popular, it can take a while to get that picture of the gardens without other people in it. Especially if there are 3 young girls wanting to get that perfect Instagram picture to upload.
There are several benches in the shade around the top of the garden.
Delicately manicured sunken garden which looks something out of Europe

name: BurgerBoss
reviews: Wanted to try a Ramly burger done right. I think we chose right cause the special (comes with egg) double burger with cheese was delicious. The gentleman working the stand were top notch - super friendly and fun. They took there time making a delicious messy burger from scratch - served right from grill to table. They even rounded down cause we didn't have 50 sen. Check it out if you are in the area!

Best burger at Jalan Alor Markets! Social media famous, a must try when in KL. It’s been a privilege to watch this establishment grow into a popular burger joint. Price is unbeatable for the quality and taste. Highly recommend.

I tried the Special Double Beef Cheeseburger and it was a fun experience. Some people say it's juicy, well the patty aren't juicy at all, it's just because they put several sauces in it. The thai sauce bring a nice taste. What's coming out strong is black pepper, like a lot, be aware.
We were the only one at the stand and it took like 14min to get the burger, a bit slow

name: Sansuke
reviews:
Totally recommend this! Authentic Japanese food and absolutely lovely family that made the food. They were so kind and hospitable. We are so thankful!

Try the red sea urchin. My kids loved the ikura and engawa aburi sushi.

Excellent food and ambience. The restaurant is run by a family of three who are very hospitable and friendly even though they do not speak much English. They gave free gifts to the children and were kind and warm towards all of us.

Staff is the sweetest and the most helpful. Food is really really tasty and we had a great time in there chatting with other cute guests. I recommend that place to everyone! Tofu, beer and tuna sashimi in the pictures :))

name: Pulau Café
reviews:
Visited the cafe and ordered the Unagi Open Sando, Apple Matcha, and Basque Burnt Cheesecake.
The unagi had a lot of bones — almost every bite, which really affected the eating experience.
The apple matcha has a very unique flavour.
Basque burnt cheesecake was not bad, quite enjoyable.

Overall experience is okay, but the unagi dish needs improvement.

Visited on 1 January with a group of five after randomly finding this place on the RED app. We wanted to try something different from the usual Western cakes—new year, new experience!

The food pleasantly surprised me. Parking can be a bit challenging as it’s in a busy area, but the quality of the food definitely makes up for it. The coffee and cakes are a must-try—especially the cakes, they were excellent.

Definitely a nice treat-yourself spot (maybe after payday 😄). Would come back again, though the place isn’t very OKU-friendly. Also, make sure to call ahead to reserve on busy days.
This is a rare gem of a cafe , tucked at the corner of a street. Small and excellent vibe. Coffee is good. Love the cakes with mochi. Cheese cakes are good too. Price is not cheap .

name: Midagahara
reviews:
One of the stop from 立山馳 station which is about 30 minutes bus ride!

There are two hotels right here. Because it is at 1930 meter elevation, so both hotels serve alcohol. Both hotels are very nice also.

There is a wooden walkway you can walk around during the summer months. But it was covered by snow when we visited in mid-May!

This station is surrounded by mountain and most of the time is above the cloud line.  Great photo opportunity location!

This place is well worth a stop! Roughly 30mins from the lower station and 20 minutes from Murobe. It is even more wonderful if not too cloudy as you will have great views of the mountains. In my opinion, this is better than the walk around Murobe as it doesn't seem like most of the crowd is interested in making a stop here. Taking the longer route rather than the shorter one is recommended if you have around 1.5h to 2h until the next bus (you will be asked to reserve your next bus slot when you disembark here).

The place is surreal! It’s indeed stairway to heaven. I love it and I cried when I left. #1 most beautiful place in Japan for me. I took the 45m course (the short one) due to the time constraints but 100% will come back. This is the highlight of the alpine route!

name: Lorong Petaling 2 - Old Kuala Lumpur Street Art
reviews: A hidden gem tucked within the bustling streets of Kuala Lumpur, Lorong Petaling 2 offers a glimpse into the city's rich heritage through its beautifully crafted murals. The artwork here highlights old trades and cultural elements, preserving the nostalgia of the city's past while adding a modern artistic touch. The alley is well-maintained and provides a unique backdrop for photography enthusiasts. Whether you're a history lover or a street art admirer, this spot is worth a visit to experience the creative fusion of tradition and contemporary expres

Must see!
Painted on the side of a building and very well maintained!
Historical, cultural, unforgettable!

Lorong Petaling, better known as Petaling Street in Kuala Lumpur, offers a vibrant and culturally rich experience for both locals and tourists. This bustling street is famous for its lively atmosphere, traditional Chinese architecture, and an array of street vendors selling everything from fashion, souvenirs, electronics, to local delicacies. The red lanterns strung across the walkway give it a unique and nostalgic charm, especially at night when the street comes alive with lights and energy.

Food is a major highlight — you’ll find delicious Chinese snacks like wantan mee, roasted duck, muah chee, apam balik, and herbal teas at very affordable prices. There are also halal options nearby, making it a great spot for all types of visitors. The vendors are generally friendly, although bargaining is expected when buying goods.

One point to note is that the area can get very crowded, especially during weekends and holidays. It’s advisable to keep an eye on your belongings. Cleanliness has improved over the years, but there’s still room for better waste management.

Overall, Lorong Petaling is a must-visit spot if you want to soak in KL’s heritage, shop affordably, and enjoy street food in a lively atmosphere.

reviews: CowCow Ice cheese cup is my absolute favourite! I always had it back in Manila. I love how smooth the cheese tastes and blends perfectly. This is my first time having it in Kuala Lumpur and it truly never disappoints. The staff was really friendly too. Thank you for your service!

this was my first time trying cheese ice cream (how have i not seen it until now???) and it was way better than i expected. i got the twist soft serve with vintage cheese cone. the milk soft serve was mildly sweet but creamy, and the gouda soft serve had a great balanced flavour. the cheddar cheese cone was so tasty - very savoury so it pairs great with the ice cream. if you’re anything like me, i always want ice cream but have trouble finishing it. not a problem with this one!

Located at the mall near my stay, i only ordered cow cow twist with milk and cheese in a cup, the taste not too sweet, the cheese really cheesy, love it. The ice cream not so fast melted. The place had limited seat area.

reviews: Pricy street fodd, but this is a super tender, real Japanese Wagyu skewer that tastes amazing. If you buy 3, you get one free, and it costs 60RM. Best buy I had, ordered every time I was walking there.

Meh, it was okay I guess.

Really not worth any sort of hype.

I also really doubt it’s A5 Wagyu.

Oil has an old taste and you could taste the butane or whatever fuel they were using for the grill.

Women grilling and serving was pretty depressing and didn’t communicate very much. No wonder the stall was empty when we were there….

Save the money and get about 15 satay sticks for the same price as 1 wagyu skewer! Much better tasting and fairer deal.
Absolutely mouth watering Japanese wagyu beef skewers, a must try street food if you are visiting Jalan Alor night market!

Special: goat 🐐 stomach and leg available beside standard chicken and mutton

So very good food and very very Nice people ! Smell and taste amazing ! And cheap !
More photos in my Instagram : shot_by_luc

No, it's better and healthier than roti canai, its Chapati. Google it if u want to no why. I had three chapatis served fresh off the hot plate and enjoyed it with a truly outstanding small plate of lamb curry and same of dhal.  All inc a very good teh tarik kurang manis rm10!  A totally satisfying dinner that well deserves a 4 star. I'm of course ranking it from the pov of a value for money traveller.

name: モザイクガーデン
street: Higashikawasakicho, 1 Chome−6−2 神戸アンパンマンこどもミュージアム＆モール 1階
reviews: Nothing really to see here other than the Ferris wheel. It does offer views to Kobe Bridge, but no better than along the harbour.

name: ITS Thai Street Dessert
reviews: I will recommend the combo one which might cost 15 MYR, a mix of coconut and mango ice cream scoop with a mix of all biscuits made our moments.
Everywhere I travel in SE Asia I seek out the Coconut Ice Cream and this place over the course of several years it still the very best in my  opinion.

Dessert you're gonna try while in Alor Street‼️

I LOVE COCONUT ICE CREAM. I'm in love. They also give a bunch of topping, like a bunch😊 The sweetness and savory balance out. I will definitely buy this again‼️

name: George Town, Malaysia UNESCO AREA
reviews: Georgetown has a rich history dating back to the 1700s. The whole UNESCO Heritage area can be covered on foot. There are so many things to see. There are various places of worship that are very old - Chinese temples, Hindu temples, mosques and churches. Many of the buildings are old and some date back to the 1800s. A comparatively recent addition is the street art. That was a brilliant idea. The history and culture of Penang, particularly Georgetown, are captured through the art.

One of the main reasons most people visit Georgetown. Its a beautiful area, with amazing old architecture, temples and the street art you will find everywhere. Loved walking around and soaking up the atmosphere.

Charming town in Penang. Good place to view the old world architecture and eat the good food. This is a town that relies on tourism however with Covid the place hs struggles to get tourists in. Narrow cobbled way streets, beautiful sea facing esplanade and hills make this a truly fascinating destination

name: Nasi Tomato Periuk Penang
street: Mch bistro, jalan tasik selatan 30F, desa tasik, Lebuhraya Sungai Besi
reviews: Nasi tomato was goood. nice portion for brunch. beef was tender and bursting with flavor. i will come again for sure. it was located at a food court where you could find more food selection. overall experience was nice
Taste is very bad actually. Looks good bud taste is bad. Sambal very sweet

Ah, Nasi Tomato Periuk Penang – the place you go to eat your weight in fragrant rice and still somehow feel like you might need just one more helping. If you've got an affinity for Penang-style cooking and can handle a solid food coma, this place might just be your next go-to.

The Good
The tomato rice here is, without exaggeration, a bit like a magic trick – it’s fluffy, flavorful, and somehow always piping hot (like, what do they use, a cauldron?). The combination of sweet and savory spices in the rice itself makes it almost a standalone dish – but of course, this isn’t the place to settle for just rice. The curries and side dishes are everything you'd expect from a Penang kitchen, with big, bold flavors and just the right kick. Their chicken dishes (especially the ayam masak merah) have that juicy, tender perfection that keeps you coming back, even if you’ve already had seconds.

Best Part
Watching everyone hit that "I'm-too-full-but-this-is-too-good-to-stop" phase. It's like witnessing a universal experience of food-induced existential crisis. Plus, the price isn't too bad for the quality – definitely on the affordable side considering you get the kind of portions that leave you full for two days.

Final Verdict
If you’re okay with a bit of a wait, some close-quarters dining, and a food coma that lasts until next Tuesday, give Nasi Tomato Periuk Penang a try. Just don’t blame me if you can’t move afterward – or if you find yourself thinking of that tomato rice in random moments, wondering when you’ll be back for round two.

name: YUEN FONG - JALAN ALOR
reviews:
ALWAYS BE FAVORITE PORK BACON!!
The best pork bacon I ever tried, their bacon is very tasty and juicy. The ham is great as well! The price is not too expensive although their location is in tourist area.
The staff also very generous if you want to try the sample before you buy, just ask and they will give you want.
Very high recommend if you want to buy pork bacon for yourself or if you want to bring back tou your country as a gift.
The spicy pork bacon!!!! Hands down best pork jerky I’ve ever had. Excellent flavour. I’m going back for more!!

Very friendly service. Personally i think this brand serves better bak hwa than the other famous brand which store located just opposite their stall.  I love their spicy bacon, if you like spicy, you should try this. Its also with good portion of fat.

Will always come back to buy their product

name: Comptoir Ruban(Counter French)
reviews:
I was saddened by the closure of the long-established French restaurant "Trente et Un,"but I’m truly delighted that this new-style restaurant has opened.
The open-kitchen concept, where you can see the chefs at work, seems to be a trend,and it's genuinely enjoyable to watch.The atmosphere is vibrant and youthful, and the cuisine is delicate and absolutely delicious.At the same time, the essence of traditional French cuisine is still deeply felt,and I sensed that the traditions they've cultivated continue to live on in this new approach.I look forward to visiting again soon.
All the dishes from the appetizers to dissert were all tasty. The price is reasonable, high recommended.
宿泊時のディナーでふらっと来店しました。カウンター席からシェフ達が手際よくスピーディーにかつ繊細な作業をしているのを見るのが楽しかったです。みなさん真剣に気持ちを入れて仕事されていて、素晴らしいプロ集団だと感心しました。当然お料理は美しくて、美味しくて完璧でした。また来たいと思います。ごちそうさまでした。

name: St Joseph's Novitiate Heritage Building
reviews:
📍St Joseph's Novitiate Heritage Building, Gurney Paragon

Another photoshoot with Dr Crystal and Mukrawee at this beautiful heritage site. This lovely red dress was hand-sewn by Mukrawee herself, who is an enthusiast in crafting her very own wedding gowns. These ladies are extremely talented!

great place , cozy and has privacy.
however , get gloves to shake hands.

The St. Joseph's Novitiate is a historic building. Formerly a seminary founded by the Institute of the Brothers of Christian Schools (aka Christian Brothers, Lasallian Brothers, French Christian Brothers, or De La Salle Brothers), is a congregation for teaching Catholicism, founded in France by Jean-Baptiste de La Salle (1651-1719), and is now based in Rome. This Congregation also pioneered mass education in Malaysia and elsewhere in the world at that time until now.

The building, now a place for special events and functions, was used by the novitiate in the early days. Beginning in 1918 by De La Salle Brothers, the novitiate trained youth to enter the religious order. Then it is used as a teacher training college before being hired to private schools.

Now this building is a place for locals and tourists, the Gurney Paragon lifestyle mall. developed by Hunza Properties Berhad (HPB), this involves preserving colonial buildings.

St Jo now functions as a venue for private dinners, corporate events, product launches, exhibitions, or wedding ceremonies.

name: 神戸たむら
reviews:
ポートピアホテル内、和食料理屋さん！
コースでどの料理も美味！たまには高級な和食ランチもいいですね。
落ち着いた雰囲気、4階だというのにプチ日本庭園が窓から楽しめます。
車で訪れましたのでノンアルビールで妻と乾杯！美味しい料理ありがとうございました♪
老舗ホテルの和食、安定した美味しさ、安心感ある
新生児がいることを事前にお伝えすると、個室を用意していただけました。赤ちゃんも寝かせられ、たくさん配慮していただけました。雰囲気も良かったです。

name: Merdeka Square
reviews:
We were lucky to visit when the building was open with free entry! We had the opportunity to learn about its history and see many architectural models inside. It holds invaluable historical significance for our country’s independence.

Before going in, we thought it would be too hot to walk around, but it was definitely worth it. There are many cafés and rooms to explore inside the building. From the building, we could also enjoy some lovely views since it is located in the city centre. The architecture itself has many beautiful features as well.

One of the museum sections was air-conditioned and displayed many beautiful exhibits. To enter the museum, it might take some time, but usually no longer than 10 minutes.

During the visit, I was deeply touched by the words of our Father of Merdeka:

“To the youth of this country I have a message. You have a wonderful future ahead of you. Unlike us, you have a country free from any domination. You grow up with your heads held high as masters in your own country. As masters you have the future of this country rest on you. Whether our star rises or falls, it will be due to you solely.”

It truly touched and motivated me. I really liked this place and the meaningful experience it gave me.

Dataran Merdeka has improved visually after recent renovation works, especially with the restoration of Sultan Abdul Samad Building, which enhances its historical charm and makes the area more attractive for photos and heritage visits. The square now appears cleaner and more structured, supporting its role as a cultural and ceremonial landmark in Kuala Lumpur. However, some surrounding facilities, including parking and pedestrian areas, still require better maintenance, and occasional renovation works may limit full access. Overall, it remains a worthwhile destination for history, sightseeing, and city exploration, particularly during cooler hours in the morning or evening.

I have been living in Malaysia for seven months, and this was my first Ramadan outside my home country,Libya. On the fifteenth day of Ramadan, I went to Merdeka Square to have iftar there. Honestly, the atmosphere was more than wonderful. I enjoyed it very much, and we also performed the prayer at Masjid Jamek.
I wished that I had come here from the beginning of Ramadan. The families sitting around me were all Malaysian families. I did not feel like a stranger at all; instead, I felt as if I were in my own country.
I say this sincerely: I have never met people kinder and more friendly than the Malaysian people. I pray that Allah protects Malaysia and continues to bless your country with peace and safety.
I highly recommend everyone to try having iftar at Merdeka Square. It is truly a wonderful and unforgettable experience.

name: Menara Kuala Lumpur
street: 2 Jalan Punchak, Off, Jalan P. Ramlee
reviews:
Visited midweek  end of Feb, no queues for entry or lifts, the combo ticket is worth purchasing to get the open air sky deck as well as the observation.
Amazing views of the city, especially on a clear day like we had. With little people there we were able to take time to look right around and get some good photos.
Also great to see from the ground from around the city, especially lit up at night

My visit to Menara Kuala Lumpur was absolutely amazing! The view from the observation deck is simply breathtaking — you can see the entire city skyline from above, and it’s especially stunning during sunset and at night. 🌆✨

The place is clean, well-organized, and the staff are friendly and helpful. The Sky Box experience is a must-try for those who love a little thrill and want incredible photo opportunities! 📸

It’s one of the best attractions in Kuala Lumpur and definitely worth the visit. Highly recommended for tourists and locals alike!

The view from sky terrace was amazing! You can even see Genting Highland like a floating city from here! Staff were all very friendly. Overall experience was excellent! I prefer Sky terrace over observation deck, personal preference. As of February 6th 2026, the ticket fee (for Malaysians) for observation deck was RM30, sky terrace RM50, combo (observation deck + sky terrace) RM55. Sky terrace last entry is at 9.30pm, observation deck last entry is at 9.50pm.

name: Atsuta-jingu Shrine
reviews: A truly spiritual and serene experience. While the grounds and the ancient architecture are breathtaking, what made my visit unforgettable was a kind Japanese elder who shared the shrine's deep history with us. Learning about the significance of the sacred sword and how the rituals work added a layer of respect to the visit that I wouldn't have had otherwise. The ancient camphor tree is a must-see. Highly recommend taking your time to walk the forested paths!

This shrine holds one of the three Imperial Regalia (sword)used for the coronation of the Japanese Emperors. The sword, however is not available for viewing. The shrine is a very tranquil spot within Nagoya, with easy access by public transportation and private car.  The grounds are very carefully maintained. Best time of year to visit would be spring or fall, as the museums were closed for the New Year holiday season.

Came to this Shinto shrine at Atsuta Ward before having lunch at a nearby restaurant. A very cool and breezy walk from the tori gate to the main hall.  Along the way, you get to see various historical lamp pieces.  And of course, you will see the great giant Camphor Tree and also the iconic walls of stacked, decorative sake barrels known as Kazaridaru donated by the breweries for as offering to the deities.

name: Atsuta Hōraiken Honten
reviews: I came at 405pm on a Tuesday evening and there was only a short queue. After few minutes, they started to register us and given a time of 430pm. At 430pm sharp, they called all the groups with 430pm to enter. I think come in an evening will have shorter queue. The unagi definitely worth it and really delicious. You can spend time to visit atsuta jingu before the evening queue.

Other than the restaurant doesn’t take reservation and the wait time can be very long (in our case it was over 2 hours), this eel fish specialty restaurant is excellent. Highly recommended you leave you name to the restaurant and they will tell you around what time you should come back, then go to nearby izakaya (Japanese tavern) or a cafe to have a drink and some snacks before the proper meal. The eel fish is grilled to perfection, they teach you to eat it in 3 different, personal favorite is still eating the original way without any extra seasonings or soup. Highly recommended the grill eel fish liver, it is very tasty and the taste texture is surprisingly chewy instead of silky. Service wise, is friendly and efficient once you get into the restaurant. Atmosphere wise they have a tiny little Japanese garden which is quite pretty, the dinning hall are very traditional style meanwhile you get to seat on comfortable chairs and proper table instead of tatami.

The restaurant maybe iconic by historical events but the current culinary skills and services are not good. Another tourist trap catering mainly for Asian expats. After waiting for about 90 minutes outside we were allowed by “big boss inside” and were greeted by “cold” acting unfriendly staff. There was kind of quiet and eery atmosphere as people silently awaited “famous” food. The food arrived after more than 25 minutes and was not same as advertised, the website food photos and actual food photos are so much different. There is almost no unagi in the bowl and the strips of seafood covering boiled rice have thickness of fried bacon. After having unagi in many places like Tokyo or San Francisco we were totally surprised by poor food quality and dissatisfied. On the top of that the menu is overpriced at least 5 times costing ¥5000+ while the better unagi dish at local market is about ¥1100. Overall we were totally disappointed and had a very bad experience. Lessons learned don’t ever believe web media food stories.

name: Pinang Peranakan Mansion
reviews:
A beautiful and very enjoyable visit.
What we liked most is that the mansion doesn’t feel like a dry museum — it feels like stepping into someone’s home. The rooms are elegant, colorful, and full of character, especially the furniture, porcelain, glass displays, and the wedding bed.
You don’t need to read every description to enjoy it; just walking through, observing the details, light, and craftsmanship is enough. It really shows the blend of cultures and the sense of refinement and family life.
Not too long, not overwhelming  just the right pace. Definitely worth visiting if you want something cultural but still relaxing

Love the tour here! She really told the stories here and very happy to answer our questions (questioning is encouraged)! Although it can be crowded but the place is super cozy with air conditioning at many places! I had a full 2-hour visit here! Strongly recommended!
Tips: when you buy the ticket, it is valid for another Peranakan house too!!! You can also find cheaper ticket online but do check the name and location properly. Also, do check out the peranakan play time before visit too!

Was it fun? Look at my photos!!!!!

This museum offers the best stage performance in Penang — do not miss it.
For me, it was one of the most interesting and memorable performances I have ever seen in my life.
