As a museum, it is also very well done. You can see many everyday objects that show how Chinese families lived here in the last century, which makes the history feel very real and personal.

Most of the staff were friendly and helpful. However, one Chinese-speaking guide was extremely unprofessional — she showed no passion for her job, rolled her eyes at visitors, and made the experience uncomfortable. Honestly, she should not be working here.

If you speak English, I strongly recommend choosing an English-speaking guide, as they are much more professional and welcoming.

Overall, the performance alone is worth the visit, and I would still highly recommend this qqplace.

name: Atsuta Houraiken Matsuzakaya Branch
street: Sakae, 3 Chome−30−8 Matsuzakaya Nagoyaten South Building, 10F
reviews:
How could you say you’ve visited Nagoya without trying hitsumabushi?

A must-try local specialty, hitsumabushi is a luxurious dish where grilled eel is served over rice, together with accompaniments such as seaweed, spring onions, wasabi and a broth of some sort. Its unique, 4-stage way of eating allows the dish to be savoured and enjoyed to the fullest.

Atsuta Houraiken is one of the most famous hitsumabushi restaurants in Nagoya, claiming to have invented the dish. They have multiple branches in the city itself, this one arguably the most accessible, located on the 10th floor of the Matsuzakaya department store in Sakae. When arriving at the store, there will be a line to collect a queue ticket which indicates, very accurately, what time to come back to the restaurant, depending on the current wait time. We went at 5.50pm on a Wednesday, and we were seated by 6.50pm exactly an hour later.

As for the food itself, a single set of hitsumabushi sets one back 4400 yen. The price is definitely on the steeper side, but this is to be expected as it is by all means an indulgent dish. This was my first time trying hitsumabushi, and I was absolutely blown away by the whole experience - the crispy, flavourful eel perfectly complements the rice, and when eaten together, creates an otherworldly taste - savoury and sweet at the same time, with a tinge of smokiness. I especially enjoy how the layer of rice just underneath the eel is still slightly infused with the flavour of the unagi. All in all, it was an extremely satisfying meal and was well worth the wait - I would go so far as to say that this was the best meal I had in Nagoya. This place does their hitsumabushi so well that I almost thought about going back a few days later for seconds.

Highly recommend, this would be your best bet if you are looking to try hitsumabushi!

Fantastic meal. After visiting four unagi restaurants in Nagoya, this one stood out as my favourite. I was concerned it might be a tourist trap at first, but it exceeded expectations. Arrive early to get a queue ticket, so you won’t have to wait too long. Get yourself the egg and black sesame ice cream too!

Could've given 6 stars easily! The best unagi ever tasted in my history of unagi eating. A must try when in Nagoya. There's typically a waiting line but it's worth it. It only takes 10-15 mins of waiting. This is only one of the branches and not the original place as the original place is 6kms away from us compared to this branch which is 800m away from us only. So we decided to go here as the original place has also a waiting line so it was risky for us to travel and end up waiting for too long. 😅 But again, as the reviews say, it's worth the wait! Service is excellent as staff understands English. The atmosphere is a restaurant style as it is in a mall compared to the original one which is an old restaurant. Around 100+ years i think but the quality is excellent! Again, a must try for unagi lovers and for the non-lovers which will surely change their opinion! TOTALLY WORTH IT!!

name: Suzuka Circuit Park
reviews:
Suzuka Circuit was high on my list for places to visit while in Japan because I love Formula1 and everything Honda. It did not disappoint eventhough there was no race on the day I visited.
It would really make a big impression on small kids and their families as the Park is full of attractions for the under 10 year olds.
I also wanted to buy lots of Honda merchandise but the shops did not live up to my expectations unfortunately.
The Honda Racing Gallery has a nice collection of engines, used F1 cars and a few bikes. Love to go here again when the F1 is in town! It is best to book a hotel at the circuit for easy parking and less walking.

Really good place for family with small kids until late teenager. You can play simple bump car up until riding a go cart. There are also mini motorbike that adults can ride as well. The time attack concept to get license is awesome. However, do not expect you will get the best time as the machine differs in quality. Some are just not tuned to the max speed so even if you can drive well, it may not be able to speed enough. Other than that, really nice. You can even see the race track. Go on weekdays for a much quieter experience.

Enjoyed taking our son here. Not as busy as other amusement parks but the rides are just right for small children. We enjoyed the Suzuka Ciruit Challenge, driving on an actual racing stadium. Perfect for the kids that are into race cars!

name: Kikuseidai (Observation Platform)
reviews:
Absolutely must visit place in Kobe! Recommended to visit a little earlier before sunset so you can check out both the day view and night view!

You can drive or take the cable car here, most people will use the Mt Maya Cable Car as its the most convenient. We visited at early December and it could get really cold with strong winds up here so be prepared.

If you're planning to visit via cable car:
- be sure to check the official schedules at the official Mt Maya website.
- We made the mistake on visiting on a weekday which the last cable car back will depart before the sky went fully dark. It operates later in the night in the weekends however.

Definitely one of the best night views I've ever seen but plan accordingly if you plan to arrive by cable car.
Amazing view over Osaka bay. The cable car is old but works perfectly. The best way to enjoy is the spot is to hike from the town and ride down with cable car.
Worthwhile trip at night to see the glimmering city skyline. There is a cafe at the top to provide respite from the cold during winter.

name: National Monument
reviews:
I had a wonderful visit to National Monument (Tugu Negara).

It’s a very quiet and peaceful place, perfect for reflection and appreciation of Malaysia’s history.

The monument itself is impressive and beautifully designed, surrounded by well-maintained gardens and greenery that add to the calm atmosphere.

You can truly feel the historical significance of the site as it honors the brave heroes who sacrificed for the nation.

It’s a meaningful and respectful place to visit while in Kuala Lumpur.

Highly recommended for anyone who appreciates history and a serene environment.

Tugu Negara (the National Monument) is a must-see landmark in KL. The bronze sculpture is incredibly impressive and grand, standing as a powerful tribute to those who fought for the country's freedom. The surrounding park and the botanical gardens make it a very serene and beautiful spot.
​It’s perfect for a peaceful stroll to admire the fountains and the intricate details of the monument. A great place to escape the city buzz and reflect on Malaysia’s history. It's free to enter and very well-maintained. Highly recommended for a quick but meaningful visit!

As a Malaysian tourist, i highly recommend visiting Tugu Negara, one of the most significant historical landmarks in Malaysia. Located just minutes from Kuala Lumpur’s city centre, this monument stands as a solemn tribute to the brave soldiers who sacrificed their lives during Malaysia’s struggle for freedom, particularly during World War 2 and the Malayan Emergency. It’s not just a monument, it’s a symbol of unity, resilience, and national pride.
The site is easily accessible by car or public transport, with ample parking and well-maintained pathways, making it convenient for families and international visitors alike. The surrounding area is beautifully landscaped, offering a peaceful environment for reflection and photography. Accessibility is also commendable, with ramps and clear signage for visitors with mobility needs.
For Malaysians, Tugu Negara is a reminder of our shared history and the price of independence. For non-Malaysian tourists, it provides deep insight into Malaysia’s past and values, making it more than just a photo spot, its an educational experience. Pair your visit with nearby attractions like Perdana Botanical Gardens for a full cultural day.
Whether you’re a history enthusiast or simply exploring Kuala Lumpur, Tugu Negara is a meaningful stop that connects you to Malaysia’s heritage.

name: Ghost Museum
reviews:
We all had so much fun at the Ghost Museum! I think it was one of our highlights, and wasn't expensive at all.🙂
I won't spoil it by going into too much detail, but the ghost models are pretty good, with some info about different ghosts/legends along with some fun along the way.
Our youngest is right into ghosts and monsters and I think this was one of the biggest smiles I've seen from her in a while!
I'd highly recommend the Ghost Museum for families around Georgetown.👍

The staff were very friendly and helpful. The second we step foot into the premise, they assisted me and my friends to the ticket counter to buy some tickets. For Weekday IC tickets are Rm24 as for weekend I'm not sure. But it was worth it, me and my friends had lots of fun in there. 😁😁

As we walk along the pathways of the museum, we noticed how creative and interactive the displays were. It’s almost like we were part of the stories, being the ghosts and imitating the storyline. How amazing, spectacular, extraordinary and thrilling it was. 🙂🙂🙂

ANYWAYSSS i love it, i felt like im at my inner peace zone, the staffs are WOW, the displays are WOWWWW and the atmosphere is ‘AHHH LOVING IT’!!!

name: The Tokyo Restaurant
street: Level 4, Lot 10, Shopping Mall, 50, Jln Bukit Bintang
reviews:
Here for dinner tonight and we decided to go for the Beef Steak and Lamb Chop 🤍

From my personal taste, I’d rate the steak 6/10 and the lamb chop 8/10. The steak is priced at RM199, but honestly, it didn’t really feel worth it as it comes with around 10–15 pre-cut pieces and a portion of fries only.

The tiramisu cake is good — definitely worth trying!

Wasabi edamame was something different and interesting to try too.

Last but not least, thank you Sofea for the great and warm hospitality 😊

I recently dined at The Tokyo Restaurant and had such a great experience! The food was absolutely delicious, everything we ordered was well-prepared and full of flavor. The highlight for me was definitely the rib eye steak. It was cooked perfectly, juicy, tender, and seasoned just right.

Special thanks to Aiman who served us he was friendly, attentive, and made sure we were comfortable throughout the meal. His service really made the experience even better.

Will definitely come back again. Highly recommend if you’re looking for good food and great service! 🍽️✨

I recently visited Tokyo Restaurant and had a mixed but mostly positive experience.

The food was amazing and very delicious definitely the highlight of the visit. The serving time was also very fast, which I really appreciated.

However, the vibe felt a bit unusual. The servers would sometimes run across our table and scream or talk very loudly without warning. This might be normal for regular customers, but for new customers it can be quite shocking. I think the atmosphere could be improved by being a bit more mindful of guests who are not used to this style.

Overall, great food and speed, but the service style could be calmer to make all customers comfortable.

name: Tek Sen Restaurant
reviews:
Best Chinese food I've had. We ordered the double roasted pork in chilli which was unlike any pork dish we have had before from a Chinese restaurant. The crispy chicken with sour plum sauce, sambal water spinach, fried rice and sweet and sour pork were also delicious.
Arrived at 5pm and there was a long line already but got seated at about 6:15, was glad the food was so good after waiting in the heat- made it worth it.

What is a double roast pork? Today I just had it.  It is actually shaorou (roast pork) slided to bite size and they fried with char siew sauce. Almost every table has it cos it's delicious.  Just this and one bowl of rice is actually good enough.

But then, there is the super delicious n soft n fresh asam stingray also. The world treat me really well as i get to eat so delicious food.

Even the lime juice is nice and ordered an extra one cos I am trying to recover from diarrhea (from the not so good mussel from the nonya seafood buffet on genting cruise)

This place opens at 1130am, we reached at 1140am and already full. Joined the queue and stood for 40min watching you tube.  Those who are even later will need to queue in the sun, cos the queue stretches out of the sheltered walkway. So, next time I will come at 1115am, so that I can be on the first seating.

The Michelin shop is worth the wait.  The staff all efficient and fair, and also ask if we are ok to share table, which cut down waiting time too.

Will come back for sure!!!!

The food is excellent, it's definitely worth the wait if you haven't tried it yet.
The staff is courteous and efficient.
We had The roast pork with chilly, braised pork trotter, mapo tofu and pea shoots with garlic for a table of 4.
Most dishes come in 2 serving sizes, small and large. We ordered 4 dishes so we we're recommended to get the small serve, which were enough for us, since we're not big eaters.

However we thought we could have polished a bigger serving of the pea shoots.

Everything was delicious, I can't think of anything bad to say.
They also accept card payments for those  who are wondering.

name: Pik Wah Bar & Cafe 碧华楼 | 烧腊 .咖啡. 酒吧. 串烧 （茨厂街）
reviews:
Pik Wah Café & Bar in Kuala Lumpur is a cosy little spot that offers a pleasant break from the city’s bustle. Portions are on the smaller side but reasonably priced, making it a comfortable choice for a light bite or casual catch-up. The service is attentive and welcoming, which adds a nice touch to the overall experience.

Their coffee is definitely the highlight, well-brewed, aromatic, and worth stopping by for. However, it can be slightly disappointing that quite a number of menu items are already sold out or unavailable as early as noon.

The rest of the food is decent, though there’s room to elevate the quality further, especially considering its prime location. Still, a nice café to drop by if you’re nearby and craving a good cup of coffee.

Bustling, lively Cantonese spot with plenty of energy. We arrived right before lunch hour and were seated immediately. The whole place is noisy with people rushing about, which adds to the authentic Cantonese eatery vibe. Service is quick enough despite the crowd, though tables are set quite close together.

Portions are on the smaller side. The fried rice cakes were good and tasty, definitely the highlight of the meal. Claypot coffee and tea were nothing to shout about, just normal, straightforward drinks. Overall, a decent place if you enjoy a fast-paced, bustling dining atmosphere.

This Chinatown establishment serves the most unique claypot Ho Ka Sai. The blend they use favours a strong dark roasted coffee with the chocolate Milo notes coming through in the after taste.  It may not suit every palate, especially if strong coffee is not to your taste. We loved its distinctive, memorable characteristics! Serving size is also generous for the Jumbo pot.

We had steamed yam cake and fried glutinous rice for breakfast. The food was great, albeit on the pricier end of the scale. This is expected given the location. I would not say this is a touristy place at all despite the prices being on the higher end for this type of cuisine. It seemed many KLites were enjoying their weekday breakfast when we went.

name: Marini’s on 57
reviews:
Located on the 57th floor of Petronas Tower and the view are spectacular. Great service by the staff and they were very attentive to our needs. Celebrated friend's 31st anniversary and the restaurant were nice to prepare chocolate treats to celebrate the occasion.

They assortment of breads paired with butter were given to start. We had the Burrata and asparagus as entree and we enjoyed both. The fillet mignon were done to perfection, with the sauce or simply with salt just added different dimension to the steak. The lobster tail with Angel Hair is the other dish that the ladies had, tastefully done and very yummy.

Overall, very good experience and would visit again. Do note that there are dress code requirement, do not go with Bermuda/slippers.

#ThrowBack
Marini’s on 57 is truly a magical spot for a romantic evening in Kuala Lumpur. We visited on Qixi Festival (七夕), celebrating our time together, and the breathtaking views of the city and the iconic Petronas Twin Towers made the night unforgettable. The atmosphere is elegant and intimate, creating the perfect setting for a special celebration.

The service was warm, attentive, and professional, making us feel truly cared for throughout our evening. Every detail, from the seating to the lighting, was thoughtfully arranged, enhancing the overall experience. Even without drinks or desserts, the ambience alone made our night feel incredibly special.

We will always cherish this memory, and we highly recommend Marini’s on 57 for anyone looking to celebrate a romantic and unforgettable moment with someone special. 💕

Six of us had dinner here on 3 Feb. Love the views and ambience here. The staffs are also attentive and friendly. The food is tasty. The restaurant also arranged free chocolates for me and my wife who are celebrating our 31st anniversary.

name: Bijan Bar & Restaurant
reviews:
Beautiful little place near Changkat selling pretty authentic Malaysian food. Came for the Ramadan set menu and the food quality and quantity were amazing. The set for 4 people had plenty of variety and everything was delicious. The service staff as well were extremely attentive and the environment was beautiful, intimate and pleasant.

One of the only issues we had was making a reservation. The WhatsaApp reservation number is unresponsive and was unable to help me. When I called they assured me that they had my reservation but that did not turn out to be the case. I asked to pre-book the set menu but they said I had to call marketing. I called on the day to confirm my reservation and they confirmed with me but when I arrived they didn't have it. In the end I still got a table but this was an unnecessarily frustrating process. This needs to be more streamlined.

Bijan Bar & Restaurant really delivers proper Malaysian food!

Had the Istana Set for dinner — truly makan like a king. The flavours are deep, fragrant and comforting, with a beautiful balance of smokiness, spice and savoury richness. Spicy but not overpowering, rich without being jelak — my heart was screaming after tasted each of the food - really shiok and sedap gila.

No gimmicks, just honest Malaysian flavours cooked properly. Cosy ambience, good service, perfect for family dinners or bringing overseas friends.

Confirm will come back. Highly recommended 👍

Definitely will come again, first of all I would to say big thanks to all the staff and manager name Dilla, their service was fantastic and superb. In addition, all the food are super yummy and delicious. We have served with 5star fine dining service in Bijan Restaurant here. Must try the prawn fritters, masak lemak, paku pakis, beef rendang if im not mistaken the dishes name, the beef absolutely tender. the fish very fresh and must try the dessert. I cant remember the dessert name..can refer the photos..like chocolate moist durianThanks Dilla & team for the great hospitality🩷

name: The Mugshot Cafe
reviews:
Great coffee spot the service was fast and friendly the menu is on the big blackboard behind the counter or you can order from the connecting shop that has patisserie items.
The food menu is limited yoghurt with fruit topping, bagel and eggs on toast and then many many cakes and crossants.
The waiter happily requested the chef make my scrambled eggs with no milk cream or butter and they were perfect for me. Crossant was indulgent and sweet and the cream cheese filling was just enough. I happily stayed there a while doing some trip planning and went back for coffee the following day. Definitely a spot to try. Staff lovely and welcoming

The setting and atmosphere of mugshot are very enticing. The pastries look beautiful and there is good seating. It was not the best cappuccino I’ve ever had - very milky. The pastries are not as good as they look. Very sugary and sweet. Almost too sweet! Just get one. The staff was lovely and very helpful. I would go back, but would order differently.

We have had breakfast here for most of our week here and the food and coffee is always good.  The bakery next door has the most amazing range of pasties, cakes and breads you can take food between the stores - excellent

name: The Loft - Love Lane
reviews:
Really enjoyed all the items we ordered. The wood fired pepperoni pizza has a thin crust that was well done with the edges being crispy. Pulling each slice of the pizza was a delight to see the long cheese  pull. Mac and cheese, and the lasagna were just perfect with the right amount of cheese and no overpowering. The mushroom soup in the bread bowl was thick and creamy with the right texture that wasn't too thick or too watery.

Overall we had a good dining experience here and all the waiters were attentive to our needs, constantly checking in on us if the food was OK.

Excellent fire oven pizza, which we enjoyed along with delicious smoothies and dessert. The stunning decor and ambiance of the place is also very noteworthy. It's an absolutely gorgeous restaurant in the heart of Georgetown. And we also enjoyed our evening stroll through Love Lane to conveniently arrive here and thankfully we didn't have to deal with too much traffic. Love Lane is a hub for dining out and bar hopping. Highly recommend The Loft.

We tried this restaurant after seeing good reviews and found the ambiance nice. The spaghetti carbonara was a hit as well as the tomato soup. Unfortunately, the pizza dough was not great and the sea bass we ordered was not very fresh. The service was great and the waiter super attentive. Parking was difficult and very limited so you may need to park further away.

name: Monster. A Garden Cafe
reviews:
Thank you for being a cat cafe that actually knows how to look after their cats! All the cats here look like they've been looked after very well, and are all quite happy. My friends and I are very happy with the service and the kind helpful staff.

The food was also incredibly good! I would recommend the popular caramel biscoff croffle or the curry set :)

To others please note:
If you have bags with you, keep them off the floor! As expected of animals they have the chance to get peed on, but don't blame the cat. We had a small incident that the staff handled quickly and gracefully.

All the cats here are soooo cute, omg!!!! I love all of them, and my favourite is this one cat that my girlfriend and I call DIVA because she’s such a diva with her face and her jewellery!! So cute!!!!

We only ordered two drinks to fulfil the minimum requirement to enter. Both drinks were good, and I loved the presentation. The staff were very nice and friendly. She also gave us a friendly reminder on how to handle the cats.

A must-try café if you’re hopping around Pasar Seni!

The service is good. The cat all was so cute. Just the price of food and beverage was quite expensive, l order one dessert it cost me RM25(not included tax) amd the cat snack was RM 6.5  each , but is taste good. I think the more valuable thing is can see the cat and touch them.

The first cons is we want to wait about 30min and no fan at that area. Because it limited space at there.

I think the best sitting area is the place near the door which can see some of the cat sit or laying infront of you. So cute 🥰🥰🥰.

name: Halal Ramen Honolu Osaka Namba
reviews:
Best meal I had in all of Japan was the spicy fried chicken ramen. It had a great kick. It was absolutely delicious!
They only have about 10 seats in the restaurants but it’s worth the wait.
They only take cash, and only take $1000 yen bills. The staff is very nice and will give you change if you have larger bills. You order via a vending machine that prints a ticket for you to hand to the chef to prepare your order. Very cool experience.
Highly recommend!

The chicken broth is very tasty umami flavours. The ramen is chewy and soaked up the broth nicely! The chicken pieces is generous. The spicy one elevates the flavour further.
Depending on the time, it may not have a long que. The shops is small that fits only small number of seats.

had dinner on my first night in osaka. we ordered mini wagyu rice bowl, dumpling and chicken ramen. the food were all delicious!!!!!. wagyu slice melts in mouth and had a nice flavour. waiters all are helpful and friendly. can pay via cash or card. will come back for sure ⭐️

name: Guan Di Temple Chinatown Tun H.S Lee
reviews:
Guan Di Temple, Chinatown KL

Located along Jalan Tun H.S. Lee in the heart of Chinatown, this temple feels surprisingly peaceful once you step inside. Despite the busy streets outside, the interior is calm and quiet, with the soft scent of incense creating a serene atmosphere.

The red lanterns, traditional architecture, and the statue of Guan Di give the temple a strong cultural presence. It’s well-maintained, clean, and respectfully preserved.

Outside the temple, you can conveniently buy oranges for offering, which makes it easy for visitors who want to pray.

If you’re exploring Petaling Street and looking for a quiet, spiritual break from the city’s hustle, this temple is definitely worth a visit.

Went on 31 January.

It is quite interesting that some donation boxes will have recorded voice of well wishes in Cantonese after individuals insert money into it. It is an interesting feature.

Did not take photos of interior as a form of respect.
Beautiful,sacred place,smells from the incense sticks what you feel in your nose and many people full with faith and blessing.Step into the temple and you will feel something too…

name: Corridor of Light / Tunnel of Light
reviews:
The best experience outside of Nagoya! Approximately 1hr travel via bus but well worth the time and effot.

Gardens were truly beautiful, complemented with yellow spot light, mist and calming music. The light show was stunning and the tunnel of light builds up the excitement leading to the light show. There are restaurants inside, ample seating area and vendors machines. I love it here! Weather was chilly but not freezing early December.

Beautiful place and experience during the winter evening light up. Awesome flowers and lights, especially of Mt Fuji made it a memorable visit.

On Christmas Day in 2025, we were at Nagashima Spa Land in the morning, Mitsui Outlet in the afternoon and here in the evening.

A very instagrammable place worth visiting during autumn illuminating light season. Try to visit in the afternoon to visit the flower garden and see the the illuminating lights after sunset.

To get here, you can take trains from Nagiya station. I took the Meitetsu bus from level 4 Meitetsu bus center. The directional signs are a bit confusing as there us a shopping mall inside too.

To buy ticket, it is at level 3. If using Suica card, just queue at the 22 bus lane, one bus hourly. No need to buy ticket in advance. The bus journey is about 35 min and it stops just outside the Nabana No Sato Garden.

Entry is $1500, with a 500 yen meal voucher. I choose to get a drink, about 350 yen, no refund. There is corn chowder, ice cream and several restaurants too.

Best time to visit is around 3-4pm as illuminating light starts around 5.10pm. Check the schedule online or inside the garden.

If you like flowers and lights, it is a nice place to enjoy the evening.

name: Jawi House Cafe Gallery
reviews:
Stopped by Jawi House Cafe Gallery in the afternoon with a few friends and it turned out to be a really pleasant break while exploring Georgetown.The place has a charming heritage feel and the small gallery inside adds a nice cultural touch.
We shared a few drinks and light bites while chatting, and everything was nicely prepared. The atmosphere is calm and cozy, which makes it a good spot to sit for a while and relax.
Service was friendly and welcoming, and we never felt rushed.

Overall a lovely place to spend a quiet afternoon with friends in Georgetown.

We had a very nice experience at Jawi House Cafe Gallery in Georgetown. The staff were extremely kind and friendly, and the service was excellent from start to finish. The food was outstanding – the salads were fresh and full of flavor, and the meat was very tender and literally falling apart. The prices were reasonable for the quality. Overall, a very good restaurant that we would definitely recommend.

We had a beautiful meal here. Food was very tasty. We had the beef rendang - very tender and delicious. Also different rices and mixed vegetables. We had the cheesecake and lemon tart for dessert. No complaints. The setting is like sitting in somebody’s home in their dining room, which is cool. Low music playing in the background so very easy to talk, good for someone who wants a quiet restaurant. Staff very friendly and gave us recommendations based on our requests. We came here because the restaurant was mentioned in our ‘Lonely Planet’ book on Asia, and very glad we did. We would highly recommend.

name: Laksalicious
reviews:
We came here to try their signature asam laksa and nasi ulam. Unfortunately, the nasi ulam was already sold out when we visited around 6pm on Friday. So I ordered their nasi lemak with rendang ayam instead.

I have to say both of them were delicious and satisfying! The laksa cost us RM12.90, but it had a visibly generous amount of fish flesh in the soup. The taste was really good, with nice fish umami and a balanced sour and spicy flavour. The rendang ayam was really good as well. Definitely coming back again to give the nasi ulam a try next time.

First off I must compliment them on setting up a comfortable place to eat. Having aircon in hot Malaysian weather is always an added bonus. The day I came, the waiters seemed understaffed and flustered. But they still went around their job with a smile.

As far as what they offer. Naturally laksa. It's, after all, called laksalicious. They even have a laksa themed drink. They serve two types of laksa. The assam version and the creamy version. If you like both, then you can order the mixed version. I was intrigued by the mixed version. My verdict? If you are undecided about the taste at this place, order the mixed version. It doesn't come pre-mixed, it comes with both types of soup interestingly separated in the bowl. My suggestion? Try both sides of the bowl individually before you mix them. At least you will know if you prefer the assam version here, the creamy version or the mixed version. I was pleasantly surprised by the taste of the mixed version. The tangy assam tempered by the creamy soup. The creamy soup watered by the assam soup. It had my palate confused and it's a great sensation. The thick noodle (you have a choice of thick or thin) was also prepared well.

I didn't get a chance to try the rest but the menu is quite extensive. For those who don't like laksa, they have nasi lemak, they have delicious looking desserts and also appetizing looking crackers and snacks. In short, it's a comfortable aircon chilled place to get a good meal. But it's a very sanitized version of how I usually have my laksa.

Visited the Michelin-recognized Penang Road Famous Laksa, and it truly lived up to the reputation! The laksa itself was bursting with authentic flavours — tangy, slightly spicy, and perfectly balanced without any ajinomoto taste. Every bite felt fresh, and the noodles had the perfect texture.
The cendol was equally impressive — creamy coconut milk, fragrant gula Melaka, and just the right sweetness. It was refreshing and not overly sweet, making it a perfect companion to the laksa.
The highlight for us was the Laksa Mojito — a clever twist on a classic beverage that was super refreshing and a fun way to enjoy the meal.

On top of that, the owner was super friendly, welcoming us warmly and making the whole experience even more enjoyable. The whole visit felt genuine, local, and absolutely satisfying. Definitely a must-visit spot if you want to taste real Penang flavours with quality and hospitality you can trust!

name: Bubba Gump Shrimp
street: Shimaya, 6 Chome−2−61 ユニバーサル・シティウォーク大阪 5F
reviews:
We had the onions rings and garlic bread to start and the shrimp scampi and Texas cajun chicken sandwich as mains.

The onion rings were a huge portion. Flaky exterior, not too oily. Inside were thick, sweet onions. Pretty good. Garlic bread was great - simple with good garlic and butter flavors.

Shrimp scampi was quite the let down. Sauce was not as expected - flavors were off. Chicken samdwhich was thin but nicely seasoned.

Service was pretty good.

First time trying at this restaurant at Universal City Walk at Osaka with Forest Gump theme! Great and very pleasant experience! Tried the prawn broth with rice and bread, prawns with veg and coleslaw! We ordered one alcoholic drink and one non-alcoholic drink, and we were given the glasses to keep as souverniors! Kudos to Shinizaki-san and her team! Yummy food and great staff with excellent service!

The service was excellent, and the staff were very friendly—especially Ms. Chitose, who made the visit even more memorable with her warm and attentive service. I celebrated my 30th birthday here, and they surprised me with a dessert cake, a photo souvenir, and Bubba Gump stickers, along with a special “Happy Birthday” message they signed for me. It was such a thoughtful gesture and truly made my day feel extra special.

Highly recommended for anyone visiting Universal Studios Osaka, especially if you’re celebrating a special occasion!

name: Maguroya Kurogin Kuromon
reviews:
I had the Kamatoro tuna at Kuromon Market in Osaka, and it was absolutely unforgettable. Kamatoro is the rare collar cut of the tuna, known for its incredible marbling and richness, and this one did not disappoint. The texture was unbelievably tender and buttery, practically melting on my tongue with every bite. Unlike fattier cuts that can sometimes feel heavy, this Kamatoro was light, clean, and perfectly balanced, letting the natural flavor of the tuna shine.
The taste was exquisite subtly sweet, rich, and incredibly fresh, with absolutely no fishy smell at all. Each slice had a perfect firmness that gave way to a silky smoothness in the mouth, creating layers of texture that were utterly satisfying. Eating it reminded me of why Japanese tuna is so prized, and it felt like I was tasting a level of quality that is very hard to find elsewhere. The experience of Kamatoro at Kuromon Market is one I’ll never forget, a true highlight of my time in Osaka for any seafood lover or sushi enthusiast

Impeccable service by Taka-san and the whole crew. One of the best tuna experiences we had during our trips to Osaka and Tokyo, with a tailored approach to how you’d like your tuna prepared (we opted for Kamatoro and Chutoro with rice). The Kama-toro cut was especially impressive, perfectly paired with their signature soy sauce. Would recommend it over Otoro! (Also, would recommend raw over aburi!)

Go early to avoid the crowds! We were there just before 9am!

Although it’s on the pricier side, the freshness of the sashimi, the quality of the food, and the attentive service make it absolutely worthwhile. Had seconds in as many days and will definitely be back the next time we’re in Osaka!

Food: by far the best tuna I’ve had. You can choose which cuts of the tuna you want and how you want the chef to prepare it. I opted for the sushi and sashimi preparation. Every bite tastes like heaven.
Service: polite and friendly. They also serve hot tea to keep the customers warm while seated outside during winter.
Atmosphere: Come early to avoid the crowd! Also be prepared to sit in the cold outside during winter. Not suitable for group dining and really, just eat and go.

name: Cafe ETC
reviews: My go-to cafe since 2022. Just a random cafe we passed by and decided to give a try. The price is so reasonable, which is cheaper than other cafes nearby. The latte only costs RM8, and it’s good. The taste more on the strong side, but it’s still good and consistent. My favourite definitely the waffles and latte. Carbonara also worth to give it a try. Portion wise, just nice. Plus point, they have lunch deals during weekdays. Weekend can be a bit crowded. So, please give it a try on this cafe!

Good foods here and the price kind of reasonable. Fast service however the waiter kind of busy and it took a while the waiter to notice us when we want to make our order. Notice that it happened to other customers as well. By the way their seafood udon is the bomb. So delicious! And i love their mocha. Definitely will come again

One of the best food I've ever had at a cafe. I highly recommend for other people to try as the menu is quite variant, range from English to Japanese foods. If there's anything I wish they could improve on, is the portion 😂. Oh, I had mushroom sandwich and salmon spaghetti, both are very good.

Also if you're coming, I suggest to come via MRT (Pasar Seni) as there's barely parking nearby and it's not that far from the MRT station.

name: Kobe Beef Steak Restaurant Mouriya Sannomiya
reviews:
Incredible experience and one of the best meals I’ve ever had. What made it so memorable was the amazing service and hospitality.

Keep in mind that they are serving Kobe Beef, so it is going to cost you, but it is truly worth it. Would recommend this to anyone that truly loves good quality meat and excellent service

The food was delicious! I got the coursed meal with the Kobe sirloin. It was almost too much food but it was so tasty so I made it work. The staff was attentive and our chef with amazing. He provided recommendations for the best way to enjoy each item.

Lovely place to go. Wanted to have a Kobe steak experience while here on holiday. Arrived early as it was a Saturday.

I went for the Kobe Rump 150g, you also get miso soup, salad,  accompaniments
and coffee included in the price, along with a chef whose skills are amazing.  He explained what dips and souce go with the steak.

All the staff were attentive and the restaurant was beautiful.

If you get the chance please go and enjoy the beautiful food and staff.

name: BAAN26
reviews:
Service was prompt and polite. Food was great especially the mango sticky rice. Little rice, full on sweet mango and thick coconut cream. Next favourite dish was the salted egg squid. Also love it that you can request the dishes to be made less spicy.
Just a note for those who wanted to bring small kids, they only have 1 highchair available.

A bit pricey for me but taste wise is not disappointing because all of the dishes i ordered tasted so good! One of the best restaurant for that authentic thai food experience.. major love for the tomyam!

Despite the location, were one only can expect have a good drinking places, we were suprised to have good thai food with plenty of choices, cosy, although little warm for spicy food but still very nice and authentic, will be back ☀️

name: Stellar Coffee
reviews:
Stellar Coffee is a solid stop if you’re around the Petaling Street area in Kuala Lumpur. Located inside REXKL, it’s easy to include in one trip while exploring Chinatown.
The space isn’t very big, but it’s cozy and comfortable. They have both indoor and outdoor seating, and the overall vibe feels relaxed and artsy, matching the creative atmosphere of REX KL.
I ordered the Mont Blanc, and it was genuinely good. The espresso was bold and clean, well-balanced with the milk, and not overly sweet. It’s not just aesthetically pleasing — the flavor actually delivers. If you’re into more serious, strong coffee, they also offer options that cater to that preference.
Overall, a proper coffee stop in KL, especially for those who appreciate quality and well-executed drinks.

Came here specifically because they have oat milk — and stayed because everything else was just as good.

Great coffee, smooth and well made, in a quirky little space that’s perfect to chill for a while. Relaxed vibe, cool setup, and a proper coffee feel rather than just another generic café.

And honestly… meet the cat 🐱 That alone is worth the visit.

Would happily come back.

Stellar Coffee

Tried their Economy Ice Black and Business Class Hot Black today. Not a coffee expert, but I could actually taste the flavour notes they described, so that’s a plus 👍

Personally, I still prefer my coffee darker and stronger, so this one feels a bit on the lighter side for me. But quality-wise, the coffee is well made and smooth.

Overall, still a nice coffee place to chill, especially if you enjoy lighter, more refined coffee profiles ☕️✨

name: Constant Gardener Coffee
street: Ground Floor, Penang Chinese Chamber Of Commerce Building, 9, Lebuh Light
reviews:
Came across this coffee shop, had a tasting set which i had to try!
Great atmosphere with old espresso machines and plants throughout.
Water available to grab, warm, cool or cold!

Espresso was smooth, bold with sour after taste.
Long black was softer on the sour but more flavourful.
Latte was sweet and nice, not as punchy after espresso 😋

Cakes looks lovely but really good if your looking for specialty coffee in George Town.

Great coffee, truly. So great that every single one of us ordered more than one cup. Unfortunately, that still wasn’t enough to earn us the basic right to sit in peace.

Despite being paying customers, we were repeatedly interrupted — first by the staff, then by the owner — like some kind of tag-team harassment routine, all because we had empty cups from another café on the table. Empty. Cups. Not drinks. Not trash. Just the crime of having existed elsewhere before.

Apparently, the real specialty here isn’t coffee, but obsessive table surveillance. I would’ve happily thrown the cups away, if Penang streets magically had trash bins every five meters. They don’t. Shocking, I know.

Instead of focusing on making customers feel welcome, the staff seemed far more invested in policing our table like it personally offended them. It honestly felt less like a café and more like a very caffeinated interrogation room.

If you enjoy good coffee served with passive-aggressive interruptions and an inexplicable hostility toward empty cups, this is the place for you. Otherwise, drink fast, sit stiff, and for the love of god — arrive with absolutely no evidence you’ve ever visited another café in your life.

Well at the end of the. The owner offered a paper bag to hide the illegal cups. Very creative. Nicely executed.

Constant Gardener Coffee in George Town is genuinely one of the finest coffee spots in Penang. Thoughtfully run by its owner, SK, the café reflects a deep commitment to quality and detail in everything they do.

They offer a wide and carefully curated range of coffee options, catering to both classic preferences and more exploratory palates. Every cup feels intentional and beautifully executed.

Their Winter White, in particular, was outstanding — easily one of the best beverages I’ve ever had. Balanced, nuanced, and memorable, it perfectly represents the café’s dedication to craft.

A must-visit for anyone serious about great coffee in Penang.

name: Sakana Japanese Dining
street: G11, Ground Floor, Petronas Twin Tower, Jln Ampang
reviews: A good Japanese restaurant, very conveniently located that you can sit outside where it was very quiet and not hot. In principle, a decent menu, everything was fresh, but for some reason the sushi was very small, no, it was tasty but small. They cook quickly, an interesting system of self-ordering. In general, it's good for 4 stars.

I genuinely don’t understand how this restaurant earned such high ratings, that’s the reason I decided to try it. The portions were shockingly small, and the sushi was clearly not fresh. It honestly tasted like cheap, frozen supermarket salmon. For the prices they charge, this was extremely disappointing and nowhere near worth it.

Now available at SAKANA, Suria KLCC 🔥

Big flavours in every bite 💖 that’s what this new menu is all about.

✨ What to try:
🔹 Fatty Tuna Handroll – melt-in-your-mouth luxury
🔹 Grilled Unagi Handroll – sweet, smoky perfection
🔹 Salmon Ikura Avocado – creamy + briny with a pop
🔹 Vegetable Handroll – light, fresh, and flavourful

🍜 Spicy Duck Ramen – rich broth, tender duck, slurp-worthy noodles

🍨 Dessert Parfaits:
🍧Matcha Red Bean (earthy + refined)
🍓Strawberry Vanilla (creamy + nostalgic)

🍹 Mocktails you'll love:
🍑Tropical Passionfruit Plum
🍋Yuzu Lemongrass

📍 Suria KLCC, G Floor

#SakanaKLCC #SmallBitesBigFlavour #JapaneseDiningKL #LuxuryEats

name: 甘發茶樓 Kam Fatt Restaurant
reviews:
Chanced upon this place as it was near our hotel. Went in and a chinese uncle (I assume was the boss) took our orders and kept rushing us, saying other tables are waiting and food will take long to serve. We did not even take a long time ordering, and apparently he says that to every table. In the end, the food came super fast (which was a plus point), but it contradicts what he was saying to customers. You should not rush customers to order just because another table is waiting to order.

Environment wise we went upstairs and it was air conditioned and cozy.

Food wise it was just average. The dried tossed noodles lack flavour. Fishball taste like supermarket type, but soup was tasty. Curry noodles was flavourful and cockles were fresh. Kaya toast was over toasted, kaya spread was thin, but overall still tasty.

Would return if I am at the area and the service is better. *The rest of the staffs were very friendly and efficient*

As we arrived early, one of the suggested place for breakfast was here.  This place is nice and clean with the food prep area outside of the cafe. We ordered some eggs and toasts. Coffee was ok but the toast was a little too burnt and crispy. I couldn't help but ordered a small portion  of the curry mee to try. Not bad. Very fragrant and the chicken was tender.  Didn't get to try the nasi lemak but looks good from the menu. Not too bad overall.

Food is delicious, service is fast. Lots of locals. I went @8am and within 5 minutes after ordering the food is on the table. People coming in constantly. The restaurant is always full.
Bumped into the owner and ordered the hidden menu item with help. Fresh fish soup with 2 kinds of noodles.
Servers are multi lingual. I can hear them speaking English, Chinese and Japanese

name: Pinchos Tapas Bar
reviews: Came to this tapas bar in changkat and it did not dissapoint ! The food was spectacular and the Vibe was upbeat and fun ! Tried a variety of tapas and it was so good from the meat platter with cheese to the gambas alio to the octopus with patato! Sangria here was refreshing and gets you in the mood for a fun time !

⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐
A fantastic tapas spot in the heart of KL — great food, atmosphere and service.

Absolutely loved our visit to Pinchos Tapas Bar. The moment you step inside, the place has that warm, lively Spanish energy — dim lighting, cosy seating and a really nice buzz without being too loud.

The food was excellent. Every dish was fresh, generous and full of flavour. The chorizo, prawns, patatas bravas and croquettes were standouts, and the salad was surprisingly delicious and well-balanced. Perfect to share and perfect with a glass of wine or sangria.

Service was friendly, fast and genuinely welcoming. Staff know the menu well, offer great recommendations and keep the evening flowing nicely.

It’s a great spot for a relaxed dinner, date night or catching up with friends. Pricing is reasonable for the quality, and the whole experience feels authentic and enjoyable.
If you love tapas or just want a fun, delicious night out in KL — highly recommend.

We truly enjoyed the food here on Valentine’s Day. My partner loves Spanish cuisine, and he especially enjoyed the anchovies. It was my first time trying them, and I absolutely loved the experience

We would definitely love to come again. Ayu and Htun served us, and we were so happy with their excellent hospitality. We felt very welcomed and really enjoyed the warm atmosphere throughout the evening.

To Ayu: Thank you so much for your wonderful service. I truly appreciate the care and attention you give to every customer I could see it throughout the dinner. Hope you have a wonderful day. Till we meet again 😊

name: Street Art - Brother & Sister on a Swing
reviews:
Exploring the street art around George Town is a great experience, but I strongly recommend searching by the artwork names to avoid getting exhausted. For example, look for famous ones like “Brother and Sister on a Swing” and “Little Children on a Bicycle.”

If you just walk around randomly trying to find them, you can easily get lost and completely drained, especially in the heat. The weather is very hot and humid, and if you’re not used to it, it can really wear you out and even make you feel sick or close to heat exhaustion.

Plan your route, save the artwork locations, and go prepared with water and sun protection. The art is worth seeing just be smart about how you do it.
We enjoyed ourselves amongst all these wall paintings. We had souch fun as jou can gather from our pictures.

A Must-See Street Art in George Town 🎨

The “Brother & Sister on a Swing” street art is one of the most charming murals in Penang. It beautifully captures a simple childhood moment and brings a nostalgic, joyful feeling when you see it in person.

What makes it special is how it blends perfectly with the old heritage buildings around it. It feels lively yet authentic to the character of George Town. It’s also interactive — you can pose as if you’re part of the swing, which makes it a fun photo spot.

It may be simple, but it’s definitely one of the iconic pieces that adds personality to Penang’s street art scene. Worth stopping by if you’re exploring the area.

name: Da Bao Restobar
reviews:
One of my favorite restaurants in KL.
I’ve never had bao this good before. The concept of the restaurant is really cool, and the whole vibe makes the experience even better.
The bao are big and super tasty honestly, one is already enough to make you full. I highly recommend trying the pork bao, it’s my favorite.
The service is kind and friendly. I’ve already been back twice and will definitely return again

Visited Dabao Restaurant in Chinatown and really enjoyed the overall vibe. It’s a relaxed place to chill, especially if you’re having drinks with friends.

We had some drinks and ordered the Spicy Fried Chicken Mantou. The fried chicken was very crispy, fried just right without being oily or overdone. The chilli was very flavourful and quite spicy, which paired really well with the chicken and added a strong kick.

The mantou itself was soft and fluffy, making a great contrast with the crispy chicken. The combination worked surprisingly well and was very satisfying.

Downstairs is the main restaurant area, designed in a modern and stylish way with Chinese elements, making it comfortable for dining while still feeling trendy.
Upstairs, there is a bar counter and cocktail bar, with a more Western-style, chill atmosphere that’s perfect for relaxing and having drinks.

They offer a wide selection of cocktails, with over 30 house-crafted cocktails to choose from, which makes it a great spot for cocktail lovers. The upstairs bar feels laid-back and cosy, ideal for hanging out with friends after dinner.

Food is average here. Mantau could be softer. Steamed it maybe a little longer? The filling could be more tasty.
The taiwanese fried chicken rice was not to my liking. Chicken not well marinated enough. The inner meat was tasteless, bland. The sesame oil sauce was too strong. Mixed with pickled vegetables, edamame, and broccoli, it just didn't blend well to my liking.
The stuffed boneless chicken wings were a little overly priced. Just 2 wings stuffed with, I still could not make out what was it? A little like fish ball like texture, and certain part tasted like pork fat?

name: Chinatown Hostel by Mingle - Rooftop Private Jacuzzi with Bar
reviews: Very noisy. I was given the room directly next to the balcony overlooking the street. It was extremely noisy all night and my room shook when people went onto the balcony, opening the door. I could deal with the noise but the door being opened jolted me awake. Very poor quality sleep. Room was small but good for the price. If you book here, bring ear plugs.

A really brilliant hostel! The staff are super friendly and helpful when answering any questions. They have 24 hour reception and are always keen to find a solution to any problem. The rooms are clean and the beds are comfortable. Also have fantastic showers with plenty of hot water and good pressure! There are also multiple places to hang out and therefore the hostel is very social and encourages people to have a great time with others. My favourite hostel in KL!

Amazing hostel with the best & friendliest staff! Perfect location in chinatown near tons of restaurants. Very social with events going on every single day, the pub crawl was my favorite and only cost 10 Ringgit. Jacuzzi had a nice view but was kinda dirty- still sat in it most days though lol. Rooms were average for a hostel, very tight quarters. The only reason i’m rating it 4 stars instead of 5 is because of the bathroom situation. While there were several shared toilets and showers that were cleaned daily, there are only TWO sinks for the entire hostel which was a struggle. I found myself waiting in line to brush my teeth several times.

name: Ziyafat Restaurant
street: No.22 & 24, Ground Floor, Jln Bukit Bintang
reviews:
Came here to accompany a friend for dinner. She have eaten there couple of times and she likes it. I've never had a buffet style Pakistani food, thus it was interesting.

We took some kebabs and a piece of meat with a small bowl of dhal, one naan and two mango lassi. I just tasted two bites of naan with the dhal and small chunk of kebab, it was okay. I rather have a freshly cooked, hot from kitchen kinda food, but oh well, I wasn't hungry.

I think I prefer other Pakistani restaurant. It kinda feels like cafeteria with restaurant price. And my friend had to pay RM 40 for all that, minus my drink which I paid it myself.

Well maintain restaurant in heart of the city, food taste it good, self service, we were craving for some masala spicy food, the restaurant did not disappoint us..
You can get a wide spread of dishes, many options to explore chicken, lamb and vegetarians can get a quite handful of options..
Tried a lot of their food which was good ,satisfied while leaving the restaurant..
But every dish contents a lot of oil, which was a bit let down..but definitely worth the money we spent .

Self service, they will pay after you eat.
No worries, not a high charge, very reasonable compared to other area.
A lot of meat item available.
Pakistani restaurants are good.
You must try if you are not a vegetarians.
By the way, they serves nice asian milk tea.

name: Penang Street Art - Kids on bicycle by Ernest Zacharevic
reviews: An iconic mural in Penang. recently restored by the artist. It still has its charm, and it is a great photo spot! Zacharevic's Little Children on Bicycle Mural - The restored version is said to be slightly more detailed than the original

We walked on the street of many shops and tried to find the wall art. It then suddenly started pouring with rain so we nearly missed the art. We only found the "boy on the chair" and bit away from here and the bike one. It would be great to walk around when you have time to see others. Great area!
Penang street art started soon after George Town was designated a Unesco World Heritage Site. Its beautiful and showcasing of intricate art and rich cultural heritage.

name: Gurney Bay Park
reviews: Gurney Bay Park is a lovely spot to unwind and enjoy the sea breeze in Penang. The park is clean, well maintained, and has wide walking paths that are perfect for a stroll or a jog. I enjoyed the open green spaces and the views of the coastline—it’s especially beautiful during sunset when the sky reflects on the water. There are also benches and shaded areas where you can sit and relax while watching families, joggers, and people just enjoying the outdoors. It’s a peaceful escape from the busy city streets, and a perfect place to take a break, have a picnic, or simply enjoy the coastal scenery.

This is one of my favorite place to enjoy my early morning walks. It is safe, bright, and the walking paths are well maintained. It offers a great environment.  The breaking of dawn is very soothing. I love this place.

well organised and spacious spot for morning/evening walk. Such a nice place to bring family here and unwind. It’s clean and only open for pedestrians & bicycles so it’s quite safe to jog here. It’s also a good sunrise spot + perfect seaview.

name: Kuromon Sushi
reviews: We would 1000% recommend this place, Amy (her nickname) who is the chef there went above and beyond for us. She came over to deliver the food herself to the table, explaining the various dishes! All the fish was incredibly fresh, we had some of the best sashimi and tempura in Osaka. Thank you for making our time in the city so special 🧡

Absolutely delicious sushi, sashimi, tempura and the best oyster we’ve eaten on our trip to Japan! Highly recommend. Clean, welcoming and great friendly service. The menu is huge so plenty of choice for all tastes, including vegetable choices. The price seems really reasonable so happy all round 👍🏻✌🏻

Very friendly and welcoming staff. The brightly lit restaurant is also attractive and inviting. Fish was good, however not as good a selection of nigiri/sashimi as the restaurant across the street, seemed to be a bigger focus on bowls + prepared dishes.

name: Arabella Restaurant
reviews: Food is actually quite alright. The place was empty during my early lunch the staff were polite, could have moved a little faster but alright. Advice: pick a table away from one of the electric fly zappers high on the walls otherwise all you will get is the very regular occurrence of flies meeting an electrifying death !

Wow, I have never eaten food this good! The Ceasar salad is like nothing I have ever tasted! I cannot eat it all, but I want too!
I am in KL for 4 days,and I already want some more!
Amazing Middle Eastern cuisine. The staff are friendly and the prices are reasonable. I love that you can smoke shisha inside the restaurant. Highly recommend a visit.

name: La Chica Mexican Grill • Changkat Bukit Bintang
reviews:
What a cracker place.

Food was amazing, service top notch. Music and vibe was amazing for a Friday night.

Kids were stuffed which with older teenagers can sometimes be challenging.

Price was cheap compared to Oz. Essentially 5 margaritas for $30 we had a great night.

Must do if you’re nearby and wanting a fantastic night.

A little taste of Mexico in the heart of Kuala Lumpur. The staff are very friendly , and they understand English and serve with splendour 😊enjoyed the margaritas and tacos, and if you sit outside you get to enjoy the views and check people out.You can also play snooker, pool downstairs if you wanna chill drink and do an activity.I highly recommend if you are on Holiday.

Food - best quote suites for this restaurant "No one can eat just one". Serves one of the best Mexican food with authentic flavors.

Place- nice and comfortable. Interesting atmosphere overall adds to the comfort

Price - value for money.

Team- Super friendly team and recommends you one of their best cuisines and drinks. I was served by  Raghu. He recommended good drinks to us. I am pasting his photo here.

Drinks- long island ice tea and their tequila shots has made my evening.

name: Kobe Beef KISSHOKICHI Sannomiya Store
street: Sannomiyacho, 1 Chome−9−1 センタープラザ Ｂ1階
reviews:
Absolutely incredible experience. This was hands down the best food I’ve ever had. The Kobe beef was unbelievably tender, perfectly cooked, and melted in my mouth with every bite. The marbling was beautiful and the flavor was rich without being overpowering — just pure perfection.
The staff was welcoming and attentive, and you could tell they take real pride in the quality of their beef. The presentation was elegant, and the whole meal felt special from start to finish.
If you’re in Kobe and want an unforgettable meal, this is the place. Worth every yen — I would come back in a heartbeat.

We found this restaurant by chance, and it did not disappoint at all. The ambience was cozy, even though the restaurant is small.

The service was excellent! The chef, Mr. Kawasaki, was very friendly and made us enjoy our lunch even more. The food was delicious and reasonably priced.

We will definitely come back again someday!
Excellent cuts of Kobe beef at affordable prices. Everyone was so friendly and accommodating. The beef was so tasty and cooked just right. I just wish there was more rice haha!

name: Indigo Restaurant • The Blue Mansion
street: Cheong Fatt Tze Mansion, 14, Lebuh Leith
reviews:
The Blue Mansion has a rich history, and I highly recommend starting with the guided tour before dinner, as it adds valuable context and enhances the overall experience. Customer service was exceptional—one particular staff member who recently joined truly stood out and made my partner and I feel genuinely welcomed, though I regret not catching his name.

The food, however, was average overall, with the wagyu short ribs being the only standout dish. A major downside was the reservation system. Despite having a 5:00 PM booking, the restaurant did not open until 6:30 PM, resulting in a long and unnecessary wait. I strongly suggest calling ahead to confirm timings.

Positives
•	Excellent customer service
•	Informative guided tour
•	Wagyu short ribs

Negatives
•	Poor reservation system
•	Average food

What a fantastic lunch we had at Indigo. All the 5 dishes were delicious and beautifully presented. The service was caring and impeccable. I highly recommend this lunch on your trip to Penang. It surpassed our expectations. Thank you to the manager for allowing us to have a late lunch that day. We really appreciated it.

We had the pleasure of dining at this restaurant on New Year’s Eve, 31 December 2025, and it was an exceptional evening from start to finish. The food, ambience, and the staff’s attentiveness and excellent service all contributed to a truly memorable experience.
Live evening entertainment was provided throughout the night, adding warmth and an inviting sense of occasion to the atmosphere. We felt genuinely welcomed and valued as guests.
Every dish was beautifully executed; however, the standout for us was the Wagyu char siu, which was simply exquisite. A wonderful way to welcome the New Year.

name: Bukit Bintang Food street
reviews: Bukit Bintang Food Street... there's no point in writing about it; you have to see it, walk through it, and try everything they serve. Everything is prepared right before your eyes, it looks beautiful... and tastes delicious... and that unique atmosphere. Wow.

Bukit Bintang Food Street is chaotic in all the ways that make street food exciting — loud, crowded, a bit messy, and packed with energy. It’s one of the best places to sample a mix of local flavours, with Thai stalls, Chinese kitchens, seafood grills, barbecue spots, and plenty of beer options lining both sides. The night view is easily the highlight; the lights, steam, and constant movement give the whole place a vibrant atmosphere that makes the food taste even better.

You’ll deal with some traffic, some waiting, and a bit of confusion, but that’s normal here and part of the charm. And once you cross to the other side of the street, you’ll notice it’s filled with massage parlours, giving the area a totally different vibe from the food-heavy side. Overall, it’s a must-visit if you want an authentic late-night KL food experience with plenty to explore.

Bukit Bintang Food Street is a nice place to visit if you enjoy exploring different food options in one area. There are many food stalls offering a mix of local and international dishes, making it easy to find something you like. The atmosphere is lively, especially at night, and the location is very convenient. However, some parts of the street can be a bit dirty, especially during busy hours. Overall, it’s still a fun spot to walk around, eat, and enjoy the Bukit Bintang vibe.

name: Pacific Restaurant & Bar
reviews: Great experience, quick service, friendly staff, and an amazing live band that kept the energy high. They even sang a song for us — fun and memorable hospitality. Definitely worth a visit! 🍻🎶
This was a nice place to start the night.  Food is good and the staff is friendly.  It is also a good place the listen to some live music and have a cold beer.  Cheers.
Good corner pub with good ambience and great food! Live music starts in the evening. Very nice place to chill.

name: Murni Discovery Bukit Bintang
reviews: Big portion, great taste, worth it. My brother and I ordered 3 foods and we were stuffed! All of the foods were served in just a short while and they are tasty. Thier prawn fried rice were full of prawns (not gigantic but big enough and I get to enjoy almost every scoop with a prawn in it) and they are well balanced, fish and chips were great, spaghetti was cooked to al dente and the sauce was just nice, grilled chickens were juicy except black pepper sauce (I'm not a fan of black pepper sauce). Maybe you can add the option for mushroon or oriental sauce in the future? Just a suggestion. For the price we paid and the portion of food they serve, totally worth our money. Will revisit this place in the futute 👍😋

I had such a fantastic time here that I’ve become a regular! The food is always good. Every time I visit, I notice new updates like a new TV and lights, which really shows that the owner is proud and invested in making it even better. I can feel that as a customer and as a business owner.

A huge thank you to Rakibul Hassan! You’ve been amazing, and every time I come back, you greet us with a sincere smile and a warm welcome. It makes us want to come back again and again!

Came with family and ordered few spaghetti (one with Salmon) and nasi goreng with butter chicken. They served cendul complete with red beans, cincau and corn. Overall the food was good. They should make the atmosphere more cozy.

name: BELLA BOCCA Namba
reviews:
Farm to Table - this quite uncommon here in Osaka so it’s good to see Bella Bocca open their second branch in Osaka.  They have their own farm and here, we have an opportunity to have a large variety of fresh vegetables in a very delicious way.  It easy to see and taste the love and dedicated that goes into the vegetables as well as their preparation. The salad bar alone is worth the visit - they also have a variety of condiments and dressings to make your salad to your tastes.
Their menu is not for vegetarians but the staff was quick to accommodate my dietary needs.  Unfortunately, the chef failed to add a bit more oil, salt, and pepper to the dish to make up for the missing flavors that the meatless dish would produce.  I just used the condiments from the salad bar to make my dish the way I wanted -  it it would’ve been nice if the chef had handled it. It may be that not enough vegetarians come here and the chef isn’t used to making dishes without the meat.
The meal was topped off with their home made tiramisu which seems to be what they are famous for.
This restaurant is already crowded and the locals know it well, but we need more farm to table restaurants and I hope more people come to this place not only to enjoy a great meal, but also to show entrepreneurs that this model can be successful.  I will definitely be back again and will put this into my list of regular restaurant to visits.

I came with my friend who’s a vegetarian and we loved that the menu was able to accommodate both of us fantastically! My friend loved the extra creaminess that the potato gave to her cream pasta and i loved the depth of flavour packed into the chicken confit, which looked otherwise unassuming. Plus points for the salad buffet, which comes FOC with your order of a main. Not sure if it applies for dinner. Was also served by a really cute and friendly wait staff! Would highly recommend!!

Stumbled across this place while looking for pizza for my toddler on a hot day. Another restaurant just a couple of meters away told us to wait outside in the hot sun so we left and decided to try out this place. The young lady server was so welcoming.. she even helped my wife negotiate the pram up and down the small step leading into and later out from the restaurant (I had my hands busy with another kid). Food was really great - locally sourced and environment was very conducive. But the service is what really made the day for us. Highly recommended and we will be back if in the area again!

name: Bintang Walk
reviews: one of most happening area in kl. have middle east, chinese pull noodle here, also street artist performance art. but beware, always have ukat parking even after midnight. and beware of pickpocket here.

Bukit Bintang is one of well known districts in Kuala Lumpur with a couple of shopping malls and a multitude of restaurants. I saw a lot of Chinese tourists making different kinds of poses in front of the intersection which I find it rather interesting.
Effective road crossing. Full of tourist and non Malaysian on weekend nights. Truly a hotspot of Malaysia. Many basking performances over the area too.

name: Kapitan Bangsar
reviews:
Great service despite walk-in requesting for a table for 10!
The friendly staff reorganized some seats for us.

Food came hot and not a very long wait.
We ordered Garlic Nann (it’s quite big for one- so I shared so I can get others and Briyani)
Drinks we order are a variation- teh Tarik, Mango lasi, KopiO, ice lemon tea etc

So Happened almost all the dishes we ordered looked and tasted similar 🤭
Tandoori chicken was great
We ordered Mutton Briyani - The rice is tasty but the Mutton is like lamb chops, not cooked with the rice and very tough.
The rest of the food like butter chicken, vegetables and other curried dishes are pretty ok ◡̈
I don’t mind coming again but will
Check other dishes, not similar
(Maybe the surface could suggest or remind us)

My comfort food, everytime I visit KL I would either dine in or order online. My go to meal is chicken briyani and it never disappoints!!!!❤️ Taste always been consistent and the tandoori my lordddd😩 100/10

Nice indian cuisine. Verdict: bit salty
And also paneer not soft. Very tough and hard.bpapadam is chargeable .

name: Pucks Coffee
street: Back Portion, 180, Jalan Tun H S Lee
reviews:
This is a trendy cafe down in the Chinatown area in Kuala Lumpur.

This is a modern cafe for the local and younger crowd.

They have a nice variety of baked goods.
Loved the lemon and blueberry loaf.
The Latte looked amazing. But too much milk and it was barley warm. Disappointing 😞
But this place is a vibe with that free wifi.
You have to be a people's person.  You could end up at a table with several different individuals.  Cool.
I would go back again. Definitely.

The atmosphere is great here, especially when it is so very spacious compared with others I have visited in my 4 days in KL. The slice of cake I had was tasty and a nice little break from all the walking. I had a nice chat with a young KL local who knows Pucks Coffee rather well to know that there are two more outlets.

Dropped by Pucks Coffee, KL & had an unexpectedly great experience thanks to Ange

Super friendly, attentive & genuinely warm, the type of service that actually makes your drink taste better lol. She checks in without being intrusive, rmbs small details & makes the whole place feel a lot more welcoming

If you're coming here for your caffeine fix, hope you get served by her. Solid customer service 😉

name: The Daily Dose Cafe Penang
reviews: Hands down the best latte coffee (hot) in Georgetown so far! In fact I ended up ordering a second ! We stayed for breakfast and can throughly recommend. Lots of great food options, super fresh and great vibe. Thank you team! We will be back.  (Also great fun watching the dog pets visit in buggies and various dress for Chinese New Year -  it’s a pet friendly cafe …but scrupulously clean btw)

A cozy and pet-friendly café set in a charming heritage building. The atmosphere is relaxed and perfect for casual hangouts. The staff are exceptionally friendly and attentive, especially towards furkids — their genuine love for animals truly stands out. The café offers a wide variety of Western and Asian dishes, paired with fragrant, good-quality coffee, and even provides pet food, which is a lovely bonus. Although parking can be a bit challenging, the overall experience is excellent and strongly recommended, especially for pet lovers.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ 5/5

We absolutely loved our meal here! We ordered the Little Big Breakfast, the Spicy Prawn Pasta, and the Yogurt Bowl and everything was seriously so, so good! The flavours were amazing and the portions were just right.

What made the experience even better is that they’re dog friendly. They even serve proper food for dogs! My puppy finished his entire salmon bowl and mind you, he’s a very picky eater. Seeing him enjoy his meal so much made our day.

Highly recommended for both humans and furkids! Will definitely be back! 🐾💛

name: Kyoto Katsu • Suria KLCC
street: Lot 418, Level 4, Petronas Twin Tower, Persiaran Petronas
reviews:
What I liked about it : The food taste nice. They also give condiments.
: It is design simple but nice.

What can be improved : The prices are a bit on the higher side, gjven the order size.
: Some crew members did not pay attention at times. If was not crowded when we came, but there were times that we needed to call multiple times before they came to us.

Total expense was RM 205 for 2 pax

Surprisingly, enjoyed the katsu here, after trying out other places.

Had the chicken katsu and seafood katsu (fish & prawns). Loved the seafood katsu, especially the fish. They are also generous with their refills for the cabbage.

Staff are friendly and attentive, but it can get busy so it can get a little difficult to catch their attention at times.

Would most likely come back here again if i'm around and up for some katsu.

The food we had was enjoyable. The Katsu had a light crisp coating and hamburger steak was tender and tasty. We were disappointed when we were told the Garlic Shoyu & Nagoya Miso Sauce options were not available for the hamburger as this is what I wanted after having tried it in Tokyo. I don't think tartare is the right condiment to have with hamburger steak. I also could not order the Nagoya Miso Chicken Katso as that was not available. I thought the chefs cooked everything fresh, so perhaps thought that these sauces are preprepared and they simply ran out? I had the chicken katsu curry instead. However we returned a few nights later to try again, because the hamburger steak is what we wanted most and then we're told again it is not available with the sauces I previously mentioned. If this is permanently unavailable then why is it on the menu? We walked out on our second visit and you lost our business for this.

name: Night Market Bukit Bintang, KL
reviews: Definitely worth a walk through at least. Spectacular range of stalls. Ample dine in seating. Felt very safe and festive.

In my opinion it is a must see in Kuala Lumpur. A place full of cultures and flavours with very special atmosphere of a traditional market. Bring cash to pay, they don’t accept cards. Prices are fine - you can get a snack for 5-10 RIN and a dish for 20-30 RIN. Everything we tried was very tasty 👌 There is a durian fruit too 😊

A must visit place with a wide variety of food choices. It can get very crowded, so if you’re not comfortable being surrounded by hundreds of people, you may want to avoid peak times. Prices are reasonable.

name: Kolam Biru
street: River of Life, Jalan Tun Perak
reviews:
A convergence point of the Klang River and the Gombak River.
Next to Majid Jamek Sultan Abdul Samad (MRT/LRT station).
Beautiful when blue light is on starting from evening. Additional fog effect is about every 15 minutes till 10pm.
Come early a bit before 9pm for optimal effect at night.

It’s now merge point between 2 Rivers’s   Original a tin mine were it all started in KL u can see a lot of smoke ( manufactured not real ) coming near the water wall edges the reason is to cover the bad smell of the water as it has alot of minerals

Impressive everything thing is getting a new touch. One big round to walk around an awsome walking place. I started from central market parking which is flat RM10 after 5pm.
The Birthplace of KL: This specific point is where early tin miners first landed in the mid-19th century to open mines in Ampang. It is widely considered the birthplace of the city.

​Masjid Jamek: In 1909, the Masjid Jamek Sultan Abdul Samad was built right on this confluence, cementing the site's importance to the city's culture and religion.

Today, it serves as a scenic waterfront park where people gather to watch the fountain shows and see the mist effects against the backdrop of the historic mosque and the modern city skyline.

name: Hinode
reviews: If you like “clams”, then this is the spot & it’s worth the journey. Historic restaurant that’s been around for over 100 years. All local clams, hand picked by the owner. Very entertaining and traditional…you’ll need to speak basic Japanese.
Ryotei style restaurant specialized in local "Hamaguri" clam dishes.

母娘で夢にまでみた 創業100年になる老舗料亭の蛤料理「日の出」さんへ 春頃に電話し予約日が12月19日 とやっとその日が参りまして、やっと来店できました。

待った甲斐が有りました。こんなにアツアツぷりぷりの桑名蛤から出る自然の旨味でこんなに美味しすぎる蛤は食べないと言いあらわせないうえ、親切にご案内、ご説明くださり感激しました。

今回は蛤懐石にしました。お造りや はまぐり鍋（しゃぶしゃぶ）、焼蛤、磯辺揚げ（海苔巻天ぷら）、蛤バター焼など
はまぐり鍋は蛤のしゃぶしゃぶ1人5個ずつ鍋の蛤を食べられました。
日の出の「はまぐり鍋」は、漫画『美味しんぼ』に登場したことでも知られる名物なだけあり
また食べに来たい。こんなに頭に残る美味しさは
また必ず旬の5月6月に来てみたいです。

予約するなら11月に電話しなければいけないとの。来年頑張ります☺️👍

name: Moontree House
reviews: Lovely independent bookstore/cafe with a calm and peaceful atmosphere. Perfect if you want a place to read and relax with a good cuppa. The book selection is eclectic, with various titles on social issues/feminism/gender studies in both Chinese and English. Remember to take your shoes off at the door, and ask for permission before taking photos :)

It is so quiet and clean that I could feel enjoyable and a little bit stressful at the same time. I am a little bit stressed since I should behave well here by not making noise. After getting to used to it, I could stay resting for a while myself. This place could be good for being focused in studying, reading or contemplating.
