Books are priced reasonably. So happy to find qiu miaojin books n I bought one ❤️ Nice n peaceful atmosphere. The charm is in its humble and cozy decorations, simple yet comforting choice of food and beverage, the LGBTQ and feminist literature books (albeit most of them are in mandarin), little handmade trinkets from local artists. A cute little place to unwind in the midst of chaos of kl china town. Would love to visit again.

name: Mikoto Sakae Station Store
reviews: The best charcoal edamame that I've ever had! Everything else from the set menu was also great, especially the charcoal chicken. Friendly staff, upbeat and welcoming atmosphere, and pristine washroom. Reservations are highly recommended (via Tabelog), as they had to keep turning people away.

Initially, our experience at the yakitori restaurant was confusing. No staff explained the ordering process when we were seated, leaving us puzzled. After some searching, we found pamphlets on the table that clarified how to place our order. We also discovered utensils tucked away in the table drawers on our own. Despite the rocky start, the food was a revelation. When our dishes arrived, they were exceptional—some of the best yakitori we’ve ever tasted in Japan, making the visit truly memorable.
Best Tori ramen in Nagoya. Rich flavour but not salty at all! How amazing. The Tori is so tasty. Can’t wait to visit this place again! Thank you for the yummy food.

name: Jojoen Nagoya Sakae
street: Sakae, 3 Chome−3−1 マルエイガレリア 3階
reviews:
Made reservations a few months ahead, this was the pattern if you would like to visit Jojoen Restaurants, no matter in which area of Japan, and especially for those with superb views.
We ordered : Yakiniku Lunch Set(Mix) ￥4,000, and Yakiniku Lunch Set(Ginmi) ￥6,500
Quality of food was good as usual.  Service was attentive.
Overall environment of the restaurant was clean and comfortable.
Recommended!
We have 2 lunch special set. One is 3000 yen and the other is 4000 yen. I prefer the 4000 yen one as it tastes better.

Jojoen has always been in my top 2 for à la carte yakiniku, but today I tried their lunch set—and it’s such great value for money! While the beef quality in the lunch set isn’t as premium as the à la carte options, it’s still well above the average yakiniku standard. Plus, their service is exceptional, and they even offer an English menu!

name: Rumah Penghulu Abu Seman (The Penghulu Abu Seman House)
reviews:
Our visit to Rumah Penghulu Abu Samen in Kuala Lumpur was entirely unplanned, yet it turned out to be one of the highlights of our trip. We thoroughly enjoyed the experience, especially the exceptional guided tour, which brought the house and its history vividly to life.

The visit offered a rare and insightful glimpse into how prominent and respected figures lived in the region in earlier times. What impressed me most was not only the richness of the culture—shaped by the house’s role as a hub for cross-cultural exchange—but also the thoughtful way in which lifestyle and architecture were adapted to the local environment.

Architectural details such as the squared columns, the modular kitchen, and the well-designed ventilation system clearly reflected both practicality and sophistication. Overall, it was an engaging and highly rewarding visit that I would strongly recommend.

Visiting this place is a unique and one-of-a-kind experience in the centre of KL, especially if you’re into culture, architecture, and history. Make sure you go for the guided tour at 11am or 3pm. I got a lovely and funny tour by Jasmine and I couldn’t recommend it enough.

I wish there were more accessible and well-maintained historical sites like this in KL (instead of new malls 😭). Entrance + guided tour can be bought in person (RM10 for Msian/RM20 non-Msian). The guided tour also includes a 20 min video on how the house was relocated to KL. The tour itself was an extremely informative walk through of the site and the tour guides were really friendly. The house is a very well-thought out showcase of Malay culture and History. I highly recommend including this in your itinerary when visiting KL!

name: まえなか
reviews: A small place with tasty food. Sushi were good and udon noodles as well. The egg in the noodles was super sweet. There is a free tea that actually was really good. For the price this is really good option to grab some food. Can order a set with noodles and sushi or just sushi. There are different types of sushi to choose. For noodles can choose udon and soba. Service is nice. The place is ok. Can pay only by cash and Pay Pay.

Sushi was so nice with an affordable price.
Staffs were also super lovely and kind.
Great local restaurant right next to arima onsen station.

We preferred cold soba over hot udon.

While many places focus on sleek, modern aesthetics, I stumbled upon a quaint and charming little spot in Arima that truly warmed my heart. I was surprised to find we were the only table there for over an hour — it definitely deserves more love.

For just 1,000 yen, you can get a satisfying meal: a comforting bowl of warm udon or refreshing cold soba noodles, plus some fresh sushi - 5 pieces. Even better, they have Asahi on tap — a rare treat at a place this cozy and affordable.

What made the experience even more special was the all-ladies staff. They were so kind and attentive — I genuinely wished I could tip them! Please consider supporting small local businesses like this one. It’s these hidden gems that truly make travel memorable. I hope this review helps others discover this special place. 💛

name: Tamadono Fountain
reviews: Actually i went to the alphine route...and here the murodo ice wall...very nice place to visit...and i just walk to the fountain...to see the fresh mountain spring water...

The clear and delicious water flows from mountain. You can drink the water and can also use a container to take some away. Moreover, seems tthat there's no regulation how to drink (unlike that in a Shrine).
Natural view in early May. Watch out the steps. It's slippery.

name: Mano Plus GMBB
street: GMBB, Unit GM-G-01 at, 2, Jalan Robertson
reviews: Great place for craft & hobbiest. Creative Community Mall of 10 floors of excitement. Each floor is  a different uniques experiences. Exploring arts, culture & heritage.

love this store and the building. though abit too quiet n empty.

what I love:
- many hidden gems. from traditional Malaysian culture products w modern-international taste, local & international curated products
- one stop shopping.
- affordable price but no need to bargain
- they even carry Freitag, Zurich based brand that make a bag & acc from used-circular materials.

what I hope it can be polished
- better visual merchandising, to make it look better and appealing
- better access for tourists. mrt/train.

A very interesting mall. If you are into arts (mainly local artist)，do pay a visit. Check if they have events, it will make it more worthwhile to visit. Still a very new mall with such concept, so do expect some shops are still vacant or under renovation.

name: genpei 食の蔵・おばんざい家-げんぺい-
reviews: Delicious, and the staff were very friendly.  The kids udon was very tasty and the ice-cream was the best we have tasted.  The chicken and fish had a great flavour, we look forward to coming back.
Delicious
三重県にある「げんぺい」は、体にやさしいおばんざいが楽しめる素敵なお店。一品一品が丁寧に作られていて、どれもホッとする味わいでした。メインはもちろん、小鉢や副菜まで手抜きなしで、ご飯が進みます。落ち着いた雰囲気で居心地も良く、つい長居したくなる空間。おばんざい、まさにバンザイなお店です。

name: Kobe Steak Kizuna
reviews:
Visiting Kobe Beef Steak Restaurant Kizuna Sannomiya Station was a delightful accident. I stumbled upon this restaurant while browsing Google Maps, and what a fortunate find it turned out to be! The moment I stepped inside, I was struck by the serene and pristine atmosphere. The restaurant was impeccably clean, creating a calm and inviting dining environment.
The staff were exceptional—warm, attentive, and genuinely kind. Their service was thoughtful and gentle, making us feel welcomed from start to finish. The chef, in particular, stood out for his dedication and professionalism while preparing our teppanyaki. He was focused yet approachable, taking the time to patiently explain each ingredient with care and enthusiasm, which added a special touch to the experience.
The food itself was a testament to the chef’s skill, with every dish cooked to perfection right before our eyes. What truly left an impression, however, was the heartfelt farewell. As we left, both the chef and staff escorted us to the door and waved us off until we were out of sight—a gesture that was incredibly touching and rare.
I’m so grateful for this unforgettable dining experience and the warmth of the Kizuna team. I wholeheartedly wish their restaurant continued success and a steady stream of happy customers. Highly recommended!

This is by far the most expensive restaurant that we've been to since we arrived in Japan, but also the best food we've ever had.

Everything we had along the course meal was perfectly handled by the master.

We enjoyed the dinner, thank you so much. 😊
Best kobe beef restaurant. Chef is friendly and nice . Food is superb. Highly recommended. We ordered a set lunch . Come with salad , appetizer rice , miso soup and Japanese tea.

name: Esplanade Sea Wall Heritage Trail
street: Kompleks Makanan Medan Renong Padang Kota Lama, 11, Jalan Tun Syed Sheh Barakbah
reviews: I walked along the Esplanade Sea Wall Heritage Trail during my visit to Penang, and it was a pleasant and relaxing experience. The trail runs along the waterfront near George Town and offers nice views of the sea, making it ideal for a slow walk. Informational panels along the route explain the history of the sea wall and the area’s role in protecting the city, which adds educational value. While the trail itself is simple, many people will appreciate its calm atmosphere, coastal breeze, and historical context. It is a good stop between major attractions rather than a main destination.

The Penang Esplanade is a lively and scenic spot right by the water, perfect for a stroll or to just relax and enjoy the view. The open space is great for taking photos, watching locals go about their day, or catching a cool breeze while exploring George Town.

You can see historical buildings nearby, which adds a nice mix of heritage and nature to the area. There are also benches and shaded spots if you want to sit and take it all in. It’s especially beautiful in the late afternoon when the sun starts to set, creating a peaceful and picturesque atmosphere.

The Esplanade is a must-visit if you want a relaxing break while seeing some of Penang’s history and waterfront charm in one place.

Beautiful and peaceful place by the sea! The Esplanade Sea Wall Heritage Trail is great for a relaxing walk with a nice sea breeze and scenic views. You can enjoy the heritage vibe, watch the waves, and see nearby landmarks like Fort Cornwallis and City Hall. It’s clean, well-maintained, and has spots to sit and enjoy the view — perfect for an evening stroll or peaceful time by the water

name: 黒部平パノラマテラス
reviews: My favorite stop in the Tateyama Kurobe because of the view.
One of the best view of the whole route
view while going up

name: At Nagoya Monument Oasis 21
reviews: One of Nagoyas main attraction. Beautiful at night.
Very beautiful, especially at sunset.
I took photo in Nagoya lettering here! No queue at all 😆 and the iconic building and tower as a background!

name: George Town World Heritage Incorporated (GTWHI)
reviews: Iconic building. Should take a photo here
George town world heritage.
Historical landmarks everywhere in this area... Must visit... So many events during Georgetown Festival in July n August...

name: Penang Heritage Trust
reviews: Very interesting place. Excellent free guided tour.
Thanks for the hospitality and introduction about Penang. So great and wonderful!!
A great place to find unknown info on the history of Penang. Book a tour with them and you will cover a full morning of history seeing George town, pier, the fort and the church's.

name: Teppan-yaki Kokoro
street: Hatobacho, 7−2 ホテルラ・スイート神戸ハーバーランド 2階
reviews: The chef was very nice. He kept seeing if we wanted something, he even helped us to stamp the parking ticket. And the beef was even better! We ordered three different courses, they were all delicious and worth the price! The kobe beef was really tender and juicy.

The beef and all courses was out of this world. Kobe A5 cooked by the best chefs with amazing views.
Melt in the mouth beef. Every dish was perfected and couldn't fault anything.
Staff were very attentive and friendly. Chef also made a good effort in speaking English as our Japanese isn't the best.
Must visit if in Kobe for an amazing experience.

A must try and well worth a visit if you're looking to experience kobe beef teppanyaki style (with a view of Port Kobe).

Not only was the food delicious but all staff & our chef Ishihara were incredible from start to finish! Their warm hospitality was what made our day-trip to Kobe very special. They did their best to explain each dish in English plus its ingredients, were very attentive, and by the end they gave us many laughs with communication via translation apps. They even helped us take a picture on the outside patio to commemorate the night.

We've never felt more welcomed and definitely recommend others visiting Kobe to try this restaurant!

name: Wagaya
reviews:
お店の方、みんなとても親切で笑顔が素敵でした！
食事がとても健康的で、とにかくとっても美味しかった！
絶対また行きたいです😊
とても美味しかったです。ひっきりなしにお客さんが来られるので、早めの時間帯に行かれた方が良いと思います。

久し振りにランチいただきました、𓆝
わがや定食のサンマです。
干物は骨、尻尾まで 余す事なく完食です。
温かい雰囲気と家庭的な味が ホットしますね♪

name: Sakura Sakae Entertainment Restaurant Nagoya
street: Nishiki, 3 Chome−16−5 スローアートセンタ
reviews: Saw that this place was showing the Olympics and decided to stop in for a drink or 2 in the evening; the staff are so friendly and the drinks are really cheap.

名古屋🍜らーめん🍜めぐり　番外編
SAKURAさん🐖💨

昼休みに
富山らーめん🍜の看板みて入店👀

らーめん、見つけれず

巨大なスクリーン📺️👀✨あったり、
ソファ〜席とかもオシャレですね🎵

らーめんの謎は解けず(笑)

通りがかりに富山ブラックのポスターを見て、ラーメン屋と間違えて入店😅笑

ラーメン食べるのに一番おしゃれなソファーの半個室に通されました！

味は美味い！麺は中心が生っぽい感じがしたがこんなものか？！

水はセルフですが、知らずに水ください！と言ったらセルフですよーでも、持ってきます！と、お水を下さいました！ありがとう😊

お好み焼きのりきゅうさんが経営されてるみたい。
外観、内観、外構、とてもおしゃれです！
他のメニューも食べてみたいと思いました！
ヽ(´▽｀)/

name: Gran View
reviews: As a Canadian; this place introduced us to canned rum and coke. Staff were friendly and has a great view of the track.

Pretty decent drinks, pizza and fries.

The best thing about this place is the view of the final corners on Suzuka circuit

Staff was very friendly and got us our food very quickly
Brilliant place, great pizza and birds eye view of the track!

name: Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route - Transportation Division
reviews: What's there to say? Just look at the pictures and just go!! So beautiful! Along the way, stop by the kurobe dam to take photos of the alpine mountains 🏔️ and take a slow walk along the snow wall. There are 6 modes of transport, so be very vigilant of your timings especially if you're traveling alone. Check weather conditions before proceeding with the route. Also. Have an open mind, there are many inconsiderate tourists.

Japan's most famous snow cliff is the "Snow Wall," or Yuki no Otani, on the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route. The 20-meter-high snow wall is naturally formed by the accumulation of thick snow during the winter and is open to the public in spring, typically from mid-April to mid-June. Visitors can hike among these snow cliffs for a unique experience amidst the breathtaking scenery.

I have no idea why people can give a 5 star to such a messy unorganized company. Apr 17, snow was said to be the reason, instead of cancelling some morning tickets, all were kept loading onto the cable cars. We were delayed getting on the cable car by two hours and there wasn't enough time for going to the end station at Ogizawa. We were hushed and rushed to go from 2:10pm in 4 hours. No sight seeing, nor getting out to see the snow wall which is has too deceitful photos on the web. We were push and hurried to transfer from one vehicle to another, barely make it to the last bus service. I feel so humiliated and the chaotic mess of people got stuck waiting at all the stations was a joke. Besides, why the shipping of luggage has to be started at Toyama? We didn't know service was delayed until we were at Tateyama, to late to back out as luggage was already shipped. Why luggage has to be in Shinano-Omachi and not in Ogizawa or Nagano. We had an express bus ticket from Ogizawa to Nagano that we couldn't get off at Shinano-Omachi! There were many tour groups got stuck the same time. A tour guide mentioned the schedule was delayed very often. This part of journey is the most disappointing and upsetting and it made me feel like I don't want to go visit Japan again.

name: 天串 桑名駅前店
reviews:
昼飲みで利用させて頂きました。
個室でゆっくりと飲めて良かったです。
また利用したいと思います。

name: Machan
reviews: What an amazing little restaurant! There’s a grand total of about ten seats so it’s a bit of a squeeze, but the food is amazing and the staff are very friendly and accommodating. Food is sort of Asian fusion, there’s a bit of Thai, bit of Indonesian and so on. Not so expensive either. Check it out!

This is an amazing find. If you are looking for something different or just authentic Sri Lankan food, look no further - this is the place to come.

Food is excellent - authentic flavourful and colourful. The food takes me back to my home town in Sri Lanka where I have had yellow rice with multiple curries each bringing with it a unique taste to each bite.

Vibe is authentic Sri Lankan too. They were playing Jayasri when we entered - it truly took us back. The staff were very welcoming, kind and polite. We couldn’t have asked anything more.

A definite must visit if you come to Nagoya.
Good services , Good food , Good mood

name: Alor Corner Curry Noodle
reviews: Tucked in a tiny corner near the entrance of jalan alor. Don't be put off by their shabby setting, the standard of their noodles is just as good as those in fancier eateries. I had their curry noodle for breakfast.. Packed full w ingredients and the curry soup spicy and delicious.. I will be back the next time i visit kl. Recommended
Still good the curry noodles with kuey teow. Original from mother pass to daughters already.
Delicious laksa from an aunty street vendor. So, so, so delicious. This is the ‘basic’ laksa with no add-ons (add-ins?).

name: Umashikuni Sakaba Heihachiro
reviews:
5人でコース料理。コース料理とは思えない料理の質。どれも美味しかったです。
飲み放題にしてましたが、料理も飲み物も提供が早く、ノンストレスで楽しむことができました！
全品写真撮りたかったのに、美味し過ぎて、楽し過ぎて撮り忘れるぐらい。
次はコースではなく利用したいです。

インスタでオープンしたのを見て予約しました！
テーブル席が半個室の様になっててゆっくり過ごせました。
料理も美味しかったです！
お酒がメガサイズあってうれしかった。

早めの時間に2人で利用しました。初めはガラガラでしたが、週末というのもあり19時ぐらいには結構席が埋まってました。
料理は地元の料理があるので旅行者の人が来たり、連れて行くには良いかもしれないです。注文はタブレットでお会計の目安もわかります。味も悪くないのでいいと思います。
お値段は普通接客も普通ですが、私の場合お会計の時が微妙でした。
メンバーで割り勘する関係で1万円を1000円とかにして欲しいぐらいだったのですが、その話題が出る前に、「（両替）しませんよ！」みたいな感じで気分が一気に悪くなっちゃいました。女性の店員さんでしたが機嫌が悪かったのか、両替はトラブルがあったのか知りませんが。

来店する際には、事前に割り勘出来るようにメンバーで細かい紙幣を持ってないといけないようです。
お会計以外はそんなに悪いお店ではないので桑名に遠方から友人が来たらもう一度ぐらい行ってみて、また微妙な感じだったら三重人さんとか、なな色さんとか別のお店に行くと思います。

name: Street art by Julia Volchkova " The GOLDSMITH"
reviews: Super amazing and awesome street art! Wow I'm so surprised how amazing the wall's art is. Really impressed. Did not take many photo bcs I was busy taking the beauty of art using my eyes, lol. I am so amazed. Really! Thank you and kudos for them artist!
Awesome place to see art and have a meal
Awesome place, a must visit place in KL

name: Eco Ride Malaysia
reviews:
late September-2024

Fabulous first experience with Nick. A very careful and helpful gentleman who gave me tips about best  time and how-to reach and parking and where to take  lunch.

Send in enquiry and all will follow from there. Have a WhatsApp app ready to ease communication.

Credit card payment is possible.

Valuables are to be carry on. Big items can be left in van, if you were joining at base.

Have mini water bottle, small towels (sweat) and cap/hat (be careful for wind though).

Proper shoe (not slipper) is highly recommended.

Children of 7 years old and above is fine.

Beautiful architectures and explanation.
A little break near ice cream stall and souvenir stall is arranged also (own payment).

If wished to, a quick visit into mosque is possible too - robe will be provided, not sure about charge though).

Wow what a great experience we loved every minute of while worth doing and Nick was a awesome tour guide that spoke excellent English . Our group of 4 where 53, 60, 63 and 66 and we all able to navigate our way around the Segway easily .

Best option to visit Perdana Botanical Garden!!! Whole area is quite big and you would get tired if you plan to go by foot 😂😂😂
The road was made for segway. The price of tour is reasonable + that's a kind of new experience 🤩
The guide (Nickkie) was so patient and professional. He even took a lot of photos and filmed all time (after sent everything to us) 🥰🥰🥰
Thanks Nickkie for such a wonderful adventure!!! 😘
PS: We will surely do that again on our next time in KL 🤩

name: The Tree of Hope
reviews:
Largest Mural In KL 2020- Tree Of Hope
Please Come Have A Look If you near by 🌄
It's crazy how much detail was put into this! Beautiful!

name: 彩虹天桥
reviews: 夜景确实惊艳，霓虹灯倒映在玻璃幕墙像打翻的调色盘，随手一拍都是大片。但座位太抢手，周末最好提前订窗边位；菜品味道中规中矩，冲着拍照来值得，专程觅食可再考虑。
晚上的燈光七彩繽紛非常漂亮，十分值得到來拍照。

name: Port Of Nagoya Public Aquarium
reviews: Absolutely loved it. We are from California and are very familiar with the world-famous Monterey bay aquarium but honestly this one is just as good. It's not as large but I think it showcases the fish really well through the exhibits like the theatre and the amphitheater where everyone watches the whale and dolphin training. The whole place was very impressive and I recommend all to come here. They also have a really interesting exhibit about japanese expeditions to Antarctica, along with the actual boat (that I did not get the chance to see).

Amazing exhibition of both alive and well preserved species.
Took us over 5hours to slowly view everything that was available.
Make sure to get a pamphlet with event timings not to miss the amazing dolphins show!
Highly recommended!

This aquarium is a great place for a one-day trip, especially for families. There are many interesting exhibits, and both kids and adults can enjoy the experience. The atmosphere is nice and relaxing, making it perfect for spending quality time together.

name: Georgetown UNESCO Historic Site
reviews:
Georgetown, Penang is an absolute gem. I recently visited and loved everything about this town ,the beautifully preserved heritage buildings, vibrant street art, charming cafés, and incredible food scene. Every street has its own character, blending history and culture so effortlessly.
It’s lively yet relaxed, rich in tradition yet modern in vibe. Whether you’re walking through the old streets, exploring local markets, or enjoying the waterfront, there’s something special at every corner.

Beautiful old architecture buildings with many converted to restaurants, shops etc. You can just walk around admiring the beautiful architecture, colors, some recently painted. Since CNY is around, there are lanterns and lights and lively atmosphere with many tourists around. you can visit during the day to enjoy the view and also in the night to enjoy the lighting.
Great place to relax and chill. Other than the traffic, Penang is good for nostalgia with great food. The people are friendly and very nice. Hope to visit again soon.

name: Penang Street Art
reviews: This is a must-visit photo spot in Penang, known for its many art pieces, handicrafts, and iconic murals. It is especially popular on weekends, with shops open from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m., along with numerous restaurants and seafood eateries. The best time to visit is in the evening, when the sunset creates a beautiful backdrop for photos.

This is a must-see if you’re visiting George Town. We took a rickshaw, and the driver showed us the various street paintings, some of which are actually inside shops. It’s great fun, but as with most tourist attractions, it’s best to visit at a quieter time.

The area is compact enough to explore on foot, but a bicycle ride can make it easier to cover more streets. Going early morning or late evenings is recommended. Many of arts are cleverly integrated into doors, windows, bikes and swings. Penang street Art is a highlight of Georgetown and is a must visit.

name: Jalan Alor Food Street
reviews:
⭐️Must Visit Place in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia

Visited Jalan Alor in Kuala Lumpur and it’s truly a paradise for food lovers! This place is heaven for foodies. The street is lively and vibrant, with countless food options everywhere you look.

You’ll find all kinds of seafood like crab, lobsters, oysters, and many more dishes I didn’t even know the names of. There are endless seafood choices, though personally, I still feel the seafood quality and taste I experienced in Vietnam was slightly better.

I tried satay for the first time in my life, and it was absolutely delicious! The taste with the curry/peanut sauce they provide was amazing. For dessert, I had a soufflé for the first time — it was super fluffy, soft, and the taste was next level (as shown in the video I uploaded).

The place is very crowded, but that’s part of the unique experience and energetic vibe.

Highly recommended for anyone who loves exploring new food and flavors! 🌟

Jalan Alor is a must-visit destination for food lovers and one of the most vibrant street food streets in Kuala Lumpur. From an Indian perspective, it feels similar to exploring famous night food streets like Mohammed Ali Road or local night markets — full of energy, aromas, and endless food options.

The street is packed with stalls serving freshly cooked dishes like Satay, grilled seafood, fried noodles, roasted chicken wings, and a variety of Asian specialties. The live grilling and open-air seating create a very lively and authentic experience. The atmosphere, especially in the evening near Bukit Bintang, is vibrant and perfect for walking, exploring, and trying different foods.

However, vegetarians may face some challenges. Most stalls focus heavily on meat and seafood, and even vegetable dishes may be cooked in shared woks or with sauces that contain fish or oyster ingredients. Pure vegetarians should confirm with vendors before ordering. There are still some options like fried rice, stir-fried vegetables, and fruits, but choices are limited compared to non-vegetarian options.

Also, it’s highly recommended to carry cash, as many small stalls may not accept cards or digital payments. Having local currency makes ordering easier and faster.

Overall, Jalan Alor offers a fantastic street food experience with great energy, authentic flavors, and a lively atmosphere. It’s a must-visit in Kuala Lumpur, especially for those who enjoy exploring local food culture.

Crazy enough, I had one of the best Vietnamese and Chinese foods there on this street.

The fact is I loved it so much that while I was staying in KL for over 6 months for work, I came to his street at least once a week, to have Vietnamese foods, and some Thai coconut ice cream.

There are plenty of other foods from different cruises that you can find here though. Great selection of sea foods as well.

name: Damascus Bukit Bintang
street: and, Corner of Jalan Bukit Bintang, Jln Sultan Ismail
reviews:
I’ve been wanting to visit Damascus Restaurant for quite some time, but the queue has always been incredibly long. This time, we decided to drop by around 3am and were pleasantly surprised to walk in without any waiting time.
The environment is grand and beautifully reflects Syrian culture, creating a warm and authentic dining experience. Service was good overall — the staff were friendly, welcoming, and attentive despite the late hour. The menu offers a wide variety of choices, making it quite difficult to decide what to order.
I especially loved the Shish Taouk rice with skewer — it was aromatic, flavorful, and well-marinated. The Chicken Shawarma was tasty as always, consistently satisfying. The Kabsa chicken with rice was just okay for me personally, but I must say the chicken was tender and juicy.
I’ve actually been a loyal customer of their shawarma for over 10 years, dating back to when they operated next to Sungei Wang Plaza. I truly miss those days — it was still crowded, but without the long queues like today.
Price-wise, I would say it’s reasonable considering the portion size, quality, and overall dining experience.
I would definitely return again to explore more items from their extensive menu.

We tried this highly popular Syrian restaurant over the Chinese new year holiday. Tried their Kabsa rice. It was delicious. The rice was flavourful and chicken soft and juicy. The shawarma plate was good so was the Creamy Chicken shawarma. We also tried their hummus and tabbouleh. The hummus was smooth and delicious but the pita bread that came with it was cold. I enjoyed the tabbouleh. Will come back to try the other offerings.

We ordered shawarma(arabi plate), mix grill(chicken & lamb), cheesy kunafa, chicken kabsa Saudi, Turkish coffee and tea teapot. It was very tasty, I like the mix grill the most, it cm with some pita kinda bread, very soft. For me the Turkish coffee was very strong. Tea was nice. The service is good. Environment and their restaurant deco was pleasant and nice. The area itself a busy place so quite hard to find  parking spot but somehow you can find parking at nearby mall or hotels/apartment/office building. Pls Waze parking spot. Price is ok.
Overall good food with great ambient.

“Just my taste buds talking—yours might gossip differently. Try it yourself!”

name: Higashiyama Zoo and Botanical Gardens
reviews: It's a really nice zoo. Lots of animals. A monorail to see everything from up high. And an amusement park.  Today we just walked around the Zoo and not the Gardens or amusement park areas.   But the Zoo part was plenty as it was pretty humid and being a Sunday it was very busy. Even with the crowds most of the lines to see the animals moved quickly and swiftly.   This is a great place for kids and families.  Or on a date or by yourself as there's plenty to do and see.

Although the animals look cute, its a very cruel place.

Many of the big cats and other felines are in small cages. If you watch them, they just walk around in circles. Its extremely cruel.

Many of the animals are also from hotter climates, like the elephants, hippos, rhinos, etc. Yet they are just left exposed outside during the winter.

These animals deserve better living spaces and better care and attention.

This is my 2nd visit to this Amusement park & Zoo.

The park was actually really busy, but today is a Sunday, so lots of families were out enjoying the Autumn sun.

The ride and attraction area is very well kept with reasonable prices. I paid per ride and it worked out better as I only wanted to ride 5 attractions.

There were plenty of vending machines, a gift shop and food.

Be aware, it's very hilly with a lot of steps!

I didn't go to the Zoo as I only visited for the Amusement park.

Slope Shooter was the standout attraction, which is very unique, being the only one in the world I know of.

name: Atsuta Houraiken Jingu
reviews:
Came here for lunch, and be prepared to wait.  Come early if you can and to take the queue. number.  While waiting you can head over to the nearby Atsuta Jingu Shrine. A definitely must-eat food if you are in Nagoya for the first time! The eel is grilled to perfection and you can enjoy the food using the 3 recommendations by the restaurant.  And finally for the last portion, take 1 of the 3 recommendations that you enjoy most as the final portion.  A sumptuous lunch to start the trip!  Last but not least, there’s a limited inhouse dessert, it is just right and not so sweet to roundup the lunch!
Service is good, Food is excellent, Atomsphere is good.  Price paid is for 2 sets and 1 dessert.

🌟At Atsuta Houraiken in Nagoya, Aichi for their celebrated Hitsumabushi (eel dish)!

🌟A restaurant known for long queues, so I went after lunch hour, past 2pm but still waited for more than an hour, omg!

🌟The Hitsumabushi traditional dish is preserved over 150 years. The aromatic, tender Unagi with charred skin is grilled over binchotan charcoal dressed in flavourful secret sauce passed down through generations.

🌟There are 4 guided steps to eating this deliciousness, divide the portions.
Eat the Unagi on its own with rice. Eat with condiments. Eat with soup. And eat however you like. It was Oishi.

Insta @yummmmmmmmonica

Tried the unagi three-way (Hitsumabushi) set and it was absolutely delicious! Each style had its own flavor and texture, and the overall presentation made it feel like a special experience.

I ordered the large portion and was pleasantly surprised — the amount of eel and rice was generous and definitely worth the upgrade. Would highly recommend this for anyone looking to try something beyond the usual unagi bowl.

name: Halab Gate Shawarma
reviews:
It was nearing a 5 but a few flaws that left it at 4. A great shawarma restaurant in the heart of KL though. They have a quick vendor downstairs and a restaurant upstairs.  We came here after my friends Ramadan fast and ordered a big platter with drinks and rice.

Whilst the price was fair, a few things limited my limited 5. The food took so long unfortunately for the amount of staff standing around without work to do and the amount of people in the restaurant.

With our platter the lamb chops were overcooked and the chips were a mixture of 2 different kinds which ruined the perfect board.

Friendly staff and well priced and would love to come back again

If you into the food with view of Bukit bintang and monorail. Then yes it is nice. But if taste wise. Normal not really value for money. 💰
No outside food/drink allowed. Mineral water option only cheapest drink rm6. Kabsah lamb maybe max 2 pax serving. Rm45. Kunafa rm25. You can get cheaper nearby. But amount you pay is for the seating place and ambience.

I was (still am) so disappointed.

After that burrito experience I opted for the chicken shawarma while my date had the mixed shawarma( chicken & beef).
Besides online reviews, I wasn’t expecting much other than a decent shawarma and It wasn’t that.
Could be a bad day, but it (chicken) was quite dry and there was very little sauce in the shawarma. It was at least compensated for by the garlic sauce they provided.

The mixed shawarma wasn’t as bad, but still not worth the price.

I would consider giving it a second try only because I don’t believe people can rave so much about it only for it to be that bad.

Their service is quite fast and efficient for the traffic they receive so I guess they have that on lock.

name: Sri Maha Mariamman Temple
reviews:
A Gateway to Divine Beauty 🕉️
Standing before the Sri Mahamariamman Temple in the heart of Kuala Lumpur's bustling Chinatown, I'm struck by how this 150-year-old sanctuary holds its ground amid the urban chaos. The towering Raja Gopuram rises like a technicolor dream against the city skyline, each of its five tiers adorned with hundreds of Hindu deities frozen in intricate poses.

The morning light catches the temple's vibrant palette—brilliant golds, deep turquoises, warm terracottas—colors that seem to pulse with life even as traffic swirls around its entrance. This is the beauty of KL: ancient devotion and modern life existing in perfect, chaotic harmony.

As I step closer, removing my shoes at the threshold, the street noise fades. Inside, the scent of incense mingles with fresh marigolds, and the cool tile feels sacred beneath my feet. This is where Thaipusam begins each year, where thousands of devotees start their pilgrimage to Batu Caves in acts of faith that humble any observer.

Travel tip: Visit early morning (around 7-8 AM) to experience the temple during prayer time when it's most atmospheric. Dress modestly—shoulders and knees covered. Photography is welcome outside, but always ask permission before photographing devotees or the inner sanctum.

The temple asks nothing of you except respect, but gives everything—a glimpse into Malaysia's rich tapestry of cultures, where a Tamil shrine stands proud on Jalan Bandar, welcoming all who seek beauty, peace, or simply wonder.

This temple is a beautiful example of detailed architecture and vibrant cultural design. The moment you arrive, the colors and intricate carvings immediately stand out. Every part of the structure is covered in impressive artwork, statues, and patterns that show an incredible level of craftsmanship. Even if you’re not familiar with the cultural or religious background, the visual appeal alone makes it worth visiting.

The atmosphere feels calm and respectful, with people quietly moving around, offering prayers, or simply appreciating the surroundings. It’s not a large place, but the design is rich enough that you’ll find yourself stopping to look closely at every section. The entrance tower especially is stunning, filled with layers of detailed sculptures stacked beautifully from bottom to top.

It’s a nice spot to take a short break from the busy streets outside and appreciate a piece of historic and artistic beauty right in the middle of the city.

Great Hindu temple in the centre of KL, we grouped Sri Maha Mariamman temple with Petaling market, Central market, Merdeka square and Sultan Abdul Samad building into a single walking tour.  The temple is absolutely beautiful and so intricately decorated with figures, you see something different every time you glance at it.  We intended to go inside, but because of the cover-up policy (which we respect) and 34 degrees, it was way too hot for us!  However we did manage to get a slight glimpse to satisfy our curiosity!  Worth a visit but choose a cool day if possible.

name: BE KOBE Monument (Meriken Park)
reviews: This place is a respite midst the bustling of Kobe. You can see the meriken wharf, kobe tower and the port all from thos park. The park is  meeting place for youth and adults alike. People just stroll and take in the scene. I love that there are a lot of art installations around the park. Here also lies the memorial for the deadly kobe earthquake in the 90s. You cant help but feel an array of emotions when you're here..but overall, this is a must visit!
A cultural landmark. Vast place to walk, play and relax. Got to see the iconic BE KOBE monument. There is a nearby observatory to visit. On the whole, not crowded. A great place to take photos.

Kobe’s an underrated gem — modern but mellow, stitched neatly between the mountains and the sea. The city feels curated without being sterile; food’s excellent, people are easygoing, and it never tries too hard to impress.

What really stands out, though, are those manhole covers — tiny bursts of art on the pavement. Each one is like a postcard under your feet: vivid depictions of Kobe’s skyline, harbor, flowers, or the Port Tower, painted with surprising precision. It’s the kind of detail that says a lot about Japan’s relationship with aesthetics — beauty even where you don’t need it.

name: THIRTY8 Restaurant, Bar & Lounge
reviews:
Went there for tea time. The tea time set was RM168 per person, which isn’t cheap, so our expectations were quite high.

Most of the desserts were delicious, and the overall portion served was quite substantial. However, one dish — the green bean mix with salmon — was very disappointing and did not go well together at all.

The service was generally okay, but not very attentive. We often had to raise our hands for quite a while or call the staff several times before getting their attention. The staff were also not very fluent in English, which made communication a bit difficult.

On the positive side, the ambience was good, especially with the nice view of KLCC. It was not too crowded, so the environment was quiet and comfortable.

Overall, it wasn’t a bad experience, but it didn’t quite match the price we paid. They didn’t even provide wet tissues, which felt like a basic service omission at this price point. There is definitely room for improvement.

We had a wonderful breakfast at THIRTY8 Restaurant, and the experience was made even more special by a lovely staff member named Mimi. She surprised us with a cake to celebrate our recent marriage, which truly touched our hearts. On top of that, she kindly took photos of us and even printed them out as a keepsake.

Her thoughtful gesture, warmth, and excellent service made our morning unforgettable. Thank you, Mimi, for going above and beyond to make our celebration so meaningful. We truly appreciate it! 💕

We really had a great time at Thirty8, the service was fantastic and top notch. The view is simply stunning. One small inconvenient was just that we were seated at a table for 2, it was quite cramped especially that we have a toddler with us seated at the baby chair. The waiter was really helpful with food suggestions and was very attentive. The food is just nice, but ive tasted better steaks before, I like the cake tho, the presentation is very nice and the taste is good, but they misspelled my name, but thats fine. Overall, it was a nice dinner, would recommend this place for special occasions.

name: Sunway Velocity Hotel
reviews:
This was our second time staying at Sunway Velocity Hotel, and we would like to express our appreciation to the management for the excellent service provided by one of your staff members, Fazraf.
Initially, we were staying at another hotel, but unfortunately, the service did not meet our expectations. We decided to check out on the same day and made a last-minute booking at Sunway Velocity Hotel. It turned out to be the best decision for our family.
During our late-night check-in, Fazraf at the front desk was extremely helpful and welcoming. He patiently explained all the hotel facilities and ensured that our family would be comfortable throughout our stay. His professionalism and warm hospitality immediately made us feel at ease.
When we entered the room, we were pleasantly surprised by how spacious and comfortable it was. Once again, the hotel did not disappoint us, just like our previous stay. Sunway Velocity Hotel has consistently met our expectations.
We sincerely hope the management will convey our heartfelt appreciation to Fazraf for his outstanding hospitality and service. Staff like him truly enhance the hotel’s branding and ensure that guests’ expectations are not only met but exceeded.
Thank you for another wonderful stay.

First time staying at Sunway Velocity and I can’t fault iIt. Seamless arrival experience; smooth, fast and friendly. The room was clean and comfortable. Swimming pool on the top floor was nice with a fantastic view of the city. As the Hotel is connected to the shopping centre access was very convenient. Breakfast buffet was ok but don’t expect a huge variety. Plenty of places to eat at the adjoining shopping centre. I would definitely stay here again and happy to recommend Sunway Velocity to family and friends. Keep up the good work.

I had a very pleasant stay at Sunway Velocity Hotel Kuala Lumpur. The staff were all very friendly and helpful. The location is excellent, very close to the mall which makes it easy to shop and find food, and also near the hospital.

I came to Kuala Lumpur to accompany my family for treatment at Velocity Hospital, so the location was very convenient.

Special thanks to Fazraf Sher (Assistant Guest Relations Manager) for preparing a lovely birthday surprise for me. I really appreciate the thoughtful gesture.

Highly recommended hotel! ⭐️

name: Uzomuzo
reviews: Randomly crashed into this store after finished shopping around and my god, one of the best ramen i ever had in my life. Highly recommended

Tsukemen Ramen in Osu area, to order ramen has to go inside the shop and order with the machine, cash only I think.

I order the original one, the GOD. Can choose hot or cold ramen, and level of spicy! 1,150 yen. I ordered cold and spicy level2 (the staff suggested)

Very unique taste, the noodles chewy, when mix with egg yolk and sauce in the bottom of the bowl is so delicious!

Interesting small restaurant with friendly service and special noodles ordered thru the vending machine (accepts cash only). We were a family of 4 and were asked to wait to be seated.  We were finally seated in front of the bar counter, where we got to watch the young chefs preparing our noodles. Nice firm noodles dipped in a special sauce with 3 levels of spiciness to choose from.
Before we knew it, our bowls were already emptied 😋
If there should be any improvements to make, I would suggest to include English menu on the vending machine plus allowing credit card payments on the vending machine.

name: Norm Micro Roastery
reviews:
We ordered a few mains to try. We all agreed that the pork ragout pasta and the conchiglie with seasonal mushrooms were very good. The pasta sauces were unique and tasted quite different from what you usually get at other places. The pasta itself was cooked perfectly al dente. However, the rice paper in the conchiglie dish was a bit oily and not crispy at all.

The seafood pumpkin risotto was creamy but not overly heavy, which we liked. The Norm shakshuka was fairly standard, but the focaccia served with it was nice and chewy.

In comparison, the fried chicken waffle was a bit disappointing. The fried chicken wasn’t crispy enough, and the waffle could have been crispier as well.

I really enjoyed the atmosphere here—the mix of concrete, high ceilings, and natural trees creates a very relaxing environment.

The service was good and attentive. The food arrived beautifully presented.

The slow-cooked pork ragout pasta had great flavor and the pork was tender, but it was unfortunately a bit too salty for my liking.

While the Norm Daily Scrambled was absolutely perfect—the eggs were silky and the bread was great. Veggies were fresh too.

Overall, a beautiful spot for dine in with high-quality ingredients.

Beautiful space with a calm, minimalist vibe — perfect for brunch or a slow afternoon coffee. We tried the fried chicken burger with fries and their brunch plate with poached eggs, pulled meat, greens, and a crispy croquette. Presentation was lovely, and the flavors were generally good and satisfying.

Service was pleasant and the food came out nicely plated. However, for the price point, the portions could be slightly more generous. Still, it’s a nice spot to chill, enjoy good food, and indulge in their aesthetic atmosphere.

name: Sin Sze Si Ya Temple
reviews:
A small but nice and historical temple, a short walk from Pasar Seni LRT/MRT interchange.
Next to it is a museum about the temple, Yap Ah Loy, the local Chinese communities and Kuala Lumpur.

This is a temple where my mum prayed, when we first came to KL 50 years ago. Then it was only ocassionally as we stayed outside KL.

It is a temple highly respected and regularly prayed to by most of the Chinese in Malaysia.

As usual, in the old days, the temple history, meaning and significance is via verbal communication from devotees to beginners or those coming for spiritual guidance and help.

Nothing is written as in those days, the spiritual energies were not questioned but just accepted.

Well, the temple must have helped a lot of people, as the temple survived all developments around it.

They even showed how over the years. the temple had given out scholarships to help deserving students education.

High rise grew around it and yet, the temple stayed put. In those days, the incense scent is very overpowering and strong. Lots of coiled incense.

Now, as we visited the temple, we found a lot of innovative changes, the monies for incense offering easy to pay. RM 2 per pack.

There is a diagram on the notice, stating where to pray. So we just prayed.

The Energies were so peaceful and nice that we just sat peacefully on the bench outside in meditative state but appreciating the feel of it.

Then we got up, an arrow on the wall to our left, whilst on the bench in front, says Left to Museum.
We followed that to a door on the behind road that says Sin Sze Si Ys Temple Museum.

Entrance fee was just RM 5 for  senior citizen and RM10 for others.

But the encouragement to bring your family is there, for families of up to 8 people, you go in for RM5 each.

AND it is so so worth it! Literally, it was a BIG Eye-Opener to the History of how Kuala Lumpur came about, the contributions from the Chinese, especially the real historic history that we learnt before, as school kids in the 1960s of Kapitan Cina, Yap Ah Loy 叶亚來 (pinyin Ye Ya Lai) (now no longer emphasised and downplayed in present day politicised history subject taught in government national schools.). The young will not know this, and it is sad when real history is lost.

So, please come, visit this temple's trustee efforts to keep history alive and real.

The temple worship significance is that Yap Ah Loy had been an assistant to another man called Seng Meng Lee 盛明利 (pinyin sheng ming li), who was Kapitan of Seremban Sg Ujong. Later, Yap Ah Loy became Second Kapitan of Sg Ujong, encouraged by Seng Meng Lee.

Yap Ah Loy was invited to Selangor by another Hakka, called Hui Siew 丘秀 (pinyin qiu xiu).

And Seng Meng Lee  盛明秀was killed in 1861.  Yap Ah Loy carried his body to fight till got away and was buried at Seremban.
Later Yap Ah Loy got into the Selangor Civil War. and Seng Meng Lee appeared in his dreams to guide him in war strategy and help clear witchcraft.
As a result, Yap Ah Loy brought his body to his house in KL and deitify him as an immortal called Sin Si Ya  仙四爷。

In 1869, Yap Sze, Yap Ah Loy close friend, was also killed whilst helping Yap Ah Loy. Yap Sze was deitified as Si Sze Ya 四师爷。

This is the origin of the two deities being worshipped for their heroic effort to help Yap Ah Loy win and bring peace to KL.

came to help Yap Ah Loy. He was killed.

If you're looking for a ridiculously atmospheric oriental Taoist temple in the heart of Chinatown (nr to the fab Texas Chicken—much better than KFC!) you can't get any better than this little diamond. The wooden carvings are exquisite, the statues showcases all manner of facial expressions, incense sticks burning gloriously everywhere,  and even the requisite strong sunlight rays penetrating through the roof (creating diagonals of dust and incense smoke) make you feel like you've step into a Somerset Maugham novel...

name: Quivo - Pavilion Bukit Bintang
reviews:
I came here for lunch because I liked the layout from the outside which blends a casual yet polished dining room with lively outdoor seating, perfect for people-watching as shoppers stroll by. The design leans contemporary, with playful touches like bold floor tiles, bright-coloured stools, and striking lighting that gives it a relaxed but refined feel.  ￼

Whether you arrive during the afternoon lull or the evening peak, the space is inviting rather than formal, making it a great choice for both post-shopping lunches and sunset cocktails. Loved the friendly staff and upbeat atmosphere!

Quivo’s menu is an eclectic yet cohesive celebration of Mediterranean flavours with global twists like, wood-fired pizzas, seafood, burgers, pastas, and grills with nuanced spice profiles and fresh ingredients.  ￼

Standout Dishes & Impressions:
Pesto & Soft Shell Crab Aglio Olio spaghetti. I enjoy their ziti in pink sauce and prawn as well as their Seabass Burger

The only downfall is the portions are rather small for the price.

I can’t wait to go back and try their Seafood Risotto which looked delicious.

Definitely worth a visit!

Food presentation is lovely. Food is quite tasty - we had the lamb shank and fish and chips. The best thing here I must say is the service. We were served by Lutfi and Boy, and they were very attentive, updating us on when the food would be ready, and very quickly clearing the plates so we would be comfortable.

4/5 ⭐

We visited Quivo during their lunch set hours and it was a really good experience. The lunch menu came with a starter and a main, which made it great value for somewhere inside Pavilion.

For starters, one of us had the Caesar salad and the other had the soup. Both were fresh and well-presented — the Caesar salad especially had a generous amount of chicken and croutons.

For mains, we ordered the spaghetti bolognese and the seafood pizza. The bolognese was rich, flavourful, and the portion size was just right. The seafood pizza was thin, crispy, and topped generously with tomatoes, herbs, and seafood — way better than expected and a nice change from the usual.

The atmosphere was stylish and comfortable, and the service was good even though the place gets busy during lunchtime. Overall, Quivo is a great choice if you want a solid, good-quality meal in Pavilion with a relaxed vibe and good presentation.

name: Leong San Tong Khoo Kongsi
reviews:
A stunning 19th-century Chinese clan house in the heart of George Town, Penang. This is not just a temple—it’s a monument to migration, identity, and wealth from the Hokkien Khoo clan who sailed from Fujian to Southeast Asia.

The architecture is breathtaking: intricate granite pillars carved with dragons, richly gilded wooden panels, detailed porcelain roof ornamentation, and a dramatic central courtyard that glows in late afternoon light. The main hall houses ancestral tablets and a beautifully adorned altar, giving it a living spiritual presence rather than a museum vibe.

Historically, it reflects the power of Chinese mercantile networks during the British colonial era. The original structure was reportedly so grand it was struck by lightning—locals believed Heaven disapproved of its extravagance. The rebuilt version is more restrained but still magnificent.

Best visited early morning or near sunset for softer light and fewer crowds. Entry fee is modest and well worth it. Clean, well maintained, informative exhibits inside.

Leong San Tong Khoo Kongsi in Penang, Malaysia, is one of the most prominent Chinese clan associations, established in 1851 by Hoklo immigrants from Sin Kang village, Fujian. It served as a vital social, welfare, and religious hub for the Khoo clan. The original, lavishly designed clanhouse was destroyed by fire in 1901, believed to be the "wrath of god" and was rebuilt as a smaller, exquisite, and architecturally renowned complex in 1906.

Key historical details include:

Origin:
Founded in 1851 to honor ancestors and the Patron Saint Tua Sai Yah (a deity worshipped by the clan).

The Fire of 1901:
A massive, highly ornate structure, often compared to an emperor's palace, was destroyed by fire, which locals believed was divine punishment for its opulence.

Rebuilding:
The current, more modest (but still highly detailed) structure was completed in 1906, featuring intricate carvings, ceramic, and gilded wood.

Function:
It served as a kongsi (clanhouse) for managing the clan's welfare, education, and ancestral worship in the British colony of Penang.
Design: It showcases traditional Southern Chinese architecture with unique additions like a courtyard, a theatre stage, and eclectic 19th-century colonial influences.

Today, the complex is a major heritage site in George Town, representing the wealth and social influence of the Chinese merchant community.

Khoo Kongsi is easily one of the most impressive clan houses in Penang. The place is big, beautifully restored, and very richly decorated, showing just how wealthy and influential the Khoo clan once was. From the moment you step in, the details really stand out.
The main hall is the highlight, with intricate carvings, gold-painted beams, and colourful panels covering almost every surface. The craftsmanship is amazing and gives a good idea of how grand a Chinese clan house could be at its peak.
There’s also a basement exhibition area where you can learn about the history of the Khoo clan, how they settled in Southeast Asia, and see “walls of honour” highlighting notable clan members over the years. Definitely worth a visit if you’re interested in Penang’s heritage.

name: Hard Rock Cafe Universal Citywalk Osaka
reviews: My server for the night was Ayaka and she was very attentive. She knows I’m a blink and when BP’s MV came on the tv, she initiate to take photos for me. I came for the famous beef fajitas and it was as good as always. At the end, while I was having my dessert, she noticed I finished my beer and last order was over, she offered me a glass of iced water. Excellent service!!

Had such an amazing experience at the Hard Rock Cafe after a day at a universal studios. Toko and Trang were very accommodating and kind. We advised in a passing comment it’s our honeymoon and after our meals all of a sudden a song came over the speakers. The tvs said congratulations and the whole staff came out and celebrated with us and provided a beautiful message on a plate with a sundae. Then took our photo and provided a beautiful written card and a drawing of us. I just can’t explain the little gesture absolutely made our night and day.  Thank you Hard Rock Cafe ♥️♥️

Hard Rock anywhere is cool. Hard Rock Osaka made Hard Rock, Rock Hard…..This location is amazing.
My server was Rebecca and she made the afternoon amazing. Rebecca is probably one of the best hostess I’ve had in a long time.
Excellent experience.

name: Il Bacaro
reviews:
It was an amazing dining experience from start to finish. The food felt genuinely authentic, with comforting, traditional Italian flavours and some really thoughtful seasonal options.

We shared a few dishes for lunch (photos attached - they look delish 😋 )The antipasto was fresh and generous, perfect for the table. The inferno pizza had a nice kick without being overwhelming, and the base was nice and crisp, it was definitely my favorite. The parmesan risotto with foie gras was super creamy and indulgent.

The seafood linguine aglio e olio was packed with flavour, with plenty of fresh seafood. The baked seabass was cooked beautifully and kept simple, which really worked. We also ordered the cheese platter, which was great for sharing and had a good mix of flavours.

Dessert did not disappoint !! The chocolate Etna was rich and satisfying, and the tiramisu was classic and well balanced.

Staff were friendly and attentive. and the cosy, old-building atmosphere made the whole meal feel warm and relaxed. Great portions, perfect for sharing with a group. Would definitely come back.

We stumbled upon this Michelin-starred restaurant while strolling down the street. Despite not having a reservation, they were incredibly accommodating and promptly found us a table. The daily special menu, displayed prominently on a blackboard. There’s a regular menu. We tried items from both, all were good.

We indulged in a delightful array of dishes, including the refreshing Mango Tango drink, the creamy Fresh Burrata, the succulent Boneless Chicken Thigh, the aromatic Saffron Spaghetti with Grilled Prawn, and the decadent Affogato. Each dish was meticulously prepared, bursting with freshness and flavor, without any overpowering saltiness. The pasta dish, in particular, surpassed my expectations and rivaled the culinary delights I had experienced in Naples.

Highly recommend Spaghetti Vongole and lamb shoulder.

Our culinary adventure was so enjoyable that we couldn’t resist returning for dinner. As we were leaving, we couldn’t resist making a reservation for another dinner, eager to savor more of their exquisite cuisine.

Excellent food, service, and environment.

However, we didnt quite understand 50% the English language spoken by the waiter who took our orders. This could create confusion. Maybe he spoke Italian English. We could only understand Malaysian English.

We ordered a special pizza of the day, $68. We requested a tuna version because my friend couldnt eat beef. The waiter agreed. We were served an excellent tasty pizza. But we were not sure if there was any tuna on the pizza. I mean, three of us couldnt recall tasting any tuna on the pizza. So, either there was so little tuna on the $68 pizza or the waiter forgot to tell the chef to put tuna on the pizza. I strongly recommend waiter to write down the orders of customer next time yeah.

The steaks were excellent. It came with tasty mushroom.

name: Cili Kampung - Suria KLCC
reviews:
Had such a lovely dining experience here! The food was packed with flavour — authentic, satisfying, and every dish we ordered met expectations. Nothing disappointed.

Special shoutout to the waiter who was warm, attentive, and genuinely pleasant throughout the meal. Service like that truly elevates the experience. And of course, great company is always a bonus 😉

Now let’s talk about the real show-stealer — the Bukit Kelapa! Wow. I’ve been eyeing this dish since my last visit to their Hartamas outlet, and it absolutely did not disappoint. Such talk of a town la this dessert — definitely a must-order.

Only one tiny feedback: please consider changing or replacing the seat cushions. I’m on the shorter side, and once seated, the cushion kind of sank in — feels like it’s been well-loved over the years 😂 A small comfort upgrade would make the experience even better.

Overall, a very enjoyable meal and a place I’d happily return to.

Honestly surprised this place has such good reviews, as the chicken curry and grilled squid weren’t as tender as we expected (we make better at home 😅), and I’m not even sure that was a coconut milkshake.

That said, the restaurant itself is nicely designed and has a cozy atmosphere. The servers however weren’t as accommodating as others we’ve been to. Good thing Madam Kwan next door saved our lunch.

I really enjoyed the authentic Malaysian food @Cili Kampung! Flavourful ingredients and generous portions of serving. Refreshing drinks.

Great ambience, nice decoration suit with the restaurant theme beautifully. Inside have basin to wash hand.

We waited for food not long which means they were not instant kind... Staff are friendly and attentive.

The restaurant was quite crowded and could get the queue long at peak hours.

If I have a chance I would like to go back for their food again, overall I'm happy with this place, product and service. Worth money we spend around 90rm each for this lunch.

name: Midtown BBQ Nagoya
reviews:
This place is very welcoming of foreigners which is great, a lot of international workers who speak English is great too. The food was delicious & the BBQ chicken was cooked perfectly, so juicy & marinated well. Loved the chips too so crispy and crunchy. Our let down was that we felt quite uncomfortable whilst eating, we sat at the bar where there was a female bar attendant & a male worker sat at the bar with us (who didn’t seem to be working at this time) but it felt like we were interrupting their flirting the whole time, it felt awkward to sit and eat next to them. We ate and left quick soon after that.

Loved the non alcoholic options too. Shirley temple was delicious.

Attended a party held by Aichi Connection and it was such a blast! Honestly I can't wait to have a meal here because the food smelled heavenly while we were taking care of our tickets.

There seemed to be indoor seating and outdoor seating so you can dine while watching Hori river. I also saw a second floor/loft, heard it was available for dinner parties.

It is an American BBQ restaurant, so a lot of the staff speak English very well. Such fun people at every corner of the place 😄

As a Canadian, I got recommended here. Flavors hit like back home and very friendly staff. Learned they brew 9 different ale’s locally here in Nagoya. Had the 1/2 rack spareribs + A5 brisket slice w/ brisket sauce poured over mashed potatoes. *chef kiss*

name: Restoran Sai Woo
reviews: Late night and was really hungry since we hadnt had our dinner yet. Tried char kwee teow, lemon chicken, and tofu hotplate. All were delicious and the serving time was very fast too. Love the char kwee teow the most I guess but we added some soy sauce since it wasn’t too salty when it arrived. The workers are nice so we really enjoyed eating here. Lemon chicken was also really good.

I come from Singapore!
What has that gotta do with this review....? Because one of our national dish is chilli crab, and here in KL I found one that will embarrass many and let them suck their thumb (or fingers)!
It was only because of the good reviews of the crabs, that I decided to  give this a try after so many times at Wong ah wah (famed for their chicken wings). And... I wanted to make a point to prove that Singapore's chilli crabs are better... But not this time!

But let's talk Abt my first dish, the Hokkien Mee... One of my fave dish in KL. But knowing this is a halal restaurant made me think ..how can they replicate this without pork lard?! Indeed, it does lack that lardy aroma but it was probably as best as they could have done. With their chicken pieces marinated well, it was still an above average dish. For this, I will give a 7 out of 10.
But but but ... This entire review is mainly focusing on their Chilli crab!
Mine was a small one @90rm, probably weighing about 450-500g.
Decent pricing at such a touristy area, but it's the taste, the freshness and tenderness that blew me away!
The meat was sweet and exceptionally (I say a 10 out of 10) tender. Not sure how they managed to do that! It was just unfortunate that I was eating alone and couldn't order the bigger crabs, as those would be so much easier to enjoy and savour the chunky meats!
The sauce was interesting... This may have divided opinions... It tasted very much of ginger, egg, capsicum... Not commonly used for chilli crabs in SG. And it has that tinge of acidity... Maybe from lemon, like or vinegar? The taste was familiar, but yet uniquely delicious. Everytime I managed to scrap a bigger chunk of meat, I would dip the whole thing into the sauce and momentarily time travel to paradise... Sedap!
The free 3 little steam buns I had were decent, but somehow, the sauce doesn't stick as well onto it, as would the usual fried ones I had in SG. But its free... Why shd I complain! ;p
Eventually, this was the first time I drank so much of the chilli crab sauce in my life... I almost wanted to order a bowl of white rice to go with it!
Only strange thing... The dish came within 10min. For a restaurant so busy, and to imagine cutting a live crab, and to cook, it's hard to imagine how they did it... Unless it's not live??? But who cares, when it taste better than most lives one I had.
The only better crabs, disregarding the sauce and how it was prepared was Jumbo in SG and the birth place of Sri Lanka crabs.... In Sri Lanka!
For a lack of budget, or for convenience, this KL crab is good enough for me.
My rating for the crab... 9 5 out of 10!.I will be back!

Overall dinner dining experience is fair.
The Restoran seems to be managed and run by friendly Burmese.

Ordered all small size dishes.
Escargots with dry shrimps gets a 7.5
Oyster and fried egg gets a 7

Enjoyed the spicy Kam Heong Balitung a lot especially !! Brought back loads of good memories …

name: Niku and...
reviews:
I recently visited “Niku and…” a small restaurant tucked inside Osaka’s Kuromon Market, and it was a delightful experience. I ordered the salmon and tuna sashimi, and both were exceptional remarkably fresh, with a clean, delicate flavor that showcased the quality of the ingredients.
The texture was perfect, practically melting in my mouth.
The atmosphere was relaxing yet welcoming, capturing the energy of the market while maintaining a cozy, intimate feel. The service was impressively fast, with staff who were warm, attentive, and genuinely friendly, making the meal even more enjoyable. Despite the high quality, the prices were very reasonable, offering great value for such fresh seafood.
My wife enjoyed it so much that she ordered extra sashimi to take home for a late-night snack, which speaks to how memorable the food was. Overall, Niku and… is a fantastic spot for fresh, affordable sashimi in a vibrant setting. I highly recommend it to anyone exploring Kuromon Market near Dontonbori.

The Kobe beef and salmon bowl at this place is a standout. The Kobe beef arrives perfectly seared—rich, buttery, and deeply savory—while the salmon bowl offers a lighter, silky contrast and well-balanced. Service is attentive, and the dining space feels clean and inviting.

Uncomfortable sitting area, not even a proper table and chair. Sushi rice bowl tastes normal like you eat sushi in other countries. Miso soup is the more terrible miso soup that I have ever try- very salty and taste like soy sauce plus water. Eel taste good, if you walk into this restaurant, recommend eel food only. Fairly expensive for this quality

name: KAPITAN TANDOORI HOUSE SDN BHD (TTDI)
reviews:
My first time here..😅. Its a mamak shop presented in a slightly upper level ambience. 😁

The place looks nice from the outside🤩 and even the interior looks cozy and spacious. It has its nearest rival being QBistro TTDI. Altho the food here its actually a mix of northern india meals like Kulchas etc.

Food wise , the taste was acceptable befitting the price which is higher than average mamak ie eg. Mohsin of TTDI.

Although, unfortunately ,i cant compliment on the efficiency/ hospitality of their mamak staffs 🤷🏻‍♂️. Despite potraying itself as an upgraded mamak, the staffs unfortunately for me, didnt really fit that upscale image. Maybe it was just my luck that nite to have this.😔 I would say, despite the classy ambience of the restaurant, the treatment from the staffs was.. crude- ish. 🤷🏻‍♂️😅

Some although appearing to understand bahasa Malaysia, still ended up taking our order wrongly and the best part was their reaction.  when i calmly told them, we ordered only 1 teh Tarek, the staffs immediate reaction basically gave me the impression , that the order was correct and i was giving him a problem. He took it away with not even a nod and cold expression. And the bill as u guessed it, had i not checked, had still recorded the wrong order. 🤷🏻‍♂️🤷🏻‍♂️.

And while taking our orders, believe it or not, our waiter ( ironically didnt live up to this jobscope 😭😂)was so restless and fidgeting like he was rushing to the toilet😂. How was i supposed to make my order with you fidgeting up n down like youre holding your pee?😂😂 I didnt ask him but i nevertheless quickly finished our orders avoiding from asking him any questions about the meals in the menu.

As far as he is concerned, i was supposed to know what all the menu is about🫩🫩. The size, the ingredients etc. no need to ask because he is " rushing to the toilet". 😂😂 Arghh stress la aku!😂

These are small issues but for a restaurant with this  brand and price range,  it should have been more accomodating. QBistro has one of the best staffs training. When they brought wrong orders, when told to them nicely, most of them will nicely nod and APOLOGISE. 🥰

Here, contrary to their semi classy mamak image, the staffs unfortunately lack the warmth and classy treatment which is normal if you visit the  normal curry scented ambience in a  normal mamak.

So, this was my first time and i was hoping to have a mamak standard equivalent to QBistro but alas, i feel for now QBistro ( altho not perfect) still reigns number 1 in ttdi.

For the owner of ttdi Kapitan, i know you often have  full house every day during lunch hour but dont let that factor makes yu nonchalant about keeping courtesy and pleasant treatment  as part of your sop.

We who r living nearby dont mind the above average price but pls make sure, your price and service tax is worth our visit. I just cant picture myself coming here again for a delightful experience but im sure it doesn't matter for u since so many other patrons will just come nevertheless.😂🤷🏻‍♂️

Competition is high in this neighborhood. A  few famous brands called Vanggey  and even Copper Chimney opened previously in TTDI but closed down and theres only a few known major reasons. One of it is definitely lack of customers which didnt justify the cost.

So thats it. 👍

Walking around Tmn Tun looking for something to eat before finally deciding on Kapitan and ordering the chilli beef with briyani.
The dish arrived accompanied by a small bowl of raita and a similar for curry.
The briyani somehow lacked the distinct flavours of ghee and saffron. What i tasted was merely coloured rice.
The beef was good. Spicy but not chili hot, and tasty.  The Curry and raita was unremarkable.
Service was good.

I was genuinely disappointed. Ordered their briyani special of the day—RM23, which is not cheap—and it was served at room temperature. The rice and chicken were not hot, not even warm, just sitting there like it had been left out. The rest of the dishes we ordered were the same: room temperature and completely underwhelming. For food at this price point, serving meals hot is the bare minimum. This was my first visit and it will definitely be my last. Not coming back.👎🏼👎🏼👎🏼👎🏼🤮🤮🤮

Apa macam dei?!!!!

name: Narrow Marrow
reviews:
The Toddy Lunas was a refreshing surprise, light and aromatic with a subtle boozy kick that felt both local and playful. It’s not overpowering that making it perfect.

I love the Espresso Bailey Tiramisu which has a tense espresso flavour, creamy texture and just enough Bailey’s to elevate it without turning it overly sweet.

The Matcha Latte was decent with a smooth finish but not too diluted or overly milky.

The eclectic interior adds character into the cafe, making it an ideal spot to unwind or catch up with friends, definitely not for kids.

Beautiful interior. Rustic concrete decor. Well designed with plenty of usable seating
Friendly staff. Comfortable air con and forest psytrance music.

4/5
Colombia/Brazil(Dark Roast): Hot Americano, Chocolate and slight acid notes. Smooth, but tastes more like a “Medium” roast.

4/5
Kaluea Tiramisu . It was good tiramisu. Airy and Creamy, but it had “Zero” alcohol taste. Plus the portion was “hella” small. Very Disappointed.

Would definitely visit again for their coffee options 👍☕️🙏

If this review was helpful, please give it a 👍

Happy Eats ☕️🍰🥩

A must-visit café if you’re in Penang! The place has such a chill vibe — great music, comfy seating, and a beautifully artsy interior. The open bar setup adds a nice touch, and the staff are super friendly and welcoming.

The drinks are delicious, and the menu itself is really creative and fun to browse through. Definitely try their tiramisu — it’s soft, not too sweet, and absolutely delightful.

Perfect spot to relax, sip a good coffee, and soak in the cozy atmosphere. Will definitely come back next time I’m in town! 🌿✨

⭐ Rating: 5/5 – Great coffee, lovely people, and amazing vibes!

name: Briyani Asif Bukit Bintang
reviews:
Wow! This food was incredible. The photos do not do justice to the taste, smell, and flavor.

Firstly, the place was very busy and the staff were incredibly welcoming, fast, and polite. I choose paneer masala, garlic naan ( must have), aloo gobi, and mango lassi. The spice level was perfectly suited to my preference and all dishes were very flavorful.

If you arrive to a neighboring hotel late in the evening like me, I suggest you look no further and come here for an excellent meal!

So today me & Family decided to jln jln cari makan at Pavilion Bukit Bintang. We were looking around for real Arab food. Not the kind where you find in shopping centers or mamak. After walking around we found this Place. Small looking Arab Food place. As we scan the manu outside we were greeted by a nice smiling 😃 Arab Guy . After some chit chat we decided to try la...And I must say this is Authentic Arab Food. Try the Teh Milk Tea & also The briyani rice..or yes..the nan is awesome.

I ordered Tandoori Roti and Lamb Kadhai. It was the worst food of my life that I have eaten till date. I am a chef in a restaurant and I know very well whether the mutton is fresh or not. I ordered Mutton Kadhai in the restaurant. It was completely raw from inside and cold like freezer temperature. The service here is not good at all. The food tasted very bad and was smelling bad. I was very forgetful. It was about to be 10 pm at night when I went there and not a single customer was there. I had to understand that their food is not good.

name: Emily's Steakhouse Kuala Lumpur
reviews:
We had a lovely dining experience at Emily Steak House, KL. The food was nice and delicious overall. The steak was well cooked, and we really enjoyed most of the dishes. The ravioli was slightly salty for our taste, so we shared our feedback with the crew. They were extremely kind and professional, and they immediately replaced the dish for us. That gesture truly touched us and showed how much they care about their customers.

The service was excellent, warm, and attentive throughout our meal. The ambiance was great—comfortable and relaxing—which made it a perfect place to enjoy our food. My husband and I felt very comfortable and truly enjoyed our time there.

Overall, we had a great experience and will definitely come back again. Highly recommended!

The location is on a quiet street, creating a peaceful atmosphere. It's easily accessible on foot from TRX Mall and the Sleeping Lion Hotel.

The staff is very friendly and professional, from booking via WhatsApp to arriving. We were served with the same level of service as hotel staff.

The food is well-presented and fresh. All the flavors are just right, not overpowering. The warm atmosphere adds to the deliciousness, making it a perfect place to gather with family and friends.

Had a great dining experience at Emily Steak House! The steak was cooked perfectly — juicy, tender, and full of flavour. The sides were delicious, and the overall atmosphere was comfortable and welcoming. Service was friendly and attentive too. Definitely a nice place for a satisfying steak meal. Will come back again!

name: Kutsurogiya
reviews: Come here for the experience & comforting home cooked feel dishes. The queue does get long so be sure to queue early. I prefer the wagyu dish overall which I forgot to take picture of it as it was delicious kobe beef if I am not wrong. If you are in Arima Onsen , this place is a must visit .

Reservations are not available, so we went early to wait in line.
We arrived around 4:00 p.m. and were still in the middle of the line.
Fortunately, when the restaurant opened at 5:00 p.m., we were able to get in with the first group. 😆

Very cozy environment inside, it’s very traditional Japanese setting.

Staffs were really helpful and kind.

Foods were great.

Unforgettable moments! 💗

It’s a wise choice to dine here as the food here is very decent. The favouring is not much and they are more original taste. I would recommend to order the beef set as compared to other seafood set. The queue is quite long so please be there at least 30minutes from the opening time to secure your slot.

name: Yin's Sourdough Bakery & Cafe • Mid Valley
reviews:
We had a late lunch here and the overall experience was good. The staff were friendly and welcoming. We ordered the big breakfast and the beef shakshuka, both served with sourdough bread. The portions were quite filling and the food was tasty.

We would definitely come back to try other items on the menu.

If you enjoy kombucha, do try their lemon version, it’s very refreshing.

We ordered salmon dishes and they were all right. It would have been good if we could change the butter rice for mashed potatoes for one order. We liked that the apple pie was not too sweet. Bill is for 3 pax.
