Went to this outlet in MV on a public holiday.. hmmmm..packed...luckily got a last table outside...made order thru their QR code .. but had to wait very long for food..hzzzzzzz.... guess thier kitchen can't cope with orders...anyway.. the salmon wrap i ordered was good..drinks decent .

name: Cafe Bistrot David
reviews:
I never realised Café Bistrot David was a concept by David Chin (of Dave’s Deli fame), with the guiding hand of his son Darren Chin, the Michelin-starred chef. I’ll admit - my expectations of Franco-Italian cuisine done locally were modest at best. But oh boy… I was gloriously, deliciously wrong.

While it’s clear that the seasoning has been thoughtfully fine-tuned to flatter local palates, the soul of the kitchen remains unmistakably European. The techniques, restraint, and balance speak with a continental accent - subtle, confident, and assured - leaving behind no doubt that this is French cuisine interpreted, not diluted - right down to the crisply starched linen table cloths.

The small plates, designed for sharing, were a parade of quiet triumphs - escargot, burrata, mussels, and charred cabbage - each bursting with flavour and fragrant with fresh herbs, butter, white wine, balsamic, citrus, and spice. They arrived not as mere starters, but as confident statements, winning over every palate around the table. The paella loaded with “cooked just right” fresh seafood was authentic down to the crispy, caramelized, toasted rice crust on the bottom - socarrat.

The steak, alas, was the rare blemish on an evening otherwise dripping with delights. The medium-rare Angus needed better aging, more precise trimming, bolder seasoning, and a surer hand with the carving.

And then there was our birthday cake, wrongly delivered to another table - a jarring blunder that jolted the rhythm of an otherwise flawless service, however briefly.

Fantastic food and great atmosphere! The beef bourguignon was rich, tender, and full of flavour… pure comfort in every bite. The croissant wagyu burger was another standout, buttery and flaky with perfectly juicy wagyu beef inside. You can tell everything is made with care and quality ingredients. Service was friendly and attentive, and the place feels warm and relaxed. A lovely spot for brunch or dinner with friends and family - definitely one of TTDI’s gems!

It was a very last minute dinner get together for my friend and I. Decided to try our luck and get a table at Cafe Bistrot David. Fortunately there was and we had plenty of time to eat n leave by 8.15pm for the next placing.

The food was delish. As it was just the 2 of us, we could only order the grilled honey corn cob (super addictive) and the mixed seafood paella. Lovely with the crusty rice base. Just a tad bit salty. Overall, it was a delicious meal! Must come back with the rest of the gang and try more dishes :)

name: Kasturi Walk
reviews:
Recently visited Kasturi Walk which is at walking distance from Jalan Petaling Market and next to Central Market.
It is an outdoor market which is good for shopping and local street vendors offering local food, souvenirs and handcrafted items.

This market is clean and well maintained. It just a short lane which is beautifully covered from top.
The prices are little high, you should always bargain and negotiate before buying anything and same applies in Central market also.
Recommended to walk through this place and exlpore the area.

Nice little market strip near Central Market and Chinatown. It’s a good place to walk around, check out souvenirs, and grab quick street food. Lively but not too overwhelming, especially in the morning.

"Where tradition takes flight 🪁✨
The golden wau - Malaysia's answer to the sky, adorned in intricate patterns that whisper stories of harvest seasons and ancient craftsmanship. Each curve and detail tells a tale of patient hands, bamboo frames bent with precision, and centuries of heritage painted in gold.
Once flown over rice paddies after harvest, these magnificent kites would dance in the monsoon winds, their humming melodies carried across the fields. Today, they stand as proud symbols of Malaysian identity - gracing currency, inspiring art, and reminding us that some traditions deserve to soar forever.
Looking up at this beauty against the Malaysian flag, I'm reminded that travel isn't just about places - it's about the stories woven into every culture, the artistry preserved through generations, and the moments when you pause to marvel at something truly extraordinary. The wau isn't just a kite. It's poetry in motion, history suspended in air, and a golden testament to the beauty of keeping traditions alive.
Have you ever encountered a piece of cultural heritage that stopped you in your tracks?

name: Jao Tim
reviews:
First time at Jao Tim..made possible by my daughter Rajes.Christmas eve treat for us..table lamps lit up added pomp to the atmosphere.
We were there to support and listen to Clinton Jerome Chua..our very own up and rising Malaysian born singer-songwriter who hails from Miri Sarawak.His songs from his latest album tribute to his dear mum who was part of his musical and singing journey that started from singing in the church choir.He was accompanied by Fadz on the guitar. We enjoyed the dining and music. The show ticket were priced RM120 /pax  with 60 minutes of beautiful. Christmas rendition and it was certainly full house and sold out night

Heard rave reviews about this place hence I headed there; saw that it was Christmas night so I thought it would be fun! Price was about RM80-100? I paid RM86 that night, just for entry. Quite pricey but I wanted to do something different.

It was quite a cozy space, probably fit only around 30pax?

The singers were alright, but not what I expected.

Also, I felt uncomfortable as it was getting a bit preachy halfway through, like I was at a sermon for a little bit as they were singing some church songs.

On the flip side, the sound system is great and location is pretty central.

Wish they would have expanded the food menu a bit more as they only offered sandwiches and rice bowl.

Would come again for their renowned jazz nights instead!

Had a great time listening to live music with Melissa Anne. Sound system was good enough and not to deafening even when seated right in front.

The drinks were hit and miss but with the snacks it makes up for it.

Do make reservations and get your tickets as walking in might not get you a spot in to enjoy the live music session.

name: Chan She Shu Yuen Clan Ancestral Hall
reviews: Sin Sze Si Ya Temple is a beautiful and historic temple near Petaling Street. The architecture is detailed with traditional carvings and red lanterns. Peaceful atmosphere despite being in the busy city area. Worth a short visit for cultural experience and photos.

With the Merdeka 118 skyscraper immediately behind this beautiful clan hall it creates an interesting juxtaposition between old tradition and modernity. Dedicated to Chinese sharing the surname Chan (and similar variations) the clan hall showcases gorgeous southern Chinese temple architecture, in particular the carvings on the facade and well crafted guardian statues. The inner courtyard is majestic and encases a serenity in a rather noisy area.
Beautiful and cosy Chinese temple. Entrance fee 5 MYR. Toilet 1 MYR. There’s filtered water available.

name: Shachirin Atsuta
reviews:
Really great food and the staffs are super kind and nice.

1. Great food with different spice level
2. Great service and really friendly
Shoyo ramen was good but the rest were excellent!
very good tasting, good ramen people were nice too i liked it.

name: Menya Kiyo Nagoya Sakae
reviews:
I got a Hachiko with a bit of extra ramen for a total of 980 yen. The shellfish-and-soy broth was absolutely fantastic -- the first sip was a "wow" of shellfish. The rare pork was very tender, moist, and flavorful -- oh, but if you're scared of rare, just swish-swish in the hot broth.
The noodle has an interesting texture to it. It's like in the middle of ramen and buckwheat soba.
One of the best bowls of ramen I had. In case I return to Nagoya, I will definitely have a meal again here.

We tried all 3 types of ramen.

It totally changed my perception of shoyu ramen, as I'm more of a tonkatsu ramen person.

Nice broth flavorful yet smooth.

I love the madake ramen the most.
Umai! Ramen were delicious! 😋 So good! The soup was also amazing. I enjoyed it very much. I don’t like the pan-fried dumplings though. The fillings were too wet and mushy.

name: Cara Caro Cafe
reviews: I had a great experience at Cara Caro! The staff are extremely friendly and make you feel welcome as soon as you walk in. Ordering is easy; you just place your order and make payment at the counter. The food is absolutely amazing, bursting with flavor in every bite, and it’s clear they put a lot of care into it. The drinks are also incredibly refreshing, perfect for cooling off or just enjoying alongside your meal. Overall, it’s a wonderful spot for a satisfying meal and a relaxing time.

Great Bohemian Cafe with instagramable places almost everywhere inside the cafe. Cozy Comfortable. Food was OK. Great for hangouts with friends and couples; slightly noise environment due to open *drink counter / half kitchen concept. 3/5 STARS.

Edited:  Here for the 4th time. Brought my parents here for breakfast, yum!! The breakfast sandwiches and half n half were good! But waited for almost 1 hour due to lots of customers. However, it's comfortable to just sit and enjoy the vibe.

1st impression upon entering this cafe, you felt at ease, relaxed, classic, perfectly comfortable. The food is not too cheap. I really like the sourdough French toast, it was yummy! The Ying Yong latte (mix of Earl Grey n coffee), the Earl Grey was overpowering, made the tea slightly bitter. Overall, it's a great place to chilled out and relax.

Revisited this place for lunch. The chicken roulette was superb! The chicken meat is so tender and moist👍👍. Gulai shrimp spaghetti was good too. As for the Earl grey cheese cake, it's not too cheesy, too bad I didn't taste the Earl grey flavor. But it's not too sweet that I like.

name: UNIQLO Fahrenheit 88
reviews:
On our arrival we stayed at Impiana hotel which was close to the Pavillion mall. So went there to hang around and have some dinner. We all like UNIQLO and we headed to it. We visited the Uniqlo Farenheit
They have a good location with 3 levels and an excellent view to the concert that was held there outside due to the New Year.
However, after my visit to Japan last year and UNIQLO prices there, these store prices seemed quite expensive to me.
As a result we did not purchase anything here and left.

Regularly been visiting Uniqlo in every different outlet, can’t imagine the bad experience happened in Fahrenheit 88 Bukit Bintang.
Overall was very good those SA are willing to help and keep on welcoming customer, until the payment section it make me up sad.
I think is the older staff only will provided this kind of customer service…

received bad service from first floor a female fitting room staff Today 13 feb about 1:40pm. At first I have already feel about her attitude when I walk in the fitting room. She mention about 4 clothes are allowed to fitting but i have 5. So i double confirm if its 4, and she just show four fingers without any words. Fine, maybe she’s busy with the clothes.

Second, when we finished fitting. She told us that two person are only not allowed in the fitting room and she even say that she have already mention it before we go in the fitting room. Okay I understand that two person are not allowed. But she should not lied. Bcoz I didn’t even know she said about it face to face and she even make a knock gesture. So assume that she got knock the door but we didn’t heard any knocking. So, I ask her to double confirm if she knocks and she say no. I feel falsely accused about this situation.

I hope Uniqlo can educate well about staff attitude and enhance the service quality. Even you have your own personal emotions please don’t bring it to your work. I believe nobody wants to be treated like that as a customer. Thank you.

name: The Steakhouse KL
reviews:
First visit to this establishment after reading through the reviews.

I ordered Caesar salad, smoked duck and the ribeye.

The smoke duck was paired nicely with avocado and orange- bringing a delightful experience to the palate.

The ribeye was juicy and portions were decent (300grams). It came with various types of salt and your choice of sauce.

The service takes the cake for me- staff were attentive to our needs and were prompt in their service.

Worth a visit if you are in the bukit bintang area.

Amazing steak, they give you little potato soup and warm bread to start with 6different salts. The steak melted in your mouth so if you want a good steak come here! Service also 10/10 super friendly staff thank you!

Stopped here based on previous Google recommendation. Have to say it's one of the best restaurants I've ever eaten in. Food was spectacular as was the service. Food was very reasonably priced and the house red wine was delicious. Do stop by if passing. You won't be disappointed.

name: Nasi Lemak Alor Corner
reviews:
I had anticipated a more favorable experience with the Nasi Lemak; regrettably, it did not meet expectations. The rice lacked the anticipated fragrance, and the fried chicken's flavor profile was unremarkable, though it might suffice for a group seeking a quick meal.

On a positive note, the stall's staff demonstrated commendable friendliness and efficiency.

The food was delicious. the nasi lemak portion was big for one person, I shared with the others.
Prices reasonable for us who looking for this type of food for breakfast.
They also provide various snack for 3-5 RM. They already packed which each consist 3-5 pieces of snack.

If you are Indonesia people, dont be worry, they have Indonesia people as they employee.

For the service, i love it. Because they always smile to the customer. Since i mever got it from most of stall that i visit before. Ita really thrilled me and feel satisfied with their service.

One of the best nasi lemak I have ever tasted.

It has a long queue but it is all worth it.
Love the atmosphere in the morning. Just sir bu the road side. It was actually calming. Enjoying the food while people watching.

Amazing morning vibe!

name: Siampot Buffet Steamboat & Grill KLCC
street: G1.108, GF, Golden Triangle, Jln Ampang
reviews: Tucked away behind Wisma Central, Siampot  was a fantastic discovery! For around RM40 per person, the buffet offers an incredible spread including a variety of meats, fresh vegetables, drinks, ice cream, and even delicious roti pisang. Their tasty (and spicy!) sauces really complete the experience. Service was excellent, with staff helpful at the start and letting us enjoy our meal at our own pace. The tender meat and fresh vegetables were highlights, and the lively atmosphere with students, added to the overall charm. Just a heads-up: there's a charge for leftovers, but since you cook your own food, that's perfectly fair. Highly recommended for a great steamboat experience!
Eventhough you think about the price, taking the exact amount of food to eat, no wastage, the food is fantastic here. I love it here with the KL vibes.

Had a steamboat here and everything was great, except for the tom yam soup. It was a bit too watery and lacked the rich flavor I was hoping for. If they could improve the tom yam, it would be perfect! Other than that, the food was good, and overall, it was worth the experience.

Their customer service is excellent .

name: GOCOCU
street: Minatojima Nakamachi, 6 Chome−10-1 ポートピアホテル本館 30F
reviews: Amazing spread with superb views. Delightful to have yakult and other healthy juices. Watermelon radish was a bonus find!
Great food . Honestly, not many varieties but enough for a breakfast meal. Good views and atmosphere though. Staff were very friendly and helpful.
Horrifically over priced for such a mediocre restaurant. It’s a trap.

name: Senju Osu
reviews: Came here to grab a takeaway. So lucky that there was no queue after 1500. The food is simple but tasty. 5 pc is just right for me. Seat is limited in the shop.

I stopped by here because I heard it was so delicious. There were about three tables to sit and eat, and there were a ton of products prepared to take away. But, of course, eating the meal while sitting there was the most delicious. The rice was slightly cooled, chewy and deliciously prepared, and the fried shrimp were savory and sturdy. The seaweed was also delicious.

A hidden gem in Osu area!

It's a rice ball stuffed with deep-fried prawn, half wrapped in seaweed sheet. Very delicious - rice is cooked well, taste is well balanced.

When we went there it is take out only day. So we took one package (5 pieces) and find a quiet spot in Osi to devour them... wish we got more, haha. The place itself is very small, only two table 4 seats each.

name: I Love KL Statue
reviews: How does a person remember their visit or a city? That's what this statue holds. Any tourist visiting the city would stop by this place for a capture to memorise their visit. The installation is put up around 600 meters from the popular central market, easily walkable for everyone. There're a couple of old historical goverment buildings around the statue, giving a historical view to the place. It's quite open, airy so you won't feel hot unless it's peak summer time of the day. Well maintained and clean for visitors to sit close to it and get a picture to rejoice their memories.

Located right at the edge of the historic district, the "I Love KL" statue is a vibrant, must-visit landmark that serves as the perfect gateway to the city’s heritage. Situated right in front of the Kuala Lumpur City Gallery and a short walk from the back side of Dataran Merdeka, this spot is incredibly photo-friendly and acts as a colorful, modern contrast to the grand British-era architecture that surrounds it.
The entire area feels like a step back in time. As you stand by the statue, you are treated to a view of majestic colonial buildings featuring red brickwork, arched windows, and copper domes, such as the Sultan Abdul Samad Building and the National Textiles Museum. These structures beautifully showcase the Neo-Saracenic and Moorish styles popular during the British period.
I highly suggest visiting during the day, especially in the early morning or late afternoon, to capture the best photos when the natural light hits the intricate building details and the bold red of the statue perfectly. Because all these landmarks are within a few minutes of each other, it is an easy, walkable experience that blends the city's modern branding with its deep historical roots.
What? Why? Because tourists need a snap to prove they were here. Perfect for a quick photo, but don’t expect anything else — it’s all about the picture moment!

name: Fujigaoka
reviews:
A chicken yakiniku restaurant. The main grilled meats are "waka," a tender meaty chicken, and "nami," a chewy parent chicken, marinated in a miso-flavored sauce.
Other tasty dishes include "seseri" and "sunagimo.
To top off the meal, be sure to order the Torinabe Udon.
All the dishes are tasty and inexpensive, so you will be satisfied.
The restaurant is affiliated with Fujigaoka Shokudo in Hisai City.
駐車スペースはすごく多い。

夕飯は鈴鹿市南部にある｢ふじがおか｣へ。
松阪名物の鶏焼肉がいただけます。

訪問したのは平日の午後5時前。
定刻より早めにオープンしていたようです。
既に2組が入っていました。
6時頃には店前の駐車場もほぼ満車です。
土日はもっと凄いんだろうな。

【とり焼 若+セセリ+キモ焼+砂キモ焼+めし 大】
やっぱり鶏焼肉で一番美味いのは若鶏。
プリプリジューシーな食感で油乗りもよく、
濃厚な味噌ダレと絡んでさらに美味しい。
セセリは数量限定のため個数制限あり。
こちらもコリコリ食感が楽しめます。

キモ焼も捨て難いです。
柔らかいキモはなぜこんなにも美味いのか。
とろける舌触りに鉄分を感じる深い旨味。
大人の味ですよね。

松阪まで行かなくてもレベルの高い鶏焼肉が
頂けるのは嬉しい限りです。
ごちそうさまでした。

以前友人に教えてもらい彼女の良子と初訪問させて頂きました。
初心者なので取り敢えず「とり焼き」の「若」を2人前と数量限定の「せせり」を2人前と「キムチ」「手羽揚げ」と「みそ汁」を注文しました。

手羽揚げは塩コショウか甘辛ダレが選べますが塩コショウでサッパリ頂きました。
2人ともご飯は最初に「大」を注文しましたが少食の僕でも更に「大」をおかわりして食べてしまう程食欲がかき立てられペロリンチョでした。
その後「とり焼き」の「並」を単品で注文して最後に「とり鍋うどん」で〆ました。
とり肉ってこんなに柔らかくて美味しいもんなんだとつくづく思いました。
食べ終わって後も胃がドーンとしてないし
連日でも行けそうです。
平日なのですぐに入れたし良かったー(^ ^)

name: Atsuta Houraiken Matsuzakaya B1F Shop
street: Sakae, 3 Chome−３０−8 Matsuzakaya Nagoya Main Building, B1F
reviews:
This is one of the most unique restaurants I’ve had the pleasure of dining at. My family and I visited without a booking, so we had to wait for a bit until our queue number was called. However, once inside, we were treated to a delightful dining experience.

We started with a few side dishes, including some incredibly fresh sashimi, which was absolutely delicious. We also enjoyed a serving of grilled unagi, which was perfectly cooked and full of flavor.

The highlight was the main unagi dish—it was filling, flavorful, and unlike anything I’ve had before. What made it even more special was the personalized touch: they provide specific instructions on how to enjoy the dish, adding to the unique experience.

If you find yourself in Nagoya, I highly recommend stopping by this restaurant for a memorable lunch or dinner. You won’t be disappointed!

The eel rice is very tasty. We also ordered the fish liver. It’s a very small dish but tastes so good. It definitely worth going.
We arrived at 6pm and waited for 30minutes to get our table. When we left, there was already a long queue and the waiting time was 60 minutes. So you should go as early as possible to avoid crowds.

Can really taste the charcoal in how they roast the unagi, not many places do it like this! We got there on a Sunday at 3pm and had to get a ticket to wait 1.5 hours for a table. Luckily you're situated in a really big department store so go early, get your ticket and walk around and come back at your allotted time

name: Flaon • Petaling Street
reviews: Very nice cafe, can catch the fish and bring home! Able to see merdeka 118 too! The view is stunning 🤩 the food is beautiful too! Love it so so much!
Lemonade cold brew so good 👍🏻 Kids friendly, can catch fish here
Very good 👍🏼 their coffee is very good. Their desserts are very delicious too! Worth visiting

name: MountBatten Cafe
reviews:
Walked past yesterday on the way from Lokl Café (which was excellent) and came back purely because of the name. Glad we did.

Ordered my usual caramel latte with oat milk… but no caramel here. Instead — Biscoff or butterscotch. I went with the butterscotch and it was spot on. Rich, smooth and properly comforting. Sweet but balanced, not overpowering. They’ve got oat milk too, which is always a win.

Quirky moment — every table for four had a “strictly reserved for 3 pax or more” sign. Completely understand the rule when it’s busy, but it did make for a slightly awkward scene: two couples in an otherwise empty café, seated right next to each other while the larger tables remained off-limits. A bit funny, a bit strange.

That aside, great coffee and a relaxed vibe. Worth a stop if you’re wandering this part of KL.

We stumbled upon this cafe while looking for something sweet. We ordered the tiramisu cake and a butterscotch latte.
The ambience was very calm and relaxing as there were only a few customers at that time.
The staff were friendly and welcoming, and the songs played made the atmosphere even more enjoyable 😄😄. My friends and I spent around 2 hours there doing some fun activities ⭐.
We would definitely come again to try their other dishes 😺.

I’ve lost count of how many times I’ve had Mountbatten’s fish and chips — it’s absolutely to die for. So good every single time. Their main dishes are consistently satisfying and well done. The only downside for me is that the cakes are often a bit too dry, and the air-conditioning can feel slightly warm at times. That said, their flat white is excellent and very reasonably priced at RM12 compared to other local cafés. Overall, still a solid spot for comforting food and good coffee.

name: Kobe Steak Meriken Wharf Motomachi
reviews:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ An Unforgettable Kobe Beef Experience

We had the pleasure of dining at Kobe Steak Meriken Wharf Motomachi during our recent trip to Kobe, and it exceeded all expectations! This place is an absolute gem for anyone seeking authentic Kobe beef in a welcoming atmosphere.

The food was phenomenal. We ordered both the rib eye and sirloin, and both cuts were cooked to perfection - incredibly tender, marbled beautifully, and bursting with flavor. Every bite literally melted in our mouths. The quality of the ingredients was evident throughout the entire meal, from the appetizers to the dessert.

The ambiance struck the perfect balance between elegant and comfortable. The restaurant has a warm, inviting atmosphere .

What truly set this restaurant apart was the staff and chef. Everyone was incredibly friendly and attentive without being intrusive. The staff went out of their way to make sure we were comfortable and even helped us navigate the menu with patience and helpful recommendations. The chef is also very friendly and engaging as well.

If you're in Kobe and want an authentic Kobe beef experience with exceptional service, we highly recommend Kobe Steak Meriken Wharf Motomachi. It's worth every yen!

Highly recommended! 🥩✨

Exquisite Kobe beef plates, the Beef Sashimi is delicious as well. But the best part is the staff’s attention.

We walked in without reservation (I recommend /setting a reservation in advance as place is usually packed) and were welcome to our seats. We were asked about which country we were from, we got a flag of said country, and the whole experience was in English.

We then met the owner, who also cooks the meat for you. He’s a great guy who will make conversation about your country, while exchanging jokes and making sure you’re welcome. He invited us a glass of Japanese wine that would pair great with the meat, and it did.

After our food he took pictures with us, gave us traditional Japanese clothing and a katana for the picture as well. I had q great time, and I’m sure you will too. We will definitely come back.

First kobe beef experience in my life.

& This restaurant did not disappoint.

I thought A5 beef was good this was a whole new level!! There is lots of kobe beef restaurant out there but if you have the chance do come here!!

The experience is like fine dining & the server & master are all super friendly & nice!! There is a nice complimentary key chain & dessert on our trip. Super nice of them!!

Server speaks great english as well!

I felt like i was part of the family warm they had there! A really super awesome experience 100/5 star.

Super highly recommend this place!!

name: SARIKAKA
reviews: Despite there are quite a few other restaurants close by, we decided to come give it a try... Although they have a rather limited and small menu and do not have a big number of choices, their noodles is very good and their fried chicken as well. Their service is pretty good as well... But depending on which staff you fall into, you may have a waiting staff more gentle than the others. We enjoy their food, thank you for your hard work! But since this is Taiwanese cuisine, may I suggest you expand a bit more the menu so customers can have more than 1 choice of rice to choose from your menu? May I suggest you hve fried rice? We will come back in the future and taste your food again! We hope you will be so kind as to expand the menu to include more rice items or fried rice items? Thank you for your hard work!

taiwanese home cooking 🥰🥰🥰

cute little place.  very friendly staff who speak english.  the cucumber was amazing.  highly recommend the cabbage dumplings and the dry noodle beef.  side veggies dishes very good as well.
Really delicious Taiwanese food! The jipai, beef noodles, and Taiwan Ramen were incredible, and we finished off with some mango shaved ice.

name: Temple of Fine Arts KL
reviews:
Saw very nice Indian artifact & collectibles there .. on display, for sale, also Indian clothes & fashion accessories. Was there for lunch .. parking is a nightmare.
Food served in restaurant is vegetarian.. nice food .. mango lassi is good

Buffet Vegetarian. RM30 for the buffet lunch and if you order Bru Coffee is separate charges. Staff are friendly, superb classic ambience, good music and good food.  You should go and try out for yourself. They have lunch and dinner.

I was totally disappointed with my experience when I called to enquire classes for my kids. The person who answered the call (a male staff who refused to share his name) was extremely rude in responding to my questions. Even before I could ask my next question, he hung up on me.

I called back politely to continue my enquiry, but he bluntly said “No, I don’t have time to answer” and ended the conversation again. If a receptionist or front-desk staff behaves this rudely to potential customers, I can’t imagine how students would be treated.

I strongly urge the management to address this matter immediately. Please review your CCTV footage dated 8 October 2025 at 5:38 PM for verification. Incidents like this reflect poorly on the organisation’s professionalism and customer service standards.

name: Nasi Lemak Uncle Bob Jalan Alor, Bukit Bintang
reviews:
If you're around Bukit Bintang, you've seriously gotta check out Nasi Lemak Kukus Uncle Bob. We loved it so much that we actually ended up doing take-away two nights in a row! On the first night, we tried the Ayam Goreng (fried chicken), and it was spot on, perfectly crispy and paired so well with their fragrant steamed rice.

We couldn't get enough, so we went back the next night specifically to try the Paru Balado (spicy lung). It was just as satisfying, with a great spicy kick that was super flavorful. Everything we had was great, and the best part is the price is really affordable. It’s a total win for a satisfying meal in KL, and we highly recommend it!

The Best Nasi Lemak everrr in Bukit Bintang. open 24 hours makes us easily to looking food if we are hungry in the midnight, I always brunch and dinner here for my 6 days in KL . TASTE Good also!! my favorite is Paru Sapi😍,  waiters and seller they are so friendly, and nice person..

The best Nasi Lemak in Bukit Bintang Kuala Lumpur. open 24 hours, good taste, clean, and staff sooo friendly and keep smiling while they deserve the food.. my favorite is Rendang daging, I always eat here for brunch and dinner.. its make my trip more Happy🫶🏼🥰

name: Gourmet Street at Lalaport BBCC
street: Ground Floor, LaLaport BBCC, 2, Bukit Bintang City Centre, Jln Hang Tuah
reviews:
Gourmet Street at Mitsui Shopping Park LaLaport is an interesting dining zone with plenty of potential. Designed as a dedicated food street within the mall, it brings together a wide mix of restaurants and cafés in one lively area, making it convenient for groups with different tastes.

The space is especially pleasant in the evening—once the lights come on, the atmosphere feels warm and inviting, giving it a charm that encourages you to linger. The variety of dining options is one of its strengths: some outlets offer genuinely authentic dishes, others focus on more creative or modern menus, while a few are fairly average. Still, the overall setting helps make dining here an enjoyable experience.

That said, Gourmet Street feels slightly limited by the mall’s 10 pm closing time, which cuts short what could otherwise be a vibrant late-night dining destination. With longer hours, it could truly come into its own as a go-to food spot rather than just a mall dining area.

Gourmet Street at LaLaport BBCC is the place to go if you're looking for a peaceful escape for lunch. We went on a weekday and loved how peaceful it was. No crowds, just good food, reasonable price and a super chill vibe. Perfect for a relaxing lunch break.

⭐ Vibrant and Cozy: A beautifully designed, pedestrian-only food street.
⭐ Diverse Cuisines: A great mix of Japanese, Western, Mediterranean, and local fare.
⭐ Peaceful Vibe: Surprisingly quiet on a weekday! We had a relaxing, stress-free lunch.
⭐ Alfresco Dining: Many spots offer outdoor seating, perfect for people-watching.

An open air concept walkway, not inside the mall, where you can find plenty of restaurants and cafes. Quite a nice place to explore with natural lighting or enjoying your food while it is raining.
Located at Lalaport Bukit Bintang City Centre.

name: Chateraise Patisserie @ Isetan Concourse KLCC
reviews: One of the best mochi in the KL! There, I said it! Never a day I'd go to KLCC without getting one of it. So yummy! My favourite would be the green tea because the flavour was so fresh forward and unapologetically strong. And the chocolate was slightly dark which gave an excellent dance of cocoa on the palette. For the mango, my nephew said it was tad sweet yet the cream balanced it. So very gooood!

It happened that my daughter had a birthday and the first thing that came to mind was Chateraise. There are so many choices, it must be delicious, and it is definitely said to be fresh from Japan. This is my daughter's favorite. All the breads are also decorated very beautifully.

On Friday, 02/05/25, I placed an online order for a cake with a requested delivery time between 3:00 PM and 3:30 PM.
At around 3 PM, I noticed a driver had accepted the delivery, but by 4 PM, the cake had not yet arrived.
I contacted the driver and was informed that the vehicle had broken down. However, the system showed the cake as already delivered.
I then attempted to contact the store. Although it was difficult to reach them at first, I eventually got through after multiple calls.
To their credit, once I was able to speak to someone, the staff responded responsibly and followed up on the issue.
They arranged for a replacement cake to be delivered and also included some mochi as a goodwill gesture.
Overall, while the experience was initially frustrating, I appreciate the store's effort to resolve the matter.

name: Unafuku Atsuta
reviews: Found this quaint little spot selling unagi don, which we found to be a Nagoya speciality, on our stopover during our drive from Tokyo to Osaka. They serve a two-style unagi don, one with the typical glaze and another salted. Highly enjoyable experience and a great find! Reviews did not disappoint!
We came from Thailand for this restaurant. Such a brilliant and fascinating tastewith nice staffs. Highly recommended.
Great place to eat fresh and delicious unagi. I especially enjoyed the one without sauce which I haven’t tried before

name: TEPPAN DINING 集 栄店
reviews:
Teppan Dining is a Japanese interactive culinary experience where chefs cook fresh meats, seafood, and veggies on a large, flat iron griddle (teppan) right in front of guests, often with theatrical flair and communal seating, focusing on fresh ingredients cooked with skill and served hot. It's known for dishes like teriyaki chicken, fried rice, and grilled steak, offering a social, transparent, and engaging meal.

Key Characteristics:

Interactive Cooking: Food is prepared in full view, allowing diners to see the chef's techniques and ensure freshness.

Communal Atmosphere: Guests often sit around the griddle, fostering interaction and a lively dining environment.

Theatrical Elements: Chefs might perform knife tricks or other showmanship, adding to the entertainment.

Fresh, High-Quality Ingredients: Focuses on premium meats (steak, shrimp, chicken), fresh vegetables, and sometimes sushi.

Menu Staples: Includes fried rice, yakisoba, miso soup, and savory pancakes (okonomiyaki).

Experience Details:

Setting: U-shaped seating around a central griddle, with an open kitchen concept.

Dishes: Proteins (beef, shrimp, scallops), vegetables, fried rice, noodles, and dipping sauces.

Authenticity: While Western versions feature antics, traditional Japanese teppanyaki is more refined, focusing solely on the ingredients and slow cooking.

Etiquette & Tips:

Respect fellow diners' personal space at communal tables.

Engage with the chef and enjoy the show.

Try dipping sauces and traditional sake for a fuller experience.
Really enjoyed the food being cooked in front of me. Quite expensive for a typical lunch but it was worth it. I love the aquarium in the middle too.

What surprised  me when entering the restaurant was the huge aquarium with baby sharks swimming inside. Besides visually stunning, it served as a privacy screen in the center of a huge U shaped 18 seater counter table.

The staff were really  friendly and attentive . Young Chef Toy Yamashita was our assigned chef. He speaks a little English , and cheerfully communicated and answered all our questions as he cooked effortlessly. While we liked every dish served, the lobster thermidor and Kagoshima wagyu steak were outstanding , and we ate up every grain of the special rice - both steamed and fried.

Thank you for such a delicious and delightful meal and evening! Certainly recommended for special occasions.

name: Kitchen Nagoya
street: ＪＲ名古屋駅 Nagoya Umaimon Dori, 1 Chome-1-4 Meieki
reviews: Tried the Nagoya speciality Miso Katsu… it’s a unique twist to the regular tonkatsu. Located inside the JR Nagoya Station. It’s a must try when visiting here…
First time eating Nagoya's specialty. The food is made very well. Full of flavor and the meat is tender. Rice is super soft. The chicken wings were delicious. The place is busy during dinner.

- Miso pork with chicken wing
- Miso pork with fried shrimp
Food was great and not too salty. Chicken wings were juicy and spiced well.
The best thing is free refills for the sliced cabbage, miso soup and rice!
Quite popular! We waited a while for 3 sets of people but the line moved fast and they helped order before entering.
Worth to give it a try!

name: Kitchen Nagoya
street: Meieki, 1 Chome−1−4 JR名古屋駅名古屋うまいもん通り 太閤通り口
reviews: Tried the Nagoya speciality Miso Katsu… it’s a unique twist to the regular tonkatsu. Located inside the JR Nagoya Station. It’s a must try when visiting here…
First time eating Nagoya's specialty. The food is made very well. Full of flavor and the meat is tender. Rice is super soft. The chicken wings were delicious. The place is busy during dinner.

- Miso pork with chicken wing
- Miso pork with fried shrimp
Food was great and not too salty. Chicken wings were juicy and spiced well.
The best thing is free refills for the sliced cabbage, miso soup and rice!
Quite popular! We waited a while for 3 sets of people but the line moved fast and they helped order before entering.
Worth to give it a try!

name: Dayang Ros Cafe & Flower Boutique
reviews: Did not go to the cafe, always there for the flowers. Price is very reasonable. The flower arrangement is gorgeous. They know how to mix the flower to produce beautiful bouquets.  There are 2 separate shops, so do check out both of them.

I ❤️ 😍 💖 ❣️ 💕 💘 ❤️ 😍 💖 ❣️ 💕 💘  all the flowers.

Here also has a simple cafe. Lunch time got set lunch which is value for money.

The atmosphere of dining at AC seated place and clean. Very well decorated.

I just bought the flower from them.
There was a small issue with my order, but Dayang Ros handled it really well. They were sincere, responsive, and made the effort to fix things properly. I truly appreciate the way they took responsibility and made sure I was happy in the end. Because of that, I would definitely recommend them 😊

name: 創作鮨ダイニング ICHIZUSHI
reviews: Like many family run business, Cosy and friendly. Most imptly serves really great sushi/sashimi. Finding the place may be challenging especially after dark but just follow your Google Map.
Nice staff n good food good atmosphere
Delicious food  😋

name: Kuan Yin Temple
reviews: Right next to the monorail station, this elevated little gem of a Buddhist temple is a pleasant surprise being somewhat in the shadow of the bigger and more famous Clan temple across the road (Chan She Shu Yuen Clan Ancestral Hall). The statues (esp. the bodhisattvas) are rather cute and fearsome at the same time. There's some lovely decorated wall titles and considering the busy road outside it's a haven of quiet and serenity.

Went there on 31 January. Walking distance from a MRT station.

Not a lot of visitors even though it was a weekend. Have various deities present, including Guan Yin, Fortune God and Guan Gong.

Did not take photos inside the temple as a form of respect.
One if the oldest Toaist Temple in KL, for those that do not want to drive can hop to the LRT and stop at “Maharajalela” station.  By the way their opening hours is from 9:00am.

name: ラバンビ
reviews: Lamb yakiniku place, delicious meat and other foods! Reasonable prices, nice atmosphere.

駅前のサンファーレから桑名一番街に抜けてすぐにある「Rvambi」は“三重県唯一のラム肉専門店”なんだそうです。商店街中ほどの曲がった突き当りにあるんですが、とっても明るい看板や提灯が目印になっているのでかなり目立ちます。

店内は暗めなんですが各テーブルをスポットライトで照らしていて高級感のあるインテリアです。焼肉もできるので各テーブルにノンスモークグリルが置けるように換気扇が配管されていますね。オレは一人だったし焼肉の予定はなかったのでカウンターでゆっくり静かに飲ませていただきます。

暑い日だったのでまずはレモンサワー。シャーベットのような氷が乗っていて見た目も涼やかです。

肉物のメニューを待つ間に安定のポテサラをいただきます。ゴロゴロとしたジャガイモなんだけどクリーミーで少し酸味のあるドレッシングを使っていてサッパリした味わい。

最初のラム料理は「仔羊のユッケ（990円）」。柔らかく臭みの少ない仔羊を特製ダレで絡めたユッケはとっても食べやすくラム初心者でも行けそう。

ラム料理といえば「ラムチョップ（590円）」。香草パン粉で表面をカリッと焼き上げてあって香ばしくて美味しい。
通常の「ラバンビの元祖ラムチョップ」以外にも「トマトチーズラムチョップ」や「ガーリックチリラムチョップ」などもあっていろいろ食べ比べるのも楽しそうですね。
今回はちょっと一杯の感じで入ったのでジンギスカンは食べませんでしたが、仔羊の一頭買いをしているだけあっていろいろな部位が食べられるジンギスカンの食べ比べなども良さそう。

珍しいラム肉専門のお店✨
専門店ならではの色んなラム料理が食べられます。生ハムや串カツ、ユッケや焼肉などなど。ラム好きにはたまらないですね〜🌝
満席なことが多いので週末は要予約です！
とっても美味しかったのでまた行きたいです〜

name: Jigokudani Valley
reviews: Trail is closed now but you can still the volcano on the way from mikurigaike pond to raichoso. You can smell the sulfur smell and you can see gas coming out from the valley.

Visited may 23rd
Roughly 15 min walk from the Murodo main hub. Very unexpected sight, and i was so happy to find out Murodo was more than just the wall
It is so good to walk around while seeing the beautiful mountain peaks of Tateyama. as well as Mt. Tsurugi.

name: Tachibana
reviews: Stumbled upon this place through google reviews. Loved the sushi especially the battera and anago - SOOO flavourful and good! Kid’s meal options and kids chairs available. English menu also available upon request.

1100 yen for a very luxurious lunch set. I paid 1760 for a VERY luxurious sashimi boat. The lunch sets come with a salad, small side dish, and a very delicious red miso soup. Very cheap for what you get.

Service is very friendly, toilets are clean with proper hand soap and paper towels.

This place is a hidden gem you should definitely consider if you're visiting the nearby Atsuta Jingu Shrine!
Lunch set tastes good and no queue

name: Gurney Drive
reviews: Gurney Drive is the heart of Penang's nightlife! Come here at sunset to enjoy the sea breeze, then head to Gurney Drive Hawker Center. After eating, take a leisurely stroll along the newly renovated Gurney Bay; the area is very neat, pedestrian-friendly, and has a very modern vibe. If you feel too hot, just cross over to Gurney Plaza or Gurney Paragon mall. A must-visit place if you want to experience both the modern and traditional sides of Penang in one location.

The new park in Gurney Drive, built on reclaimed land has created a large recreation area for both locals and tourists. Best to visit in the early morning or before dusk when it's cooler. Only a portion is completed as some areas are still under development.
Famous for local street food and seaside vibes. Plenty of food choices at night. A nice place to walk and eat.

name: Teppanyaki Grill Tajima
street: Minatojima Nakamachi, 6 Chome−10-1 神戸ポートピアホテル 本館2F
reviews:
Although I was able to converse in Japanese, the restaurant’s staff were able to assist me and welcome me in English. I really appreciated this!

The host also provided us with a special small gift after I stated that we were celebrating our proposal. I was extremely impressed by him and this kind gesture!

We ordered the regular beef course and it certainly wasn’t just “regular”. The chef prepared the food in front of us and explained each ingredient. He offered us with options for toppings and also gave us suggestions. The meat choices were tough to choose from, but ultimately it felt as though any choice would be a good one.

The meat was by far the most impressive part. I can certainly say without a doubt that it’s the best I’ve ever had and will ever have. I’m really glad that I ended my first day in Kobe at this restaurant.

I’ll recommend this place to my family, friends and coworkers for sure.
ランチに黒毛和牛のコースを楽しみました。庶民なのでなかなかこういうところに来る機会がないのですが、やっぱり良いものを使った料理は良いですね。美味しく、ボリュームもちょうどよく、元気が出ます。

2月14日
御正月プラン

美味しいのは当然
その上で、おしぼりの気遣い。
最初は暖かく交換時は冷たいおしぼり。

ご馳走様でした

name: Chulia Street Lok Lok
reviews: This is my favorite Lok Lok stall. It's affordable, has a wide variety of choices, and the dipping sauces are delicious. Every time I visit Penang, I always come back to eat here

There are plenty of choices. Strongly recommended to dip with the own made stay sauce. It goes well with the sauce. Price is  affordable as the portion of each stick quite big. Must try if u are in Georgetown
No-frills DIY kinda lok lok store - pick the skewers you want, boil it in the pots, and then proceed to pay. Don’t forget to add the sauces - they are what make the skewers tasty and sinful!

name: Jalan Alor, Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
reviews: If you find seller didn't puy price in the menu, better you ask before deciding to buy. Iam shocked when i pay for ice milo much more expensive than at the restaurant. Be careful for moslem, many snack and dishes here are not halal. Better you ask
Avoid this place if you prefer hygiene
The best eating street in Kuala Lumpur.a whole street big around 5.00pm no. Traffic allowed andvif you like seafood you will love JL Alor

name: Chazu
reviews:
すご〜く美味しかったです！
以前から気になっていたお店でした。
小さなお店ですが大人気店の様で、店舗前の駐車場では足りずに別の場所で待機しました。
優しいオーナーさんがメニューの紙を渡してくださり、メニューが決まったらメッセージで送信してください、とのこと。
駐車場が空いたので移動し入店。
カウンター5席のお店で、長居してのんびりするタイプのお店ではないので回転が良く、意外と早く入ることが出来ました。
炙りしめ鯖とたたきマグロのお茶漬けにしました。
しめ鯖の炙り具合い、酢締め具合が本当にちょうど良くてびっくり。
たたきマグロも筋や脂臭さもなく滑らかでまろやか。
結構海鮮丼は食べに行きますが、このネタはいいけどこれはダメ、と当たり外れが多い中、しめ鯖たたきマグロともとても美味しく大満足のランチでした。
はじめに観た時にはちょっと少ないかな…と思いましたが、お茶碗の底が結構深く、更に最後はお出汁でお茶漬けにして頂くのでお腹いっぱいになります。
お店もオーナーさんのご趣味とのことで
雰囲気いっぱいの素敵な装飾となっています。
また伺い、今度は別のメニューを頂いてみたいと思っています。
ご馳走様でした！

ここはお茶漬け専門店ですね！中に入ると超絶イケメンのお兄さんが出迎えてくれました🙌笑もうそれだけで満足ですが、店内は目をひくオブジェがずらっと並んでおり一気にお店の雰囲気に包まれました😌インテリア雑貨はお兄さんが厳選して飾り付けされてるみたいで空間作りに熱心な方なんだなと思いました！😲👏
ここではサーモン系のメニューが好評みたいなので全部乗ってる"サーモンとまぐろのたたき茶漬け"を注文しました〜！お茶漬けだけかと思ったらそれぞれ違うジャンルの小鉢も一緒に添えられており色鮮やかでした🙌✨そして実食！もうめちゃめちゃ美味しかったですね👍サーモンの焼き加減､香り､食感とまぐろのたたきのとろけるような食感と濃厚な旨味が合わさり極上でした🙇‍♂️薬味で更なる味変を楽しめたので大満足でした!!😋次はドリンクも注文します😉👍✨

開店時間前でしたが、車を止めていると店の方が出てきて、どうぞお入りくださいとの事。入り口のそばにはかわいいネコちゃん！
店内は狭くてカウンター5席のみですが、凄くいい感じに仕上げられています。
「博多明太とハラスのお茶づけ」、「サーモンのレアステーキと北海道産たこの茶漬け」をいただきました。
運ばれてきた品を一目見て、その美しさに驚き、そして食べてみて、いわゆる『お茶漬け』をここまでの料理に高めることが出来るのかと感心しました。
丼の上には豪華なネタが敷き詰められていて、自分でアツアツの出汁をかけていただきます。
少しお値段はしますが、それだけの価値は十分あります。
食後のコーヒーも美味しかったし、カフェオレなんかカップ満々でした。
もう少しゆっくりしたかったけど、後からの客の事を考えて早々に退散しました。

なお、駐車スペースは店前の2台分だけですが、何せ席数が少ないので、充分かと‥

name: 水族館南側緑地
reviews: Amazing
The night view is different !🌿🌿
水族館南側緑地にある広場。景色が良くて緑もあって、ベンチもあり散歩には最適だと思います。

name: Old Kuala Lumpur River of Life Mural
street: River of Life, Leboh Pasar Besar
reviews:
The Old Kuala Lumpur River of Life Mural is a striking visual tribute to the city's rich history and cultural heritage. Depicting scenes from Kuala Lumpur’s early days as a tin mining settlement to its rise as a modern metropolis, the artwork blends intricate details with vibrant colors, making it a compelling attraction.

Situated along the River of Life, this mural enhances the area’s transformation into a scenic waterfront destination. The combination of history, art, and urban renewal makes it a must-visit for both locals and tourists.

Beautiful and meaningful mural completed in 2020 as part of Kuala Lumpur’s River of Life project. Located near Masjid Jamek, it vividly depicts scenes from the city’s past, including traditional riverside life. The mural adds charm to the riverbank area and is a great photo spot. A nice surprise for anyone exploring central KL on foot.

The Old Kuala Lumpur River of Life Mural is a captivating and vibrant addition to the city's landscape. The intricate artwork beautifully depicts the river's historical significance, showcasing scenes of bustling trade, cultural activities, and the evolution of Kuala Lumpur. The murals serve as a visual journey through time, offering a glimpse into the city's past and its connection to the river.
The vibrant colors and detailed illustrations make the murals a feast for the eyes. Whether you're a history enthusiast or simply appreciate street art, the Old Kuala Lumpur River of Life Mural is definitely worth a visit.

name: Tanamera
street: Central Market, G25, Jalan Hang Kasturi
reviews:
I was visiting Kuala Lumpur on vacation and during one of my daily sightseeing walks I stumbled across the Central Markets an indoor market filled with boutique stores, food stalls and the usual tourist gift shops. It has quite a few hidden gems and makes a change from the name brand malls which are all over KL.

I came across Tanamera a store supplying all-natural personal care and home spa products, with this being their first store which was opened in 2008, this is a great little store with a range of high-quality essential oils, massage oils, soaps and a range of well-presented personal care products.

I purchased the Lemongrass and Ginger massage oil and essential oils and all of these products are absolutely amazing, my only regret is that I did not get some more of their fantastic products, oh and did I forget to mention the first-class customer service, the young lady who served me was super professional and polite representing Tanamera in the best possible standard, thank you for your great customer service, really appreciated.

If you are visiting or live in KL, get down to the Central Market and check out Tanamera it’s a hidden treasure for all of us who value our personal health, hygiene and wellbeing.

I went to this shop last Sunday, and the products there have their own unique charm, which can provide a sense of relaxation. What's more, this particular product is made in Malaysia! The staff at the shop were incredibly friendly, and I absolutely loved their service.
Local Malaysian chain store selling some very interesting products like balms, soaps, essential oils, creams, and so on.

name: Central Market
reviews:
Visited Central Market Kuala Lumpur and it was such a vibrant and cultural experience. The building itself has a charming heritage look, and inside it’s filled with local art, handicrafts, souvenirs, and traditional items.

I loved walking around and exploring the small stalls selling batik, handmade accessories, and Malaysian snacks. The atmosphere feels lively and colorful, especially with street performances and nearby attractions like Petaling Street just a short walk away.

Overall, Central Market is a great place to experience local culture, shop for unique gifts, and enjoy the heart of Kuala Lumpur. Perfect for both tourists and locals who appreciate art and tradition.

Central Market is vibrant and lively, filled with shops and food halls. You can find a variety of items - from local food products and textiles to Malaysian souvenirs - and there are also dining options inside.

However, prices tend to be on the higher side. If you're looking for more budget-friendly options, you can walk a few minutes to Jalan Petaling for cheaper finds.

Central Market also know Pasar Seni for local is a vibrant cultural hub in the heart of Kuala Lumpur city.
It is a centre for Malaysian culture, art and craft situated in significant historical heritage building that has come a long way from it early beginning as a wet market built in 1888 and now turn to a delightful destination for tourists, shoppers, and art lovers.
Today, Central Market Kuala Lumpur is one of a must visit destination. It is not just a retail experience, but to be there also a heritage experience offering a wonderful visual treat and appreciation of Malaysia heritage and architecture as you walk in inside the building.
Central Market Kuala Lumpur emphasis on art is also evident with the transformation of Central Market Annex’s to house a variety of art galleries to include illusion 3D Art Museum, and Art House Gallery.
Central Market Art Lane, on the other hand is an art corner comprising of 10 unique studios that features exciting works of art by local artists.
Recommended to pay a visit at Central Market Kuala Lumpur whenever you are in town.

name: Aquaria KLCC
street: Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre, Jalan Pinang
reviews:
It is easily one of the best spots in the city for a family outing. The exhibits are stunning, but the highlight has to be the underwater tunnel(⁠*⁠´⁠ω⁠｀⁠*⁠)
There are actually two gift shops! One is located right after you exit the aquarium tunnel and there’s another large one right at the main exit:))
°‧ 𓆝 𓆟 𓆞 ·｡°

Year 2025 ended with a wonderful time at Aquaria KLCC! The entire place gives you a magical underwater experience.
The wonderful and a calm ambience with well designed exhibits.
Of course it was a bit crowded as it was school holidays and lots of tourists. However, the place was clean and organized giving a relaxing and exciting atmosphere.
The tunnel walkway is an amazing highlight, bringing you up close to sharks rays turtles gliding through along with many other species.
The unique species in every section is truly fascinating.  The small colourful fishes and the red jelly fishes were simply mesmerizing.
It takes around one to two hours to explore the entire aquarium leisurely

It was payment at the counter for a breathtaking experience on a weekday afternoon.
A must-visit attraction in Kuala Lumpur!

​I recently had an absolutely fantastic experience at Aquaria KLCC! This world-class oceanarium truly deserves its reputation and my perfect score of 5 out of 5 stars.
​The highlight of the entire visit was definitely the underwater tunnel. Walking along the moving travelator as majestic stingrays and powerful sharks glided effortlessly above and all around me was a breathtaking and unforgettable experience. It felt like being completely immersed in the deep blue sea!
​And I must give a special mention to the red jellyfish—they were mesmerizing! Their vibrant colour and graceful, pulsing movement were hypnotic and easily my favourite exhibit of the day.
​💡 Pro Tip: Avoiding the Crowds (Crucial!)
​While the aquarium itself is stellar, there is one major piece of advice I can offer to ensure you have the best possible visit:
​DO NOT go during a public holiday or school holiday!
​Seriously, the crowds during peak periods are super duper crowded. It can significantly detract from the experience by making it difficult to move, see the exhibits clearly, and fully enjoy the tranquil atmosphere of the tanks.
​The best time to go is on a weekday, ideally right when they open or later in the evening to have a much more relaxed and intimate viewing experience.

name: Berjaya Times Square
reviews:
I recently spent a day at Berjaya Times Square in Kuala Lumpur, and it was a fun and memorable visit! This massive shopping mall has so much to offer — from delicious snacks to interesting shops and great bargains — making it a great place to explore.

While walking around, I enjoyed a warm chocolate stick snack that tasted soft and sweet — a perfect treat to recharge during my shopping adventure.

One of the cool shops I visited was Hot Market Plus. It’s a colourful and cheerful store with well-organized displays full of cute and affordable accessories, quirky gifts, keychains, and décor items. I loved browsing through all the fun little finds — it’s a great place to pick up budget-friendly gifts or souvenirs.

I also stopped by the Eco Shop, which had a wide range of everyday essentials and household items at very wallet-friendly prices. From kitchen tools to practical daily goods, everything was easy to find and offered good value.

Another highlight was SQ, where they had some amazing sale deals — like pieces from Open Line 29 and other items priced at RM19! The selection was stylish, affordable, and perfect for finding good fashion bargains while enjoying my time in the mall.

Overall, Berjaya Times Square is more than just a mall — it’s an experience. With tasty snacks, colourful stores, cute finds, useful essentials, and great sales everywhere, I had a great time and would definitely visit again! 😊

It's a amazing experience for tourists. There's two type of stay here. One side is star classified hotel and one side is service apartment.  place to do shopping with easy access from the mono rail. Compared to other shopping malls goods are bit less expensive. The Berjaya theme park also located inside and kids will enjoy it. All festivals are making colorful here.

We are very satisfied with op our stay! We have been loyal Berjaya customers for 10 years, wherever we go. Berjaya Times Square is our base, where we always return during our stays in Malaysia. The excellent service and familiar face of the staff always make us feel at home. Thank you, Florina! You are a gem within this organization.
Hospitality 10
Food 10
Rooms 10
Staff 10
Facilities 10
Location 10

street: Wilayah Persekutuan, Lingkaran SV2 Lingkaran SV2
reviews:
Very nice atmosphere 😃
We embraced the cny lion dance🎈

Appreciate the conveniences for shopping exposure & a touch of ' China town'

∆Nevertheless It's very really excellent if the car park centre without garbage odour for eliminating germ or bacteria infection. Nice to maintain hygienity. Most importantly to eliminate the odour trap inside the car when passenger open for going in the mall & closing the car door when departure
*Day of visit @ 18 Feb 2026 大年初二🍀

Sunway Velocity Mall is a really nice place to hang out. It has a wide variety of shops and food choices, so it’s easy to spend hours there without getting bored. The mall is clean, spacious, and well organised, which makes walking around very comfortable. It’s also easy to access and has a lively but relaxing atmosphere. Definitely a good spot to shop, eat, and spend time with friends.

The camera at the car park entrance always fails to read the plate number of my car (Pajero Sports) so I have to reverse and forward my car many time, sometimes upto 10 times until I'm tired of it and decided to leave. I changed the number plate and the problem remains the same. It's proven the machines problem. The management is informed many time but they refused to correct the mistake. Finally one day when I was struggling to get the reader to read my number plate, I hit a car behind who come too close to my car at the back. I loss RM1500 to compensate for the damage of the car. I'm fed up and upset with this mall. All cars with number plate at higher level, I advise you don't enter the car park of velocity mall. You will end up stuck at the car park entrance, or worse like in my case, accidentally hit another car. Another reason for not visiting this mall is, the arrogant attitude of the management. They know their problem but they don't care.

name: Penang Little India
reviews: Totally lives up to its name. It’s full of vibrant colourful flower offerings for the Hindu temple nearby, few supermarkets selling Indian goods, yummy Indian restaurants and a famous samosa stall.

Very lively and vibrant section of the old town district of George Town. Lots of Indian shops, eatery, stalls, groceries, and mostly Tamil temples. Mostly South Indian stuffs with some Punjabi/Sindhi businesses and cuisines. At times like evenings, it even emulates the same atmosphere of a typical Indian market.

Little India in Penang is a colorful and lively area that’s full of culture, music, and amazing food. Walking through the streets, you’ll hear Indian music playing from shops, see bright fabrics and decorations, and smell the spices from nearby restaurants. The atmosphere feels energetic and welcoming, and it’s a great place to try authentic Indian dishes, sweets, and snacks. I enjoyed just wandering around, browsing small shops selling jewelry, clothes, and souvenirs. It’s a small area but packed with character, and it gives you a different cultural side of Penang that’s definitely worth experiencing.

name: Little India Brickfields
reviews:
A Most Delightful Sojourn to the Indian Quarter of Brickfields
"Pray, allow me to recount a most capital excursion to that vibrant enclave known as Little India in the district of Brickfields. As a child of India myself, I found my spirit quite uplifted by the sheer abundance of familiar treasures and the robust character of the place.
The streets are a veritable kaleidoscope of colour, where the eye is met with grand arches and the finest Indian wares showcased with great pride. One may find an array of exquisite textiles, glittering ornaments, and spices of such potency they would surely satisfy the most discerning merchant. The culinary establishments are equally numerous and divine; from the traditional banana leaf rice to the savory thosai, the flavours are as authentic as those found on the banks of the Ganges. Truly, it is a sanctuary for the senses."

A Chronicle of Its Noble Origins
To truly appreciate this quarter, one must look to its history, which is as sturdy as the material that gave the district its name.

The Great Reconstruction (1880s): Following a calamitous fire and flood in 1881 that laid waste to the wooden structures of early Kuala Lumpur, the British Resident, Sir Frank Swettenham, decreed that all future buildings be constructed of more durable brick and tile.

The Birth of the Kilns: To meet this new mandate, the enterprising Kapitan Yap Ah Loy established vast brickworks in this clay-rich region. The district soon became the heart of the town’s masonry, earning it the moniker Brickfields.
The Coming of the Rails: In the late 19th century, the British authorities established the main depot for the Malayan Railway here. To man these iron horses and maintain the tracks, many diligent labourers and civil servants were brought from South India and Ceylon (now Sri Lanka).

A Settlement Endures: These pioneers established their homes, schools, and magnificent places of worship—such as the Sri Kandaswamy Temple (est. 1902) and the Buddhist Maha Vihara (est. 1894)—transforming a simple industrial field into a thriving cultural bastion that endures to this day.

Little India in Brickfields is a colourful and lively area that’s worth a visit if you’re nearby. The streets are full of bright shops, Indian music, and the smell of spices in the air, which makes it feel quite vibrant and different from other parts of KL.

There’s a good variety of shops selling traditional clothing, jewellery, snacks, and groceries, and prices are generally reasonable if you’re looking for something specific. The food options are also decent, with several authentic Indian restaurants and sweet shops to try.

However, it can feel quite crowded and a bit chaotic, especially during busy hours. Some areas aren’t the cleanest, and you may get approached quite often by people trying to sell things, which can make it less relaxing to explore. It’s more of a quick cultural stop than a place you’d spend a long time wandering.

Overall, it’s an interesting spot to experience Indian culture in Kuala Lumpur, but probably best visited with modest expectations and a short time frame in mind.

A meaningful cultural experience for our family

I took my kids to Little India Brickfields, and it was a very meaningful experience for us as a family. My parents are of Pakistani origin, and my children may never have the opportunity to visit India or experience that side of their heritage through their mother’s family. Bringing them here felt like the next best thing.

As you walk through the area, you hear Indian music playing in the background, see vibrant clothing shops, street stalls, flower and garland-making alleys, and even clothes hanging from balconies above. There’s a strong sense of culture and everyday life woven into the streets, which made it feel authentic and alive rather than overly touristy.

While it’s not India itself, it truly is the next best thing—a wonderful way to experience the sights, sounds, and atmosphere. We stopped for a quick bite (dhaba chai and pakoras), and since it was raining, we didn’t linger too long. That said, you don’t need to spend hours here to appreciate it. We were in and out in about 30–45 minutes, and it was well worth the visit.

A great cultural stop in Kuala Lumpur, especially for families wanting to introduce their children to South Asian heritage and traditions.

name: Meriken Park
reviews:
Meriken Park feels like Kobe taking a deep, relaxed breath. Wide lawns roll out toward the harbor, the sky seems bigger than it has any right to be, and the sea light turns everything a little cinematic. It’s open in a way that’s surprisingly rare in Japanese cities — not just physically spacious, but emotionally unhurried.

What makes it special isn’t a single landmark, but the everyday life unfolding across it. Locals wander by with dogs trotting happily ahead, kids dart between playground equipment, couples sit on the grass sharing snacks, and older folks stroll the waterfront paths with no particular destination. No rush, no tight sidewalks, no pressure to move along — just people existing outdoors.

With the harbor stretching out front and Kobe’s skyline behind, the park becomes a soft meeting point between city and sea. You can hear gulls, distant ship horns, and the low murmur of conversation carried on the breeze. It’s the kind of place where you end up staying longer than planned, simply because it feels good to be there.

For a traveler, Meriken Park offers something unexpectedly gentle: a glimpse of everyday leisure that feels more coastal Europe than dense urban Japan — spacious, social, and soaked in blue sky.

Home to iconic red Kobe Port Tower and the Kobe Maritime Museum. Meriken Park (メリケンパーク) is a beautiful waterfront park in Kobe's port area. Built on reclaimed land, it is a park covered with lawn, playground, harbour view sitting area and open courtyards with a collection of modern art installations and fountains placed sparingly. Water drinking fountains & Toilets can also be found at the park.
1995 Great Hanshin Earthquake devastated the area. Remains of the fallen ports are still a vivid reminder of mother nature strength. These damaged structures now become a memorial that commemorates the many victims who were killed in the port during the earthquake.
To reach there it is about a ten minute walk south of Motomachi Station or just across the sightseeing cruise terminal from Kobe Harborland.
Beautiful walk and open spaces for visitors to sit or run or take photos or practice their stunts as you can see in the video. The day I went was a beautiful day so it really helps.

name: Kobe Harborland
reviews:
Almost every week we go there as a family or with friends. The lights, decorations and events or activities that happen here, form an unforgettable memory for me. Kobe usually sleeps early, unlike Osaka or Toko. But this place is usually up till late into the night and that gives it one advantage when comparing other places in the city. Every section there has a memory with me. So, this place is a special one in my heart.

Good place to relax in very good lighting props. Good options to choose and eat, lots o places to sit, it doesn't matter of it's a solo walk or a walk with family or a walk with friends, this place has something to cater to them all.

The view of Kobe Harborland at night is very nice.. illuminated with various lightings.
Plenty of shoppings and dining options are available at Mosaic, umie and Anpanman. I only walked there to dine and sight seeing for 2-3 hours so didn’t have time to explore most of the area.
Pretty sure the Ferris Wheel offers spectacular view of Kobe harbour.

Plus: very nice scenery - one of the best in Kobe city. The atmosphere is fantastic with a large balcony where people can sit in groups and enjoy the food and coffee from surrounding shops. Minus: all the shops will close around 10 PM.

name: LaLaport Bukit Bintang City Centre
reviews:
Lalaport is a very nice mall and a comfortable place to walk around. It is not crowded, which makes the experience relaxing compared to many other malls in the city. The layout is spacious and easy to navigate, so it never feels rushed or cramped.

One highlight is the rooftop area, where you can enjoy a great view of Merdeka 118. It is a nice spot to take photos or just relax after shopping. The mix of shops and food options is decent, making it suitable for casual browsing rather than heavy shopping.

Overall,  a pleasant and calm mall to visit, especially if you prefer a quieter shopping environment with a good city view.

LaLaport is a modern and spacious shopping mall with a good mix of shops, dining options, and entertainment. The layout is comfortable for walking around, and the atmosphere feels clean and family friendly.

There is also a Mitsui Outlet section, although the number of stores is quite limited and not as extensive as the Mitsui Outlet near KLIA. Still, it’s a nice place to spend a few hours shopping, eating, or just hanging out.

LaLaport Bukit Bintang City Centre is a dream mall for fans of anime, video games, Japanese goods, and well-designed retail spaces. Clean, calm, thoughtfully curated, and blissfully free of pretentious luxury clutter. If you love Japanese culture, this is your mall.

Full Review (5/5): A Japanese Retail Wonderland in the Heart of KL

People who criticize LaLaport Bukit Bintang City Centre either have no idea what an actual dead mall looks like… or they’ve become so accustomed to overstimulation, noise, and overcrowded spaces that a bit of calm sends them spiraling. Because make no mistake: LaLaport is not dead. It’s different. And refreshingly so.

Walking into this mall feels like stepping into a compact slice of Japan—minus the jet lag and the language barrier. It’s thoughtfully designed, easy to navigate, and most importantly, filled with shops that appeal to people who want more out of retail than yet another parade of overpriced handbags and clothing boutiques.

LaLaport is, quite frankly, one of the best malls I’ve ever visited.

If you love anime, video games, or Japanese culture, this mall feels curated specifically for you. You’ve got anime figures and merch lining the shelves of specialty stores, the ever-reliable Animate, the solid electronics spread at Nojima, and dozens of other Japan-forward shops that make browsing feel genuinely fun again. It’s the kind of mall where you want to spend time—not because you’re hunting for sales, but because it’s actually interesting.

And perhaps my favorite part? The absence of all that unnecessary extravagance that plagues certain other malls in KL. No endless rows of luxury megabrands. No performative window-shopping from people pretending they’re two paychecks away from a Louis Vuitton spree. Instead, you get a grounded, refreshing environment where the focus is on goods that people actually use and enjoy—electronics, collectibles, Japanese snacks and homewares, and gaming gear.

It’s clean, it’s modern, and it feels purpose-built for people like me who want substance over flash. In many ways, LaLaport offers what I wish more malls did: a clear identity. It knows what it is and who it’s for.

And for me, it’s pretty much perfect.

name: Madam Kwan's Suria KLCC
street: Lot 420- 421 Level 4, Madam Kwan's, Petronas Twin Tower
reviews: The standout here is definitely the food but unfortunately not the service, which is why I could not give 5 stars. Although we had a reservation we were quickly taken to a table and then left there with no menus and no indication of when or how we would order. After 5 minutes we flagged down a passing waiter to request some menus, he was not overly friendly, just put them down on a table with a QR code which he pointed to, to order ourselves. The food arrived reasonably quickly and thankfully the flavours did not disappoint. The satay skewers and beef rendang was delicious. Good portion sizes for fried rice too. At the end when paying, I was a little shocked by the extra service fee and extra tax, I thought this would have been built into the prices or sign posted more clearly on the menu of the additional charges, perhaps this is standard practice in KL, as I have only just arrived. When paying at the register, the girl named 'Ivy' could not even manage a smile & did not say thankyou to the customers spending their money at your establishment, it was like we were an inconvenience to her day. However aren't the customers essentially paying your wages? Otherwise if you don't enjoy your job, go work somewhere else.

Had a very satisfying meal at Madam Kwan’s in Suria KLCC. The menu covers several of the Malaysian favourites and is perfect if you want to try local dishes in one place. The highlight was the nasi lemak and curry dishes – fragrant rice, nicely balanced sambal and tender meat, very comforting and flavourful.
The restaurant is usually busy and there can be a queue, especially around lunch and dinner, but the turnover is fairly quick. Service can feel a bit rushed at peak times, yet staff remain polite and the food generally comes out reasonably fast once you’ve ordered.
Prices are on the higher side compared with hawker centres, but that’s expected given the location inside a premier mall right by the Twin Towers, and the air‑conditioned, comfortable setting. Overall, it’s a solid choice for first‑time visitors or anyone craving dependable Malaysian comfort food in KLCC.

Was wanting to try local local food of Malaysian Pedigree. We enjoyed our dining at Madam Kwan. The service was good. We had problems ordering from the QR code and Vijay was happy to assist get the food delivered to us. We had Samaira hoon Ng, egg Assam, prawns and fried rice with veggies and egg. Vijay was very helpful to us, and I make sure the food is delivered on time. We also tried the local Kopi, and it was really nice. All the food was good. We were not wanting to have food without MSG/ajinimotto  and Vijay made sure that is done.

name: The TOP Penang, Theme Park Penang
reviews:
Visited The TOP in Penang, and it is a fun and family friendly attraction with plenty to do for all ages. The complex has multiple levels of activities, observation decks, and playgrounds, making it engaging for both kids and adults.

One highlight is the view from the observation area, which offers a panoramic look at Penang and the surrounding coastline. It’s a great spot for photos and enjoying the scenery. The indoor sections are well-designed, clean, and safe, allowing visitors to explore comfortably even on rainy days.

We’re a group of four friends and visited The TOP Penang. A must-visit attraction is the Sky Bridge Glass Walk.

The most amazing part is walking high above the city with glass panels under your feet ,it feels very adventurous and a bit scary at the same time.

The view is absolutely stunning. You can see the whole of Penang, and the sunset view from up there is incredible. The night view is super duper beautiful too.

Highly recommended🥰❤️

I visited The TOP Penang in George Town and it was one of the most entertaining and activity packed places I went to during my trip. What I like most is that it’s not just one attraction, but a whole mix of experiences inside one building, so you really get value for your time. The observation levels give you wide views of the city and coastline, and the Rainbow Skywalk and glass floor sections add a fun challenge, especially if you are not used to heights. It’s exciting but still feels safe, and it’s perfect for photos.

Inside, there are many themed attractions, interactive exhibits, and family friendly activities, so both adults and kids can enjoy different parts of the place. You can move at your own pace, take breaks, and explore section by section without feeling rushed. It’s also a good escape from the heat since most areas are indoors and air conditioned. Some spots can be crowded, especially during peak hours, but the facilities are well maintained and staff are generally helpful. Overall, The TOP Penang is a solid choice if you want a mix of views, light adventure, and indoor fun all in one stop while visiting Penang.

name: Havana Bar & Grill
reviews:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 5/5 – Highly Recommended!

Had an amazing time at Havana KL. The salmon pizza was absolutely delicious — the cheese was perfectly salty and melted in the mouth. Fresh ingredients and great flavor all around.

Service was excellent, with super friendly staff. Special thanks to Khushbu, who was very helpful and even assisted us with free Wi-Fi.

Great food, great service, and a nice, relaxing atmosphere. Will definitely come back again!

We had a fabulous time on Chinese New year dancing and drinking some iconic and well priced cocktails. The staff were attentive snd helpful and Tony the DJ did well. We had sooo much fun and it was getting busier when we retired for some supper at midnight. We didnt eat so I cannot comment on the food

A very nice bar! Good beer, good music, friendly staff. You can pay by card. I didn't stay long, I just had a beer and left because the street is full of lots of other nice bars that are worth trying.

name: Batu Ferringhi Beach
reviews:
Penang’s most famous stretch of sand — more resort strip than wild coastline, but still charming in its own tropical way.

The beach runs long and wide, lined with hotels, palms, and water sports operators. Sand is decent (not Maldives-white, but pleasant), and sunsets can be surprisingly beautiful when the sky clears — warm orange melting into the Malacca Strait. 🌅

Daytime: Jet skis, parasailing, banana boats. It’s lively, slightly commercial, and sometimes crowded on weekends.
Evening: The famous night market appears — souvenirs, clothes, gadgets, street snacks. That’s where the real energy shifts from beach to bazaar.

Water quality can be variable, especially after rains. It’s not the cleanest swimming beach in Southeast Asia, so think of it more as a “walk, relax, watch the sky” beach rather than a deep-dive swim destination.

Historically, the name “Ferringhi” comes from “Farangi” (foreigner), reflecting earlier encounters with European traders and pirates along the Malay coast — a small linguistic fossil of colonial-era maritime history.

The actual beach is very nice and a good place to walk or get a suntan. There are two main downsides. Although we did see people in the sea, there are signs up saying beware of jellyfish. Secondly there are certain areas you can get a chair and an umbrella for a very cheap price, the problem was they were literally plastic chairs you would use at a table and looked like they had been used for many years. There were some slightly better sun beds at the far end of the beach available, but even those were very old and tired looking. Plenty of boat ride options available.

I think M’sia is not known for pristine beaches. If you are a beach person, personally Id recommend Thailand or Indonesia. That said, if solely comparing within M’sia. Langkawi island is better than Penang Island. Water slightly less murky and not so many garbage on the beach. More foreigners friendly as well.

name: Kwai Chai Hong
reviews:
Stepping into Kwai Chai Hong this Chinese New Year is like walking right into a vibrant, living folk tale. For 2026, the hidden alleyway in KL’s Chinatown has transformed into a glowing sanctuary for the "Guardians of Legacy" (十二福星).
​A Walk Through the Guardian’s Lane
