​The first thing that hits you is the canopy of lanterns—cube-shaped and bursting with the playful, bold colors of Cloth Tiger folk art. Each one depicts a different zodiac animal with that signature wide-eyed, protective gaze meant to ward off bad vibes and usher in health and luck.
​As you cross the iconic Red Bridge, you’re greeted by the star of the show: the 7-foot-tall "Guardian of Triumph." Since 2026 is the Year of the Horse, this blue-hued masterpiece stands proud with intricate patterns of victory flames and delicate chrysanthemums. If you look closely at the sculptures, like the frog perched on the horse's side, you’ll find hidden auspicious symbols tucked away in the details.
​Why It’s the Best Alley Walk in KL
​It isn't just about the "gram-worthy" backdrops (though there are plenty!). This year’s collaboration with guardian Malaysia feels deeply personal. It’s a tribute to the "quiet love" in our culture—the kind that doesn’t always say "I love you" out loud but shows it through protection and the keeping of traditions.
​Traveler’s Tip: The installation is open daily from 9:00 AM to midnight, but the magic really happens after 7:00 PM. The contrast of the glowing lanterns against the rustic, mural-covered brick walls creates a nostalgic atmosphere you won't find anywhere else in the city.

Kwai Chai Hong is a beautifully restored hidden alley tucked behind the busy Petaling Street in Kuala Lumpur. What used to be a neglected lane has been transformed into a vibrant cultural space filled with murals inspired by 1960s Chinatown life.
The artwork reflects everyday scenes from children playing in the alleyways to small local vendors,giving visitors a glimpse into the area’s history. It’s compact, easy to access, and well maintained.
If you’re exploring Chinatown in KL, this is a quick but worthwhile stop. It adds a meaningful layer to your walk beyond the usual market experience.

Nostalgic Vibe: Tucked away in KL Chinatown, this restored heritage alleyway brilliantly captures the "golden era" of the 1960s. The interactive murals and pre-war architecture offer an immersive glimpse into old-school local life.

Vibrant Art: The current installation features twelve sculptural Zodiac Guardians inspired by the traditional Cloth Tiger folk art. The centerpiece is a striking 7-foot tall lead Guardian, making it an elite spot for photography.

Interactive Elements: By scanning QR codes next to the murals, you can listen to audio stories that bring the heritage scenes to life with sound.

Perfect Ambiance: Beyond the art, the alley is surrounded by trendy cafes and bars, such as the famous Bunn Choon Egg Tart shop nearby

name: Honmaru Palace
reviews: A fascinating view into the history of Aesthetics of the Edo period. Though much of the primary construction was destroyed by America during the second world war, the dedication of those committed to the preservation of History has allowed for the Reconstruction which is magnificent. A gem.

The Honmaru Palace of Nagoya Castle is a true masterpiece of traditional Japanese architecture and craftsmanship. Reconstructed with meticulous care using original techniques and materials, the palace offers a rare glimpse into the opulent lifestyle of feudal lords during the Edo period. Walking through the elegant tatami rooms, you’re greeted by breathtaking gold-leaf screens, hand-painted sliding doors, and intricate wooden carvings that reflect the grandeur of the Owari Tokugawa clan. The atmosphere is peaceful and deeply respectful of history. Every corner feels like stepping into a living museum. It’s amazing to see how much effort has been put into authenticity. Whether you’re a history buff or simply curious, the Honmaru Palace is an unforgettable and enriching experience, well worth the visit.

The palace is very well reserved and orderly. I appreciate how they had a good crowd control and ensure visitors could have enough space to walk and pause and enjoy the beauty of the artworks. The golden artworks were well restored and I was amazed by the beauty!

name: Envi Skydining
street: Menara TA One, 22, Jalan P. Ramlee
reviews: The view was ok, maybe because we were seated on the other side of the restaurant. If you would want a better view, best to state it in your reservation. The food was good, enjoyed the meals. The waiters are quite efficient. The parking is on the 6th floor which is quite long winded as it is based on 2a, 2b, 3a, 3b all the way to the 6th. If you are not a fan of such parking, best to park at a public parking below and take a few minutes walk. When you see the Starbucks, that is Menara TA. You need to take the lift to 33th floor at the G lift. Then another lift to 36th floor.

We love food but usually prices of the food is important, but nothing is worse than having paid so much for frozen food. Better to have had street food western food which would have been freshly made. This is an honest review, and its about the honesty of the restaurant to give their customers fresh food moreover like a place like this. The food is not recommended but the view is great.

Nice views.
Dining at level 36 - Spectacular views.
We were here for lunch - there are Lunch set comes with a drink. I picked my coffee. Love my lamb chop ✅

name: The Starhill
reviews:
Starhill Mall in Bukit Bintang is a charming, boutique-style shopping destination with a refined and relaxed atmosphere. Though compact in size, it offers a well-curated selection of restaurants and cafés serving a variety of cuisines. Come True Café stands out in particular, with its pleasant outdoor seating that overlooks the lively Bukit Bintang street—perfect for people-watching alongside good food and coffee. The only drawbacks are the heat and a potential waiting list for outdoor tables.

A true highlight of the mall is the Eslite Spectrum bookstore, a beautifully designed space that’s a joy to explore whether you’re a book lover or not. If you time your visit right, you might also catch one of Starhill’s frequent events, featuring pop-up shops and live entertainment, which add extra vibrancy to the experience.

Starhill Gallery – oozes luxury minus the crowd

This mall is legendary, dating back to the days when the land where Pavilion now stands was still a school. Many of the high-end brands are here — some with names I can’t even pronounce. 😁

Lots of cafés, boutiques, an art gallery and even a bookstore. I like coming here to chill and escape the crowd and noise outside. It’s a great spot for quiet hangouts.

The toilets are decked out in marble with gold accents — pure luxury. The mall is always spotless. But the best part? Parking is only RM5 for the first 3 hours. Hard to believe, but true. Two exits available: Jalan Bukit Bintang or Jalan Imbi — pick your poison.

Only qualm: they’re still using a dinosaur payment system. No QR, no TNG, strictly old-school. But RM5.00 for 3 hours.. I’m not complaining.

So this was my first time entering this building, i used to walk pass this area, from pavilion to every part of bukit bintang, i even stayed in fahrenheit couple of times... there is actually a very fancy bookstore inside, this place is actually so nice, so fancy, unlike all the crowd outside! Its heavenly romantic

name: leaf & co. cafe
reviews:
I really enjoyed the overall vibe here—great atmosphere, nice music, and the coffee was excellent. The staff were friendly and welcoming, which made the experience even better.

A couple of things to note:

The toilet at the back felt a bit scary; maybe it could use some improvement.

The food portions are generous, which is great, but I’d prefer the sauce served separately or with less sauce. By the time I got to the end of my bread, it was quite soggy.

Overall, a lovely spot with good coffee and a nice ambiance. Just a few tweaks would make it perfect!

Nice interior design, played authentic Chinese Old Folks songs as BGM, creates an old Shanghai feel when spending time here. The cafe offers several vegetarian menu. Below are the food we tried and my personal review on the taste:

1. salted egg croissant: 3🌟 salted egg filling taste fairly standard but the texture of the croissant is too soft. Crispy croissant texture can enhance the overall taste experience.

2. Cronboloni Blueberry: 3🌟expected blueberry flavour stands as the main body but lemon cheese flavour overpowered the blueberry flavour. Croissant texture can be more crispy instead of soft.

3. Openfaced mushroom bagel: 3.5🌟 filing taste like ginger stir-fry mushroom with some cream cheese or milk (taste in Chinese cuisine) - a somewhat different combination with a bagel (a western cuisine). I like the innovation.

4. Oatmilk latte: 4.5🌟 the coffee bean carries a nutty body, blends well with the oatmilk. Not sweet and taste quite good!

Tried this cafe for a quick catch up with friends. Quite popular on a weekday tea time. Order by scanning the QR code placed at the table.

Unfortunately, the promo for cake and drink was not available for the entire festive week.

The walnut and carrot cake was good and I liked it more than the strawberry ice cream cake.

The coconut latte had a tinge of green, so not sure about that.

Service, depends.

name: Tokyo Street
reviews:
Pavilion level 6
Decorated in Japanese style. Pretty photogenic. Few bench seats there- able to take a break as well.
Most Japanese shops and restaurants there, like Daiso and Maisen.

I had an amazing time exploring Tokyo Street in Berjaya Times Square, Kuala Lumpur! This vibrant, Japan-themed section is a gem, with authentic Japanese restaurants, cute dessert spots, and shops selling everything from anime merch to traditional snacks. The decor transports you to Japan, making it perfect for a quick cultural escape. It’s a bit crowded on weekends, but the lively atmosphere and variety of food, like sushi and ramen, make it worth a visit. A must for Japan enthusiasts!

Be careful if you’re a foreigner
Woman from this store dust wanted to sell me hair clips for 200$🤣🤣🤣

name: Suzuka forest garden
reviews:
Feb 28, 2026
Quite expensive (2000 yen) but beautiful. Hard to reach, but during blossom season there’s a shuttle bus from Kintetsu-Yokkaichi station. This bus doesn’t show up on Google when you try to look for the route, so make sure to check the official website for the schedule.
Amazing garden! But public transport is limited to go there. Totally worth it. Check their Instagram to see their updates before going just in case.

Japanese plum blossoms is in full bloom....very impressive!
nicely maintained
We visited on 22.03.2025 and enjoyed the beauty of the park .
In the exit area there is a tree which had both white and pink flower in it . (Same tree) Don't miss it ..must visit place.:)

name: Maruya Honten - JR Nagoya Station
street: Meieki, 1 Chome−1−4 名古屋うまいもん通り
reviews: The one on the Meitetsu Department store closed as the whole department store closed, so this one is the only one in the Nagoya station left.  There is just one thing to order here and that is the Hitsumabushi or grilled eel with rice eaten 3 ways.  One on its own, two with the garnishes and three with garnishes and the light dashi broth.  My fave remains to be just eating it as it is.  There was a 20 min wait forming and I was there around 5:30 PM on a Monday evening.  Fortunately the line moved fast.

Famous Hitsumabushi (grilled eel) from Nagoya. Located under the JR station. We came for lunch on Saturday and waited about 1 hour, but the queue was well organized and staff were attentive. The restaurant is small. The grilled unagi was very fragrant and delicious. I ordered the mini Hitsumabushi with half an eel and 200g of rice — just the right portion. There are three traditional ways to eat Hitsumabushi, and all were amazing. Highly recommended!

Enjoyed the typical Nagoya unagi, cooked perfectly with crispier outer part and soft inner side. From the layout, the restaurant is on high demand, quite few chairs lined up for guests in waiting. I went there after lunch hours, didn’t have to wait.

Service is efficient and in detailed explanation on how to enjoy it. If you are passing Nagoya Station, highly recommend a visit here.

name: Al Halabi Gourmet Restaurant
reviews: We went during Ramadan on a lunch time and we had the entire place to ourselves. The service was top tier and the ambiance will immediately teleport you to Istanbul. The interiors have this tukish vibe to it. Very sophisticated, colorful, elegant and quintessentially Arabic. The food is good. I forgot to take photo of the mixed grill platter we ordered and almost finished half of it when I remembered. It was alright but i think flavor is not as prominent as their other competitors like Halab or Saba Restaurant. Overall it is always a nice experience.

This place is at the dining loft in pavillion. Good Arabic food. The shish tok was tender and juicy. Salad was very refreshing. The ambience is really good. You can buy fruits and nuts as well here. Staff is courteous and explained well on why to order.

I don't know why anyone would give this place less than 5 stars plus! The food was delicious. The service was kind and efficient, and it has an excellent atmosphere. I would highly recommend all of the dishes! We had a party of 25, and the owner did a fabulous job making everyone happy! Go try it! You'll love it!

name: Royal Lake Club
reviews: Visited with a member. The club is old but well maintained. The staff from the reception to the servers were courteous. Multi cuisine food at awesome prices. Mamak, kopitiam and Indian among the varsity. Nice view from the sunset bar

went here for Iftar buffet. nice ambience. have surau and library (for members only) too. it's an old building so the layout a bit old too. But, it's a nice private club. very nice surrounding with amenities. heard that have live band performance too. Must come again if have the opportunity 😁

Club of excellent gentlemen & ladies. A club of rich heritage. Warm people, good food, good drinks. 135 years of history yet still so well maintained. Keep up the good work. Thank you for the invitation.

name: Hikiniku no Toriko
reviews:
Food was not tasty. Never had hamburger this bad before. The price was also high considering the food quality. I also ordered the drink+pudding set. The ice coffee was terrible. Pudding was okay.

We sat at the counter, the chair was shaky, the countertop wasn’t clean, I saw dried rice on it.

The food was really good—rich, creamy, and flavorful. The dish was well-presented and paired nicely with the sides. The ambiance is also very nice and cozy, perfect for a relaxed meal. Would definitely come back and recommend this place!

Comfort food done right. Creamy, flavorful, and perfectly balanced with fresh, tangy sides. The sauce was silky and rich without being overwhelming, and everything on the plate worked together. Simple, cozy, and absolutely delicious.

name: Mosaic Big Ferris Wheel
reviews:
Riding the Mosaic Big Ferris Wheel モザイク大観覧車 was a really amazing experience. For only about 800 yen and a 15-minute ride, it feels very enjoyable and great value. The wheel moves slowly, giving plenty of time to enjoy the scenery without feeling rushed.

As you go higher, the view opens up beautifully—you can see Kobe Port, the city lights, and the gentle coastline all at once. In the evening, the illuminated buildings and reflections on the water make the scene especially memorable. It’s a peaceful ride, and the height gives a wonderful feeling of floating above the city.

Whether during the day or at night, the panorama from the Ferris wheel is impressive, but nighttime is particularly charming with all the lights around the port area. It’s a short ride, but the view and the atmosphere make it feel really special.

A lovely experience and definitely worth trying when visiting Kobe Harborland. 🎡🌊✨

When someone asks me which part of Japan do I have most fun in, Kobe will actually be in my answer. And part of the reason is due the great time I have at Kobe Port Tower and Mosiac Big Ferris Wheel.

The ride on the Mosiac Big Ferris Wheel is a pretty short one, in a good way actually. Since this means that the waiting time is shorter, so we get to ride on the wheel shortly after we purchased the ticket. While on the wheel, we get to see the beautiful landscape of Kobe Harborland from elevated angle. And it is amazing that some of the building structures actually look different from a different angle. It is fun, tempered with excitement of being suspended high up above the ground, and also idyllic and safe at the same time. The changing lights of the ferris wheel makes us feel like we are in dazzling fantasy land. When we get off the Ferris Wheel, we are still feeling the excitement of the ride. That's the charm of the shorter ride: one gets off while still immersing in the thrill of the ride, where the good memories lingers.

Ferris wheel in Japan, checked off my bucket list! This is such a nice area with plenty of shops and eateries as well as this gigantic rainbow colored ferris wheel by the water! The views from here were really nice especially during sunset hours. For 10 minutes and 800 yen, I got a fantastic view of the city. Tickets can be bought at the door (I think cash only).

name: Kobe Beef YAZAWA Hankyu Sannomiya Store
reviews: We wanted the Kobe beef experience in the heart of Kobe without overdoing it (I’m not a big beef lover), so this place’s lunch set was just perfect! Our server Kou is a sweetheart and made us feel welcome. The food came out quick and they knew enough English to make it the easiest process. Booking a reservation through Tabelog was easy too, so I recommend it!

Decided to have sukiyaki here randomly. The food was great and the service was good. The sukiyaki was a bit on the saltier side for me but still enjoyable. Just add a bit of water when they top up your water. I prefer the leaner cuts since Kobe beef (and most Japanese wagyu) is almost always marbled nicely. Sake paired nicely to cut some of the grease. No complaints. Kou was very kind and was very helpful. Keep up the great service!

So we came to Kobe specifically for Kobe beef but didn’t have a place in mind. As we were just wondering about in a bit for back street we saw this cute little place. Ko, who was our server spoke to us in English and told us about the place and meat.

I should preface that in our group of 4 there was 1 from Argentina and 1 from Colombia, this is to saw meant is beyond important.

We decided to order 4 prime Kobe beef sushi, 4 prime Kobe beef at 110 g (we had the lunch menu so we had a salad, bowel of rice, and some soup), and we decided to share a prime Kobe beef sirloin (this was the best of the best cut).

Omg absolutely incredible. Ko gave us his recommendations and they were SPOT ON.  The meat was perfect and just melted in your mouth. There were things they brought out that you could try with the Kobe, but honestly the meat didn’t need it. Best meal that we could have imagined.

Also the other sides were good too.

Really really enjoyed this place and we feel fortunate that we stumbled on it. If you want to try Kobe beef, this is the place to do it. Ko was absolutely fantastic and was incredibly attentive to us. He even explained some Japanese concepts to us!

name: La Boca Latino Bar & Grill, Pavilion KL
reviews:
I love South American food, first time coming to this restaurant and enjoying the Chilindrón for my dinner. It’s a great recommendation from MR SHEHAB. He’s very friendly, giving warm welcome, detailed service to all customers ensuring everything are in place for us to enjoy the food. He’s an asset to this restaurant ⭐
The lamb is tender & I love the aromatic rice.
Instagrammable bar settings & also the vibrant ambiance. Will return again for sure, great service & quality authentic food. Keep it up! 👍

Food 10/10
Service 11/10

Nice atmosphere and authentic cuisine!
If you like Latin American food you should definitely try this place!

All the worker here are happy and very polite!
Big thank you goes to Shihab!
Gave me the best recommendation on drinks and the burrito

Had dinner here with friend from Australia and his kids. We were welcomed with a warm greeting by the smiling staff and seated at a nice corner. The ordering process was smooth and food was delivered fast too. All the staff were very friendly and courteous. Food and drinks were equally good too. Pricing is based on the location, so can't complain 😃

name: 伊勢丹 Isetan The Japan Store
street: Lot 10 Shopping Center, 50, Jln Sultan Ismail
reviews: It is generally a nice place to dine in. However, my experience at the Muar Otak-Otak stall was disappointing. I was asked to leave because the stall owner was unable to cope with the crowd. While I understand that Chinese New Year is a busy period and she was managing both cooking and serving alone, the way the situation was handled was unprofessional. Customers should be addressed respectfully, even during peak hours. I hope the management takes steps to improve service standards moving forward.

The sushi and bento counter is the best for me. The sushi price is very reasonable. The bento set also is value for money.

Those sushi purchased can be searved dine in.

There are also reasonable price of wahyu and other high quality beef.

I 😍 🥰 😍 🥰 😍 🥰 😍 🥰 😍 🥰 😍 🥰 😍 🥰 😍 🥰 😍 🥰 😍 🥰 😍 🥰  the environment and definitely my choice of places to eat some Japanese food at affordable prices.

Their bakery shop is my favourite! During Black Friday, they had perfume sales ans I managed to grab some. There’s so much ti explore here. Japanese restaurants, snacks, groceries, bakery, clothing, bar, and more food. Waste your money here.

name: Rokkaen
reviews: Very interesting house with a beautiful garden. I liked wandering inside.
England and Japanese styles building.  We can feel the vintage of past year. The park is also quiet. It is nice to walk around the park.
Lovely garden and the old house with England 🇬🇧and Japanese🇯🇵 style. You can walk with flash air.

name: DIN by Din Tai Fung at Suria KLCC [No Pork No Lard]
street: Suria KLCC, Lot 417 & 417A, Level 4, 405, Persiaran Petronas
reviews:
If you’re craving world-class Xiao Long Bao in the heart of Kuala Lumpur, Din at Suria KLCC is a top-tier choice. This pork-free outlet maintains the brand's legendary standards, serving delicate, soup-filled dumplings with impressively thin skins.

The shrimp egg fried rice is a masterclass in texture—fluffy, fragrant, and never greasy. While it’s often busy, the service is remarkably efficient. It’s the perfect spot for a refined yet casual lunch after exploring the Petronas Towers.

First time dining here with my partner, and we had such a great experience. We went after 8pm, so the crowd was light. The staff were really friendly and welcoming, which made us feel comfortable right away.

Our food arrived within 10 minutes and we finished everything quickly. Special mention to the Shrimp and Chicken dumplings. The flavours just burst in our mouths! 😍

We also tried the viral chocolate xiao long bao, and it was absolutely divine.

Definitely coming back again with the family!

Food is good, really.
The service however is a mixed bag. They move very efficiently and get your orders promptly and this run in pretty good order.
But there is no greeting. Not the one where people just read their script, a genuine hello with a "How are you today?" kind of greeting.
However, when I was leaving the restaurant they did say thanks for coming and please come again.
I went there for lunch as well as dinner and was served by the same waitress but she didnt seem to recognize.
Probably they are too busy.
And I hope kitchen staff dont serve the customer, or at least change the uniform when serving.

Shrimp and egg fried rice is a must, order spicy one.
But dont order the one with chicken strip as they dont taste any better and you get less shrimp.

name: River of Life
reviews:
A beautiful urban spot to walk, unwind, or even go for a morning run. The river area is clean and well-maintained, with a nice contrast between the historic buildings and the modern city skyline. It’s especially peaceful early in the morning before the crowds arrive.

A great place to slow down and appreciate Kuala Lumpur from a different perspective.

I was genuinely amazed by the River of Life in Malaysia, especially when viewed at night—it’s nothing short of spectacular. The entire riverscape transforms once the sun sets, with vibrant lights dancing across the water and illuminating the nearby buildings in a way that feels almost surreal. The atmosphere becomes incredibly enchanting, as if the whole area has stepped into a different world.

What makes it even more captivating is the story behind this stunning attraction. The River of Life initiative, launched by the Malaysian government back in 2012, aimed to rejuvenate the Klang and Gombak rivers and turn them into a lively, valuable waterfront for both locals and tourists. And today, you can truly see that vision realized. The LED lighting displays, gentle waves of fog drifting along the river, and the mesmerizing color-shifting fountains create a nighttime spectacle that feels both modern and magical.

Strolling along the riverbank is a relaxing experience on its own—you can take your time wandering the pathways, snapping beautiful photos, and soaking in the mix of historic architecture blended seamlessly with the vibrant pulse of the city. It’s a place that invites you to slow down and simply enjoy the moment.

Another great thing is how accessible it is. The River of Life is within walking distance from both Merdeka Square and Central Market, making it an easy addition to any Kuala Lumpur itinerary. Whether you’re exploring during the day or visiting at night for the full light-show experience, it’s definitely a spot worth seeing.

The River of Life is one of Kuala Lumpur's most underrated gems, offering a quiet and serene escape from the city’s usual hustle. Because it is often overlooked by major tour groups, you’ll find fewer visitors, making it a peaceful place to walk and soak in the atmosphere. The area is famous for its vibrant street art, with massive, colorful murals painted on the riverside buildings that tell the story of the city’s history and culture.
One of the most charming highlights is the presence of local caricature artists stationed along the walkways; you can get a personalized sketch for just 15 Ringgit per person, making for a wonderful and affordable souvenir. From the main viewing bridge, you get a stunning, unobstructed view of the Masjid Jamek Sultan Abdul Samad, where the two rivers meet.
While the "Blue Pool" mist and light show are spectacular at night, a daytime visit is equally rewarding for admiring the murals and the mosque's architecture in detail. It is a very short walk from Dataran Merdeka, making it easy to combine the two for a relaxing morning or afternoon tour.

name: Hitsumabushi Bincho Dai-Nagoya Building Branch
reviews:
Tried an eel rice restaurant inside the Nagoya Building and it was a really nice experience. The set meal was around ~6000 yen per person and came with the classic style of enjoying eel rice in three different ways.

First, you try the eel rice as it is to enjoy the original flavor. Then you can add condiments to change the taste, and finally pour broth over the rice to make ochazuke. Each way gives a slightly different experience, which makes the meal more interesting.

The set also included dessert, and the yuzu ice cream was surprisingly good — refreshing and a perfect finish after the rich eel rice.

Overall, a satisfying meal if you’re visiting Nagoya and want to try a proper eel rice set.

Best Unagi i’ve ever had period!!
It’s been a month and i still think about this dish. Normally, i don’t really like the bone texture of the unagi but this. You can clearly see the bone but do not taste it. The sauce not overly sweet and the unagi itself is crunchy on the outside and still soft on the inside.
It's a famous dish in Nagoya, with an average price of around 800-1000 baht. There are three steps to eating it, but it's basically the same as eel rice bowls in other cities.

name: Owada
reviews: Wonderful Una-don experience in Nagoya. I am well aware that Nagoya is famous for Hitsumabushi but since I had a shima-ochazuke for lunch, I decided to just for a traditional una-don and I feel slight regret for my decision as I really loved their Una-don... now I am curious how wonderful their Hitsumabushu will be, lol. I am definietely coming back here again in the future. If you want to enjoy your delicious, juicy unagi with a beautiful garden view right next to you, come to Owada.
Most customers are locals, the service is excellent. But the way they cook the unagi is the usual way we’re used to.
the quality is very high and the taste is same every time

name: Hameediyah Multi Concept Dining @ Bukit Bintang
reviews: We went here for dinner to try Murtabak and Nasi Kandar and it did not disappoint. We did feel a bit taken advantage of with the recommendations re. the nasi kandar options as those really inflated the price of the dish to 80% of the bill. Nonetheless flavors were there especially with the sambal and caramelised onions (deffo take this with the chicken) and atmosphere was good. 2 improvement points: okra was cold and the chef added like 7 different gravies which really was too much. A good place to go as long as you know what you want to order.

I simply wasn’t expecting this when i first heard that we’re going to have lunch at a nasi kandar place . Step inside and you would realize that the shop is beautifully renovated with nice warm lighting and relaxing music . There isnt a heavy smell of food items being fried which usually sticks to your clothes, so I guess ventilation here is good. Service is polite and courteous, not hurried. Food items displayed clean and pleasant to the eyes . We ordered our food and sat upstairs where it was cool with AC . I wanted to taste their roti canai as well and was told that roti only served before 11:00am . Overall, a nice lunch dining experience.

Hameediyah Multi Concept Dining at Bukit Bintang is a great spot for a satisfying nasi kandar experience. There’s a wide variety of dishes, rich and flavourful gravies, and the taste is consistently good. The restaurant is comfortable despite the lively surroundings, with quick service and efficient staff. Definitely a must-visit place if you’re craving proper nasi kandar in the heart of the city.

name: Tim's Teapot Terrace
reviews: I really enjoyed my visit! The tiramisu was delightful, and the overall vibe of the place was just so pleasant. The atmosphere here is truly top-notch. I'd definitely recommend checking it out for a relaxing time.

If you love vintage english style cafe, please do come to this lovely cafe.

Muslim owned cafe. They do have surau (bonus point).

The whole interior of this cafe just beautiful. Well decorated. I bet if you bring your mum here, she will be more than happy.

I tried their pasta, cakes & tea.

Pasta : 3/5 ⭐️
Cakes : 5/5 ⭐️
Tea : 5/5 ⭐️

If you love something less sweet, try their tea.

Their Medovik Honey Cake is to die for. One of the best cakes I ever had in my life FR! I can eat the whole cake by myself.

You can also do an intimate event here.

Overall was nice experience but I don’t like to find a parking spot here. Better commute with you friends to come here.
We loved the cakes and tea, and we saw other patrons enjoying burgers, fish and chips. The decoration is cute with lots of cute teapots displayed  in open shelves. Will definitely come again.

name: Suzuya
reviews:
I liked it a lot. I had hire-katsu, but I sort of wondered if it was any better than 'roast', which was the same price (so probably more voluminous?).

However, it was succulent and delicious. The miso comes separately, which is great (you can mix your bites up with miso, then salt, then sauce...).

There are two floors - on a Wednesday  evening it was only half full and there was no need to book.

Another local tonkotsu / misokatsu joint introduced by local friend.
Visited 30-mins before lunch and packed right after we ordered.
We tried the loin misokatsu, fillet cutlet with ebi, fillet cutlet with oysters, and crab cream croquette.
They were in 2019 michelin guide so you know what that means, delicious!

A long standing traditional tonkatsu joint run by a passionate chef. There's a good reason why this place has stayed on the tabelog top 100 for tonkatsu for so many years and the chef's passion for cooking shows in everything he does.

Both the loin and fillet tonkatsu cuts are a great value for money, and they also make a great crab cream croquette.

name: Bubble Bee Cafe
reviews:
I recommend to visit to this cafe after you enjoy the vibrant and creative street art at Petaling Street Art - you can access the cafe  at the end of the street.

They are serving rice, pasta, and sandwiches for brunch and dinner - they offer FREE drinks and dessert during weekdays (12PM - 2 PM) or upgrade drinks with half-price.

We ordered dessert and refreshments. Basque burnt cheese cake taste so good and best partner with lemon grass lime soda.

You can sit and relax on this area after the long walk in Petaling Street. The ambience is homy and the service is excellent.

Overall, I recommend this to everyone who wants to rest and who enjoy dessert and refreshments.

We ordered 2 set of meals. The food and the ambiance was great!!! But we think the attendant was not having a great day, because they were not smiling from the moment we entered the cafe until we left. Hospitality could have been better.

Was strolling around the area when I came across Bubble Bee Cafe 🐝✨ I tried their plain bubble waffle as I was craving it and it was really nice and crispy 😍🧇

Loved the vintage style cafe look. The vibes inside were really good and even though the cafe is not very big it felt cozy and welcoming 🤍☕️

A nice little spot to relax and enjoy something sweet ✨

name: Yōkisō
reviews:
We didn't pay to go into the house but enjoyed the garden for free. There's an Inari shrine with vermilion torii gates, and a pretty lake with a bridge that reminded us of Monet's paintings and his garden in Giverny.
There's a tea house, too, but you can only look in from outside.
The azaleas are beautiful, but were mostly finished when we were there, while the wisteria was not yet in bloom.

It was a super nice place to visit. The building is well maintained. I liked hearing about the owner, who is the creator of the matzukaiya stores that are in all the stations. The north garden was also good. It was awesome to hear how they connected a lot of the building via underground tunnels. The staff were nice and for 300 yen it was a nice place to explore while in the area.
Slice of history and not crowded with tourists. Very well kept luxurious villa + gardens. Really easy to walk and explore. Children and elderly friendly.

name: Lim Kee Cafe
reviews:
The coffee is good. A place to stop over for a quick coffee before shopping at Petaling st 🛍️🛍️. They don't have variety of pastry, just something simple to go with ☕🍹.
This cafe is connecting to a hotel, whereby the reception counter is located in this cafe.
Keep up the good work 🥰🥰😎
Cake and kaya butter toast were good. Place is smallish and a bit dim but cozy. Food price is on the high side but then this is KL and touristy place.
This place is all above vintage classical vibes , the old retro decor redesigned to look as if it’s 1950’s cafe, sipping piccolo latte while looking at the Jalan Sultan traffic goes by

name: Hakkai
reviews: Excellent food for lunch. Quick service. Enjoyed the fried rice, soup and ramen.

2026年2月21日(土)はっかいさん初来店です！
10時40分頃に到着して2番目でしたが直後に行列がさすがの人気店ですね
店内はテーブル席の構成のみで6.か7席でした
ラーメンとチャーハンのセットにしたかったのですが大に出来ないみたいなので仕方なくチャーハン大の単品で注文しました！
パラパラで美味しいチャーハン人気なのも納得！この感じだとあんかけチャーハンの方が美味しそうな気がしました

土曜日の12:30過ぎに初めて伺いました☺
熱田神宮の帰りに行列ができていたので、気になり思わず並んでしまいました😆回転が割と早くて15分〜20分くらいで席に着けました。
チャーハン大盛（980円）・中華飯（700円）・チャーシュウ麺（700円）・餃子（440円）
を頼みました☺
チャーハンは大盛でしたが、私は普通に食べれましたが普通の方は、並で十分だと思います。中華飯も並でも量は、多いほうかと・チャーシュー麺は並で普通な量でした😊

味は、全体的に優しい味付けですが３人とも大変美味しい😋と満場一致でした😊
リピート確定です😊
また絶対に寄らさせていただきます😆
中華飯は撮り忘れてしまいました🙇

name: REXPERIENCE
reviews:
Went to rexperience that day, I went for both XPRMNT and Lucid Loop and had a mixed feeling about them, I’m actually feeling happy to see artists started experimenting on this kind of Digital Art, and Frankly I think some of the scene is graphically decent, but on the other hand I feel a bit dissapointed and I think the ticket is too expensive for such experience?

Here’s some of my honest ( just my own ) opinion.
So basically the whole Rexperience is a kind of “movie” experience where you sit and enjoy the projected Art , where the projected artwork extends to the audience area, which is quite nice for the first few minutes. However I think what’s lacking for this is, the artwork is basically a loop of scenes where there is no apparent storyline and after a while you get bored from just sitting there. I get it it’s an immersive experience. But i think if it’s that case I would prefer it to have more interaction with the audience, like intteractive art or maybe the audience can just walk around rather than sitting there (sorry but I have to compare this experience from the one I had from TeamLab), because the ticket is not cheap right. So I guess it would be better if the visual is more narrative so that the viewers wont start looking at their phones half way.

I think Lucid Loop has very decent graphic but like what I said, after 10 minutes you mind will start drifting away, but it brings you to a strange world (yet you might find something familiar in an abstract way) which I fine it quite interesting.

I personally find the XPRMNT a bit boring. Firstly the scenes are obviously 3D scanned point clouds from real world but I guess that’s not an issue. The theme is about body movement, I was expecting it to be interactive to movement, but I later found out there was supposed to be dancer but not on that day I went, so with the lacking of drancer the dancing figure on the screen became a distraction of the scene. And I think another big problem in this artwork is that nothing else in the scene relates to the theme “body movement” apart from the body figure, which I think can be perceived as superficial and lack of depth and layers. Since the scene are scanned point clouds can those particle interact or changed with the movement? And also in my opinion the switching of scenes is too sudden and lack subtlety. And I can’t really relate those scenes, why are the places chosen? And what exactly are the body movement trying to tell in those scenes?

But with all that being said, I still appreciate artists who contributed to Rexperience because I don’t see many things like this around. Cheers 😄

I went for the TAPESTRY show, and the screen began to freeze during the first half of the screening. Went on a weekend during lunch hours so there wasn’t really much of a crowd. Honestly wished it was longer and didn’t feel like it was worth the price.
Short but fun - great venue. We saw Lucid loop and enjoyed it a lot - saw xprmt next day and it was ok. Recommend lucid loop.

name: Higashiyama Zoo and Botanical Gardens Main Gate Information Center
reviews: So wide that I have to go there for 2 days to see all over this zoo and botanical garden. Redpanda, Gorillas, etc are really cute. Highly Recommend!

for me its more benefial if u buy 1200yen for annual pass because 1 time already 640yen (all access). all the facilities are great, many toilets and restaurants provided. MUST try the slides in botanical garden!

The main entrance of Higashiyama Zoo & Botanical Gardens. Admission tickets for the zoo and botanical gardens cost 500 yen for adults, while admission is free for junior high school students and younger. If you include the Higashiyama Sky Tower ticket, the adult price is 640 yen. The view from the Sky Tower is stunning, so it is highly recommended to purchase the combined ticket.

name: Sandaya
street: Higashikawasakicho, 1 Chome−6−1 神戸ハーバーランドumie モザイク 3F
reviews:
This restaurant offers value for monies lunch sets, with fine dining setting and a pianist providing soothing music.
As the set lunch consist of a few dishes, do cater ample time for the meal. In summary, it was a pleasant discovery! Recommended 💪👍

Visited Sandaya for dinner after walking through Mosaic. The restaurant offers a classy and elegant atmosphere. I opted for the 140g Kobe Loin Steak. The staff was notably polite and courteous, though I found communication challenging as they didn’t speak much English – unexpected for a restaurant of this caliber. While the cured ham was a standout, I felt the overall meal, particularly the steak, didn’t quite live up to its price point. Some portions of the steak were great, but there were inconsistent cuts beneath. The accompanying salad was standard, and the tomato soup was basic. While the ambiance and service were commendable, I personally wouldn’t return based on my culinary experience.

If you are visiting mosaic mall in Kobe this restaurant is in 3F floor at the far end, the atmosphere may not be chic and upbeat but it is certainly clean and spacious. We really did not expect such amazing and professional service, even though they do not speak much english they made an effort to explain us the menu. Every cut of beef includes, ham, salad, soup, tea, dessert + coffee. We order Wayu sirloin and it was really tender and juicy, It was by far one the best meals we have had in our 14 days in Japan. Totally would recommend this place.

name: Korean Dining Shumiyoshi Sakae
reviews:
We ordered Korean BBQ, cheese toppoki and extra side dishes. The BBQ wasn’t bad but the ttoppoki serving was very small for two people definitely not enough. The side dishes had no flavor and especially the spinach tasted overcooked and oily.
The staff doesn’t speak Japanese/ English, I don’t think they’re Korean either so communication was a bit difficult.
Food quality in so good
I love korean food

name: Pizzeria KEN
reviews: The food is delicious but pricey in my opinion ¥1900 for lunch set as seen in the photo, one can choose between a pizza or a pasta. There are 4 or 5 types of pizza and pasta with special    type adding some coat to the order.

5 stars all around. I love Naples style pizza cooked in a wood fired oven. This pizza is the best. Dough is perfect - soft but crunchy crust, perfectly seasoned sauce, mozzarella cheese still tender and not chewy or burned and basil still fresh. Salad was great as well, and the corn soup was very nice.

Very cosy and friendly Japanese family-run pizzeria.

Wood fired pizzas and Bolognese were excellent. A showcase of Italian technique with local produce and flavours tuned to the Japanese palate.

name: Brocken Burger
reviews:
We stumbled upon 📍Brocken Burger by chance while looking for parking during this year’s Formula 1 Japanese Grand Prix. With all the lots near the circuit fully booked, we ended up parking about a 30-minute walk from our gate—what felt like a setback turned out to be a lucky find.

Brocken Burger immediately caught our eye. The moment we stepped in, we were mesmerized by the interior—eclectic, bold, and full of personality, with cool vintage-style decor and racing memorabilia that gave it a stylish, laid-back vibe. It felt like a cross between a hip diner and a motorsports fan’s dream café.

We stopped in for coffee and ended up ordering burgers, and we’re glad we did—the burgers were juicy, flavorful, and freshly made, just what we needed before the long walk to the track. The staff were friendly and efficient despite the busy crowd.

If we return for F1 in Suzuka again, we’d definitely make this a regular stop—for the food, the vibe, and that unexpectedly perfect pit stop feeling.

Rating: 4.5/5

I was mesmerized with this place’s vibe! It’s giving retro/vintage style.

Their burgers were good enough. Taco rice, on the other hand, was perfection! Prices for each order was pretty okay considering the great service and comfortable atmosphere.

Definitely recommend!

Looking for a satisfying burger with hot toasted buns and well seasoned juicy beef patties? This is the place! We recommend the mozzarella mushroom burger which has a nice cheese pull. Pair your burger with a refreshing grapefruit juice as part of the drink set, and enjoy the meal!

Kobayashi san and his staff’s warm friendly smiles will make you feel right at home. We also loved the outdoor seating (with hammocks!) which was lovely on a breezy autumn afternoon.

name: 長太の大楠
reviews: Good

平安時代からこの場所にある樹齢1000年以上の楠の木。周りが田んぼだけにこの大きさはすごい迫力です。

数々の災害を乗り越えてきた楠木。しかし2020年に落雷にあい半分以上枯れてしまったらしく、正念場に立たされているとのこと。

なんとか頑張って、これからも時代を見守っていてほしい。
これからも強い生命力を見せてほしいものです。

愛知蒲郡から
多分最初の記憶は
近大に通っていた
ＯＺの下宿に
何度か遊びに行く
アーバンライナーの車窓から
見つけたのが最初かな
そこから３０年
20250512
初めて訪れました
地元蒲郡には清田の大クスという天然記念物の大楠があります
それにも負けず劣らぬ威容
しかし２０２０年の落雷被害で
枯れ枝が目立つ
現在は樹木医さんによる
再生へのケアが施され
少しずつ新芽が
戻ってきているそうです
あとは木自体の再生力に
頼ることになります
今回はブラタモリトレースツアーの
二日目
四日市諏訪神社から
白子まで
伊勢街道散策の帰り道に
立ち寄りました
タモさんが導いてくれたのでしょう
祈復活！

20251208
三河一宮
大和の大銀杏
こちらも落雷被害に遭っています
樹木上部に
葉の茂っていない部分が見えます
今年も紅葉の季節を迎えました
すごいっ

name: Alor Street Pub & Bistro
reviews: Good place to explore around Bukit bintang for foods
What a wonderful restaurant! Tasty and cheap. Lots of cooking style you can choose

If you in bukit bintang, must go here..
A lot of kind of food, fruit, beverage and beer..

And with affordable price 😎

name: Old Market Square Clock Tower
reviews:
A significant historical landmark, the Old Market Square Clock Tower stands as a reminder of Kuala Lumpur’s colonial past. Built in 1937 to commemorate King George VI’s coronation, the tower has witnessed the city's transformation over the decades. Its architecture reflects the era’s British influence, making it an interesting stop for history enthusiasts.

However, the surroundings could be better maintained, as a noticeable number of homeless individuals gather in the area. Despite this, the clock tower remains an important heritage site in the city's landscape.

Beautiful place to take a break in this busy location.

Right next to the central market and river of life.

There is an old iconic clock tower. Well arrangements for kids.

Evening time is the right time to spend here, vibrance.

Recommended to visit.

This famous Clock Tower situated in the middle of market square is also featured in the Marvel Studios Thunderbolt 2025 Movie. You can see the scenes comparison in my photos.  The area has a place to chill, hangout and take a break from the hectic bustling city of KL.

name: Harbor Walk
reviews: If you are tried from shopping in Kobe harborland, you can come to this area to relax yourselves. Here you can see the shipyard on the opposite side and potentially able to see submarine. Once you reached the edge, there is a beautiful view of the whole harbor area. The night view is also amazing if you look towards the Marine Time Museum and the Oriental Hotel. Recommended to have a short walk here if you visit Kobe.
Great assortment of shopping, and restaurants.
Nice view of Kobe skyline from the water. Easy relaxing walk. And this is not a “hiking trail”, just a paved path on the waterfront.

name: OLA FROYO CAFE
reviews:
Cute little cafe for coffee and yoghurt ice-cream. We came in after going to the Chinese temple opposite.
Clean and bright with good vibes. The guys who served us were polite.
We had two hot drinks and then a yoghurt ice-cream with oreo toppings. Rm14 for hot drinks and RM16 for ice-cream in pretty central location are quite reasonable. Steep stairs but if you are a normal human being who pays attention to where you are walking, you should be ok!
Will visit again!

Cute little spot with very tasty yogurt ice cream and a great variety of toppings. The ice cream is very tasty and the staff very polite. Strongly recommended if you are in the area and you want a small treat!

The peach drink was extremely refreshing after a long day walk under the sun and the yogurt was slightly sour but it fits my tastebud 🤭 the price was quite reasonable but one thing that would definitely make me come back here is the atmosphere! It isn't crowded and very calming for a nice little break, the decorations inside are A MISS If you don't take pictures of them 👀 the staff are also very friendly and i enjoyed my break here!  overall, i would say i recommend anybody to come here! 💗

name: 織 -Ori- by Wellbe
reviews: Too pretty to eat! Yummy and lovely variety of seasonal dishes that go well with the miso soup and koshihikari rice. The goma tofu was my favourite. I would have preferred a slightly larger portion of rice and soup though!!
Food is delicious. Great variety! Choose the set with wagyu for 2! Service is great.

I hate writing reviews unless they're super positive but feel like I need to provide honest feedback.

It's obviously a new restaurant so perhaps there are still some teething issues. It was completely empty when we came and even by the time we left so it felt lacking in atmosphere.

The food looks pretty and it is, but the taste was average - especially by Japanese standards. For the price it was also very expensive. The chawanmushi had no flavour and could have used more salt or soy sauce.

Service was friendly :)

name: Street Art - Trishaw man
reviews: Unfortunately the mural is being slowly being spoilt and defaced by the pipe above it leaking rusty water all done it. It is running right down the drivers face in just about the worst place for it to leak.
Awesome art! I never imagined it was that large scale!
Easy to find, right by the bus stop. This mural like the others is impressive- if you like this sort of thing.

name: Lombard's Landing
reviews: Sanji’s restaurant at Lombard’s Landing is an amazing experience. 12 out of 10 experience. It’s truly impressive and interactive. The performers really put their maximum effort into becoming the characters and interacting with the guests. It’s definitely a must go for OP fans. Maybe it’s catered a little towards the female audience though…

Meal: Dinner
Day Visited: Friday
Budget: N/A
Closest Station: Universal City
Reservation Needed?: N/A
Payment: N/A
Kid Friendly?: Yes
English Menu?: Yes

VIP dining is on the second floor. The meals vary between lunch and dinner but includes dishes from a number of the restaurants from around the park. Sitting on the terrace is pleasant.

Food was good. I had Hamburg and it was tasty and good portion size. Service was good except for one server who refused to let us charge the phone. The rest of the servers were friendly helpful and attentive.

name: Lostgens'
reviews:
This is a really special place in KL, especially for art/printmaking lovers, people interested in history, archives and antiques.

The place itself is decorated beautifully - many of the letterpresses, wooden tables, stools and shelving comes directly from factories which have now shut down. The people who work there vary from young interns to artists in residence, who you will often find in humorous chatter, speaking about music etc. - all of whom are lovely, warm and welcoming. You can just walk in and request for some help with printing but they also offer specialised workshops. I had quite a magical afternoon making prints, which they allowed me to do at some point independently as they got on with their own work. A lovely space in the middle of a bustling city for some solitude.
Really cool. We just stopped by to have a look and ended up buying a stack of fun prints

A humble yet radical contemporary art space that connects community, locally and internationally. Exchange your ideas, knowledge, and stories here! Other than putting up art exhibitions, they also frequently organize classes and workshops (philosophy, dance, theatre...)

name: Cigar Cartel TTDI
street: 14, Ground Floor, Jalan Tun Mohd Fuad 2
reviews:
Date of visit : Wed 20.08.25
Walked in & hit by a funky musky smell. Air humidifier does nothing. Time for a deep clean - tables, chairs, walls, bar surface, floor, sinks - everything. The cloth for wiping dining table/surfaces must be rinsed after each use. Standby more than 1 cloth. Due to the smell, only ordered drinks.

Was introduced to this place by a Penang buddy. Been here twice - each time forgot to take pictures of the food before digging in :) best, best, best place for authentic Penang Nasi Kandar. The food is really good; their curries to die for. The service is good as well; everyone is always super friendly & attentive. Highly recommended for anyone who loves a good hearty Nasi Kandar. Their pricing is reasonable for the portion & taste.

Tasty and well prepared food. But the highlight is how friendly the staff are, very attentive too. I find the shop just a little hot and stuffy, but I won't give a low rating for that cuz thats how these restaurant are. It's a me problem, not theirs. Would I come back? Yes for sure.

name: Minori
reviews:
木曽川と揖斐川の中州にある、地元の人しかわからないであろう、このお店。

検索でヒットして行きましたが、一見さんはなかなか入りづらそうですね。

入ると地元の人に愛されているよ、拠り所のような居酒屋のようです。

なので居酒屋にハズレはなし！

⚫︎2025年6月2日訪問

ランチを注文
みんな手仕込み。
卵焼き、焼き魚、ウインナー、マカロニサラダ、ひじき、お味噌汁、大盛じゃないのに大盛ご飯(笑)。

家庭的でいいですね^ ^
お腹いっぱい！

地元民に愛されている感じの居酒屋といった感じでしょうか。ランチで伺いましたが、常連さんと覚しき方がお昼から飲んでいました。
定食メニューは豊富で、もちろん一品メニューもたくさんありました。お昼の定食はボリューム満点！とてもお腹いっぱい食べさせてもらいました。感動。また行きたいお店です

平日昼間に利用
個人経営の居酒屋のランチ営業

チキンカツ定食を注文

チキンカツはミンチにした物を成形しているのか肉感は無い
サクサクした歯触りを楽しむのも
付け合わせの千切りはマヨネーズ醤油ベースのオーソドックスなもの

酢の物やヒジキの煮付と漬物は水準維持
妙な雑味などは無く素直な味付

味噌汁はあわせ味噌で赤だしでは無い
具材はおそらく日替わりで本日は南瓜
個人的には出汁が強めだがほっとする味付

ご飯は大盛りクラスを頂けた
入店した時間にもよるかも知れないが炊き上がりは良く量も申し分ない

店内は禁煙駐車場の整備は無い
昭和レトロの味わいのある店内でもある

チェーン店にはない味付を感じたいのなら利用しても良いだろう
次回は別の物も注文してみたいお店

name: The House of Yeap Chor Ee
reviews: Thanks to Joanne our knowledgeable guide for the invaluable information and narrative. There were only our group of 4 adults, so it was like a private tour. Featuring intricate mother-of-pearl inlaid furniture, fine embroidery pieces with various bird motifs and artifacts of the Yeap family. The higher floors tell the intimate story of a Chinese immigrant who worked his way from a humble barber business to becoming a successful businessman and banker. Also heartening to hear how the family has supported many others in the community with philanthropic acts and the establishment of Wawasan Open University. I highly recommend this tour.

Fantastic history of the house brought to life by the phenomenal tour guide, Joanne, who was passionate, dedicated and very knowledgeable. I really enjoyed the detailed explanations given about many of the artefacts, and the tour answered many questions I had about Penang. Would definitely recommend this museum to everyone I know.

Very enjoyable museum. Found this on Google maps knew nothing of Yeap Chor Ee. But the curator Joanne was insightful and knowledgeable about the family history. And the history of Chinese immigration in the region and beyond. Well worth a visit . Also it is close to other attractions easy to visit.
Thank Joanne.

name: Jalan Rembia Street Art
reviews: Street art was good, but few places were very dirty and really smell bad.There was some construction work was going on,with open drainage. With bad weather the day before,the floor art was all covered with mud.

This was a very run down area a few years ago, but a lick of art and loads of bars and restaurants the place is a must see in KL. Entire blocks of flats have been painted including the exterior pipes and air conditioning units.
Definitely a neat little street to see in KL and its free so you cant go wrong

name: SAKU
reviews: Very nice place and delicious food

主人の誕生日に、利用させてもらいました。スタッフさんの対応がとても感じよく、お料理はどれも本当に美味しかったです。揚げ物で胃もたれしやすい私ですが、こちらの串揚げは何本食べても胃もたれせず、サクサクとしていてとても美味しいです。コース料理を注文していたのですが、どの串揚げも試行を凝らしていて、メニューを見ず、次は何が来るかと楽しみながらいただきました。誕生日祝いに、一杯ドリンクサービスがあったのも嬉しかったです！また是非、利用させていただきます！

場所はポートピアホテル内。三ノ宮駅から無料の送迎シャトルバスが出ていてアクセス良好。
創作串かつが食べられるコースが何種類かあります。
ご飯が付いているもの、いないもの、ディナーでは串の本数10本、12本、16本等、好みに応じて選ぶことができます。もちろんコースを食べた後に一本だけ追加なとも可能。
趣向を凝らした串かつはサクッとカラッと軽い衣で胃もたれせず美味しいです。
意外な組み合わせが美味しいはちみつチーズは食べたら驚くかも。
いつも予約でいっぱいなので、突然の訪問は難しいと思います。予約してから伺いましょう。

name: 香斧飯
street: Arimacho, 839 839 Arimachō, Kita-ku, Kōbe-shi, Hyōgo-ken 651-1401 日本
reviews: You need to queue at lunch time.  But with this price and taste, it's worth to wait if the queue is not too long.  The beef one is recommended.
Waited for 1 hour to get the food. So delicious! Worthy to wait a line. Staff members were so kind and patient to arrange the room for us.
To Be Able To Eat You Must Go Early And Line Up, Lunch Closes Early

name: Sanboh Kan (Goshoboh)
street: in the building of Tocen Goshoboh, 858 Arimacho
reviews:
This hidden gem really surprised us with their well crafted menu.
They also saved us from starving because all other restaurants were closing or not accepting any customers at around 6.30 pm.
Shouting thanks to this lovely place!
Very expensive for an underwhelming meal.
餐點精緻美味，沒有過多的調味料，可以感受到服務人員的用心和主廚的精心烹調，非常推薦住宿的人預約體驗，很值得：）

name: Jalan Alor Bukit Bintang
reviews: I went there 3 times and never regret it !
Price a bit expensive for local people

Best service
Good food

name: 洋食の祥
street: Minatojima Nakamachi, 3 Chome−１−2 神戸ポートビレジ1号棟 3号棟
reviews:
比較的空いていてゆっくりできました。
ランチメニュー頼むとドリンクが200円引きになるらしく、トンカツに加えてカフェラテもいただきました。

サクサクアツアツのトンカツは食べ応えがあり美味しかったです。
次はケーキを食べに行きたいかな🎂

近くにこんな良い店ができたなんて知らなかったです。
フライモノがカリッとしてて、とても美味しい。
揚げ方を研究されたとのこと。
また来たい店^_^

name: Nagoya Castle
reviews:
My second time visiting Nagoya Castle, and it still feels just as impressive as the first time. The castle is beautiful and full of history, and the surrounding park makes it a really nice place to walk around and take in the atmosphere.

One thing I enjoyed this time was stopping by a small ice cream shop nearby — super chill and perfect for a short break after exploring the castle grounds.

If you come here, don’t forget to try the Ninja ice cream. It’s fun, tasty, and kind of a must-try when you’re around Nagoya Castle.

¥500 Adult entry, discounts for students, seniors
Nagoyajo Station Exit 7- the Nagoya Monument was there, a pretty fountain, pathway to the castle had rows of food stalls, cafes.
Nice, breezy walk to castle gates. Shaded seating areas, souvenir shops, crows and other birds, there could be a scheduled open performance play (theatre)- it's free.
Lots of photographers, you can pay for your pictures if you agree. Separate payment for entering the castle.

Beautiful place. The only part of the castle that is open to public is the Honmaru Palace in which you can enter (with shoes off) and walk to see the different rooms and segments.

The Main Keep is shut off and not allowed to admit visitors since 2018 due to an earthquake that has resulted in some structural integrity issues with the building. But the exterior is still pretty and worth to take a look!

name: Plaza Low Yat
street: 7, Jalan Bintang off Jalan Bukit Bintang LYBB
reviews: Plaza Low Yat is THE best place in KL to buy your IT [and not only] staff. Anything on Earth is there: laptops, desk tops, phones, cameras, printers, you name it. Accessories,  spare parts, consumables, repairs: all that us there too. Need a bag to carry the staff: Leather Avenue is there with good promotions. Need a drone: no issue-huge variety. Basement food court is there with fantastic choice of dishes to feed you through your shopping spree. Need cash? ATM in the basement. Plus parking etc. Cool place.

Plaza Low Yat is the best place in Kuala Lumpur for electronics and gadgets. From laptops and phones to accessories and repairs, everything is available in one building. Prices are competitive, shops have huge variety, and you can bargain for better deals. A must-visit tech hub for anyone looking for electronics in Malaysia.

One of the best electronic markets in Kuala Lumpur. You can find almost every electronic item here, from small accessories to major electronics. There are many mobile showrooms, TVs, gadgets, and a wide variety of products available at competitive prices. The place is well organized and very convenient for shopping. Food counters are also available, so you can relax and eat while shopping. A great place for electronics lovers.

name: Fahrenheit88
reviews:
Fahrenheit88 is a vibrant shopping mall in Bukit Bintang that has successfully carved out a niche as the "hub of youth and trend." It is a favorite for those looking for stylish, affordable fashion and unique lifestyle products without the steep price tags of luxury malls.
The mall is particularly appreciated for its manageable size and curated selection of specialty stores. Visitors often highlight its energetic atmosphere and its role as a key destination for high-street brands.
* Flagship Retailers: It is home to the massive Uniqlo flagship store, which spans three levels and offers one of the most comprehensive selections of the brand's apparel in Southeast Asia.
* Beauty and Lifestyle: The mall features Sephora's largest store in Malaysia right at its entrance, making it a primary destination for beauty enthusiasts.
* Specialty Zones: It hosts several unique Japanese-themed retailers and affordable fashion boutiques that cater specifically to a younger, trend-conscious demographic.
* Strategic Location: Its position directly opposite Pavilion KL makes it a convenient stop for shoppers navigating the Bukit Bintang area, offering a more casual and accessible retail experience compared to its neighbors.
Overall, Fahrenheit88 is an excellent choice for a quick and trendy shopping trip. It is less overwhelming than the larger malls nearby while still providing a high-quality selection of global and local brands.

This mall almost always have an exhibition related to arts. If you are on a trip to KL and you love arts, this is a must visit stop. And can be easily accessed via mrt.

Just take note at night time, outside theres a lot of people because its in middle of bukit bintang.

I’m reviewing this mall based on handicap accessibility. We were here for an anime exhibition. It is a nice clean mall however the accessibility for disabled are lacking. The are no handicap parking then no ramp to go to the lift. In the photo, the left side of the glass door is opened but the right side of the glass is fixed in place. It’s a glass partition so it’s difficult to go in. Fortunately it’s just big enough for a wheelchair to go through. There are no handicap toilets. On the ground floor, there are stairs to the toilet which wheelchairs can’t travel on. On the second floor, there aren’t any stairs to the toilet but again. No handicap toilets. Lastly. This place still hasn’t started their cashless payment for parking and we had to take a ticket but the auto paying machine, again, doesn’t have a ramp.

name: Kobe Port Tower
street: Hatobacho, 5−5 神戸ポートタワー 低層3 4F
reviews:
A stunning landmark that looks absolutely spectacular at night. The Kobe Port Tower lights up beautifully and creates a perfect photo spot with the dark sky as the backdrop. The design is unique and really stands out from far away.

The whole area around the tower is calm and enjoyable to walk around. It feels safe, clean and relaxing, especially in the evening. Whether you are here for sightseeing or just taking photos, this is one of the must visit icons in Kobe.

A memorable and enjoyable experience.

Breathtaking 360-degree views! A must-visit landmark in Kobe.
I visited the iconic Kobe Port Tower and headed straight for the rooftop open-air deck. The experience was truly spectacular!
From the roof, I could view the entire city of Kobe without any obstructions. The contrast between the lush green Rokko Mountains on one side and the sparkling blue sea of Kobe Port on the other was absolutely stunning. Feeling the breeze while taking in the 360-degree panoramic view was the highlight of my trip.
The view is incredibly fantastic and gives you a real sense of the city's unique geography.

Kobe Port Tower is a fantastic landmark and one of the highlights of visiting Kobe. The tower’s unique design makes it stand out beautifully along the waterfront, and the views from the observation deck are absolutely stunning, especially during sunset and nighttime when the city lights up.

The surrounding Meriken Park area is clean, relaxing, and perfect for a walk while enjoying the harbor atmosphere. The tower is well maintained and offers a great experience for visitors who want to enjoy scenic views and take memorable photos. Definitely a must-visit spot when in Kobe.

name: Osu Shotengai Shopping Street
reviews:
Osu Shotengai Shopping Street in Nagoya, Japan — one of the city’s most popular stroll-and-shop areas 👇  ￼

⭐
describe it as a lively, eclectic shopping street with a mix of traditional charm and modern fun — sort of a local, less tourist-y version of big shopping districts like Tokyo’s Asakusa or Osaka’s Shinsaibashi.  ￼

🛍️

✔ Variety of shops & finds
•	Hundreds of stores selling clothing, souvenirs, vintage goods, anime cards, and quirky items.  ￼
•	love the vintage and unique boutiques, leather shops, and matcha shops with friendly owners.  ￼
•	There’s also a Don Quijote, gachapon/arcade spots, and places where you can find unusual souvenirs.  ￼

✔ Street food & eats
•	Many food stalls and casual restaurants offering local snacks like Taiwanese-style fried chicken, tanghulu (candied fruit), and other street eats.  ￼
•	Food is often a highlight — fun to try as you walk.  ￼

✔ Covered arcades & walking vibe
•	Covered walkways mean you can explore even in rain.  ￼
•	it’s a pleasant place to stroll, browse, and people-watch without crowds as intense as major tourist districts.  ￼

✔ Local atmosphere
•	More locals than tourists some days, giving it an authentic, lived-in feel.  ￼
•	Close to Osu Kannon Temple, which many visitors include in the trip.  ￼

👎 Common Critiques

✘ Not a huge luxury shopping scene
•	Some found it underwhelming compared to big fashion streets like Osaka’s Midosuji or Namba.  ￼
•	not all shops are interesting, and they ended up buying little.  ￼
•	Stores can start closing in early evening (many around ~6 pm).  ￼
•	Not a place for high-end fashion or massive malls — it’s more casual and local market-style.  ￼

🧠 Tips from Reviews
•	Visit on weekday or early to avoid weekend crowds.  ￼
•	Allow a couple of hours — you can easily stroll, snack, and explore side alleys.  ￼
•	Combine with a temple visit (Osu Kannon) and local cafés.  ￼

⸻

Summary: Great for casual shopping, street food, quirky souvenirs, and relaxed wandering. Best if you enjoy exploring lively local markets rather than big brand shopping malls.  ￼

Enjoyed exploring Osu Shotengai Shopping Street. The area has a lively, old-school charm with a great mix of traditional shops, street food stalls, thrift stores, anime goods, and small local boutiques. It’s the kind of place where you can wander without a fixed plan and still have fun.

There’s plenty to snack on, and prices are generally reasonable. The covered arcade also makes it comfortable to explore even in bad weather.

It can get crowded at times, but overall it’s a vibrant and character-filled shopping street that’s worth a visit when in Nagoya.

We have lunch and spend the rest of the afternoon shopping. Osu Shotengai Shopping Street is not as crowded as most of the shopping streets we have experienced in Japan. The walking streets are wider than the other shopping streets. So the shopping streets are easier to see and navigate. However, the Osu Shotengai Shopping Street does not have as many different kinds of stores. We ended up only purchasing a few things.

name: Kobe Harborland umie Mosaic
reviews:
Kobe Harborland umie Mosaic is a beautiful and lively place to visit, especially if you enjoy shopping, dining, and scenic waterfront views. The area has many unique shops offering mosaics, handmade gifts, and charming souvenirs, making it a great place to explore and find special items.

There are also many nice restaurants and cafés with outdoor seating where you can enjoy delicious food while looking out over the port. The view of Kobe Port Tower and the Ferris wheel is absolutely amazing, especially in the evening when everything is illuminated. It’s a wonderful place to relax, walk around, and enjoy the atmosphere of Kobe’s harbor.

It’s a nice area with several malls and harbour front view. There’s a ferris wheel and across the harbour a port tower and a hotel that light up at night. Notable shops and restaurants include 3 coins. Uniqlo GU Zara Seria Krispy kream gyukaku and many more. However it lacks luxury shops and overall speaking the quality of shops is not as nice as those in bigger cities.

Kobe Harborland umie is a prominent shopping and entertainment complex located in Kobe's waterfront area. The complex is divided into two main sections, North and South, connected on the first and third floors. It offers a wide array of retail stores, restaurants, a food court, and a movie theater, making it a popular destination for both locals and tourists.

Visitors appreciate the mall's accessibility via public transportation and the convenience of parking validation for purchases over 2,000 yen. Additionally, holders of the Umie card receive the first hour of parking free.

The complex is seamlessly connected to the Mosaic mall, which features international restaurants, shops, and entertainment options, including a movie theater. The observation deck in the Mosaic area provides picturesque views of the Kobe Harbor, especially during twilight.

Overall, Kobe Harborland umie offers a comprehensive shopping and entertainment experience, making it an ideal place to spend a few hours exploring, dining, and enjoying the scenic harbor views.

name: Hisaya Ōdōri Park
reviews: Quite nice green passage through the center if the city. Very inviting for a cozy stroll at day and night away from the crowds. Nice views for pics of the TV tower , sculptures and more. Lots of dining options along the entire stretch. Great venue for weekend fairs.

I almost missed this part of the town. Who would know there is an Eiffel Tower in Nagoya.🤗
I love you Nagoya, you have been so good to me, all the wonderful food, lively city, temples & shrines. I have had a wonderful time. Thank you!!🙏🏻❤️
This small park is in the middle of the street and has an iconic view to the tower. The park has some trees, some benches and a big plaza. It’s easy to pass by.

name: Tarbush Restaurant Bukit Bintang
reviews: One of the best restaurant serving the best food and top service! The waiters over there are very friendly and respectful. The food are super tasty and worth every single penny spent. On top of that, one of the main reason I go to that restaurant almost every week is because of one particular waiter, Shamim who treats me like a friend and give the best customer service! He definitely deserves a raise and promotion for the hard work and excellent job he is doing!

I've been putting this place on my wishlist ever since I saw it on Tiktok. However, all I can say is; it's pretty underwhelming.

We had to wait almost 25 minutes for the chicken. And the chickens are pretty dry. I was hoping for a more juicier meat, especially when you see the way they cooked their meat on social media. Honestly, for a place that boasts that their chicken are juicy, I wouldn't necessarily agree with that. The batter is good albeit again, a bit dry. It stayed on the skin even when you tear them apart. So for that, I give them props.

However, for the price that is a bit upper it is underwhelming to say the least. I probably wouldn't recommend this place to people, especially if they wanted to try the fried chicken. Maybe the Arab rice (although I haven't tried that one). A shame, really. It's definitely a case of my experience didn't align with my expectations.

From the outside, it may seem like a small place because the terrace is quite small, but once you go inside, you realize the restaurant is spacious and comfortable.

The food was very good and exceeded our expectations. We especially loved the shawarma. Well prepared, flavorful, and generously portioned.

Overall, a very positive experience. Definitely a place we would recommend and visit again.

name: Ho Kow Hainam Kopitiam
reviews:
From kaya toast to nasi lemak, this place gave us a great first impression of Malaysian cuisine. Overhyped? A little. Tourist-y? Yes. But still very deserving of 5 stars.
The kaya toast is outstanding — we tried several places in KL, Ipoh, and Penang, and this was the best. We arrived just before 9am on a Tuesday and had no wait, which was a bonus.
They have seating upstairs and the stairs are quite steep, so not ideal for elderly guests. QR code ordering was super convenient for tourists.
Would definitely return and recommend to first-time visitors.

Although the queue may look daunting, this place offers quick, efficient, and thoughtful service. It is best to come early, as the wait can be a test if you are impatient, but it is absolutely worth it. Note that if you come with luggage cases they will secure and place them aside in a luggage hold section for you.

Food is served promptly, and everything we tried was delicious. The menu is quite impressive, offering traditional Malaysian Chinese dishes that work perfectly for breakfast or lunch. Options range from classic kopi and toast to cheong fun and even croissant sandwiches. What impressed us most was the quality of the local coffee, which was rich, flavourful, and aromatic, easily one of the best we have had.

The interior decor is modern, neat, clean, comfortable and well designed, with a clever nod to the nostalgic feel of old school coffee houses, keeping only the best elements- making the dining spaces practical. The space is flexible, with tables that can be easily rearranged to accommodate both small and large groups. They even have a modern dumbwaiter for the staff to avoid having to carry food and plates up and down those steep staircases, which is a nice touch. The restaurant spans over three floors and two shop lots so there’s plenty of tables to fill.

The only issue is I ordered a take away tea for my uncle and requested no milk- as he’s lactose intolerant and the staff took the order with no issue. However, the tea had milk in it :/

Impressive service!  This is a super crowded place, you would think you have to queue very long, but because of their efficient way managing the queue, we only waited for less than 10min on a 8am Friday morning.  While waiting, we already ordered through the qr system. Once seated , upon confirmation, all food served within 5 mins steamy hot.  We couldnt finish a cake and asked to tapao. The staff took the cake, within 30 sec returned and packed nicely... Wow, McDonalds also not that fast like them... All staff very trained. They are highly focused, move around swiftly.... excellent.

Good good n great rustic ambience. Lovely and love it. Next time will return.

name: LUCK BROS KOPI @ Petaling Street
reviews: Revisiting the cafe at its new location. Lucky indeed to get seats almost immediately despite the big crowd for dinner. The Curry Mee was huge and tantalising, thick curry with the right level  spiciness. Salted Egg Chicken Chop was good, thick salted egg sauce packing up kicks in the meal. The Nasi Goreng was a bit heavy in flavor for us, but overall a good serving. Kids Roti Canai and fries surely make the young one happy. Charcoal roasted Coffee was just nice but could have been lesser charcoal flavor. Overall dining was enjoyable.

I have been a fan of LUCK BROS KOPI at Petaling Street for a while now. I visited three times throughout 2023 and 2024 and always had a great experience. Sadly, coming back in 2026, I noticed things have really gone downhill.
The salted egg chicken rice used to be my favorite order here. This time, the portion of chicken was much smaller and the salted egg sauce tasted very off. It was actually quite disgusting. I also tried the Maggi mee soup but it was a total letdown. The broth tasted like it was mixed with other noodle soups, which is not what you expect from a top rated cafe in Kuala Lumpur.
I understand that this is a busy restaurant in Petaling Street but that is no excuse for serving poor quality food to loyal customers. It is a real shame because I used to recommend this place to everyone looking for local Malaysian food. I hope they can get their standards back to where they used to be.

Nasi lemak is the greatest.I'm so excited to share my love for nasi lemak with you all today! 🍚 It's truly a culinary masterpiece, a symphony of flavors and textures that never fails to delight. it's an experience. 🌟 I highly recommend trying it if you haven't already! You won't be disappointed. #NasiLemak #MalaysianFood #Foodie #ComfortFood #Delicious

name: Clan Jetties of Penang
reviews:
View @ Clan Jetties Of Penang.
.
These are a series of historic waterfront settlements, built by immigrants from the late 19th century onward. These 7 communities were established as floating villages on stilts, allowing residents to avoid property taxes by building over water. Over time, the jetties evolved into vibrant hubs of maritime labor.
.
Each jetty is associated with a specific Chinese Hokkien clan, such as the Chew, Tan, Lee, Lim, Ong, and Yeoh families, plus a Mixed family jetty, reflecting the strong kinship networks that shaped early settlement patterns.
.
Today, they remain both heritage attractions and functioning homes, with the Chew Jetty, Tan Jetty, and Lee Jetty being the most visited.

We enjoyed our stroll down the jetties and managed to pick up some nice souvenirs. We bought a few sling bags for only 10MYR each which we bought for family and friends back home. The jetties are kept tidy and the souvenir shops are neatly packed and fairly priced if you consider it being a top tourist attraction.  We walked to the end of the jetties and took some nice photos over the water.

The path at Clan Jetty is safe to walk, with villagers’ houses on both sides. There’s a slight odour in some areas, but overall the scenery is beautiful and not too crowded. Along the way, there are souvenir shops selling kids’ clothes, keychains, and snacks, and the prices are quite cheap compared to other souvenir shops. You can also see fishing boats under the jetty, and the murals on the houses make for attractive photos. The property is clean and well-maintained.

Although we missed the sunset, we still got some beautiful pictures. One unexpected encounter with a local uncle on a motorcycle changed the atmosphere briefly—he was asking people to move away, probably because some visitors went into his boat service area, which closes at 6pm even though the jetty officially closes at 9pm.

Overall, Clan Jetty is scenic and peaceful, but it’s good to be mindful of private areas and local activities.

name: Chili's @ KLCC
reviews:
Nice view of the KLCC park from this restaurant window tables. Service is tip top, food was delicious and reasonably priced. Refillable fruit juice and soft drinks.
I love their tacos. Filling and delicious. Will definitely return again.

Chili’s Bar & Grill at KLCC has a great, lively atmosphere—especially during the holiday season. The view of the Christmas tree adds a festive touch and makes the dining experience more enjoyable.

The staff were very friendly, attentive, and clearly hardworking despite the crowd. Service was smooth and welcoming, which made us feel comfortable from start to finish.
