The food was satisfying across the board. The nachos were absolutely mind-blowing—crispy, generously loaded, and full of flavor. The wings were juicy, the sizzling chicken fajitas were fragrant and tender, and the pasta and salmon were nicely done. A solid spot for classic American comfort food.

The menu has been updated, and there are fewer grilled dishes now.
The food is generally good, and the portion sizes are reasonable for the price.
The fried chicken sandwich, however, is a bit dry and not very juicy.

Overall, a decent spot if you’re after a casual meal, but some items may not be as satisfying as expected.

name: 888 Hokkien Mee
reviews: Aaaaabsolutely the best Hokkien mee ever! The shrimp broth is rich and flavorful without any fishy smell, and the roasted pork is so tender, it pairs perfectly. There’s usually a queue, but it moves really fast, like 2 minutes per person. Totally worth the wait!

The best and most flavorful prawn hokkien mee I've tried so far.❤️ very thick layers of flavor and super enjoyable to eat. The roast pork even soaked in the soup still remains crispy and flavorful. The place is just abit too warm inside.

Reached 888 Hokkien Mee around 3.30pm and it was already pretty full. Definitely recommend coming closer to their opening time — can’t imagine how packed it gets in the evening. Make sure you secure a seat before placing your order, otherwise you might end up with food but nowhere to sit.

Despite the crowd, the queue moves fast. Tried the Hokkien mee, lor mee and oyster omelette — everything was good and satisfying. Worth the wait. Oh good to add roast meat! Double shiok

name: Black Kettle
reviews: First time here and already loving the environment, cozy yet relax. Ordered a salmon and quattro pizza, both are delicious! Highly recommend the cappuccino brulee too which is perfectly balanced of sweetness and coffee aroma. Will be back again!

Black Kettle offers a wonderfully comfortable and spacious environment, perfect for anyone looking to relax, work, or host a small event. The layout gives customers a sense of freedom and privacy, making it easy to enjoy your time without feeling crowded.

Their croissants look incredibly appetizing, with that golden, flaky texture that immediately catches your eye. The coffee is exceptionally good — rich, smooth, and brewed to perfection.

Overall, Black Kettle is a great spot to unwind, enjoy good pastries, and savour excellent coffee. Highly recommended!

Ordered the Egg Benedict, mushroom soup and a matcha latte.
The environment was quiet and comfortable, and the service was good.
The Egg Benedict was quite nice, with a moderate portion size.

name: Penang National Park
street: Pejabat Taman Negara P. Pinang jalan Hassan Abbas
reviews:
We visited the National Park Penang where we had a fantastic day and experience. We hiked the 1 - 1.5 hour tour to the turtle beach where we visited the sanctuary and chilled for about an hour. The boat picked us up and brought us to the monkey beach where we spent another hour and enjoyed a coconut. After that the boat took us back to the spot where we started the day.
We started around 1 pm and finished around 5:30 pm.
Entrance fee is 50MYR per person and the boat fee was 120MYR per group (2 pax). Cash payment only but there is an ATM next to the entrance.
Coke Zero 6MYR
Coconut 10MYT

Feel like nature and Hiking this is a perfect place. Mix of jungle trails and beaches. I did the monkey beqch hike to the lighthouse. All the way to Monkey Beach is very moderate but when you get to the lighthouse part its pretty much uphill. Not much is he in the lighthouse it's you can't go in it, but you can go around the area. they have restrooms up there. How long do we go get to see a bunch of Wildlife, monkeys, massive monitor lizards and one sea otter. You can take a dip in monkey Beach, water is okay there and not to deep. Want complaint is so  trash and plastic bottles everywhere on the beach. I saw one some dead fish and one dead turtle...which was pretty sad!

Better than I expected, very good customer service, quick and easy. Very nice boat driver, beach was a little dirty but not bad overall, 10/10 experience. 100% recommend coming here in the morning instead of afternoon as it gets really hot. Toilets are dirty but it works for me, really nice people on the island. Absolutely recommend coming here to get away from work!

name: Port of Kobe Earthquake Memorial Park
reviews: A deeply moving and beautifully maintained memorial. Port of Kobe Earthquake Memorial Park (神戸港震災メモリアルパーク) offers a powerful tribute to the victims and survivors of the 1995 Great Hanshin Earthquake. The preserved section of the damaged waterfront serves as a stark and emotional reminder of the earthquake’s impact, while the informative displays provide meaningful context. It’s peaceful, respectful, and educational—an important stop for anyone visiting Kobe. The park’s location along the harbor adds to the experience, making it a place of both reflection and quiet beauty. Highly recommended.
would definitely recommend if you are looking for a place to learn more about the impacts of earthquake on kobe’s port. also next to the port which is very scenic during sunset.

☑️A special place where people can recall terrible damages earthquake and natural hazards had been caused for our lives and then could have feasible solutions to protect our environment.
☑️This water area is protected by concrete coastal structures which are placed close together to mitigate wave attacks from sea.

name: Kobe Cruise Concerto
street: Higashikawasakicho, 1 Chome−6−1 神戸ハーバーランドumie モザイク 1F
reviews:
Had teppanyaki course (5pm session).
Food: it was my first time trying Kobe beef and it was melting.
Service: they didn’t bring the ordered drinks, until they were reminded. The drinks menu is overpriced.
Atmosphere: the chef cooked and served within 30 min, after that he leaves. There was no live music, no additional entertainment, unfortunately.

The evening cruise was just lovely.  Had a great time.  The city lights on the evening cruise is something I whole heartedly recommend.  Food was good along with professional photographers going around to snap your photos (for a few of course). I did the iron chef and it broke down to about 95 bucks a person.  Not bad for a cruise and delicious dinner.

You can board the ship without ordering the food here. Free view on third floor outside deck and inside cafe aquamarine (you can sit down without ordering the food or drink).

Beside that on first floor on lobby behind piano is also free view.

There is also music and song perfomed by local musician inside the ship

View is ok at night if you want romantic experience but in my opinion if you want to aee scenery better at day. Great experience and view for 2 hours long. Very recommended.

name: Brands Outlet Fahrenheit88
reviews:
This Malay female staff was being very rude and made me really upset. She rolled her eyes and sarcastically gave a comment about not buying after trying.
??? Customers have the option to purchase whether they like it or not. And I only tried for like fifteen minutes with two pieces, I really don’t understand why she’s being so rude about it. PLEASE don’t work if you can’t provide proper services.
Worst shopping experience ever, pls train your staff proper manners😅😅😅😅
Very good quality cloth store with affordable price.I have bought several cloths amd1 caps for my kids.

I had a very disappointing experience at BO. I purchased a product and returned within five minutes to change the color, but the staff refused, even though the receipt clearly mentions a 14-day exchange policy.
The staff behavior was rude and unprofessional, and they claimed the policy had changed on the spot. Overall, a very poor experience that did not meet my expectations.

name: Miyakishimen
street: Jingu, 1 Chome−1−1 熱田神宮境内 くさなぎ広場
reviews: Kishimen (flat udon) is one of Nagoya’s specialties and this shop sells a really good version of it. The dashi broth has a good balance of sweet and savoury flavours to it and is great for warming yourself up now that the weather is getting cold. If you’re getting the set meals, I highly recommend getting the one with the kakiage on rice because it tasted even better than the kishimen itself. Crispy, not excessively oily, and they sauce they drizzle over it is like crack. Overall a good place to stop by for a meal if you’re exploring the Atsuta-Jingu shrine area, and the kakiage itself would have gotten 5 stars from me
Really enjoyed our meal here, udon + dessert, out door eating with nice view, undo noodles shop and dessert shop they are next each other! No English menu but has pictures which helps for ordering.
Kishimen here is the perfect dish to enjoy at the end of a visit to Atsuta shrine - Warm, full of flavour but also nicely balanced. Peaceful space on the temple ground. Would definitely recommend.

name: Alva KL
street: Level 99, Ascott Star KLCC, 1, Lorong Yap Kwan Seng
reviews:
I have visited this restaurant three times, and I always order the same dish because it tastes really good and suits my palate well. During my third visit, the food was slightly salty, but it was still acceptable.

The service here is excellent. Special mention to Roses, who was very helpful, friendly, and accommodating. She assisted me multiple times with taking photos and was always pleasant. I was served by her during my first two visits. On my third visit, I was served by Myra (if I’m not mistaken), who was also kind and attentive.

Overall, this restaurant offers good food, great service, and value for money. I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a good seafood aglio oglio, and I will surely return again.

This was one of the most amazing places to eat! Me and my husband celebrated our honeymoon here and the food was AMAZING!

We ordered the garlic wings, mac and cheese, beef ribs and mocktails.

The food as you can see in the pictures tasted fantastic you can tell they only used quality ingredients.

Now last but not least the staff were absolutely amazing! They gave us a table right next to the patrons towers making our pictures amazing!

Shar served us throughout the night and he was SO kind and helpful! He took our orders and our food arrived very quickly!

This is one of the best places I have eaten in KL and it is worth every penny!!!!!!

MAKE SURE YOU VISIT YOU WONT REGRET 🤩

Garlic Prawn Pasta - super tasty carbonara pasta with charcoal grilled Tiger Prawn. Amazing treats on your taste buds! 🤤 5 giant wokhay-smell Tiger Prawn with creamy pasta. defintely 666 yyds 💯

Bolognese Bliss - A perfect Bolognese pasta, 💯. Flavorful tiptop taste 😋

Chili Lime Chicken Skewers - Super ngam chicken thigh meats with zesty lime sauce. 🍋‍🟩 yum yum taste!!

Truffle Chips - The best truffle chips I have tasted in my life so far, no cap 🧢 It is hand-made properly fried, crispy and im crying with tears on every bites, 🥹😭 yummy 99!

Here comes the bad side. There were one or two male waiters who did not smile at ALL when serving us 🫠 His face was like we owe them 100k, soury and like we hurt his feeling 😑 This is what makes this review kurang 1star 😑

Overall food is tasty, worth the price. This is a good choice for first skydining experience 👍🏻

name: Queen Victoria Memorial Clock Tower
reviews: I visited the Victoria Memorial Clock Tower during my time in Penang. It is located very close to Fort Cornwallis, making it easy to visit while walking around the waterfront area of George Town. Unfortunately, the area surrounding the tower was under construction, which took away from its historical atmosphere. In addition, a garbage collection truck had crashed into the tower, resulting in a very disappointing view. I could not help but wonder how a vehicle managed to drive into such an iconic monument. It was unfortunate, as the clock tower itself is elegant and historically meaningful.

The Queen Victoria Clock Tower is a charming historic landmark in George Town. Its elegant design and bright white facade make it stand out among the surrounding buildings, and it’s easy to spot while walking around the heritage area. I enjoyed pausing here to take photos and admire the architectural details up close. The area around the tower is open and easy to explore on foot, giving you a sense of the city’s colonial history. It’s a small stop, but a nice one if you want to see Penang’s heritage and iconic sights while strolling through George Town.

The Queen Victoria Clock Tower is a beautiful historical landmark in George Town. Its classic design and well-preserved structure reflect the rich heritage of Penang. The area around the tower is clean and lively, making it a great spot for photos and a short walk. Located near the Esplanade, it’s easy to visit while exploring nearby attractions. A must-see place for history lovers and visitors to George Town.

name: Kafka Coffee
reviews:
A nice place to have a meal...⭐⭐⭐⭐🟡
Tryout the dirty latte (cold) and when it was placed on my table, was surprised to see that there isn't any ice cubes inside the drink. After tried out the drink, then I can understand and appreciate that ice cubes shouldn't be added , cos they would deliute, weaken it's natural fragrance and flavour and taste....
The presentation of the glass of drink reflects the drink name "dirty" latte as the glass surface of the drink, can see clearly it's  different tone/shade of the ingredients of the drink. Can sense the deliberate intention to let the ingredients' natural setting to mix together but leaving those that were settled onto the glass surface to remain as it's natural tone/shade...  ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Love the coffee strong flavour & fragrant⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Love the strong milk flavour & its texture within the coffee that perceive/enhance a second & third level of enjoyment & appreciation⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Food was good...⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
However the vegetarian dish, its portion of  leafy green veges seems to be a bit less... If a bigger portion of leafy green was designed the dish would be great ⭐⭐⭐🟡🟡
The portion of eggs, bread, avocado was good... ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
The mushroom was tasty & flavourful.... ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Overall was very good⭐⭐⭐⭐🟡 and there's room for improvement....

It might be a little tricky to find the place since it’s tucked away inside, but the exterior is beautiful, decorated with lush green plants that give it a refreshing touch.

Came here with my family on a Sunday afternoon, it wasn’t too crowded, and the atmosphere was calm and relaxing.

The portions were generous, I ordered the ravioli and thought it might not be filling, but it turned out surprisingly satisfying. The chicken chop was huge and packed with meat. The drinks were great too — the dirty latte had an interesting and pleasant twist.

Would definitely revisit this café!

Decided to try this place for brunch. Found this place from penanglicious site (not a very accurate site for review).
Parking is available within the vicinity, though not many. On a Saturday morning 12pm still can get a few.
Ambiance inside isn’t crowded, still had a number of seats.
Ordered a chicken p-something, cant recall the name- see the image and a matcha latte with  oat-milk no sugar.
The chicken is ok, not dry still has flavor and what not but imo just ok. Would i reorder…uhh nah i’ll pass.
Now comes the not so nice part, the matcha latte is just horrid. The powder isn’t mixed in well, it’s bitter, even with the oat-milk. It has this weird astringent dull not pleasant after taste. I know this isn’t usucha or koicha grade matcha or high end level but this matcha quality is just badddddddddd. Also, I know this isnt a specialized matcha cafe but if you decided to serve something, it should be done at least to a basic decent level.

The waiters are ok, polite and all thar. Service is fine.
Would i come back….uh….do I have to? Maybe, i guess, if i have to…

name: Cesari Pizza osu
reviews:
We had a lovely experience at Cesari Pizzeria Braceria CESARI. Service was warm and attentive, and the food overall was impressive. We ordered two set lunches — the appetizers were the highlight, especially the chicken liver pâté, which was outstanding. The pizza sauce was excellent, and the oyster & spinach special pizza of the day was surprisingly well balanced and delicious.

The only area that could use a little improvement is the thin-crust pizza. The dough has good flavour, but the crust became a bit soggy, causing the sauce and toppings to slide off. With a bit more refinement in handling the sauce-to-crust balance, it could be fantastic.

Tiramisu was enjoyable, and the yuzu ice cream had a nice, creamy touch. Overall, a very good meal and definitely worth visiting — looking forward to coming back to try more.

I visited Cesari Pizzeria Braceria CESARI and was genuinely impressed. The pizzas are excellent, full of character and depth. I tried the classic Margherita and their special shrimp pizza and the shrimp version easily became my favorite. Perfectly balanced, rich, and memorable.

Nothing will ever beat a proper Turkish Lahmacun for me, but that doesn’t change the fact: the service here is warm, the atmosphere inviting, and the pizza truly outstanding. They fully deserve their Michelin recognition.

Anyone who disagrees can go back to their cheap frozen pizza, this place plays in a different league.

A great spot for a quick bite with amazing food! Located along a whole street full of international flavours, this spot is a gem Truly italian and super fast and easy. The pizzas we had were one of the best pizzas across Japan and even italy. Flavours were on point and the super long fries are light, crispy and delish!

name: Port Island Kita Park
reviews: Because this park exists just beneath the bridge connecting Kobe port terminal and Port Island, mosto of the passers-by on the bypass way do not recognize here. Consequently, visitors here must make some detour for the purpose. Hidden place as it is, suitable for lunch or spending time in calm and stable condition, not so broad but good place for couples and families, toilet is fairly prepared, no food supply nor drinks. Parking place near by.  I appreciate this place as some hidden place.

This is a perfect spot for viewing the beautiful 神戸大橋, also the various boats passing towards both direction around the busy 神戸港. From here, you can see the 神戸大橋 is actually a double-layered bridge, with busy traffic of both direction on each layer. You can come to visit this park by walking along the 神戸大橋. The bridge and this park altogether would be a nice jogging loop route, too!
Kita Park offers an excellent view of Kobe and the Port area. Very nice walk across the bridge if you want some fresh air.

name: Osso Brasil
reviews:
It's delicious but kinda overpriced when regarding the portion size and taste, I ordered a set with chicken, salad and Brazilian fried pastries, everything tasted fine but nothing spectacular, I would love to eat here again but the price doesn't encourage me to do so, as I can eat food with the same quality and portions and pay much less money, regardless it was still a good experience.
Overall, I recommend trying the food here at least once, although I recommend avoiding chicken and salad dishes as they are pretty average.

I ordered a set of rice and grilled chicken with salad and bean soup. This is the first time I tried brazilian food. I’m very happy with this meal. The server was kindly helpful with the menu and explain them in english.

Great reprieve from all the miso and traditional Japanese food! The roast chickens are delicious. The French fries were also solid

The system is fairly simple, order your food at a ticket machine. A whole chicken is about ¥1800. If you’re eating in, I advise ordering is carved up. You can also order take away and Uber Eats was picking up chickens for delivery while we were there.

name: Misakiya
reviews: No words needed for this place. If you are looking for the best deal in town for yakiniku, this is the one for you! Cheap and delicious. How can uou ask for more🥰 On top of that, their drinks are cheap too! Cannot compare to any other places in Tokai area. Don't forget to get the soft ice cream on your way out.

Great atmosphere, a big serving with rather cheaper price, truly a place to relax without worrying the price. Strength is on pork, not on beef like most other yakiniku places. But of course, due to its fame, the waiting line is hideous. Better head there very early or very late.
The foods great and it's cozy but the waiting list is too long so if you're planning to eat here it's good to make a reservation first. ☺

name: Tan Jetty
reviews:
Tan Jetty felt quieter and more local compared to the more popular jetties in Penang. If you want a slower and more peaceful walk, this is a good place to visit.

The wooden houses on stilts and the narrow walkway give you a glimpse of traditional waterfront living. It’s simple, but that’s what makes it special. You can see fishing boats nearby and feel the sea breeze as you walk toward the end of the jetty. The view of the water is calm and relaxing, especially in the late afternoon.

There are fewer shops here, so the experience feels more authentic and less commercial. Just remember that this is a residential area, so being quiet and respectful is important. A nice stop if you want to see a different side of Penang’s heritage.

Tan Jetty is right next to Chew Jetty and is definitely a must-visit. I personally liked this place much better because of the scenery. I didn’t visit last year, so I’m really glad I came this year.

I went early in the morning and took lots of pictures. I’m sure I will remember this beautiful view for a long time — it was very impressive! I also heard this is one of the best spots for sunset, so I strongly recommend visiting when you’re in Penang.

Easy to get around. The overwater walkway offers amazing scenery, however it can become quite crowded. Unfortunately, many people seem to lose their common sense when the area gets crowded, making the walkway less safe than it should be. Be cautious while walking, especially during peak hours, as it may feel tight in some areas, so take your time and walk carefully.

name: Gurney Mall
reviews: As I'm part time student, so usually i will definitely come to this mall to relax and buy some food. Overall many varieties pf food store they have now. Mixue, shawarma, ayam gepuk, sushi and more

Gurney Mall is a small but convenient shopping complex that serves the surrounding community well. It’s not a large-scale mall, but it has all the essentials in one place — from clinics and pharmacies to convenience stores like 99 Speedmart and 7-Eleven. There are also a few popular eateries such as KFC and Subway, making it a good spot for a quick meal or takeaway.

The mall is clean, easy to navigate, and rarely overcrowded, which makes running errands or grabbing a bite quite hassle-free. While it may not offer high-end shopping or entertainment options, Gurney Mall is a practical and pleasant place for daily needs and casual visits.
First time visiting the compact mall popular among UTM KL Campus students. It has a simple and beautiful entrance with plenty of shops to cater to the mall patrons' needs.

name: Kuromon Sanpei
reviews: Nice seafood experience at the Kuromon Market. You can choose from different types of seafood, ready to eat or to be cooked for you. From king crab legs to octopus. I had a seared scallop with sea urchin, strong umami flavors, along with a piece of octopus that was bbq’ed, a nigiri platter with tasty tuna and other fishes, and a portion of sea urchin. The sea urchin was good, but I’ve had better in this market. All this with a cold beer, seating on a large table. Would recommend for groups and to try different things.

A smorgasbord of seafood offerings in a clean, organized space. We came near closing time and some a la carte offerings were tagged 50% off (半額)！ Larger sets were also discounted but less. All delicious! And fresh, even at the end of the day (family is extra sensitive to non-fresh food)
We paid (cards accepted),and sat at one of the many tables with our spoils, enjoying the food, music, and the tea on tap. There are more prepackaged items like whale(!) and pufferfish(!) but we'd had our fill. Also, bathrooms are clean, they have you take off shoes and use provided slides.

Very fresh sashimi, including tuna belly, abalone, and crab etc. Prices are reasonable and clearly labeled on each item. No issues with ordering and the staff, especially the cashier were super friendly.

name: THE GATEHOUSE
street: Meieki, 1 Chome−1−3 名古屋JRゲートタワーホテル 15F
reviews: Great value for the lunch set with fish or meat (chicken) for 3400 yen. Lovely soup, salad dish and mains with dessert. Kids plate good value at 1000 yen. Recommended. Was lovely to sit outside and enjoy the garden and have some space to relax

We went on a weekday for lunch. Their lunch set comes with a drink bar where you can enjoy unlimited drinks. You receive a plate of salad and assorted bread. For the main course, we had the fish and chicken, both of which were great dishes. I personally preferred the chicken, which had a hint of Thai-style green paste on the side (if you cannot handle spice or heat, don’t add it). For me, it was an excellent dish—the chicken is slow-cooked with capers and fennel. The fish is seared perfectly and paired with a refreshing cucumber and dill sauce. Overall, the service was great; the waiters explained the menu and asked us if we had any allergies. Helped us take a photo. Happy to have had this experience.

Great place to be with nice view. The lunch time during weekend is clouded with ladies but the restaurant is trying their best to keep providing descent services. Foods are good but bit intense and salty. Need to fetch drinks by yourself for the certain set-menu but tanked coffee and cold-tea is good.

name: Kinopio's Cafe
reviews:
Kinopio’s Café is themed around Toad and is easily one of the must visit restaurants in Super Nintendo World at USJ. The immersive Mario themed setting makes dining here a fun experience from start to finish.

Be prepared to queue, on our visit, it took about 30 minutes just to reach the ordering counter. You order first, receive a number card, and staff will arrange seating and deliver the food to your table. Menu options are limited and prices are on the higher side, but every dish is incredibly cute and well-themed.

The restaurant design is outstanding, styled as the Mushroom Kingdom kitchen with bright colors and playful decorations. There’s so much to look at, and the atmosphere is excellent.

Popular items include the Mario Burger, Super Star Rice, mushroom shaped pizza, mushroom soup, Question Block tiramisu, and Princess Peach cake. All dishes are very photogenic and perfect for taking photos. Taste wise, the food is enjoyable and satisfying.

Overall, it’s a great place to rest, eat, and take photos. Highly recommended to set aside time for this very popular café when visiting USJ—especially for Mario fans and families.

We visited the restaurant during opening hours, so there we didn’t have to wait in line to order, and I have no idea how long the line gets. I ordered the Teriyaki Chicken with Superstar Rice, the Super Mushroom Pizza Bowl, and the Superstar Lemon Squash. The Chicken was sooo good, and the sauce paired with it 👌. I had a great time enjoying the mushroom pizza bowl. I especially loved how it was served on a cheese-themed tissue, which really elevated the overall presentation of the dish. While I enjoyed the beverage as well, one of the floaters was noticeably harder than the others, which slightly impacted the overall drinking experience.

+ The staff inside were very friendly and even offered to take our picture
++ The warmth of the restaurant was a nice break from the cold weather outside
+++ The place is so cute !

You have to snag a reservation through the QR code plastered at the entrance. We kept refreshing and trying until something popped up. Think cancellations are quite common so don't give up too easily.

You're allowed entry 10 minutes before your designated time slot, and you're allowed to change your order before you actually pay.

The dining area is massive, and the animations on the wall are quite entertaining (they play a fun sequence every 20 or so minutes). The food was not bad; above average for theme park food. Teriyaki chicken was a little salty. Pizza bowl was surprisingly good. Was a little disappointed that they used the same rice base for the super star rice and the omelette rice (in which the eggs were overcooked by the way). Anyway the dining experience and the atmosphere made up for it.

name: Chinatown Penang
reviews: Chinatown Penang, street food, has both Malaysian and Indian local food, coffee shops all the time. Today I came in the morning, there weren't many shops open in the morning. The evening is probably more suitable for walking around and choosing food. For the street food experience in Penang.
World heritage site. Street art, lots of yummy dining choices. Loads of history.
Is lovely to just walka around appreciate beautiful decorations, enjoy food, visit temples.

name: Presgrave Street Hawker Centre
reviews: Smallish hawker centre with limited seating but some good good stalls. Particularly the duck egg Char koay teow cooked over charcoal. Hokkein mee also was very nice, ais kacang a little disappointing.

Loved the oyster omelette! Probably one of the best I've ever had in Asia. CKT was really good as well, but could've had a bit more wok hei.

Just be aware that they make you buy a drink to use an outdoor table, regardless of how much food you order. I found that quite odd, and didn't experience this at any other local hawker center or food court.

Everything we tried was worth coming back. The highlight is definitely the pork satay with lean and juicy meat.

The pork dumplings are meaty and tasty.

The Char Kway Tew with extra eggs is not too greasy.

The oyster omelette is not too starchy.

name: Kuala Lumpur Railway Station
reviews:
The building is undergoing renovation (my visit as of Dec2025).

Stayed there for 2++ hours waiting for ETS.
The condition there is not good when come to heavy raining. The announcement from the speaker is too soft and we cannot catch anything.
Some walkway is not well shaded/covered and will get wet during raining.

Is nice to visit for random people or visitors, but if going for ETS, better go to KL Sentral for now.

I like this station a lot since many years ago when start taking KTM and ETS, since is less crowded, better view and within walking distance to Pasar Seni and now MRT.
Beautiful old railway station in KL. We caught the train to visit the National Mosque. The station was deserted. It is a window into the past. Worth a visit.

A majestic old building in need of some maintenance but still quite functional. Inside is a clinic and ticket office (never anyone at the window, always in the back chatting but if you call out someone will come out to help you). 4 platforms and entrances from both sides of the building. You can also enter from the new entrance just north of the station which has a walkway connecting to the Pasar Seni station.  I used this station many times with no issues.

name: Spaceship-Aqua Observation Deck
reviews:
Awesome place to visit in sakae.
A three-dimensional park with various facilities, including the glass roof Spaceship-Aqua, where you can take a walk through the sky 14 meters above the ground, a large lawn called the Field of Green, a half-underground Bus Terminal, an underground event facility called the Galaxy Platform, and around 30 different shops. Spaceship-Aqua is lit up at night, so it's very popular as a photo spot.

The "Field of Green" is on the ground level where flowers and trees are planted. The "Galaxy Platform" is basement level where many events are held. Also on the ground level, there are various shops and restaurants, and a connecting to bus terminal on the second level.

The TV tower area is nice, there's a large open area there that had a bunch of people singing, dancing and taking pictures of all the women dressed up which was very interesting to see. If you go to the top of the open area which had an elevator or stairs you can get a great view of the tower and city.

Nice place to chill and take the sights of Nagoya in..
Beautiful view of the township.
Alot of eateries at the bottom levels.
Careful on the walk.. can be slippery

name: Dino's Thai Food
reviews: My new favourite restaurant in Bukit Bintang! This Thai food is super authentic, delicious and well priced. Friendly attentive staff and a nice chilled seating area out front to watch the hustle & bustle of the City.
We ordered set meal for 5pax. We changed slightly the menu from siakap 3 rasa to siakap stim limau. We added on mango salad/kerabu mangga. Tasted good. Tomyam kaw.

I saw they had an array of seafood-fish selections available. I asked the nice server if they could recommend dishes with minimal to no spiciness please. They showed me the menu choices and I finally decided on a fish Ayam Bakar dish. Of course, no spiciness.

Not bad and quite a bit of fish throughout too. It was also accompanied with sweet-n-sour vegetables as well.

name: Illusion 3D Art Museum
street: Lot 4.01 - 4.03, 2nd Floor, Central Market Annexe, Jalan Hang Kasturi
reviews: Nice, its opposite of centeral market, take stair and follow the directions 50MYr ticket price,  only one air conditioner working others rooms air conditioners were off, over all good experience

Very interesting and fun place to spend an hour. Plenty of different 3d images you can take pictures of. All designed to be more effective with another person in the shot.
Nice staff, very helpful with suggestions to get the best possible picture.
Very reasonably priced, especially for us older folk and well worth a visit!

The museum is full of fun and creative 3D art – perfect for taking unique photos 📸 But what really made the visit special was the incredibly kind lady at the entrance. She kindly offered to help take pictures, showed me the best spots and angles, and was super welcoming throughout.
Big thanks for her warmth and professionalism! Definitely recommend this place 🙌🏼

name: Timothy Cafe
reviews: The noodles were perfectly cooked, with a moderate flavor that wasn't too salty. The portion size was generous 🍝😋. The tiramisu was a bit sweet; the coffee would have been even better if it were stronger ☕️. The staff were polite, smiling, and attentive, paying attention to details. This is the best service I've ever experienced 👍💯🥰

It's in a old building that brings out so much aesthetic feel, it's located right next to Mingle and can be found easily.

We came in on a public holiday weekday and there were enough seat to occupy us. We sat and just enjoyed the cold blast of aircond alongside great music playing in the background.

We ordered our own serving of pasta and was blown away with the quality of the food itself. Pasta was cooked perfectly and the flavor was immaculate. The drinks were ok but the main focus is really the food.

Next time we shall come back again to try their mains. This is a good spot if you just want to hang out with your friends within this vicinity and be served amazing quality of food.

A good place to chill & enjoy some delicious food! The Banger & Mashed “House-Made” is good. Mashed potato is smooth and goes well with the chicken sausage.

Pasta’s seasoning is on-point too! Not too salty and the portion is just right 👌 love the overall ambience!

name: Ebisu Bashi-Suji Shopping Street
reviews: One of the more crowd3d shopping streets of Shinsabashi, many shops at night and is bustling with people. Must come and must tour if in Osaka.
This is a very long stretch of mostly covered street lined with a good mix of shops on both sides. Very popular and crowded with both locals and tourists.

Osaka is famous for bustling streets, tasting food and shoppers. We started at Namba and continued north way. Millions shops, restaurants, coffee shops, second hands for luxury goods or normal one. Be prepared for millions on the street even on weekday. This is real Osaka experience. You will probably make a break at Dotombori canal, famous part of Osaka tourist life especially when dark and it’s nicely lit. No problem when you are hungry, thirsty, missing something

name: Harborland Park
reviews:
Was here in July recently.
Not really a green park here, more a waterfront.
This place seems to be popular with the local residents here.
At night is more lively with some food carts along the waterfront.

Fun place to eat and hangout. This place has lots of food options(Kobe beef, Brazillian restaurant, fastfood Hamburgers and more. Dont forget to visit the tower and the ferris wheel. The price of the tower is between 2000 and 3000 (based on your options of wanting to visit the open deck, restaurant etc.)

There is so much to do here at whatever pace you choose. It is lovely to relax overlooking the harbour and tower. If you’re lucky maybe catch a jumping fish. Take a Ferris wheel ride. Eat or drink overlooking the harbour.
Take a cruise, or a cruise with a meal. Visit the Toy or Maritime museums.

name: Lee Jetty
reviews: The best family name bridge among several. It’s neat, non-commercial, peaceful. There were good luck wishes on every door when we walked through all the way to the water. Reading the history of Lee family is very inspiring too.

Visited this Jetty since it’s one of our surnames, and thought it was a pretty good experience since it has an extended walk way into the sea past the residents home. Do be mindful that there’s locals living there so be respectful on the way in and out! 👍🏻

Lee Jetty in George Town, Penang, is a fascinating place to visit if you want to experience the unique heritage and charm of the famous Clan Jetties. Walking through the narrow wooden walkways lined with traditional houses feels like stepping back in time, while the colorful lanterns and decorative arches add a festive touch, especially in the evening. The view over the water at sunset is peaceful and very photogenic, making it perfect for travelers who love capturing authentic Penang moments. There are also small shops and stalls where you can enjoy local snacks or buy souvenirs, adding to the lively atmosphere. Lee Jetty is not only a tourist spot but also a living community, so it’s important to be respectful while exploring. If you’re visiting George Town, this heritage site is a must-see for culture, history, and beautiful waterfront views.

name: KKV Bukit Bintang
reviews: Visited this place randomly to pick some toys for kids. This place so colourful and beautiful. They have many varieties of toys, make up items, accessories and wide range of plush toys. Located at a prime location. Quality of the Toys are good and price is also affordable. Service at the counter can be improved. Tourists can pick gifts from this store. Recommended 👍

This KKV is large and has four levels. It's an interesting experience to visit a KKV like this. Kids will definitely love it, as after wandering around the first floor, they'll eagerly climb upstairs. However, I found the contents to be similar to other KKVs.

It's not stroller-friendly, with narrow escalators, and the shopping area is difficult to navigate with a stroller.

A lifestyle retail store that sells a wide variety of trendy, affordable products, including toys, stationery, beauty and skincare items, home essentials, and a wide selection of food and drinks.

Perfect place for window shoppings as there's always something new up to date, blind boxes, imported snacks and block toys.

Warning: Visit at your own risk, you will not leave empty handed.

name: Dewakan Restaurant
street: Platinum Park, Level 48, Skyviews, Naza Tower @, Persiaran KLCC
reviews:
A curated visit. The staff tries quite hard, A for effort. The room is on a high floor facing Petronas Towers, nice view with big windows.  All hard surfaces can make it a little loud if several tables are talking.

You’re first greeted by staff with earpieces, they remind you to mind the steps and will guide you through the kitchen tour and ingredient descriptions. It’s all quite interesting as an educational and cultural experience. Perhaps a bit less so as a dining experience. I’m a westerner and have been to dozens of Michelin starred restaurants including several with this type of menu. While I do very much appreciate the effort to showcase local and unusual ingredients, if I’m paying USD$225 per person before drinks I kinda want delicious food. There were some hits and misses here.

Service is generally crisp and efficient with a hint of warmth but I’d say some staff could use a bit more training. The wine pairing at USD$95 was decent. Some desserts were quite tasty.

On balance I’d say we had a memorable evening.

We are back again and this time we brought along our relatives from the US. Everyone had a wonderful dining experience. We are fortunate to be able to enjoy their new tasting menu and they brought it to yet another level.

The Raja Brooke butterfly was very impressive!

Congratulations to the team at Dewakan!

The kitchen tour was very enlightening with the use of ample local and raw ingredients in their menu. It is also good to know their effort in supporting local farmers and produce. It is without doubt they were awarded with the first Michelin Green Star for their sustainable practices.

Service level led by Hafriz and team were top notch and yet relaxing.

Well done!

Looking forward to returning again soon.

Dewakan was a truly impressive experience. The team’s creativity and deep knowledge of local and indigenous ingredients really stood out throughout the meal. What amazed me most was how they managed to turn what seems impossible into something refined, delicious, and meaningful on the plate.

Every course showed a strong attention to detail, not just in execution but also in storytelling. The introduction and explanation of the philosophy behind the indigenous ingredients added a lot of depth to the dining experience and made the meal feel educational as well as enjoyable.

One highlight I absolutely loved was the coconut jelly with mulberry and bambangan juice — it was a delightful surprise to my taste buds, refreshing, unexpected, and beautifully balanced.

A small note for future diners: there is only one course menu available throughout the night, and it’s highly recommended to make a reservation in advance.

That said, there are two minor downsides worth noting. The lighting was quite dim, which made it a little difficult to fully appreciate the visuals of the dishes, and the course meal took about three hours to complete, which may feel a bit long for some diners.

Overall, a memorable and thoughtfully curated experience that clearly reflects passion, research, and respect for local produce. A Michelin star that is truly well deserved.

name: Ching Ching by Pandan Republic
reviews: Ching Ching by Pandan Republic is amazing! The food feels like proper homemade Malaysian cooking – love their pandan layer cake and Nyonya kuih. But the real hidden gem has to be the coffee – pandan coffee and gula melaka coffee are so smooth and fragrant. A must-visit!

It's a lovely cafe and the girls there are super nice.  I went there in August hoping to try the Pandan Cream brûlée and was all sold out.  So gutted!  I went again 2 weeks ago all the way from Sydney and sold out again! After hearing my 2 failed attempts, the  girls agreed to make a new batch for us , and 2 hours later, we headed back for that promise and had the BEST pandan cream brûlée EVER! BTW the pandan soft serve really good too :)

Thanks so much !!!!

22 Nov 2025
We were at ‘Kwai Chai Hong’ the day before but didn’t notice this store as it looked too normal to us. I only found it while craving for dessert on Google map.

Level 2 looked more cosy compared to level 1 though the steps were abit steep.

We paid RM48.40 for 3 items. They have increased the price slightly.

* Pandan Coconut Soft Serve RM15
* Pandan Layers Cake RM13
* Gula Melaka Latte RM16

The soft serve was melted quickly but had overpowering pandan flavour. The pandan cake was interesting with sponge cake and agar agar layer. The latte was fragrance and better one we had in KL.

I was abit put off by the customer service. I asked if there was any availability on level 2 when I entered. Without answering my question, the staff told me ordering should be done there on level 1. Without any delay, we ordered the 3 items.

When we went up to level 2, we were surprised with a local team of running event participants talking loudly and they were all over the place at almost every table. We observed only one of them had 1 cup of coffee from the cafe. There was a foreigner couple at the corner having their beverage.

We quickly regained our peace when the staff came up with our cake and coffee and they left.

name: Big Baba | Taman Desa
reviews:
Since I was around the Taman Desa, OUG vicinity, I Googled for a Nyonya eatery which I have been craving for the longest time and found 1 hidden eatery in the midst of a quiet shop lot area close to the kindergarten and "Physiomax" which one can view from the main road.

Fyi, this branch has other outlets at Happy Mansion (which I've visited with my family in August and they've complained it was too pricey!), PJS 11 and Damansara Perdana. This is their 4th branch.

First impression of the front entrance almost turn me off and had me looking at my map Thrice (it looked rustic, practically like a run-down salvaged restaurant. Unlike it's New look at Happy Mansion, Taman Desa's Menu presentation is pathetic.📋The Menu stand outside the entrance was so rusty and unbalanced I thought it must have been salvaged from a junk shop. (Refer to the photos attached). But the moment I stepped in, I was amazed with their old family collection of photos in frames against the walls, tagged accordingly, similar to Mom's old "Singer" brand sewing machine, the old 60s table fan look-alike from my grandparents', the pineapple🍍tarts at the counter etc, that proved me wrong. Pretty cosy on a quiet Thursday evening.

My honest opinion: Wanted to order a few small dishes since I was alone dining but the prices were too steep for the image it reflected. 😕 The menu itself tells so much of the Owner's character for Not changing it to a New or More presentable menu; maybe he wanted to keep it as rustic as possible but the pages were all dog-earred and cello-taped all over at the sides with the Peranakan cloth-wrapped menu that's musty and acrid when I flipped through with my 2 fingers 🤏🏼, I've decided to stay simple in my orders.😪 Later, the Myanmar waitress offered me the "Lunch set" menu instead, price from RM 17.90 onwards which was slightly more affordable. She brought so many other menus; like I said, it's was too deep for my pocket!💸💰💰

Ordered: 1) Ayam pongteh set 🍛RM 17.90 2) Soft taufu bergedil RM 18.00
Total damage: RM 40.35 (including 6% tax). Wanted to order "Chap chai" but none in the menu. Moreover, the veggies were overpriced! 😪 The Ayam pongteh tasted too Salty 😭, although the chicken was tender but full of bones. Even the kuah aka gravy was too little. Portion control: 3 small wedged potatoes 🥔 🥔, 3 bony chicken. But I whacked them clean coz I was famished! I requested for Sambal (wt No Extra charge👍🏻) and it was The Highlight of the meal! The Fresh coloured chilly🌶️ pounded, mixed with lots of lime 🍋‍🟩, tasted like it had a hint of "belachan" in it, made my whole meal Worthwhile!😋👍🏻 The taufu bergedil was not too bad either which I dipped it with it's own thick black-chilly sauce like a prawn paste sauce for Assam Laksa. The bergedil ingredients was diced potato 🥔, diced chicken🍗, flour and a sprinkle of scallions in it, then dipped with egg🥚for the ultimate deep-fried taste and look! Overall, not too bad.😋

The toilet 🚽 (only 1) was beautifully decorated and well maintained. A cool ambience with all the rustic decòr but the Menu presentation📋 has to be changed for hygiene purposes. The price of the meals doesn't equate with the quality of Menu presentation.

We tried the lady’s finger, kailan garlic, tamarind fish and berkedel. Everything good. The sambal that goes with the bendi was so delicious.
Sago gula Melaka was also amazing.
Happy that now Taman Desa has a baba Nyonya restaurant!

Update: tried their lunch sets! All wonderful and delightful!
Cendol is awesome. Make sure you put enough gula Melaka.

Delicious Nyonya food in a comfortable setting, perfect for family or friends to gather. They don’t serve individual portions, so it may not be ideal if you’re dining alone. Plenty of parking available in the area too. Definitely worth a try!

name: Muzium Orang Asli Gombak (MOAG)
reviews: Worth a visit to the museum if you have time and like to wonder around the road less travelled. Free entrance.

Had a great time visiting the Orang Asli Museum in Gombak. The entrance was free, and the staff was friendly, explaining about Orang Asli culture.

For improvement tho, I think it would be helpful to include more details in the health section, such as specific locations and years.

The museum is open to public and free entry. You can spend a couple of hours here to really digest the information and facts. At the time of visit, the lower level is fully air-conditioned however, the 2nd level was warm and had faulty AC. The place is somewhat similar to other "Orang Asli" museums in Malaysia. It showcases the "Orang Asli" people's life from birth till death. There are dual languages available for the display, bahasa and English.

name: Kihachi Nagoya JR Central Towers
street: Meieki, 1 Chome−1−4JR セントラルタワーズ 12階
reviews: Fantastic service, great food, nice alcohol. Overall a lovely experience. A little pricy but the quality shows, and we found it to be worth the cash.
The spicy lobster was an interesting twist.

It was right on-the-spot decision to go here for lunch to surprise my best friend’s birthday. The staff I talked to was really amiable and accommodated my request. However, the waitress who served us was not and the food was so-so.

name: Go Tarbush @Suria KLCC
street: Petronas Twin Tower, F224, Signature Food Court Second Floor
reviews:
5/5 ⭐ (honestly a 6/5 if Google allowed it)

Tarbush was one of the BEST meals we had in Kuala Lumpur. Everything we ordered was incredible. The lamb literally melted in our mouths — soft, flavourful, and perfectly cooked. The rice was perfection, light and fragrant, and paired with the lamb beautifully.

We also tried the fatayer and the samosas and both were amazing. Crispy, fresh, and full of flavour without being spicy, which was perfect for me since I can’t handle as much heat as my partner. This place really proves you don’t need spice to have flavour.

The food came out quickly, portions were generous, and everything tasted like real comfort food with restaurant-level quality. Honestly such an underrated spot inside Suria KLCC — we could talk about the food all day.

Highly recommended. If you’re in KLCC and want proper Middle Eastern food that hits every time, Tarbush is a must-visit.

✅The location is clear and easy to find
✅The food is very good
Nice to try it from time to time.

⚠️ it’s OVERPRICED
Check the receipt 🧾 for instant: 48 MR 25 MR for Orange juice 🥤, 8 MR for piece diet‼️

Tarbush serves really good shawarma! The meat was flavorful and tender, and the portion was just right. The place has a nice Middle Eastern vibe, and the service was good too. If you’re craving proper shawarma in Kuala Lumpur, Tarbush is a solid choice.

name: KOSF Osu
reviews:
The staffs are very friendly & polite! They even prepare little gifts for each of us.

I’m not a Korean food expert, I can’t say whether it’s authentic Korean food or not. But overall I think it’s pretty good. The chicken is very crispy. I like their honey chicken.

Make a reservation before you come to avoid waiting for too long. I waited for half an hour because I didn’t know this was a popular place. The waiting area wasn’t spacious & there were a lot of delivery guys kept coming. It didn’t feel very clean & the chairs were broken. That’s why I deduct 1 star from my rating.

Overall, I’ve a good experience here & would come back again!

It's a restaurant making Japanese versions of Korean food. Food wasn't bad, just not authentic Korean food. I had the bibimbap. The banchan were service, but again, Japanese side dishes, not traditional banchan.
The store's food is very delicious. I have eaten with friends many times and it is always delicious and the staff is very friendly

name: Kouragumi
reviews: Ordering and getting a table is easy. If you pick all sorts of items on their menu and bring the tuna sashimi from next door, it would be approx SGD100 per pax.  Drinks menu is slim but with the grilled food, pairing with beer is good.

First time trying out seafood especially the king crab legs from Kouragumi Kuromon Market with my lovely wife. Love the place, clean, bright, reasonably priced. It’s towards the end of the market. Tasty and delicious seafood.

One of the cheapest in the market, i guess. Though still not cheap. Grilled abalone was nicer in Toba, maybe cause it was live abalone. Service was good. We were early and they offered us to sit in their restaurant and wait even before they were opened. Free wifi

name: Anggun Boutique Hotel and Spa
reviews:
Pretty little hotel in Bukit Bintang, centrally located and close to many attractions. Very friendly staff, excellent ginger tea and water available in the lobby at all times. Breakfast in the neighboring restaurant.
Fine for a few days in KL, but for a longer stay we would prefer a larger hotel.

Genuine "boutique" hotel. Totally colonial.
Really is a bit different.
The only strange thing is that the reception is only open 1100h to 1400h. Although there are usually friendly staff around to give a hand at all hours.
Will definitely stay again.
I like the rustic setup of the hotel. My room is spacious and quiet. Location wise can’t fault at all. Lots of massage parlours and eateries in the neighbourhood. Will definitely come back to stay

name: Lim Jetty
reviews: The ability to walk around among the locals who decided to live on the jetty is really generous. Compared do Chew this is so much nicer, it’s not over run by market stall filled with trinkets( whilst that’s also nice to see) respect the locals and go out and take a peek.
Last jetty on the road, but for me the best- quiet and  with 2 temples in the beginning and at the end. Great view too.
Not as commercialised or busy as the other jetty’s when we did our Jetty tour. Nice little seating area with a pastel coloured bench. Usual nice view of the bridge from Georgetown to Penang.

name: Trattoria Yamakawa
reviews: Authentic Italian cuisine with fresh local ingredients. Lunch menu can be enjoyed from very generous 1650 yen with the combination of salad, drink and pasta. But more expensive menu with secondi piattis are those that cannot be easily found around here, so I recommend trying those at least once. My favorite was onion soup and very authentic carbonara with thick egg yolk sauce. Also their house-made cold cuts are a thing. This restaurant should never go out of business so I will regularly visit here.

A hidden gem in the city of Suzuka!

The owner has been visiting Italy since 20 years and learning all the secrets of the Italian cuisine (also speaks Italian very well).
His dishes are delicious with variety from fish, meat, pasta and pizza, all cooked with original techniques which stands out in the taste and texture.

He has brought numerous wines from all around Italy and can give useful suggestions for food-wine pairing.

During the F1 Grand Prix you can find a lot of people from the teams that visit this trattoria for some delicious treats and occasionally some drivers that take their mechanics out for dinner.

Overall a very good Italian restaurant (the best in Suzuka)!

It was a surprising experience to find this restaurant in the middle of Suzuka. As an Italian, I was pleased to find a warm service, with some waiters even speaking and welcoming us in Italian! The food was great and at modest price. The ravioli were amazing, pizza was good. I would definitely recommend it!

name: Box KL
reviews:
I stumble upon this place as I was looking for somewhere that doesn't close at 10pm and this place caught my eye but just a warning that parking is a little difficult to find. The staff was very warm and nice, and the service was pretty fast!

I sat outside, though I must say the surrounding noise of passersby, the vehicles on the road, and the train passing might be a little loud for some, but I do find all those background noise to be quite peaceful so it was great for me but do note that the smell might not be the best due to the exhaust fumes and  the possibility of garbage trucks driving beside you.

The drinks were pretty good, but the highlight for me would be the honey chicken wings, I would definitely drop by just for that, it was amazing! Can't wait to come back for those wings and trying new drinks on the menu!

Came here with my girlfriend for the first time and ordered two pastas and of course drinks. Everything tastes delicious, customer service is great and very kind, and the choice of music is *chef’s kiss*!

Bak kata orang Malaysia “boleh repeat lagi ni” Thanks for the food and experience! Can’t wait to visit again!
Came here from a TikTok recommendation and surprisingly, the food was really good! We ordered the beef aglio spaghetti @@ The staff were also very friendly. Would definitely come again 😺😺

name: SAIDO
street: Sakurajima, 2 Chome−1−33 ニューヨーク・エリア
reviews:
We had a really enjoyable meal at Saido in Universal Studios Japan. We ordered the tonkatsu set and the beef steak bowl with tempura, and everything was delicious. The tonkatsu was crispy and tender, while the beef steak bowl was flavorful and well-cooked, and the tempura was light and perfectly fried.

The waitress was very friendly and attentive, which made the dining experience even more pleasant. To finish our meal, we shared the Parfait with NY cheesecake and hojicha, it was tasty, nicely balanced, and a great way to end the meal.

Overall, Saido was a great dining choice inside the park, and we would happily eat here again on our next visit.

LOVED THIS PLACE!!! We got seated near the window so had a view of the flying dinosaur ride and it was great! We loved the food, it was aesthetic and so tasty!! The staff were extremely friendly and kept saying we were ‘kawaii’ and took a photo for us! 10/10

It’s a Japanese restaurant in the Universal studio. We tried the beef set, sashimi set and the tonkatsu set. All are delicious and well presented, the portion were generous as well. The staff were friendly and would take picture for customers. The place is rather spacious so the atmosphere is relaxing, a very precious moment after all the crowded events in the theme park.

name: 鬼仔巷文化街 Lorong Panggung
reviews: Open time At 9am on time. There are a gate if not open. If go there early you can foto own your time good foto point. Old style of Chinese history . Nice foto and good place to go this area.a lot place for fun.

鬼仔巷 (Kwai Chai Hong, Lorong Panggung) is a cultural gem in Kuala Lumpur’s Chinatown, beautifully blending history and art to revive the charm of the old Chinese community. This meticulously restored alley is adorned with vibrant murals depicting the daily lives of early Chinese settlers, transporting visitors back in time. The combination of traditional architecture and modern artistic elements creates a unique atmosphere, making it a popular spot for tourists and photographers.

As night falls, glowing lanterns add a nostalgic touch, enhancing the charm of the street. Surrounding the alley are cozy cafés, artisan shops, and local food stalls, offering visitors a taste of both culture and cuisine. Whether you're a history enthusiast, an art lover, or simply looking for a unique experience, 鬼仔巷 (Kwai Chai Hong, Lorong Panggung) is a must-visit cultural landmark in Kuala Lumpur.

Lorong Panggung in Kuala Lumpur is a vibrant tourist attraction, nestled within the city's Chinatown and easily accessible via MRT and LRT. It's generally a safe spot, bustling with tourists snapping photos. While some parts of the alley could use regular cleaning, the area captures the essence of Kuala Lumpur's rich history with migrants. Entry is free, and it's lined with charming cafés and nearby restaurants, making it a delightful place to explore. The mix of heritage and modernity gives it a unique charm. Overall, Lorong Panggung is a must-visit, earning four stars.

name: Grand Sky Restaurant
reviews:
They have air conditioned sitting inside and we love that this is not crazy packed during Sat night. A reprieve from the madness in the Main Street. Staff is not too pushy as well.

Pleasantly surprised that the food was very good. The top in our list is oyster omelette. Very impressed by how thin and crisp the starch omelette is. Oysters are plenty and juicy as well.

Next was the satay. The chicken satay has lemon grass in its marinate, a nice fragrance to the meat. Beef satay is cooked just right. They have mutton satay but we didn’t order.

The vegetable was a little “old” and doesn’t have the same texture as more tender versions.

BBQ chicken wings are great too. We were missing lime to squeeze juice onto the chicken but we did taste a hint of lime.

Honestly the KL local street food; Satay, BBQ chicken wings and Oyster Omelette were good on our 1st dinner here. However, we regretted we came back here on our 2nd dinner since the staff recommended the seafood dishes.

Black Pepper Crabs:
We asked for a bigger crab size of approximate 700g. When cooked and served, it was very much smaller than pre-cooked size. Excuse given was the crab "will shrink" after cooking... really? Even the crab shell will shrink.. are you sure? The crab was too salty and less peppery.

Sambal Stingray:
We ate a small mouthful and the meat was very tough unlike other similar moist Stingray dishes we usually eat. We left it a big portion unfinished (see photos of unfinished stingray). RM$50 for this small and "inedible" Stingray is definitely ex.

Salted Egg Yolk Prawns:
Tasted more like butter prawns and not well-seasoned with salted egg yolk.

Besides the above seafood dishes, we ordered the Yam Ring and "2 kinds" kai lan vegetables. Both are average and nothing to rave!

Overall, we were disappointed on our 2nd dinner and don't think we will be back again despite initial plans of doing so.

We ate at this place twice during our stay, and the food was very good both times. The prices are reasonable, and the staff is very kind and welcoming, which made the overall experience pleasant.

Unfortunately, the downside was that on two separate occasions we found a hair in our food, which was quite disappointing. We hope the restaurant can improve in this area, as the food and service themselves are really worth recommending.

name: GOCHIKURA 神戸本店
street: Higashikawasakicho, 1 Chome−6−1 2F 神戸ハーバーランドumie MOSAIC
reviews: If you’re looking for a delicious and affordable restaurant at Kobe Harborland umie Mosaic, I highly recommend this place! I was really surprised by how good their hamburger was — it’s delicious and very reasonably priced! Perfect for anyone who wants to enjoy tasty food without spending too much!
They’re beef delicious and juicy, also locate at the nice mall and restaurant very cosy place to have Wagyu Beef crave.

Menu was difficult to read, even with the auto translation. Not sure how to order the ala carte menu. In the end, ordered the hamburg steak anniversary set. Kobe beef appetizer taste great! Inoki Mushroom is too salty. Hamburg Kobe beef steak is not bad but can’t really tell it is Kobe beef. Kobe beef sushi is bad, no beef taste at all! Chicken skewer with special miso sauce taste like BBQ sauce, with salt is quite tasteless, overall chicken skewers are bad. Dessert is plain yogurt with caramel sauce, not bad. Shogai (Soju highball) with shine muscat is very good.

name: Goemon
reviews:
焼いてる方変わりましたか？
以前はすごく美味しく丁寧なお仕事をされてる印象でしたが、久しぶりに利用させてもらって、味も質もかなり落ちてると思いました。
物価も上がっておりますし、量が少なくなるのはしょうがないと思いますが、値段が上がって質が落ちるのは・・・

店内は小綺麗にされていて、清潔感がありました。お座敷とテーブル席、カウンターそれぞれ10名以上くらいは座れるでしょうか。

ランチは総合して普通でしょうか。

なにを食べても安心。

name: Victoria Fountain
reviews:
Kuala Lumpur's Queen Victoria Fountain, located in Dataran Merdeka, is one of the few well-preserved British colonial monuments in Malaysia. The fountain was built in 1904 to commemorate Queen Victoria's 60th anniversary on the throne. All parts were shipped from England and assembled in Kuala Lumpur. It was originally located at Medan Pasar, but was later moved to its current location due to traffic considerations.
Designed in Art Nouveau style, the fountain's main body is made of glazed tiles, with green, blue and brown colors symbolizing natural elements. Eight lions and dragon-shaped water-spouting beasts surround it, symbolizing wisdom, loyalty and strength. In the center is an octagonal marble column that supports a five-story basin-shaped structure, with a water outlet at the top. Although small in size, its exquisite carvings and historical significance make it a popular spot for tourists to take photos. The fountain is located near the Sultan Abdul Samad Building and is surrounded by many museums and historical buildings, making it a great place to explore Kuala Lumpur’s colonial history and culture.

A charming slice of colonial history right in the heart of the city. Built in 1897 to commemorate Queen Victoria’s Diamond Jubilee, this cast-iron fountain was imported from England and still stands proudly near Merdeka Square. It’s beautifully detailed and makes a great photo stop, especially with the Sultan Abdul Samad building in the background. A lovely reminder of KL’s layered past — well worth a quick visit!
Vintage and beautiful make water fountain, The fountain was sent out from Britain to commemorate Queen Victoria’s diamond jubilee in 1897.

name: Arimazen Sushi
reviews:
2026-02-26 I'm really glad that I could find a restaurant at Arima that is open for dinner and also does takeout. After hiking up Mount Rokko, I just wanted a relaxing onsen bath and a nice takeout dinner in my hotel room.

*2000 yen food trap* About to give them 4-5 star but not anymore after they charged me 2000 yen for appertizers for 2 people without letting me know. They let us sit down and brought three super small bowls of eggplant, vegetable, bean sprouts so we thought it was complimentary so we just ate and enjoyed our sushi. The food is good for the price so we were happy. Our total bill was around 8300 yen and came to pay and the bill was over 10000 yen. I asked and they showed me "here is your appertizers" what the heck! If they give you anything, please ask if it is free. I would never go back to this type of service/business. I attached the photo of food trap

Really amazing place , very welcoming,  out of this world food experience. I had the chef special and it was a multi course experience. Out of this world grilled fish and sushi! Lots of cool sushi to also try from the menu like dea urchin. Amazing restaurant thank you for welcoming me and your hard work. Gochisosama deshita. 🙏🙏

name: Medan Pasar
reviews:
​A Quiet Historic Landmark in the Old Town

Although I hardly come to this part of town anymore, I’m glad to see that this small square has been revitalized. It is now a small park featuring a fountain, some greenery, and even swings and benches for people to rest.

The Highlights:
* The Clock Tower: This is a key landmark for the "Old Town" of Kuala Lumpur and holds significant value as one of only two clock towers in the city (the other being the Sultan Abdul Samad building).
* The Park: The addition of the fountain and benches makes for a decent quick stop.

The Critique:
* Missing History: It is a shame that there is absolutely no signage sharing the history of the clock tower.
* The Atmosphere: It is truly sad to see that many of the surrounding heritage shophouses have closed down and the office buildings sit vacant. The upkeep of the area feels lacking compared to other tourist spots.
* The Crowd: The vibe has shifted significantly. The area is now frequented mostly by migrant workers on the weekends and does attract the homeless, so just be mindful of your surroundings.

Verdict: A spot with immense potential and history, but currently feeling a bit neglected and hollowed out.
Ancient one. Do visit during sunsets to witness the lightings. A well maintained place nearby the clock tower river of Life is also there to visit in the evening to witness lightings

Visited back in Jan.

The Medan Pasar is what used to be the old market square until it was moved to the nearby central market. Nowadays, the square still preserves vestiges of the old market by the concentration of banks surrounding the square. The square is okay for historical reasons and the middle of the square has the Old Market Square Clock Tower landmark of the city. Otherwise there’s not much to see around the square and the shops aren’t all that interesting either. You’ll likely pass the square at some point because of its proximity to Chinatown, Merdeka Square, Masjid Jamek etc and all the attractions around it.

name: Traditional Japanese Cuisine Kobe Tamura

reviews:
I have special japanese restaurant at Kobe Tamura restaurant.
I love the enviroment, it was so elegant and very Japanese stylish. It was so calm and definitely less people.
The food was delicious compare with the level 2 restaurant where the combination Western and Japanese style were provided.
I will choose this restaurant for next visit in Kobe, Japanese

I love Japanese cuisine because it is so simple, yet so complex and varied.

So I really tried a lot of Japanese restaurants. Actually almost everywhere in the world. But what you get here is second to none!

The compositions of the menu are definitely special! You can taste almost every ingredient even if the mixture offers a unique taste.

Perfect and minimally seasoned, so that you can enjoy the individual parts. The shoyu and the fresh wasabi are the ideal complement!

The dessert was to die for, not too sweet and super light!

And the red beans together with the matcha - the combination is the perfect ending to a perfect meal!

The restaurant does not need to hide from Michelin star kitchens!

But what made the evening really unique was the service! Even though communicating in Japanese/English and using hands and feet was not that easy! The neighboring tables also partially helped to translate individual words! Haha what an experience!

Many thanks for this unique and warm hospitality.

Dissatisfied Disappointed
Onsen tamago instead of fresh egg without explanation before they serve. Ponzu taste not good for us. I did not felt to took a picture because of disappointment. bday surprised becomes nightmare. we did not finish to eat all, since our course cost ¥34,000 plus we ate all meat only because Montainai.#credittoladystaff assisting us she's so kind.

name: Durian street food
reviews:
We stopped at the Durian stand in front of KK Super Mart on Jalan Alor and had an excellent experience. We chose two Musang King durians, and the staff were incredibly friendly and helpful. They opened a few fruits first to show us the quality and made sure we got the best ones, really great service and attention to detail.

The durians themselves were outstanding, perfectly ripe, creamy, and full of that rich Musang King flavor. You could tell the quality was top-notch, and the price was absolutely fair for what we got.

Highly recommend this stand if you want to try fresh, premium durian right in the heart of Kuala Lumpur. Great people, honest prices, and amazing fruit.
Price a bit high but nice musang king durian. Price was rm 45

name: Minato Miharashidai
reviews: Charming little spot with benches and an amazing view. A lot of Kobe, Sannomiya, the sea and islands are visible. Kitano buildings are in the foreground.

神戸に立ち寄ったときにたまたま散歩がてらたどり着いた展望スポットです。
港街の神戸らしい景色を楽しむことができます。訪れる時間帯で表情が変わるのも魅力。
朝の時間帯でちょうど天気が良かったときは朝日を眺めることができました。
人通りは少ないので一人で行くときは明るい時間帯がよさそうです。
古いですがベンチもありひと息つくことができます。観光地の喧騒から少し離れて、神戸の港町の雰囲気を静かに味わえるおすすめの場所です。

風が吹いた時に葉っぱの擦れる音しかしないような静かで落ち着く場所です。
日晴らしも良く、天気が良ければ大阪湾の向こう側まで見えそうでした。
あいにくの曇り空でしたが、遠くまで見渡せて、最高の景色でした。
30分くらい景色を見ながら過ごしましたが、一組しか通らず、のんびりと過ごすには最適な場所です。

name: Seafood Dining 1932
street: Minatojima, 1 Chome−1−6 センチュリオンホテルヴィンテージ神戸 9F
reviews:
The view was really nice from the counters, and the service of the staff was so good!! They’re so smiley and friendly and professional, thank you everyone ❤️
Food was really tasty, sophisticated, and reasonably priced too! Pistachio ice cream was so cheap and sooo delicious, highly recommended!

This is a hotel restaurant, in the middle of nowhere. Almost all customers are people staying at the hotel. They don't really expect customers from outside. The food was good over all. Prices are a bit high, and the view of the city is not the best.
This was a vintage style hotel sand to be honest they tried. I liked the room but it was really chosen for it's convenience for business.

name: Nagoya Higashiyama "Living Forest"
reviews:
前から気になっていた場所、時間がとれたので行ってきたけど自然がいっぱいでいい感じの所ですね。

自宅の近所には猪高緑地とか牧野が池緑地とかあってそれぞれいい場所なんですがここは緑地の中央部に小川（せせらぎ）があるのが他とは違うところです。

小川のあたりには芝生広場や大小の池と湿地帯、水田、炭焼き小屋がありそのせせらぎの北側南側東側が尾根みたいになっていて『ちょっとした登山コース』みたいになっているようです。

『ちょっとした登山コース』上には猪高緑地の名古屋市第２位の標高を誇る親鸞山には少しだけ高さの足りない104.9ｍの名もなき山頂があり晴れた日には御嶽山も見えるらしいです。

北側の尾根を越えて平和公園に接するあたりはハンノキ湿地という（実はほぼ池）場所やコアラさんの大好物のユーカリを栽培している場所もあって何かと楽しい。

狭い里山ですがいろいろと面白い場所です。

里山！
散歩、気分転換にときどきお邪魔します。
管理事務所にきれいなトイレがあり、ありがたい。
あまり人工的な過剰な整備がされていないところがいい。
ずっと残しておいてください。
子供と昆虫採集するのに良い。池や水路があるのでザリガニ取りもできる。階段を上がって山の方にいけばチッチゼミも居ました。街中にはいないので自然の豊かさを感じられます。
